meta.blurb_uz: Nitsshe og'ir kasallikdan tuzalgach yozgan, o'zi «eng quvnoq» deb atagan kitobi. 383 ta qisqa va uzun aforizmda u axloq, din, ilm, san'at, sevgi va bilim haqida bahslashadi. Mashhur «Telba odam» parchasi («Xudo o'ldi»), «eng og'ir yuk» — abadiy qaytish g'oyasi va Zardushtning ilk ko'rinishi shu kitobda.
meta.why_uz: Nitssheni boshlash uchun eng qulay kitob: har bir aforizm alohida o'qiladi, ko'pi bir-ikki daqiqalik. Til — XX asr boshidagi adabiy ingliz tili (C1), shuning uchun har bir xatboshining o'zbekchasi, bob lug'ati va savollar yordam beradi. Fikrlar munozarali — o'qiganda ular bilan bahslashish ham o'qishning bir qismi.
meta.author_uz: Fridrix Nitsshe (1844–1900) — nemis faylasufi va filolog. U an'anaviy axloq va dinni keskin tanqid qilgan, «Xudo o'ldi», «kuchga iroda», «abadiy qaytish», «Ubermensch» g'oyalari bilan mashhur. «Quvnoq ilm» 1882-yilda chiqqan, 1887-yilda so'zboshi va beshinchi kitob qo'shilgan.
meta.edition_uz: To'liq nasriy matn: so'zboshi va beshta kitob (1–383-aforizmlar). Inglizcha matn — Thomas Common tarjimasi (1910), Project Gutenberg #52881. Boshqa tarjimonlar qilgan she'riy ilovalar («Hazil, hiyla va qasos», «Shahzoda Qushdek-Erkin qo'shiqlari») kiritilmagan; uzun xatboshilar o'qish qulay bo'lishi uchun bo'lingan. O'zbekcha parallel tarjima — WordDrop tarjimasi: har bir xatboshi qo'lda, asliga yaqin tarzda tarjima qilingan.

themes.uz: «Xudo o'ldi» — Yevropa endi diniy e'tiqodga tayanmaydi; bu nimani anglatishini inson hali tushunmagan (125-aforizm).
Abadiy qaytish — agar hayotingni cheksiz marta aynan shunday qayta yashashing kerak bo'lsa-chi? (341-aforizm)
Poda instinkti — axloq ko'pincha shaxsni emas, guruhni saqlash vositasi.
Quvnoq ilm — bilimni og'ir yuk emas, quvonch va o'yin sifatida qabul qilish.
Taqdirni sevish — zarur narsani go'zal deb ko'rishni o'rganish (276-aforizm).

chapters.title: The joy of recovery

paras.en: 1. Perhaps more than one preface would be necessary for this book; and after all it might still be doubtful whether any one could be brought nearer to the experiences in it by means of prefaces, without having himself experienced something similar. It seems to be written in the language of the thawing-wind: there is wantonness, restlessness, contradiction and April-weather in it; so that one is as constantly reminded of the proximity of winter as of the victory over it: the victory which is coming, which must come, which has perhaps already come.... Gratitude continually flows forth, as if the most unexpected thing had happened, the gratitude of a convalescent—for convalescence was this most unexpected thing.
paras.uz: 1. Ehtimol, bu kitobga bitta emas, bir nechta so'zboshi kerakdir; shunda ham, o'zi shunga o'xshash narsani boshdan kechirmagan odamni so'zboshilar yordamida undagi tajribalarga yaqinlashtirish mumkinmi-yo'qmi, baribir shubhali bo'lib qolardi. U go'yo erituvchi shamol tilida yozilganga o'xshaydi: unda sho'xlik, bezovtalik, qarama-qarshilik va aprel havosi bor; shuning uchun odamga qishning yaqinligi ham, unga qarshi g'alaba ham doim eslatib turiladi: kelayotgan, kelishi shart bo'lgan, balki allaqachon kelib bo'lgan g'alaba... Minnatdorlik to'xtovsiz oqib chiqadi, go'yo eng kutilmagan narsa sodir bo'lgandek — tuzalayotgan odamning minnatdorligi, chunki eng kutilmagan narsa aynan tuzalish edi.

paras.en: "Joyful Wisdom": that implies the Saturnalia of a spirit which has patiently withstood a long, frightful pressure—patiently, strenuously, impassionately, without submitting, but without hope—and which is now suddenly o'erpowered with hope, the hope of health, the intoxication of convalescence. What wonder that much that is unreasonable and foolish thereby comes to light: much wanton tenderness expended even on problems which have a prickly hide, and are not therefore fit to be fondled and allured. The whole book is really nothing but a revel after long privation and impotence: the frolicking of returning energy, of newly awakened belief in a to-morrow and after-to-morrow; of sudden sentience and prescience of a future, of near adventures, of seas open once more, and aims once more permitted and believed in. And what was now all behind me!
paras.uz: «Quvnoq ilm»: bu uzoq, dahshatli bosimga sabr bilan bardosh bergan — sabr bilan, qat'iyat bilan, sovuqqonlik bilan, bo'ysunmay, lekin umidsiz — va endi to'satdan umidga, sog'liq umidiga, tuzalish mastligiga chulg'angan ruhning Saturnaliyasini anglatadi. Shu tufayli ko'p aqlsiz va ahmoqona narsalar yuzaga chiqishining nimasi ajablanarli: hatto tikanli terisi bor, shuning uchun erkalash va yo'ldan urishga yaramaydigan muammolarga ham ko'p sho'x mehr sarflangan. Butun kitob aslida uzoq mahrumlik va ojizlikdan keyingi bazmdan boshqa narsa emas: qaytib kelayotgan kuchning o'ynoqiligi, ertaga va indinga bo'lgan yangi uyg'ongan ishonchning; kelajakni, yaqin sarguzashtlarni, yana ochilgan dengizlarni, yana ruxsat berilgan va ishonilgan maqsadlarni to'satdan sezish va oldindan his qilishning. Endi esa nimalar ortimda qolgan edi!

paras.en: This track of desert, exhaustion, unbelief, and frigidity in the midst of youth, this advent of grey hairs at the wrong time, this tyranny of pain, surpassed, however, by the tyranny of pride which repudiated the consequences of pain—and consequences are comforts,—this radical isolation, as defence against the contempt of mankind become morbidly clairvoyant, this restriction upon principle to all that is bitter, sharp, and painful in knowledge, as prescribed by the disgust which had gradually resulted from imprudent spiritual diet and pampering—it is called Romanticism,—oh, who could realise all those feelings of mine!
paras.uz: Yoshlikning o'rtasidagi bu cho'l, holsizlik, ishonchsizlik va sovuqlik yo'li, bu bevaqt kelgan oq sochlar, og'riqning bu zulmi — garchi uni og'riqning oqibatlarini rad etgan g'urur zulmi ortda qoldirgan bo'lsa ham (oqibatlar esa tasalli-ku), — kasallik darajasida ko'zi ochilib ketgan insoniyat nafratiga qarshi himoya sifatidagi bu tub yolg'izlik, bilimdagi barcha achchiq, o'tkir va og'riqli narsalar bilan o'z ixtiyori bilan cheklanish — ehtiyotsiz ruhiy parhez va erkalanishdan asta-sekin paydo bo'lgan jirkanish shuni buyurgan edi — buni romantizm deyishadi, — oh, mening o'sha tuyg'ularimning hammasini kim tushuna olardi!

paras.en: He, however, who could do so would certainly forgive me everything, and more than a little folly, boisterousness and "Joyful Wisdom"—for example, the handful of songs which are given along with the book on this occasion,—songs in which a poet makes merry over all poets in a way not easily pardoned.—Alas, it is not only on the poets and their fine "lyrical sentiments" that this reconvalescent must vent his malignity: who knows what kind of victim he seeks, what kind of monster of material for parody will allure him ere long? Incipit tragœdia, it is said at the conclusion of this seriously frivolous book; let people be on their guard! Something or other extraordinarily bad and wicked announces itself: incipit parodia, there is no doubt...
paras.uz: Kim buni tushuna olsa, albatta, meni hamma narsa uchun kechiradi, ozgina emas, ko'proq ahmoqlik, shovqin-suron va «Quvnoq ilm» uchun ham — masalan, bu safar kitob bilan birga berilgan bir hovuch qo'shiq uchun: ularda bir shoir barcha shoirlar ustidan osonlikcha kechirib bo'lmaydigan tarzda kuladi. — Afsus, bu sog'ayayotgan odam o'z zahrini faqat shoirlarga va ularning nozik «lirik tuyg'ulari»ga sochmaydi: kim biladi, u qanday qurbon izlayapti, tez orada qanday parodiya mahluqi uni o'ziga tortadi? Bu jiddiy-yengiltak kitobning oxirida «Incipit tragoedia» deyilgan; ehtiyot bo'linglar! Nimadir g'ayrioddiy yomon va yovuz narsa o'zini e'lon qilmoqda: incipit parodia, bunga shubha yo'q...

paras.en: 2. ——But let us leave Herr Nietzsche; what does it matter to people that Herr Nietzsche has got well again?... A psychologist knows few questions so attractive as those concerning the relations of health to philosophy, and in the case when he himself falls sick, he carries with him all his scientific curiosity into his sickness. For, granting that one is a person, one has necessarily also the philosophy of one's personality, there is, however, an important distinction here. With the one it is his defects which philosophise, with the other it is his riches and powers. The former requires his philosophy, whether it be as support, sedative, or medicine, as salvation, elevation, or self-alienation; with the latter it is merely a fine luxury, at best the voluptuousness of a triumphant gratitude, which must inscribe itself ultimately in cosmic capitals on the heaven of ideas.
paras.uz: 2. ——Lekin janob Nitssheni qo'yaylik; janob Nitsshe yana sog'ayib ketganining odamlarga nima ahamiyati bor?.. Psixolog uchun sog'liqning falsafaga munosabati haqidagi savollarchalik qiziqarli savollar kam; va o'zi kasal bo'lib qolganda, u butun ilmiy qiziquvchanligini kasalligiga ham olib kiradi. Chunki, agar odam shaxs bo'lsa, unda muqarrar ravishda o'z shaxsiyatining falsafasi ham bo'ladi; ammo bu yerda muhim farq bor. Birida uning kamchiliklari falsafa so'qadi, boshqasida — boyligi va kuchlari. Birinchisiga falsafa kerak: tayanch, tinchlantiruvchi yoki dori sifatida, najot, yuksalish yoki o'zidan begonalashish sifatida; ikkinchisi uchun esa bu shunchaki go'zal hashamat, nari borsa, oxir-oqibat g'oyalar osmoniga kosmik bosh harflar bilan yozilishi kerak bo'lgan g'olib minnatdorlikning rohati.

paras.en: In the other more usual case, however, when states of distress occupy themselves with philosophy (as is the case with all sickly thinkers—and perhaps the sickly thinkers preponderate in the history of philosophy), what will happen to the thought itself which is brought under the pressure of sickness? This is the important question for psychologists: and here experiment is possible. We philosophers do just like a traveller who resolves to awake at a given hour, and then quietly yields himself to sleep: we surrender ourselves temporarily, body and soul, to the sickness, supposing we become ill—we shut, as it were, our eyes on ourselves.
paras.uz: Boshqa, odatiyroq holatda esa, qayg'u holatlari falsafa bilan shug'ullanganda (barcha kasalmand mutafakkirlarda shunday — balki falsafa tarixida kasalmand mutafakkirlar ustundir), kasallik bosimi ostiga tushgan fikrning o'ziga nima bo'ladi? Psixologlar uchun muhim savol mana shu: va bu yerda tajriba qilish mumkin. Biz faylasuflar ma'lum soatda uyg'onishga qaror qilib, keyin xotirjam uyquga beriladigan yo'lovchi kabi qilamiz: kasal bo'lib qolsak, vaqtincha jonu tanimiz bilan kasallikka taslim bo'lamiz — go'yo o'zimizga nisbatan ko'zimizni yumamiz.

paras.en: And as the traveller knows that something does not sleep, that something counts the hours and will awake him, we also know that the critical moment will find us awake—that then something will spring forward and surprise the spirit in the very act, I mean in weakness, or reversion, or submission, or obduracy, or obscurity, or whatever the morbid conditions are called, which in times of good health have the pride of the spirit opposed to them (for it is as in the old rhyme: "The spirit proud, peacock and horse are the three proudest things of earthly source").
paras.uz: Va yo'lovchi nimadir uxlamasligini, nimadir soatlarni sanab, uni uyg'otishini bilgani kabi, biz ham hal qiluvchi lahza bizni hushyor holda topishini bilamiz — o'shanda nimadir oldinga otilib, ruhni aynan qilmishi ustida qo'lga tushiradi: zaiflikda, yoki orqaga qaytishda, yoki taslim bo'lishda, yoki qaysarlikda, yoki qorong'ilikda, yoki sog'lom paytlarda ruhning g'ururi qarshi turadigan kasal holatlar qanday atalsa ham (chunki eski qofiyada aytilganidek: «Mag'rur ruh, tovus va ot — yer yuzidagi eng mag'rur uch zot»).

paras.en: After such self-questioning and self-testing, one learns to look with a sharper eye at all that has hitherto been philosophised; one divines better than before the arbitrary by-ways, side-streets, resting-places, and sunny places of thought, to which suffering thinkers, precisely as sufferers, are led and misled: one knows now in what direction the sickly body and its requirements unconsciously press, push, and allure the spirit—towards the sun, stillness, gentleness, patience, medicine, refreshment in any sense whatever. Every philosophy which puts peace higher than war, every ethic with a negative grasp of the idea of happiness, every metaphysic and physic that knows a finale, an ultimate condition of any kind whatever, every predominating, æsthetic or religious longing for an aside, a beyond, an outside, an above—all these permit one to ask whether sickness has not been the motive which inspired the philosopher.
paras.uz: Bunday o'z-o'zini so'roq qilish va o'z-o'zini sinashdan keyin odam shu paytgacha falsafa qilingan hamma narsaga o'tkirroq ko'z bilan qarashni o'rganadi; azob chekayotgan mutafakkirlar aynan azob chekuvchi sifatida yetaklanadigan va adashtiriladigan fikrning o'zboshimcha so'qmoqlarini, yon ko'chalarini, dam olish joylarini va quyoshli joylarini avvalgidan yaxshiroq sezadi: endi u kasal tana va uning ehtiyojlari ruhni ongsiz ravishda qaysi tomonga bosishini, itarishini va jalb qilishini biladi — quyoshga, sokinlikka, muloyimlikka, sabrga, dorilarga, har qanday ma'nodagi yangilanishga. Tinchlikni urushdan yuqori qo'yadigan har bir falsafa, baxt tushunchasini salbiy anglaydigan har bir axloq, finalni, qandaydir yakuniy holatni biladigan har bir metafizika va fizika, chetga, narigi tomonga, tashqariga, yuqoriga intiladigan har bir ustun estetik yoki diniy sog'inch — bularning hammasi faylasufni ilhomlantirgan narsa kasallik emasmidi, deb so'rashga imkon beradi.

paras.en: The unconscious disguising of physiological requirements under the cloak of the objective, the ideal, the purely spiritual, is carried on to an alarming extent,—and I have often enough asked myself, whether, on the whole, philosophy hitherto has not generally been merely an interpretation of the body, and a misunderstanding of the body. Behind the loftiest estimates of value by which the history of thought has hitherto been governed, misunderstandings of the bodily constitution, either of individuals, classes, or entire races are concealed.
paras.uz: Fiziologik ehtiyojlarni obyektivlik, ideal, sof ruhiylik niqobi ostida ongsiz ravishda yashirish xavotirli darajada keng tarqalgan, — va men o'zimdan yetarlicha ko'p so'raganman: umuman olganda, falsafa shu paytgacha shunchaki tanani talqin qilish va tanani noto'g'ri tushunish bo'lmaganmi? Fikr tarixi shu paytgacha boshqarib kelgan eng yuksak qadriyat baholari ortida alohida shaxslar, tabaqalar yoki butun irqlarning tana tuzilishini noto'g'ri tushunish yashiringan.

paras.en: One may always primarily consider these audacious freaks of metaphysic, and especially its answers to the question of the worth of existence, as symptoms of certain bodily constitutions; and if, on the whole, when scientifically determined, not a particle of significance attaches to such affirmations and denials of the world, they nevertheless furnish the historian and psychologist with hints so much the more valuable (as we have said) as symptoms of the bodily constitution, its good or bad condition, its fullness, powerfulness, and sovereignty in history; or else of its obstructions, exhaustions, and impoverishments, its premonition of the end, its will to the end.
paras.uz: Metafizikaning bu dadil injiqliklarini, ayniqsa uning hayot qadri haqidagi savolga bergan javoblarini, har doim avvalo ma'lum tana tuzilishlarining alomatlari deb qarash mumkin; va agar ilmiy jihatdan aniqlanganda dunyoni bunday tasdiqlash va inkor etishda zarracha ham ma'no bo'lmasa ham, ular tarixchi va psixologga tana tuzilishining alomatlari sifatida (aytganimizdek) shunchalik qimmatliroq ishoralar beradi: uning yaxshi yoki yomon holati, to'laligi, qudrati va tarixdagi hukmronligi; yoki aksincha, uning to'siqlari, holsizliklari va qashshoqlashuvi, oxirni oldindan sezishi, oxirga bo'lgan irodasi haqida.

paras.en: I still expect that a philosophical physician, in the exceptional sense of the word—one who applies himself to the problem of the collective health of peoples, periods, races, and mankind generally—will some day have the courage to follow out my suspicion to its ultimate conclusions, and to venture on the judgment that in all philosophising it has not hitherto been a question of "truth" at all, but of something else,—namely, of health, futurity, growth, power, life....
paras.uz: Men hali ham kutamanki, so'zning alohida ma'nosidagi faylasuf-shifokor — xalqlar, davrlar, irqlar va umuman insoniyatning umumiy sog'lig'i muammosi bilan shug'ullanadigan kishi — bir kun kelib mening gumonimni oxirgi xulosalarigacha olib borishga jur'at etadi va har qanday falsafa qilishda shu paytgacha gap umuman «haqiqat» haqida emas, balki boshqa narsa — ya'ni sog'liq, kelajak, o'sish, kuch, hayot haqida bo'lgan, degan hukmni chiqarishga botinadi...

paras.en: 3. It will be surmised that I should not like to take leave ungratefully of that period of severe sickness, the advantage of which is not even yet exhausted in me: for I am sufficiently conscious of what I have in advance of the spiritually robust generally, in my changeful state of health. A philosopher who has made the tour of many states of health, and always makes it anew, has also gone through just as many philosophies: he really cannot do otherwise than transform his condition on every occasion into the most ingenious posture and position,—this art of transfiguration is just philosophy. We philosophers are not at liberty to separate soul and body, as the people separate them; and we are still less at liberty to separate soul and spirit.
paras.uz: 3. Taxmin qilish mumkinki, men og'ir kasallikning o'sha davri bilan noshukurlik bilan xayrlashishni istamayman, uning foydasi menda hali ham tugamagan: chunki o'zgaruvchan sog'lig'im tufayli umuman ruhan baquvvatlardan nimalarda oldinda ekanimni yaxshi bilaman. Ko'p sog'liq holatlarini aylanib chiqqan va doim qaytadan aylanib chiqadigan faylasuf xuddi shuncha falsafani ham boshdan kechirgan: u har safar o'z holatini eng mohir qiyofa va vaziyatga aylantirmasdan boshqacha qila olmaydi, — bu qiyofa o'zgartirish san'ati aynan falsafadir. Biz faylasuflar xalq ajratgani kabi ruh va tanani ajratishga haqqimiz yo'q; ruh va aqlni ajratishga esa yana ham kamroq haqqimiz bor.

paras.en: We are not thinking frogs, we are not objectifying and registering apparatuses with cold entrails,—our thoughts must be continually born to us out of our pain, and we must, motherlike, share with them all that we have in us of blood, heart, ardour, joy, passion, pang, conscience, fate and fatality. Life—that means for us to transform constantly into light and flame all that we are, and also all that we meet with; we cannot possibly do otherwise. And as regards sickness, should we not be almost tempted to ask whether we could in general dispense with it? It is great pain only which is the ultimate emancipator of the spirit; for it is the teacher of the strong suspicion which makes an X out of every U, a true, correct X, i.e., the ante-penultimate letter....
paras.uz: Biz fikrlaydigan qurbaqalar emasmiz, ichi sovuq obyektivlashtiruvchi va qayd etuvchi apparatlar emasmiz, — fikrlarimiz doimo og'rig'imizdan tug'ilishi kerak va biz, onalardek, ular bilan bizdagi bor narsaning hammasini: qonni, yurakni, otashni, quvonchni, ehtirosni, azobni, vijdonni, qismat va taqdirni baham ko'rishimiz kerak. Hayot — bu biz uchun o'zimizdagi hamma narsani, shuningdek, duch kelgan hamma narsani doimo nur va alangaga aylantirish demakdir; biz boshqacha qila olmaymiz. Kasallikka kelsak, undan umuman voz kecha olarmidik, deb so'rashga deyarli moyil bo'lmasmidik? Faqat buyuk og'riq ruhning so'nggi ozod qiluvchisidir; chunki u har bir U dan X yasaydigan kuchli gumonning o'qituvchisi — haqiqiy, to'g'ri X, ya'ni oxiridan uchinchi harf...

paras.en: It is great pain only, the long slow pain which takes time, by which we are burned as it were with green wood, that compels us philosophers to descend into our ultimate depths, and divest ourselves of all trust, all good-nature, veiling, gentleness, and averageness, wherein we have perhaps formerly installed our humanity. I doubt whether such pain "improves" us; but I know that it deepens us.
paras.uz: Faqat buyuk og'riq, vaqt talab qiladigan uzoq, sekin og'riq — u bizni go'yo ho'l o'tinda yoqadi — biz faylasuflarni eng chuqur qa'rimizga tushishga va ilgari insoniyligimizni joylashtirgan bo'lishimiz mumkin bo'lgan barcha ishonch, barcha xushfe'llik, pardalash, muloyimlik va o'rtamiyonalikdan voz kechishga majbur qiladi. Bunday og'riq bizni «yaxshilaydi»mi, shubhaliman; lekin bilamanki, u bizni chuqurlashtiradi.

paras.en: Be it that we learn to confront it with our pride, our scorn, our strength of will, doing like the Indian who, however sorely tortured, revenges himself on his tormentor with his bitter tongue; be it that we withdraw from the pain into the oriental nothingness—it is called Nirvana,—into mute, benumbed, deaf self-surrender, self-forgetfulness, and self-effacement: one emerges from such long, dangerous exercises in self-mastery as another being, with several additional notes of interrogation, and above all, with the will to question more than ever, more profoundly, more strictly, more sternly, more wickedly, more quietly than has ever been questioned hitherto. Confidence in life is gone: life itself has become a problem.—Let it not be imagined that one has necessarily become a hypochondriac thereby! Even love of life is still possible—only one loves differently. It is the love of a woman of whom one is doubtful....
paras.uz: Mayli, biz unga g'ururimiz, nafratimiz, iroda kuchimiz bilan qarshi turishni o'rganaylik — qanchalik qattiq qiynalmasin, o'z qiynoqchisidan achchiq tili bilan o'ch oladigan hindu kabi; mayli, og'riqdan sharqona hech narsalikka — buni Nirvana deyishadi — soqov, karaxt, kar o'zini topshirishga, o'zini unutishga va o'zini yo'qotishga chekinaylik: o'zini boshqarishdagi bunday uzoq, xavfli mashqlardan odam boshqa mavjudot bo'lib chiqadi, bir nechta qo'shimcha so'roq belgilari bilan va eng muhimi, shu paytgacha so'ralganidan ko'ra ko'proq, chuqurroq, qat'iyroq, qattiqroq, yovuzroq, sokinroq so'rash irodasi bilan. Hayotga ishonch yo'qoldi: hayotning o'zi muammoga aylandi. — Bundan odam albatta ipoxondrikka aylanib qoladi deb o'ylamang! Hayotni sevish ham hali mumkin — faqat boshqacha sevasan. Bu — o'zidan shubhalanadigan ayolga bo'lgan sevgi...

paras.en: The charm, however, of all that is problematic, the delight in the X, is too great in those more spiritual and more spiritualised men, not to spread itself again and again like a clear glow over all the trouble of the problematic, over all the danger of uncertainty, and even over the jealousy of the lover. We know a new happiness....
paras.uz: Biroq, muammoli bo'lgan hamma narsaning jozibasi, X dan zavqlanish o'sha ruhiyroq va ruhiylashgan odamlarda shunchalik kattaki, u qayta-qayta tiniq nurdek muammolilikning barcha tashvishlari, noaniqlikning barcha xavfi va hatto oshiqning rashki ustiga ham yoyiladi. Biz yangi baxtni bilamiz...

paras.en: 4. Finally, (that the most essential may not remain unsaid), one comes back out of such abysses, out of such severe sickness, and out of the sickness of strong suspicion—new-born, with the skin cast; more sensitive, more wicked, with a finer taste for joy, with a more delicate tongue for all good things, with a merrier disposition, with a second and more dangerous innocence in joy; more childish at the same time, and a hundred times more refined than ever before. Oh, how repugnant to us now is pleasure, coarse, dull, drab pleasure, as the pleasure-seekers, our "cultured" classes, our rich and ruling classes, usually understand it! How malignantly we now listen to the great holiday-hubbub with which "cultured people" and city-men at present allow themselves to be forced to "spiritual enjoyment" by art, books, and music, with the help of spirituous liquors!
paras.uz: 4. Nihoyat (eng muhimi aytilmay qolmasligi uchun), odam bunday tubsizliklardan, bunday og'ir kasallikdan va kuchli gumon kasalligidan qaytib chiqadi — qayta tug'ilgan, po'stini tashlagan; sezgirroq, yovuzroq, quvonchga nisbatan nozikroq didli, barcha yaxshi narsalarga nisbatan nozikroq tilli, quvnoqroq fe'lli, quvonchda ikkinchi va xavfliroq beg'uborlik bilan; bir vaqtning o'zida ko'proq bolalarcha va har qachongidan yuz baravar nozikroq. Oh, endi biz uchun lazzat qanchalik jirkanch — qo'pol, zerikarli, xira lazzat, uni lazzat izlovchilar, bizning «madaniyatli» tabaqalarimiz, boy va hukmron tabaqalarimiz odatda qanday tushunsa! «Madaniyatli odamlar» va shahar ahli hozir o'zlarini spirtli ichimliklar yordamida san'at, kitoblar va musiqa orqali «ruhiy zavq»ga majburlashlariga yo'l qo'yadigan buyuk bayram g'ala-g'ovuriga endi qanday yovuz quloq solamiz!

paras.en: How the theatrical cry of passion now pains our ear, how strange to our taste has all the romantic riot and sensuous bustle which the cultured populace love become (together with their aspirations after the exalted, the elevated, and the intricate)! No, if we convalescents need an art at all, it is another art—a mocking, light, volatile, divinely serene, divinely ingenious art, which blazes up like a clear flame, into a cloudless heaven! Above all, an art for artists, only for artists! We at last know better what is first of all necessary for it—namely, cheerfulness, every kind of cheerfulness, my friends! also as artists:—I should like to prove it. We now know something too well, we men of knowledge: oh, how well we are now learning to forget and not know, as artists!
paras.uz: Ehtirosning teatrona qichqirig'i endi qulog'imizni qanchalik og'ritadi, madaniyatli olomon sevadigan barcha romantik g'alayon va hissiy tashvish (yuksaklikka, ulug'likka va chigallikka intilishlari bilan birga) didimizga qanchalik begona bo'lib qoldi! Yo'q, agar biz sog'ayayotganlarga umuman san'at kerak bo'lsa, bu boshqa san'at — masxaraomuz, yengil, uchqur, ilohiy darajada sokin, ilohiy darajada mohir san'at, u bulutsiz osmonga tiniq alangadek otilib chiqadi! Eng avvalo, san'atkorlar uchun san'at, faqat san'atkorlar uchun! Biz nihoyat unga eng avvalo nima kerakligini yaxshiroq bilamiz — ya'ni quvnoqlik, har qanday quvnoqlik, do'stlarim! san'atkor sifatida ham: — buni isbotlamoqchi edim. Biz endi nimanidir haddan tashqari yaxshi bilamiz, biz bilim egalari: oh, endi biz san'atkor sifatida unutishni va bilmaslikni qanchalik yaxshi o'rganyapmiz!

paras.en: And as to our future, we are not likely to be found again in the tracks of those Egyptian youths who at night make the temples unsafe, embrace statues, and would fain unveil, uncover, and put in clear light, everything which for good reasons is kept concealed. No, we have got disgusted with this bad taste, this will to truth, to "truth at all costs," this youthful madness in the love of truth: we are now too experienced, too serious, too joyful, too singed, too profound for that.... We no longer believe that truth remains truth when the veil is withdrawn from it: we have lived long enough to believe this. At present we regard it as a matter of propriety not to be anxious either to see everything naked, or to be present at everything, or to understand and "know" everything.
paras.uz: Kelajagimizga kelsak, bizni yana tunda ibodatxonalarni xavfli qiladigan, haykallarni quchoqlaydigan va yaxshi sabablarga ko'ra yashirin saqlanadigan hamma narsani ochishni, yalang'ochlashni va yorqin nurga qo'yishni xohlaydigan o'sha misrlik yigitlarning izidan topish qiyin. Yo'q, bu yomon did bizni bezdirdi, haqiqatga bo'lgan bu iroda, «har qanday narxda haqiqat»ga, haqiqatni sevishdagi bu yoshlik telbaligiga: biz endi buning uchun haddan tashqari tajribali, haddan tashqari jiddiy, haddan tashqari quvnoq, haddan tashqari kuygan, haddan tashqari chuqurmiz... Biz endi pardasi olib tashlanganda haqiqat haqiqatligicha qolishiga ishonmaymiz: bunga ishonish uchun yetarlicha uzoq yashadik. Hozir biz hamma narsani yalang'och ko'rishga, hamma narsada hozir bo'lishga yoki hamma narsani tushunishga va «bilishga» intilmaslikni odob masalasi deb hisoblaymiz.

paras.en: "Is it true that the good God is everywhere present?" asked a little girl of her mother: "I think that is indecent":—a hint to philosophers! One should have more reverence for the shamefacedness with which nature has concealed herself behind enigmas and motley uncertainties. Perhaps truth is a woman who has reasons for not showing her reasons? Perhaps her name is Baubo, to speak in Greek?... Oh, those Greeks! They knew how to live: for that purpose it is necessary to keep bravely to the surface, the fold and the skin; to worship appearance, to believe in forms, tones, and words, in the whole Olympus of appearance! Those Greeks were superficial—from profundity!
paras.uz: «Yaxshi Xudo hamma joyda hozir ekani rostmi?» — deb so'radi bir qizcha onasidan. — «Menimcha, bu odobsizlik»: — faylasuflarga ishora! Tabiat o'zini jumboqlar va rang-barang noaniqliklar ortiga yashirgan uyatchanlikka ko'proq hurmat bilan qarash kerak. Balki haqiqat o'z sabablarini ko'rsatmaslik uchun sabablari bor ayoldir? Balki uning ismi, yunoncha aytganda, Baubodir?.. Oh, o'sha yunonlar! Ular yashashni bilishgan: buning uchun jasorat bilan yuzada, burmada va terida qolish, tashqi ko'rinishga sig'inish, shakllarga, ohanglarga va so'zlarga, tashqi ko'rinishning butun Olimpiga ishonish kerak! O'sha yunonlar yuzaki edi — chuqurlikdan!

paras.en: And are we not coming back precisely to this point, we dare-devils of the spirit, who have scaled the highest and most dangerous peak of contemporary thought, and have looked around us from it, have looked down from it? Are we not precisely in this respect—Greeks? Worshippers of forms, of tones, and of words? And precisely on that account—artists?
paras.uz: Va biz aynan shu nuqtaga qaytmayapmizmi, biz, ruhning bebosh jasurlari, zamonaviy fikrning eng baland va eng xavfli cho'qqisiga chiqib, undan atrofga qaragan, pastga qaraganlar? Aynan shu jihatdan biz — yunonlar emasmizmi? Shakllarga, ohanglarga va so'zlarga sig'inuvchilar? Va aynan shuning uchun — san'atkorlar emasmizmi?

chapters.title: The teachers of the purpose of existence

paras.en: 1. The Teachers of the Object of Existence. — Whether I look with a good or an evil eye upon men, I find them always at one problem, each and all of them: to do that which conduces to the conservation of the human species. And certainly not out of any sentiment of love for this species, but simply because nothing in them is older, stronger, more inexorable, and more unconquerable than that instinct,—because it is precisely the essence of our race and herd. Although we are accustomed readily enough, with our usual short-sightedness, to separate our neighbours precisely into useful and hurtful, into good and evil men, yet when we make a general calculation, and on longer reflection on the whole question, we become distrustful of this defining and separating, and finally leave it alone.
paras.uz: 1. Hayot maqsadi o'qituvchilari. — Odamlarga yaxshi ko'z bilan qaraymanmi yoki yomon ko'z bilan, ularning hammasini, har birini doimo bitta vazifa ustida topaman: inson turining saqlanishiga xizmat qiladigan narsani qilish. Albatta, bu turga bo'lgan biror muhabbat tuyg'usidan emas, balki shunchaki ularda bu instinktdan qadimiyroq, kuchliroq, shafqatsizroq va yengilmasroq hech narsa yo'qligi uchun, — chunki u aynan bizning zotimiz va podamizning mohiyatidir. Biz odatdagi kalta ko'rligimiz bilan qo'shnilarimizni foydali va zararli, yaxshi va yomon odamlarga ajratishga osongina o'rganib qolgan bo'lsak ham, umumiy hisob-kitob qilganimizda va butun masala ustida uzoqroq o'ylaganimizda, bu ta'riflash va ajratishga ishonchsizlik bilan qaray boshlaymiz va oxiri uni qo'yib qo'yamiz.

paras.en: Even the most hurtful man is still perhaps, in respect to the conservation of the race, the most useful of all; for he conserves in himself or by his effect on others, impulses without which mankind might long ago have languished or decayed. Hatred, delight in mischief, rapacity and ambition, and whatever else is called evil—belong to the marvellous economy of the conservation of the race; to be sure a costly, lavish, and on the whole very foolish economy:—which has, however, hitherto preserved our race, as is demonstrated to us. I no longer know, my dear fellow-man and neighbour, if thou canst at all live to the disadvantage of the race, and therefore, "unreasonably" and "badly"; that which could have injured the race has perhaps died out many millenniums ago, and now belongs to the things which are no longer possible even to God.
paras.uz: Hatto eng zararli odam ham zotning saqlanishi nuqtai nazaridan, ehtimol, hammadan foydaliroqdir; chunki u o'zida yoki boshqalarga ta'siri orqali shunday mayllarni saqlaydiki, ularsiz insoniyat allaqachon so'lib yoki chirib ketgan bo'lardi. Nafrat, yomonlikdan zavqlanish, ochko'zlik va shuhratparastlik va yomon deb ataladigan boshqa hamma narsa — zotni saqlashning ajoyib iqtisodiga tegishli; albatta, qimmat, isrofgar va umuman olganda juda ahmoqona iqtisod: — biroq u shu paytgacha zotimizni saqlab kelgan, buni bizga ko'rsatib turibdi. Aziz birodarim va qo'shnim, men endi bilmayman: sen umuman zotga zarar keltirib, ya'ni «aqlsiz» va «yomon» yashay olasanmi; zotga zarar yetkaza oladigan narsa, ehtimol, ko'p ming yillar oldin qirilib ketgan va endi hatto Xudo uchun ham imkonsiz narsalar qatoriga kiradi.

paras.en: Indulge thy best or thy worst desires, and above all, go to wreck!—in either case thou art still probably the furtherer and benefactor of mankind in some way or other, and in that respect thou mayest have thy panegyrists—and similarly thy mockers! But thou wilt never find him who would be quite qualified to mock at thee, the individual, at thy best, who could bring home to thy conscience its limitless, buzzing and croaking wretchedness so as to be in accord with truth! To laugh at oneself as one would have to laugh in order to laugh out of the veriest truth,—to do this the best have not hitherto had enough of the sense of truth, and the most endowed have had far too little genius! There is perhaps still a future even for laughter!
paras.uz: Eng yaxshi yoki eng yomon istaklaringga erk ber va eng avvalo, halok bo'l! — ikkala holatda ham sen ehtimol qandaydir tarzda insoniyatning ko'makchisi va xayrixohisan va shu jihatdan senda maqtovchilaring bo'lishi mumkin — xuddi shunday masxara qiluvchilaring ham! Lekin sen hech qachon seni, alohida shaxsni, eng yaxshi holingda masxara qilishga to'liq qodir bo'lgan, vijdoningga uning cheksiz, g'uvillagan va qurillagan bechoraligini haqiqatga mos ravishda yetkaza oladigan odamni topa olmaysan! O'zing ustingdan eng sof haqiqatdan kulish uchun kulish kerak bo'lgandek kulish — buning uchun eng yaxshilarda shu paytgacha haqiqat tuyg'usi yetarli bo'lmagan, eng iste'dodlilarda esa daho juda kam bo'lgan! Balki kulgining ham hali kelajagi bordir!

paras.en: When the maxim, "The race is all, the individual is nothing,"—has incorporated itself in humanity, and when access stands open to every one at all times to this ultimate emancipation and irresponsibility.—Perhaps then laughter will have united with wisdom, perhaps then there will be only "joyful wisdom." Meanwhile, however, it is quite otherwise, meanwhile the comedy of existence has not yet "become conscious" of itself, meanwhile it is still the period of tragedy, the period of morals and religions. What does the ever new appearing of founders of morals and religions, of instigators of struggles for moral valuations, of teachers of remorse of conscience and religious war, imply? What do these heroes on this stage imply?
paras.uz: «Zot — hamma narsa, shaxs — hech narsa» degan qoida insoniyatga singib ketganda va bu so'nggi ozodlik va mas'uliyatsizlikka har kimga har doim yo'l ochiq bo'lganda. — Balki o'shanda kulgi donolik bilan birlashgan bo'ladi, balki o'shanda faqat «quvnoq ilm» qoladi. Hozircha esa butunlay boshqacha, hozircha hayot komediyasi o'zini hali «anglamagan», hozircha hali tragediya davri, axloq va dinlar davri. Axloq va dinlar asoschilarining, axloqiy baholar uchun kurash qo'zg'atuvchilarining, vijdon azobi va diniy urush o'qituvchilarining doimo qayta paydo bo'lishi nimani anglatadi? Bu sahnadagi bu qahramonlar nimani anglatadi?

paras.en: For they have hitherto been the heroes of it, and all else, though solely visible for the time being, and too close to one, has served only as preparation for these heroes, whether as machinery and coulisse, or in the rôle of confidants and valets. (The poets, for example, have always been the valets of some morality or other.)—It is obvious of itself that these tragedians also work in the interest of the race, though they may believe that they work in the interest of God, and as emissaries of God. They also further the life of the species, in that they further the belief in life.
paras.uz: Chunki ular shu paytgacha uning qahramonlari bo'lgan va qolgan hamma narsa, garchi vaqtincha yagona ko'rinadigan va juda yaqin bo'lsa ham, faqat bu qahramonlarga tayyorgarlik sifatida xizmat qilgan — mexanizm va kulisa sifatidami yoki sirdosh va xizmatkorlar rolidami. (Masalan, shoirlar doim qandaydir axloqning xizmatkorlari bo'lgan.) — O'z-o'zidan ravshanki, bu tragiklar ham zot manfaati uchun ishlaydi, garchi ular Xudo manfaati uchun va Xudoning elchilari sifatida ishlaymiz deb ishonishsa ham. Ular ham hayotga ishonchni oshirib, turning hayotini oshiradi.

paras.en: "It is worth while to live"—each of them calls out,—"there is something of importance in this life; life has something behind it and under it; take care!" That impulse, which rules equally in the noblest and the ignoblest, the impulse towards the conservation of the species, breaks forth from time to time as reason and passion of spirit; it has then a brilliant train of motives about it, and tries with all its power to make us forget that fundamentally it is just impulse, instinct, folly and baselessness. Life should be loved, for ...! Man should benefit himself and his neighbour, for ...! And whatever all these shoulds and fors imply, and may imply in future!
paras.uz: «Yashashga arziydi», — deb qichqiradi ularning har biri, — «bu hayotda muhim nimadir bor; hayotning ortida va ostida nimadir bor; ehtiyot bo'linglar!» Eng olijanob va eng pastkashda ham bir xil hukmronlik qiladigan o'sha mayl, turni saqlash mayli vaqti-vaqti bilan aql va ruh ehtirosi sifatida otilib chiqadi; o'shanda uning atrofida motivlarning yorqin karvoni bo'ladi va u aslida shunchaki mayl, instinkt, ahmoqlik va asossizlik ekanini bizga unuttirishga butun kuchi bilan urinadi. Hayotni sevish kerak, chunki...! Inson o'ziga va qo'shnisiga foyda keltirishi kerak, chunki...! Va bu «kerak»lar va «chunki»larning hammasi nimani anglatsa va kelajakda nimani anglatishi mumkin bo'lsa!

paras.en: In order that that which necessarily and always happens of itself and without design, may henceforth appear to be done by design, and may appeal to men as reason and ultimate command,—for that purpose the ethiculturist comes forward as the teacher of design in existence; for that purpose he devises a second and different existence, and by means of this new mechanism he lifts the old common existence off its old common hinges. No! he does not at all want us to laugh at existence, nor even at ourselves—nor at himself; to him an individual is always an individual, something first and last and immense, to him there are no species, no sums, no noughts.
paras.uz: Muqarrar ravishda va doimo o'z-o'zidan va maqsadsiz sodir bo'ladigan narsa bundan buyon maqsad bilan qilinayotgandek ko'rinishi va odamlarga aql va oliy buyruq sifatida murojaat qilishi uchun, — shu maqsadda axloq o'qituvchisi hayotda maqsad borligini o'rgatuvchi sifatida maydonga chiqadi; shu maqsadda u ikkinchi, boshqacha hayotni o'ylab topadi va bu yangi mexanizm yordamida eski oddiy hayotni eski oddiy ilgaklaridan ko'tarib oladi. Yo'q! U bizning hayot ustidan, hatto o'zimiz ustidan — yoki o'zi ustidan kulishimizni aslo istamaydi; uning uchun shaxs doimo shaxs, birinchi va oxirgi va ulkan narsa, uning uchun turlar, yig'indilar, nollar yo'q.

paras.en: However foolish and fanatical his inventions and valuations may be, however much he may misunderstand the course of nature and deny its conditions—and all systems of ethics hitherto have been foolish and anti-natural to such a degree that mankind would have been ruined by any one of them had it got the upper hand,—at any rate, every time that "the hero" came upon the stage something new was attained: the frightful counterpart of laughter, the profound convulsion of many individuals at the thought, "Yes, it is worth while to live! yes, I am worthy to live!"—life, and thou, and I, and all of us together became for a while interesting to ourselves once more.—It is not to be denied that hitherto laughter and reason and nature have in the long run got the upper hand of all the great teachers of design: in the end the short tragedy always passed over once more into the eternal comedy of existence; and the "waves of innumerable laughters"—to use the expression of Æschylus—must also in the end beat over the greatest of these tragedies.
paras.uz: Uning ixtirolari va baholari qanchalik ahmoqona va mutaassib bo'lmasin, u tabiat yo'lini qanchalik noto'g'ri tushunmasin va uning shartlarini inkor etmasin — va shu paytgacha barcha axloq tizimlari shunchalik ahmoqona va tabiatga zid bo'lganki, ulardan birortasi ustunlikka erishganida insoniyat halok bo'lardi, — har holda, «qahramon» sahnaga chiqqan har safar yangi nimagadir erishilgan: kulgining dahshatli aksi, ko'plab shaxslarning «Ha, yashashga arziydi! ha, men yashashga loyiqman!» degan fikrdan chuqur larzaga kelishi — hayot ham, sen ham, men ham, hammamiz birgalikda bir muddat yana o'zimiz uchun qiziqarli bo'lib qoldik. — Inkor etib bo'lmaydiki, shu paytgacha kulgi, aql va tabiat uzoq muddatda maqsadning barcha buyuk o'qituvchilari ustidan g'alaba qozongan: oxirida qisqa tragediya har doim yana hayotning abadiy komediyasiga o'tgan; va Esxil iborasi bilan aytganda, «son-sanoqsiz kulgilar to'lqinlari» oxir-oqibat bu tragediyalarning eng buyuklari ustidan ham urilib o'tishi kerak.

paras.en: But with all this corrective laughter, human nature has on the whole been changed by the ever new appearance of those teachers of the design of existence,—human nature has now an additional requirement, the very requirement of the ever new appearance of such teachers and doctrines of "design." Man has gradually become a visionary animal, who has to fulfil one more condition of existence than the other animals: man must from time to time believe that he knows why he exists; his species cannot flourish without periodically confiding in life! Without the belief in reason in life!
paras.uz: Lekin bu tuzatuvchi kulgiga qaramay, inson tabiati hayot maqsadi o'qituvchilarining doimo qayta paydo bo'lishi bilan umuman o'zgargan, — inson tabiatida endi qo'shimcha ehtiyoj bor, aynan shunday o'qituvchilar va «maqsad» ta'limotlarining doimo yangidan paydo bo'lishiga ehtiyoj. Inson asta-sekin xayolparast hayvonga aylangan, u boshqa hayvonlardan ko'ra yana bitta yashash shartini bajarishi kerak: inson vaqti-vaqti bilan nima uchun yashashini biladi deb ishonishi kerak; uning turi hayotga davriy ishonmasdan gullab-yashnay olmaydi! Hayotdagi aqlga ishonmasdan!

paras.en: And always from time to time will the human race decree anew that "there is something which really may not be laughed at." And the most clairvoyant philanthropist will add that "not only laughing and joyful wisdom, but also the tragic, with all its sublime irrationality, counts among the means and necessities for the conservation of the race!"—And consequently! Consequently! Consequently! Do you understand me, oh my brothers? Do you understand this new law of ebb and flow? We also shall have our time!
paras.uz: Va insoniyat doimo vaqti-vaqti bilan qaytadan «haqiqatan ham ustidan kulib bo'lmaydigan nimadir bor» deb hukm chiqaradi. Eng ko'regon insonparvar esa qo'shadi: «nafaqat kulgi va quvnoq ilm, balki o'zining barcha yuksak aqlsizligi bilan tragik ham zotni saqlashning vositalari va zaruratlari qatoriga kiradi!» — Va demak! Demak! Demak! Meni tushunyapsizmi, ey birodarlarim? Bu yangi qayt va to'lqin qonunini tushunyapsizmi? Bizning ham vaqtimiz keladi!

paras.en: 2. The Intellectual Conscience. — I have always the same experience over again, and always make a new effort against it; for although it is evident to me I do not want to believe it: in the greater number of men the intellectual conscience is lacking; indeed, it would often seem to me that in demanding such a thing, one is as solitary in the largest cities as in the desert. Everyone looks at you with strange eyes, and continues to make use of his scales, calling this good and that bad; and no one blushes for shame when you remark that these weights are not the full amount,—there is also no indignation against you; perhaps they laugh at your doubt.
paras.uz: 2. Aqliy vijdon. — Men doimo bir xil tajribani qayta boshdan kechiraman va doimo unga qarshi yangi harakat qilaman; chunki bu menga ayon bo'lsa ham, ishongim kelmaydi: odamlarning ko'pchiligida aqliy vijdon yo'q; haqiqatan ham, menga ko'pincha shunday tuyuladiki, bunday narsani talab qilsang, eng katta shaharlarda ham cho'ldagidek yolg'izsan. Hamma senga g'alati ko'zlar bilan qaraydi va tarozisidan foydalanishda davom etib, buni yaxshi, uni yomon deydi; va bu toshlar to'liq vaznda emasligini aytsang, hech kim uyatdan qizarmaydi, — senga qarshi g'azab ham yo'q; balki ular shubhangga kulishar.

paras.en: I mean to say that the greater number of people do not find it contemptible to believe this or that, and live according to it, without having been previously aware of the ultimate and surest reasons for and against it, and without even giving themselves any trouble about such reasons afterwards,—the most gifted men and the noblest women still belong to this "greater number." But what is kind-heartedness, refinement and genius to me, if the man with these virtues harbours indolent sentiments in belief and judgment, if the longing for certainty does not rule in him, as his innermost desire and profoundest need—as that which separates higher from lower men! In certain pious people I have found a hatred of reason, and have been favourably disposed to them for it: their bad, intellectual conscience still betrayed itself, at least in this manner!
paras.uz: Aytmoqchimanki, ko'pchilik odamlar uning tarafdori va qarshisidagi eng so'nggi va eng ishonchli dalillardan oldindan xabardor bo'lmay va hatto keyin ham bunday dalillar haqida qayg'urmay, u yoki bu narsaga ishonishni va shunga ko'ra yashashni jirkanch deb bilishmaydi, — eng iste'dodli erkaklar va eng olijanob ayollar ham hali shu «ko'pchilik»ka kiradi. Lekin bu fazilatlarga ega odam e'tiqod va hukmda dangasa tuyg'ularni saqlasa, agar unda ishonchlilikka intilish uning eng ichki istagi va eng chuqur ehtiyoji sifatida — oliy odamlarni pastlardan ajratib turadigan narsa sifatida hukmronlik qilmasa, mehribonlik, nafislik va dahoning menga nima keragi bor! Ba'zi taqvodor odamlarda aqlga nafratni uchratganman va buning uchun ularga xayrixoh bo'lganman: ularning yomon aqliy vijdoni hech bo'lmasa shu tarzda o'zini oshkor qilardi!

paras.en: But to stand in the midst of this rerum concordia discors and all the marvellous uncertainty and ambiguity of existence, and not to question, not to tremble with desire and delight in questioning, not even to hate the questioner—perhaps even to make merry over him to the extent of weariness—that is what I regard as contemptible, and it is this sentiment which I first of all search for in every one:—some folly or other always persuades me anew that every man has this sentiment, as man. This is my special kind of unrighteousness.
paras.uz: Lekin bu rerum concordia discors — narsalarning nomuvofiq uyg'unligi — va hayotning barcha ajoyib noaniqligi va ikki ma'noliligi o'rtasida turib, savol bermaslik, savol berishga bo'lgan istak va zavqdan titramaslik, hatto savol beruvchidan nafratlanmaslik — balki hatto charchagunicha uning ustidan kulish — men mana shuni jirkanch deb bilaman va har kimda birinchi navbatda shu tuyg'uni izlayman: — qandaydir ahmoqlik meni har safar har bir odamda, inson sifatida, bu tuyg'u bor deb qayta ishontiradi. Bu mening o'ziga xos adolatsizligim.

paras.en: 3. Noble and Ignoble. — To ignoble natures all noble, magnanimous sentiments appear inexpedient, and on that account first and foremost, as incredible: they blink with their eyes when they hear of such matters, and seem inclined to say, "there will, no doubt, be some advantage therefrom, one cannot see through all walls;"—they are jealous of the noble person, as if he sought advantage by back-stair methods. When they are all too plainly convinced of the absence of selfish intentions and emoluments, the noble person is regarded by them as a kind of fool: they despise him in his gladness, and laugh at the lustre of his eye. "How can a person rejoice at being at a disadvantage, how can a person with open eyes want to meet with disadvantage!
paras.uz: 3. Olijanob va pastkash. — Pastkash tabiatlarga barcha olijanob, saxiy tuyg'ular noo'rin, shuning uchun eng avvalo aql bovar qilmas bo'lib ko'rinadi: bunday narsalar haqida eshitganda ular ko'z qisib qo'yishadi va «shubhasiz, bundan qandaydir foyda bo'ladi, hamma devorlar orqasini ko'rib bo'lmaydi», deyishga moyil ko'rinadi; — ular olijanob odamga, go'yo u orqa eshikdan foyda izlayotgandek, hasad qilishadi. Xudbin niyatlar va manfaatlar yo'qligiga juda aniq ishonch hosil qilganlarida, olijanob odamni bir xil ahmoq deb hisoblashadi: uning quvonchini mensimay, ko'zlaridagi yaltirashga kulishadi. «Qanday qilib odam zarar ko'rganidan quvonishi mumkin, qanday qilib ko'zi ochiq odam zarar ko'rishni istashi mumkin!

paras.en: It must be a disease of the reason with which the noble affection is associated,"—so they think, and they look depreciatingly thereon; just as they depreciate the joy which the lunatic derives from his fixed idea. The ignoble nature is distinguished by the fact that it keeps its advantage steadily in view, and that this thought of the end and advantage is even stronger than its strongest impulse: not to be tempted to inexpedient activities by its impulses—that is its wisdom and inspiration. In comparison with the ignoble nature the higher nature is more irrational:—for the noble, magnanimous, and self-sacrificing person succumbs in fact to his impulses, and in his best moments his reason lapses altogether.
paras.uz: Bu olijanob mayl bilan bog'liq bo'lgan aql kasalligi bo'lsa kerak», — deb o'ylashadi va unga past nazar bilan qarashadi; xuddi telbaning qotib qolgan g'oyasidan oladigan quvonchini past baholaganlaridek. Pastkash tabiat o'z foydasini doimo ko'z oldida tutishi va bu maqsad va foyda haqidagi fikr hatto uning eng kuchli maylidan ham kuchliroq bo'lishi bilan ajralib turadi: o'z mayllari bilan noo'rin ishlarga berilmaslik — bu uning donoligi va ilhomi. Pastkash tabiat bilan solishtirganda oliy tabiat ko'proq aqlsizdir: — chunki olijanob, saxiy va fidoyi odam haqiqatda o'z mayllariga taslim bo'ladi va eng yaxshi lahzalarida uning aqli butunlay to'xtaydi.

paras.en: An animal, which at the risk of life protects its young, or in the pairing season follows the female where it meets with death, does not think of the risk and the death; its reason pauses likewise, because its delight in its young, or in the female, and the fear of being deprived of this delight, dominate it exclusively; it becomes stupider than at other times, like the noble and magnanimous person.
paras.uz: Hayoti xavf ostida bo'lsa ham bolasini himoya qiladigan yoki juftlashish faslida o'lim kutayotgan joyga urg'ochining ortidan boradigan hayvon xavf va o'lim haqida o'ylamaydi; uning aqli ham xuddi shunday to'xtaydi, chunki bolasidan yoki urg'ochidan oladigan zavqi va bu zavqdan mahrum bo'lish qo'rquvi unda yagona hukmronlik qiladi; u boshqa paytlardagidan ahmoqroq bo'lib qoladi, xuddi olijanob va saxiy odam kabi.

paras.en: He possesses feelings of pleasure and pain of such intensity that the intellect must either be silent before them, or yield itself to their service: his heart then goes into his head, and one henceforth speaks of "passions." (Here and there to be sure, the antithesis to this, and as it were the "reverse of passion," presents itself; for example in Fontenelle, to whom some one once laid the hand on the heart with the words, "What you have there, my dearest friend, is brain also.") It is the unreason, or perverse reason of passion, which the ignoble man despises in the noble individual, especially when it concentrates upon objects whose value appears to him to be altogether fantastic and arbitrary.
paras.uz: Unda shunday kuchli lazzat va og'riq tuyg'ulari borki, aql ular oldida yo jim turishi, yoki ularning xizmatiga berilishi kerak: o'shanda uning yuragi boshiga ko'tariladi va bundan buyon «ehtiroslar» haqida gapiriladi. (Albatta, u yer-bu yerda bunga zid, go'yo «ehtirosning teskarisi» ham uchraydi; masalan, Fontenelda, unga kimdir bir marta qo'lini yuragiga qo'yib: «Sizda bu yerda bor narsa, aziz do'stim, bu ham miya», degan.) Pastkash odam olijanob shaxsda aynan ehtirosning aqlsizligini yoki buzuq aqlini mensimaydi, ayniqsa u qadri unga butunlay xayoliy va o'zboshimcha tuyuladigan narsalarga qaratilganda.

paras.en: He is offended at him who succumbs to the passion of the belly, but he understands the allurement which here plays the tyrant; but he does not understand, for example, how a person out of love of knowledge can stake his health and honour on the game. The taste of the higher nature devotes itself to exceptional matters, to things which usually do not affect people, and seem to have no sweetness; the higher nature has a singular standard of value. Besides, it is mostly of the belief that it has not a singular standard of value in its idiosyncrasies of taste; it rather sets up its values and non-values as the generally valid values and non-values, and thus becomes incomprehensible and impracticable.
paras.uz: U qorin ehtirosiga taslim bo'lganga ranjiydi, lekin bu yerda zolimlik qilayotgan vasvasani tushunadi; ammo u, masalan, qanday qilib odam bilimga muhabbat tufayli sog'lig'i va sha'nini o'yinga tikishi mumkinligini tushunmaydi. Oliy tabiatning didi istisno narsalarga, odatda odamlarga ta'sir qilmaydigan va hech qanday shirinligi yo'qdek ko'rinadigan narsalarga beriladi; oliy tabiatning o'ziga xos qadriyat o'lchovi bor. Bundan tashqari, u ko'pincha o'zining did injiqliklarida o'ziga xos qadriyat o'lchovi yo'q deb ishonadi; aksincha, u o'z qadriyatlari va noqadriyatlarini umumiy amal qiladigan qadriyatlar va noqadriyatlar sifatida o'rnatadi va shu tariqa tushunarsiz va amaliy bo'lmay qoladi.

paras.en: It is very rarely that a higher nature has so much reason over and above as to understand and deal with everyday men as such; for the most part it believes in its passion as if it were the concealed passion of every one, and precisely in this belief it is full of ardour and eloquence. If then such exceptional men do not perceive themselves as exceptions, how can they ever understand the ignoble natures and estimate average men fairly! Thus it is that they also speak of the folly, inexpediency and fantasy of mankind, full of astonishment at the madness of the world, and that it will not recognise the "one thing needful for it."—This is the eternal unrighteousness of noble natures.
paras.uz: Oliy tabiatda oddiy odamlarni o'shandayligicha tushunish va ular bilan muomala qilish uchun yetarlicha ortiqcha aql juda kamdan-kam bo'ladi; ko'pincha u o'z ehtirosiga go'yo bu hammaning yashirin ehtirosidek ishonadi va aynan shu ishonchda u otash va notiqlikka to'la. Agar shunday istisno odamlar o'zlarini istisno deb bilmasalar, qanday qilib ular pastkash tabiatlarni tushuna olishi va o'rtacha odamlarni adolatli baholay olishi mumkin! Shuning uchun ular ham insoniyatning ahmoqligi, noo'rinligi va xayolparastligi haqida gapirishadi, dunyoning telbaligidan va u «o'ziga kerak bo'lgan yagona narsani» tan olmasligidan hayratga to'lib. — Bu olijanob tabiatlarning abadiy adolatsizligi.
