quiz.q: According to Nietzsche, what do all men have in common?
o: They serve the conservation of the species
quiz.why_uz: Hatto eng zararli odam ham turni saqlashga xizmat qilishi mumkin.

quiz.q: What does the ignoble person think of noble feelings?
quiz.why_uz: Pastkash tabiat olijanoblikda yashirin foyda izlaydi.

chapters.recap_uz: Barcha odamlar, yaxshisi ham yomoni ham, turni saqlashga xizmat qiladi. Axloq va din asoschilari «hayotning maqsadi bor» deb o'rgatadi. Olijanob odam pastkashga aqlsiz ko'rinadi, chunki u foydasiz ehtirosga beriladi.

chapters.title: What preserves the species

paras.en: 4. That which Preserves the Species. — The strongest and most evil spirits have hitherto advanced mankind the most: they always rekindled the sleeping passions—all orderly arranged society lulls the passions to sleep; they always reawakened the sense of comparison, of contradiction, of delight in the new, the adventurous, the untried; they compelled men to set opinion against opinion, ideal plan against ideal plan. By means of arms, by upsetting boundary-stones, by violations of piety most of all: but also by new religions and morals! The same kind of "wickedness" is in every teacher and preacher of the new—which makes a conqueror infamous, although it expresses itself more refinedly, and does not immediately set the muscles in motion (and just on that account does not make so infamous!).
paras.uz: 4. Turni saqlaydigan narsa. — Eng kuchli va eng yovuz ruhlar shu paytgacha insoniyatni eng ko'p oldinga siljitgan: ular doimo uxlab yotgan ehtiroslarni qayta yoqqan — har qanday tartibli jamiyat ehtiroslarni uxlatadi; ular doimo solishtirish, qarama-qarshilik, yangilikdan, sarguzashtdan, sinab ko'rilmagan narsadan zavqlanish tuyg'usini qayta uyg'otgan; ular odamlarni fikrni fikrga, ideal rejani ideal rejaga qarshi qo'yishga majbur qilgan. Qurol bilan, chegara toshlarini ag'darish bilan, eng ko'p taqvoni buzish bilan: lekin yangi dinlar va axloqlar bilan ham! Yangilikning har bir o'qituvchisi va va'zgo'yida xuddi shu turdagi «yovuzlik» bor — u bosqinchini sharmanda qiladi, garchi nozikroq ifodalansa va mushaklarni darhol harakatga keltirmasa ham (va aynan shuning uchun unchalik sharmanda qilmasa ham!).

paras.en: The new, however, is under all circumstances the evil, as that which wants to conquer, which tries to upset the old boundary-stones and the old piety; only the old is the good! The good men of every age are those who go to the roots of the old thoughts and bear fruit with them, the agriculturists of the spirit. But every soil becomes finally exhausted, and the ploughshare of evil must always come once more.—There is at present a fundamentally erroneous theory of morals which is much celebrated, especially in England: according to it the judgments "good" and "evil" are the accumulation of the experiences of that which is "expedient" and "inexpedient"; according to this theory, that which is called good is conservative of the species, what is called evil, however, is detrimental to it. But in reality the evil impulses are just in as high a degree expedient, indispensable, and conservative of the species as the good:—only, their function is different.
paras.uz: Biroq yangilik har qanday sharoitda yovuzlikdir, chunki u zabt etmoqchi bo'ladi, eski chegara toshlarini va eski taqvoni ag'darishga urinadi; faqat eskisi — yaxshi! Har davrning yaxshi odamlari eski fikrlarning ildizlariga borib, ular bilan meva beradiganlar, ruhning dehqonlaridir. Lekin har qanday tuproq oxir-oqibat holdan toyadi va yovuzlik omochi doimo yana kelishi kerak. — Hozir, ayniqsa Angliyada, juda mashhur bo'lgan tubdan xato axloq nazariyasi bor: unga ko'ra «yaxshi» va «yomon» hukmlari «foydali» va «foydasiz» narsalar haqidagi tajribalarning to'planishidir; bu nazariyaga ko'ra yaxshi deb atalgan narsa turni saqlaydi, yomon deb atalgan narsa esa unga zarar keltiradi. Lekin haqiqatda yovuz mayllar ham yaxshilari kabi xuddi shunday yuqori darajada foydali, zarur va turni saqlovchidir: — faqat ularning vazifasi boshqacha.

paras.en: 5. Unconditional Duties. — All men who feel that they need the strongest words and intonations, the most eloquent gestures and attitudes, in order to operate at all—revolutionary politicians, socialists, preachers of repentance with or without Christianity, with all of whom there must be no mere half-success,—all these speak of "duties," and indeed, always of duties, which have the character of being unconditional—without such they would have no right to their excessive pathos: they know that right well! They grasp, therefore, at philosophies of morality which preach some kind of categorical imperative, or they assimilate a good lump of religion, as, for example, Mazzini did. Because they want to be trusted unconditionally, it is first of all necessary for them to trust themselves unconditionally, on the basis of some ultimate, undebatable command, sublime in itself, as the ministers and instruments of which, they would fain feel and announce themselves.
paras.uz: 5. Shartsiz burchlar. — Umuman ta'sir qila olish uchun eng kuchli so'zlar va ohanglar, eng notiq imo-ishoralar va holatlar kerakligini his qiladigan barcha odamlar — inqilobchi siyosatchilar, sotsialistlar, nasroniylik bilan yoki usiz tavba va'zgo'ylari, ularning hammasi uchun shunchaki yarim muvaffaqiyat bo'lmasligi kerak, — bularning hammasi «burchlar» haqida gapiradi, va haqiqatan ham, doimo shartsiz xarakterga ega burchlar haqida — bunday burchlarsiz ularning haddan tashqari pafosga haqqi bo'lmasdi: ular buni juda yaxshi bilishadi! Shuning uchun ular qandaydir kategorik imperativni va'z qiladigan axloq falsafalariga yopishadi yoki, masalan, Matsini kabi, dindan yaxshigina bir bo'lakni o'zlashtiradi. Ularga shartsiz ishonishlarini istaganlari uchun, ular avvalo qandaydir oliy, bahsli bo'lmagan, o'z-o'zidan ulug'vor buyruq asosida o'zlariga shartsiz ishonishlari kerak, ular o'zlarini shu buyruqning xizmatchisi va quroli deb his qilishni va e'lon qilishni xohlaydi.

paras.en: Here we have the most natural, and for the most part, very influential opponents of moral enlightenment and scepticism: but they are rare. On the other hand, there is always a very numerous class of those opponents wherever interest teaches subjection, while repute and honour seem to forbid it. He who feels himself dishonoured at the thought of being the instrument of a prince, or of a party and sect, or even of wealthy power (for example, as the descendant of a proud, ancient family), but wishes just to be this instrument, or must be so before himself and before the public—such a person has need of pathetic principles which can at all times be appealed to:—principles of an unconditional ought, to which a person can subject himself without shame, and can show himself subjected. All more refined servility holds fast to the categorical imperative, and is the mortal enemy of those who want to take away the unconditional character of duty: propriety demands this from them, and not only propriety.
paras.uz: Mana bu yerda axloqiy ma'rifat va skeptitsizmning eng tabiiy va ko'pincha juda ta'sirli raqiblari: lekin ular kam. Boshqa tomondan, manfaat bo'ysunishni o'rgatadigan, obro' va sha'n esa buni taqiqlayotgandek ko'rinadigan har joyda bunday raqiblarning juda ko'p sinfi doimo bor. Shahzodaning, yoki partiya va sektaning, yoki hatto boy hokimiyatning quroli bo'lish fikridan o'zini sharmanda his qiladigan (masalan, mag'rur, qadimiy oilaning avlodi sifatida), lekin aynan shu qurol bo'lishni istaydigan yoki o'zi va jamoatchilik oldida shunday bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan kishi — bunday odamga har doim murojaat qilish mumkin bo'lgan pafosli tamoyillar kerak: — shartsiz «kerak» tamoyillari, ularga odam uyalmasdan bo'ysunishi va o'zini bo'ysungan qilib ko'rsatishi mumkin. Har qanday nozikroq qullik kategorik imperativni mahkam ushlaydi va burchning shartsiz xarakterini olib tashlamoqchi bo'lganlarning ashaddiy dushmanidir: odob buni ulardan talab qiladi, va faqat odob emas.

paras.en: 6. Loss of Dignity. — Meditation has lost all its dignity of form; the ceremonial and solemn bearing of the meditative person have been made a mockery, and one would no longer endure a wise man of the old style. We think too hastily and on the way and while walking and in the midst of business of all kinds, even when we think on the most serious matters; we require little preparation, even little quiet:—it is as if each of us carried about an unceasingly revolving machine in his head, which still works, even under the most unfavourable circumstances. Formerly it was perceived in a person that on some occasion he wanted to think—it was perhaps the exception!—that he now wanted to become wiser and collected his mind on a thought: he put on a long face for it, as for a prayer, and arrested his step—nay, stood still for hours on the street when the thought "came"—on one or on two legs. It was thus "worthy of the affair"!
paras.uz: 6. Qadr-qimmatning yo'qolishi. — Mulohaza shaklning barcha qadr-qimmatini yo'qotdi; mulohaza qiluvchi odamning marosimiy va tantanali qiyofasi masxaraga aylandi va eski uslubdagi donishmandga endi chidab bo'lmasdi. Biz haddan tashqari shoshib, yo'l-yo'lakay, yurib ketayotib va har xil ishlar o'rtasida o'ylaymiz, hatto eng jiddiy masalalar haqida o'ylaganimizda ham; bizga oz tayyorgarlik, hatto oz sokinlik kerak: — go'yo har birimiz boshimizda to'xtovsiz aylanadigan mashina olib yurgandek, u eng noqulay sharoitlarda ham ishlayveradi. Ilgari odamda qachondir o'ylamoqchi ekanini — bu balki istisno edi! — endi dono bo'lmoqchi ekanini va fikrini bir fikrga jamlayotganini payqash mumkin edi: u buning uchun xuddi ibodatga kirishgandek jiddiy qiyofaga kirar va qadamini to'xtatardi — hatto fikr «kelganda» ko'chada soatlab bir yoki ikki oyog'ida qotib turardi. Shunday qilib, bu «ishga munosib» edi!

paras.en: 7. Something for the Laborious. — He who at present wants to make moral questions a subject of study has an immense field of labour before him. All kinds of passions must be thought about singly, and followed singly throughout periods, peoples, great and insignificant individuals; all their rationality, all their valuations and elucidations of things, ought to come to light! Hitherto all that has given colour to existence has lacked a history: where would one find a history of love, of avarice, of envy, of conscience, of piety, of cruelty? Even a comparative history of law, as also of punishment, has hitherto been completely lacking. Have the different divisions of the day, the consequences of a regular appointment of the times for labour, feast, and repose, ever been made the object of investigation? Do we know the moral effects of the alimentary substances? Is there a philosophy of nutrition?
paras.uz: 7. Mehnatkashlar uchun bir narsa. — Hozir axloqiy masalalarni o'rganish mavzusiga aylantirmoqchi bo'lgan odamning oldida ulkan mehnat maydoni bor. Barcha turdagi ehtiroslarni alohida-alohida o'ylab chiqish va davrlar, xalqlar, buyuk va arzimas shaxslar bo'ylab alohida kuzatish kerak; ularning butun aqlliligi, narsalarni barcha baholashlari va tushuntirishlari yuzaga chiqishi kerak! Shu paytgacha hayotga rang bergan hamma narsaning tarixi yo'q: sevgi, xasislik, hasad, vijdon, taqvo, shafqatsizlik tarixini qayerdan topasiz? Hatto huquqning, shuningdek, jazoning qiyosiy tarixi ham shu paytgacha butunlay yo'q. Kunning turli bo'linishlari, mehnat, bayram va dam olish vaqtlarini muntazam belgilashning oqibatlari hech qachon tadqiqot obyekti bo'lganmi? Oziq-ovqat moddalarining axloqiy ta'sirini bilamizmi? Ovqatlanish falsafasi bormi?

paras.en: (The ever-recurring outcry for and against vegetarianism proves that as yet there is no such philosophy!) Have the experiences with regard to communal living, for example, in monasteries, been collected? Has the dialectic of marriage and friendship been set forth? The customs of the learned, of trades-people, of artists, and of mechanics—have they already found their thinkers? There is so much to think of thereon! All that up till now has been considered as the "conditions of existence," of human beings, and all reason, passion and superstition in this consideration—have they been investigated to the end?
paras.uz: (Vegetarianlik tarafdori va qarshisidagi doimo takrorlanadigan shovqin hozircha bunday falsafa yo'qligini isbotlaydi!) Masalan, monastirlardagi jamoaviy yashash bo'yicha tajribalar to'planganmi? Nikoh va do'stlik dialektikasi bayon etilganmi? Olimlar, savdogarlar, san'atkorlar va hunarmandlarning odatlari — ular allaqachon o'z mutafakkirlarini topganmi? Bu haqda o'ylash kerak bo'lgan shunchalik ko'p narsa bor! Shu paytgacha insonlarning «yashash shartlari» deb hisoblangan hamma narsa va bu qarashdagi barcha aql, ehtiros va xurofot — ular oxirigacha tekshirilganmi?

paras.en: The observation alone of the different degrees of development which the human impulses have attained, and could yet attain, according to the different moral climates, would furnish too much work for the most laborious; whole generations, and regular co-operating generations of the learned, would be needed in order to exhaust the points of view and the material here furnished. The same is true of the determining of the reasons for the differences of the moral climates ("on what account does this sun of a fundamental moral judgment and standard of highest value shine here—and that sun there?"). And there is again a new labour which points out the erroneousness of all these reasons, and determines the entire essence of the moral judgments hitherto made.
paras.uz: Inson mayllari turli axloqiy iqlimlarga ko'ra erishgan va hali erisha oladigan turli rivojlanish darajalarini kuzatishning o'zi ham eng mehnatkash odam uchun haddan tashqari ko'p ish bo'lardi; bu yerda berilgan nuqtai nazarlar va materialni tugatish uchun butun avlodlar, olimlarning muntazam hamkorlik qiladigan avlodlari kerak bo'lardi. Axloqiy iqlimlar farqlarining sabablarini aniqlash haqida ham xuddi shunday («nima sababdan asosiy axloqiy hukm va oliy qadriyat o'lchovining bu quyoshi bu yerda porlaydi — u quyosh esa u yerda?»). Va yana bu sabablarning hammasi xato ekanini ko'rsatadigan va shu paytgacha chiqarilgan axloqiy hukmlarning butun mohiyatini aniqlaydigan yangi mehnat bor.

paras.en: Supposing all these labours to be accomplished, the most critical of all questions would then come into the foreground: whether science is in a position to furnish goals for human action, after it has proved that it can take them away and annihilate them—and then would be the time for a process of experimenting in which every kind of heroism could satisfy itself, an experimenting for centuries, which would put into the shade all the great labours and sacrifices of previous history. Science has not hitherto built its Cyclopic structures; for that also the time will come.
paras.uz: Bu mehnatlarning hammasi bajarildi deb faraz qilsak, unda barcha savollarning eng hal qiluvchisi oldinga chiqardi: ilm inson harakati uchun maqsadlarni olib tashlay olishi va yo'q qila olishini isbotlaganidan keyin, unga maqsadlar bera oladigan holatdami — va o'shanda har qanday qahramonlik o'zini qondira oladigan tajriba qilish jarayoni uchun vaqt kelardi, asrlar davom etadigan, oldingi tarixning barcha buyuk mehnatlari va qurbonliklarini soyada qoldiradigan tajriba. Ilm shu paytgacha o'zining Siklop binolarini qurmagan; buning ham vaqti keladi.

paras.en: 8. Unconscious Virtues. — All qualities in a man of which he is conscious—and especially when he presumes that they are visible and evident to his environment also—are subject to quite other laws of development than those qualities which are unknown to him, or imperfectly known, which by their subtlety can also conceal themselves from the subtlest observer, and hide as it were behind nothing,—as in the case of the delicate sculptures on the scales of reptiles (it would be an error to suppose them an adornment or a defence—for one sees them only with the microscope; consequently, with an eye artificially strengthened to an extent of vision which similar animals, to which they might perhaps have meant adornment or defence, do not possess!) Our visible moral qualities, and especially our moral qualities believed to be visible, follow their own course,—and our invisible qualities of similar name, which in relation to others neither serve for adornment nor defence, also follow their own course: quite a different course probably, and with lines and refinements, and sculptures, which might perhaps give pleasure to a God with a divine microscope.
paras.uz: 8. Ongsiz fazilatlar. — Insonning o'zi anglaydigan barcha xususiyatlari — ayniqsa ular atrofidagilarga ham ko'rinib turibdi va ayon deb taxmin qilganda — unga noma'lum yoki chala ma'lum bo'lgan, nozikligi tufayli eng nozik kuzatuvchidan ham yashirina oladigan va go'yo hech narsa ortiga bekinadigan xususiyatlardan butunlay boshqa rivojlanish qonunlariga bo'ysunadi, — xuddi sudralib yuruvchilar tangachalaridagi nozik o'ymalar kabi (ularni bezak yoki himoya deb o'ylash xato bo'lardi — chunki ularni faqat mikroskop bilan ko'rish mumkin; demak, sun'iy ravishda kuchaytirilgan ko'z bilan, ular bezak yoki himoya bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan shunga o'xshash hayvonlarda bunday ko'rish qobiliyati yo'q!). Bizning ko'rinadigan axloqiy xususiyatlarimiz, ayniqsa ko'rinadi deb ishonilgan axloqiy xususiyatlarimiz o'z yo'lidan boradi, — va boshqalarga nisbatan na bezak, na himoya uchun xizmat qiladigan, xuddi shunday nomdagi ko'rinmas xususiyatlarimiz ham o'z yo'lidan boradi: ehtimol, butunlay boshqa yo'ldan, ilohiy mikroskopli Xudoga zavq bag'ishlashi mumkin bo'lgan chiziqlar, nafisliklar va o'ymalar bilan.

paras.en: We have, for example, our diligence, our ambition, our acuteness: all the world knows about them,—and besides, we have probably once more our diligence, our ambition, our acuteness; but for these—our reptile scales—the microscope has not yet been invented!—And here the adherents of instinctive morality will say, "Bravo! He at least regards unconscious virtues as possible—that suffices us!"—Oh, ye unexacting creatures!
paras.uz: Masalan, bizda tirishqoqligimiz, shuhratparastligimiz, zukkoligimiz bor: butun dunyo ular haqida biladi, — va bundan tashqari, bizda ehtimol yana bir bor tirishqoqligimiz, shuhratparastligimiz, zukkoligimiz bor; lekin bular — bizning sudraluvchi tangachalarimiz uchun hali mikroskop ixtiro qilinmagan! — Va bu yerda instinktiv axloq tarafdorlari aytishadi: «Barakalla! U hech bo'lmasa ongsiz fazilatlarni mumkin deb biladi — bizga shu yetarli!» — Oh, siz, kamtalab mavjudotlar!

paras.en: 9. Our Eruptions. — Numberless things which humanity acquired in its earlier stages, but so weakly and embryonically that it could not be noticed that they were acquired, are thrust suddenly into light long afterwards, perhaps after the lapse of centuries: they have in the interval become strong and mature. In some ages this or that talent, this or that virtue seems to be entirely lacking, as it is in some men; but let us wait only for the grandchildren and grandchildren's children, if we have time to wait,—they bring the interior of their grandfathers into the sun, that interior of which the grandfathers themselves were unconscious. The son, indeed, is often the betrayer of his father; the latter understands himself better since he has got his son. We have all hidden gardens and plantations in us; and by another simile, we are all growing volcanoes, which will have their hours of eruption:—how near or how distant this is, nobody of course knows, not even the good God.
paras.uz: 9. Bizning otilishlarimiz. — Insoniyat dastlabki bosqichlarida egallagan, lekin shunchalik zaif va kurtak holida egallaganki, ular egallangani sezilmagan son-sanoqsiz narsalar ancha keyin, balki asrlar o'tib, to'satdan yorug'likka otilib chiqadi: ular bu oraliqda kuchli va yetuk bo'lib qolgan. Ba'zi davrlarda u yoki bu iste'dod, u yoki bu fazilat butunlay yo'qdek ko'rinadi, xuddi ba'zi odamlarda bo'lgani kabi; lekin faqat nevaralar va nevaralarning bolalarini kutaylik, agar kutishga vaqtimiz bo'lsa, — ular bobolarining ichini, bobolarning o'zlari bexabar bo'lgan o'sha ichki dunyoni quyosh nuriga olib chiqadi. Haqiqatan ham, o'g'il ko'pincha otasining sotqinidir; ota o'g'li bo'lgandan beri o'zini yaxshiroq tushunadi. Hammamizning ichimizda yashirin bog'lar va ekinzorlar bor; va boshqa o'xshatish bilan aytganda, hammamiz o'sib borayotgan vulqonlarmiz, ularning otilish soatlari keladi: — bu qanchalik yaqin yoki uzoq ekanini, albatta, hech kim bilmaydi, hatto yaxshi Xudo ham.

paras.en: 10. A Species of Atavism. — I like best to think of the rare men of an age as suddenly emerging aftershoots of past cultures, and of their persistent strength: like the atavism of a people and its civilisation:—there is thus still something in them to think of! They now seem strange, rare, and extraordinary: and he who feels these forces in himself has to foster them in face of a different, opposing world; he has to defend them, honour them, and rear them to maturity: and he either becomes a great man thereby, or a deranged and eccentric person, unless he should altogether break down betimes. Formerly these rare qualities were usual, and were consequently regarded as common: they did not distinguish people.
paras.uz: 10. Atavizmning bir turi. — Men davrning kamyob odamlarini o'tmish madaniyatlarining to'satdan paydo bo'lgan kech nihollari va ularning bardoshli kuchi deb o'ylashni eng yaxshi ko'raman: xalq va uning tsivilizatsiyasining atavizmi kabi: — demak, ularda hali o'ylash kerak bo'lgan nimadir bor! Ular endi g'alati, kamyob va g'ayrioddiy ko'rinadi: va bu kuchlarni o'zida his qilgan odam ularni boshqacha, qarama-qarshi dunyo oldida parvarish qilishi kerak; u ularni himoya qilishi, hurmat qilishi va yetuklikkacha o'stirishi kerak: va u bu bilan yo buyuk odamga, yoki aqldan ozgan va g'alati odamga aylanadi, agar vaqtida butunlay sinib ketmasa. Ilgari bu kamyob xususiyatlar odatiy edi va shuning uchun oddiy hisoblanardi: ular odamlarni ajratib ko'rsatmasdi.

paras.en: Perhaps they were demanded and presupposed; it was impossible to become great with them, for indeed there was also no danger of becoming insane and solitary with them.—It is principally in the old-established families and castes of a people that such after-effects of old impulses present themselves, while there is no probability of such atavism where races, habits, and valuations change too rapidly. For the tempo of the evolutional forces in peoples implies just as much as in music; for our case an andante of evolution is absolutely necessary, as the tempo of a passionate and slow spirit:—and the spirit of conserving families is certainly of that sort.
paras.uz: Ehtimol, ular talab qilingan va o'z-o'zidan ko'zda tutilgan; ular bilan buyuk bo'lish imkonsiz edi, chunki ular bilan aqldan ozish va yolg'izlanish xavfi ham yo'q edi. — Eski mayllarning bunday kech ta'sirlari asosan xalqning qadimdan o'rnashgan oilalari va tabaqalarida namoyon bo'ladi, irqlar, odatlar va baholar haddan tashqari tez o'zgaradigan joylarda esa bunday atavizm ehtimoli yo'q. Chunki xalqlardagi rivojlanish kuchlarining tempi musiqadagidek muhim; bizning holatimizda rivojlanishning andantesi mutlaqo zarur, ehtirosli va sekin ruhning tempi sifatida: — saqlovchi oilalarning ruhi esa albatta shunday.

paras.en: 11. Consciousness. — Consciousness is the last and latest development of the organic, and consequently also the most unfinished and least powerful of these developments. Innumerable mistakes originate out of consciousness, which, "in spite of fate," as Homer says, cause an animal or a man to break down earlier than might be necessary. If the conserving bond of the instincts were not very much more powerful, it would not generally serve as a regulator: by perverse judging and dreaming with open eyes, by superficiality and credulity, in short, just by consciousness, mankind would necessarily have broken down: or rather, without the former there would long ago have been nothing more of the latter! Before a function is fully formed and matured, it is a danger to the organism: all the better if it be then thoroughly tyrannised over! Consciousness is thus thoroughly tyrannised over—and not least by the pride in it!
paras.uz: 11. Ong. — Ong — organik dunyoning eng so'nggi va eng kech rivojlanishi, demak, bu rivojlanishlarning eng tugallanmagani va eng kuchsizi ham. Ongdan son-sanoqsiz xatolar kelib chiqadi, ular Gomer aytganidek, «taqdirga qaramay» hayvon yoki odamni zarur bo'lganidan oldinroq halokatga uchratadi. Agar instinktlarning saqlovchi rishtasi undan ancha kuchliroq bo'lmaganida, u umuman tartibga soluvchi bo'lib xizmat qilmasdi: buzuq hukm qilish va ochiq ko'z bilan tush ko'rish, yuzakilik va ishonuvchanlik bilan, qisqasi, aynan ong bilan insoniyat muqarrar ravishda halok bo'lgan bo'lardi: aniqrog'i, birinchisisiz ikkinchisidan allaqachon hech narsa qolmagan bo'lardi! Funksiya to'liq shakllanib, yetilmagunicha, u organizm uchun xavfdir: o'shanda uni yaxshilab zulm ostida tutishsa, shunisi yaxshi! Ong shu tariqa yaxshilab zulm ostida tutiladi — va unga bo'lgan g'urur bilan ham oz emas!

paras.en: It is thought that here is the quintessence of man; that which is enduring, eternal, ultimate, and most original in him! Consciousness is regarded as a fixed, given magnitude! Its growth and intermittences are denied! It is accepted as the "unity of the organism"!—This ludicrous overvaluation and misconception of consciousness, has as its result the great utility, that a too rapid maturing of it has thereby been hindered. Because men believed that they already possessed consciousness, they gave themselves very little trouble to acquire it—and even now it is not otherwise! It is still an entirely new problem just dawning on the human eye and hardly yet plainly recognisable: to embody knowledge in ourselves and make it instinctive,—a problem which is only seen by those who have grasped the fact that hitherto our errors alone have been embodied in us, and that all our consciousness is relative to errors!
paras.uz: Bu yerda insonning mohiyati, undagi doimiy, abadiy, oliy va eng asl narsa bor deb o'ylanadi! Ong qat'iy, berilgan kattalik deb hisoblanadi! Uning o'sishi va uzilishlari inkor etiladi! U «organizmning birligi» deb qabul qilinadi! — Ongni bunday kulgili ortiqcha baholash va noto'g'ri tushunishning natijasi katta foyda: shu tufayli uning haddan tashqari tez yetilishiga to'sqinlik qilingan. Odamlar allaqachon ongga egamiz deb ishonganlari uchun, uni egallash uchun juda oz harakat qilishgan — va hozir ham boshqacha emas! Bu hali butunlay yangi, inson ko'ziga endigina tong otayotgan va hali zo'rg'a aniq taniladigan vazifa: bilimni o'zimizga singdirish va uni instinktiv qilish, — bu vazifani faqat shu paytgacha bizga faqat xatolarimiz singdirilganini va butun ongimiz xatolarga nisbiy ekanini anglaganlar ko'radi!

chapters.recap_uz: Eng yovuz ruhlar insoniyatni oldinga siljitgan, chunki yangilik doim «yomon» deb ko'riladi. Nitsshe shartsiz burchlar, ongsiz fazilatlar, atavizm va ong haqida yozadi: ong — eng yosh va eng nomukammal a'zo.

chapters.title: Pleasure, pain and power

paras.en: 12. The Goal of Science. — What? The ultimate goal of science is to create the most pleasure possible to man, and the least possible pain? But what if pleasure and pain should be so closely connected that he who wants the greatest possible amount of the one must also have the greatest possible amount of the other,—that he who wants to experience the "heavenly high jubilation," must also be ready to be "sorrowful unto death"? And it is so, perhaps! The Stoics at least believed it was so, and they were consistent when they wished to have the least possible pleasure, in order to have the least possible pain from life. (When one uses the expression:
paras.uz: 12. Ilmning maqsadi. — Nima? Ilmning oliy maqsadi insonga iloji boricha ko'p lazzat va iloji boricha kam og'riq yaratishmi? Lekin agar lazzat va og'riq bir-biri bilan shunchalik chambarchas bog'langan bo'lsa-chi, birining iloji boricha ko'p miqdorini istagan odam ikkinchisining ham iloji boricha ko'p miqdoriga ega bo'lishi kerak bo'lsa, — «samoviy yuksak shodlik»ni boshdan kechirmoqchi bo'lgan odam «o'lgudek g'amgin» bo'lishga ham tayyor turishi kerak bo'lsa-chi? Balki shundaydir! Hech bo'lmasa stoiklar shunday deb ishonishgan va hayotdan iloji boricha kam og'riq olish uchun iloji boricha kam lazzat olishni xohlaganlarida izchil bo'lishgan. (Kimdir:

paras.en: "The virtuous man is the happiest," it is as much the sign-board of the school for the masses, as a casuistic subtlety for the subtle.) At present also ye have still the choice: either the least possible pain, in short painlessness—and after all, socialists and politicians of all parties could not honourably promise more to their people,—or the greatest possible amount of pain, as the price of the growth of a fullness of refined delights and enjoyments rarely tasted hitherto! If ye decide for the former, if ye therefore want to depress and minimise man's capacity for pain, well, ye must also depress and minimise his capacity for enjoyment. In fact, one can further the one as well as the other goal by science! Perhaps science is as yet best known by its capacity for depriving man of enjoyment, and making him colder, more statuesque, and more Stoical. But it might also turn out to be the great pain-bringer!—And then, perhaps, its counteracting force would be discovered simultaneously, its immense capacity for making new sidereal worlds of enjoyment beam forth!
paras.uz: «Fazilatli odam eng baxtlidir» iborasini ishlatganda, bu ommaga mo'ljallangan maktabning peshlavhasi ham, nozik odamlar uchun kazuistik nozik gap ham.) Hozir ham sizda tanlov bor: yo iloji boricha kam og'riq, qisqasi, og'riqsizlik — oxir-oqibat, barcha partiyalarning sotsialistlari va siyosatchilari o'z xalqiga halollik bilan bundan ortiq narsa va'da qila olmasdi, — yoki shu paytgacha kamdan-kam tatib ko'rilgan nozik zavq va lazzatlar to'liqligining o'sishi evaziga iloji boricha ko'p og'riq! Agar birinchisini tanlasangiz, ya'ni insonning og'riqqa qobiliyatini pasaytirib, kamaytirmoqchi bo'lsangiz, unda uning zavq olish qobiliyatini ham pasaytirib, kamaytirishingiz kerak. Haqiqatan ham, ilm yordamida birini ham, ikkinchi maqsadni ham oshirish mumkin! Balki ilm hozircha insonni zavqdan mahrum qilish, uni sovuqroq, haykalroq va stoikroq qilish qobiliyati bilan eng yaxshi ma'lumdir. Lekin u buyuk og'riq keltiruvchi bo'lib ham chiqishi mumkin! — Va o'shanda, balki, bir vaqtning o'zida uning qarama-qarshi kuchi, zavqning yangi yulduzli dunyolarini porlatib yuborish uchun ulkan qobiliyati ham kashf etilar!

paras.en: 13. The Theory of the Sense of Power. — We exercise our power over others by doing them good or by doing them ill—that is all we care for! Doing ill to those on whom we have to make our power felt; for pain is a far more sensitive means for that purpose than pleasure:—pain always asks concerning the cause, while pleasure is inclined to keep within itself and not look backward. Doing good and being kind to those who are in any way already dependent on us (that is, who are accustomed to think of us as their raison d'être); we want to increase their power, because we thus increase our own; or we want to show them the advantage there is in being in our power,—they thus become more contented with their position, and more hostile to the enemies of our power and readier to contend with them.
paras.uz: 13. Qudrat tuyg'usi nazariyasi. — Biz boshqalar ustidan qudratimizni ularga yaxshilik yoki yomonlik qilish orqali amalga oshiramiz — bizni faqat shu qiziqtiradi! Qudratimizni his qildirishimiz kerak bo'lganlarga yomonlik qilamiz; chunki og'riq bu maqsad uchun lazzatdan ko'ra ancha sezgir vositadir: — og'riq doimo sababini so'raydi, lazzat esa o'zida qolishga va orqaga qaramaslikka moyil. Bizga qandaydir tarzda allaqachon qaram bo'lganlarga (ya'ni bizni o'zlarining raison d'être'i — yashash sababi deb o'ylashga o'rganib qolganlarga) yaxshilik va mehribonlik qilamiz; biz ularning qudratini oshirmoqchimiz, chunki shu bilan o'zimiznikini oshiramiz; yoki ularga bizning qudratimiz ostida bo'lishning foydasini ko'rsatmoqchimiz, — shunda ular o'z ahvolidan ko'proq mamnun bo'ladi, qudratimiz dushmanlariga ko'proq dushmanlik qiladi va ular bilan kurashishga tayyorroq bo'ladi.

paras.en: If we make sacrifices in doing good or in doing ill, it does not alter the ultimate value of our actions; even if we stake our life in the cause, as martyrs for the sake of our church, it is a sacrifice to our longing for power, or for the purpose of conserving our sense of power. He who under these circumstances feels that he "is in possession of truth," how many possessions does he not let go, in order to preserve this feeling! What does he not throw overboard, in order to keep himself "up,"—that is to say, above the others who lack the "truth"!
paras.uz: Agar yaxshilik yoki yomonlik qilishda qurbonlik qilsak, bu harakatlarimizning oxirgi qiymatini o'zgartirmaydi; hatto cherkovimiz uchun shahid sifatida hayotimizni bu ishga tiksak ham, bu qudratga bo'lgan intilishimizga yoki qudrat tuyg'umizni saqlash maqsadiga keltirilgan qurbonlikdir. Bunday sharoitda o'zini «haqiqatga ega» deb his qilgan odam bu tuyg'uni saqlash uchun qancha mulkidan voz kechmaydi! O'zini «yuqorida» — ya'ni «haqiqat»dan mahrum bo'lgan boshqalardan yuqorida tutish uchun nimani kemadan uloqtirmaydi!

paras.en: Certainly the condition we are in when we do ill is seldom so pleasant, so purely pleasant, as that in which we practise kindness,—it is an indication that we still lack power, or it betrays ill-humour at this defect in us; it brings with it new dangers and uncertainties as to the power we already possess, and clouds our horizon by the prospect of revenge, scorn, punishment and failure. Perhaps only those most susceptible to the sense of power, and eager for it, will prefer to impress the seal of power on the resisting individual,—those to whom the sight of the already subjugated person as the object of benevolence is a burden and a tedium.
paras.uz: Albatta, yomonlik qilganimizdagi holatimiz kamdan-kam hollarda mehribonlik qilganimizdagidek yoqimli, sof yoqimli bo'ladi, — bu bizda hali qudrat yetishmasligining belgisi yoki bizdagi bu kamchilikdan norozilikni oshkor qiladi; u allaqachon ega bo'lgan qudratimizga nisbatan yangi xavf va noaniqliklarni olib keladi va ufqimizni qasos, nafrat, jazo va muvaffaqiyatsizlik istiqboli bilan qoraytiradi. Balki faqat qudrat tuyg'usiga eng sezgir va unga eng tashna bo'lganlargina qarshilik ko'rsatayotgan shaxsga qudrat muhrini bosishni afzal ko'rar, — allaqachon bo'ysundirilgan odamni xayrixohlik obyekti sifatida ko'rish ular uchun yuk va zerikarli bo'lganlar.

paras.en: It is a question how a person is accustomed to season his life; it is a matter of taste whether a person would rather have the slow or the sudden, the safe or the dangerous and daring increase of power,—he seeks this or that seasoning always according to his temperament. An easy booty is something contemptible to proud natures; they have an agreeable sensation only at the sight of men of unbroken spirit who could be enemies to them, and similarly, also, at the sight of all not easily accessible possession; they are often hard toward the sufferer, for he is not worthy of their effort or their pride,—but they show themselves so much the more courteous towards their equals, with whom strife and struggle would in any case be full of honour, if at any time an occasion for it should present itself.
paras.uz: Gap odam o'z hayotiga qanday ziravor qo'shishga o'rganganida; odam qudratning sekin yoki to'satdan, xavfsiz yoki xavfli va dadil o'sishini afzal ko'rishi — did masalasi, — u doimo o'z mijoziga ko'ra u yoki bu ziravorni izlaydi. Oson o'lja mag'rur tabiatlar uchun jirkanch narsa; ular faqat o'zlariga dushman bo'la oladigan, ruhi sinmagan odamlarni ko'rganda, shuningdek, osonlikcha qo'lga kiritib bo'lmaydigan har qanday mulkni ko'rganda yoqimli tuyg'u his qilishadi; ular ko'pincha azob chekuvchiga qattiqqo'l, chunki u ularning harakati yoki g'ururiga loyiq emas, — lekin o'zlariga tenglarga nisbatan shunchalik ko'proq xushmuomala bo'lishadi, ular bilan kurash va olishuv, agar qachondir buning uchun imkoniyat paydo bo'lsa, har holda sharafga to'la bo'lardi.

paras.en: It is under the agreeable feelings of this perspective that the members of the knightly caste have habituated themselves to exquisite courtesy toward one another.—Pity is the most pleasant feeling in those who have not much pride, and have no prospect of great conquests: the easy booty—and that is what every sufferer is—is for them an enchanting thing. Pity is said to be the virtue of the gay lady.
paras.uz: Aynan shu istiqbolning yoqimli tuyg'ulari ostida ritsarlar tabaqasi a'zolari bir-biriga nisbatan nafis xushmuomalalikka odatlangan. — Achinish — g'ururi ko'p bo'lmagan va buyuk zafarlar istiqboli yo'q odamlardagi eng yoqimli tuyg'u: oson o'lja — har bir azob chekuvchi esa shunday — ular uchun maftunkor narsa. Aytishlaricha, achinish — yengiltak xonimning fazilati ekan.

paras.en: 14. What is called Love. — The lust of property and love: what different associations each of these ideas evoke!—and yet it might be the same impulse twice named: on the one occasion disparaged from the standpoint of those already possessing (in whom the impulse has attained something of repose, and who are now apprehensive for the safety of their "possession"); on the other occasion viewed from the standpoint of the unsatisfied and thirsty, and therefore glorified as "good." Our love of our neighbour,—is it not a striving after new property? And similarly our love of knowledge, of truth; and in general all the striving after novelties?
paras.uz: 14. Sevgi deb ataladigan narsa. — Mulkka bo'lgan hirs va sevgi: bu g'oyalarning har biri qanchalik turli xil bog'lanishlarni uyg'otadi! — va shunga qaramay bu ikki marta nomlangan bir xil mayl bo'lishi mumkin: bir safar allaqachon egalik qilayotganlar nuqtai nazaridan past baholangan (ularda mayl qandaydir sokinlikka erishgan va endi ular o'z «mulki»ning xavfsizligidan xavotirda); boshqa safar qoniqmagan va tashna odamlar nuqtai nazaridan qaralgan va shuning uchun «yaxshi» deb ulug'langan. Bizning yaqinimizga bo'lgan sevgimiz — bu yangi mulkka intilish emasmi? Xuddi shunday, bizning bilimga, haqiqatga bo'lgan sevgimiz; va umuman yangiliklarga bo'lgan barcha intilishlar?

paras.en: We gradually become satiated with the old, the securely possessed, and again stretch out our hands; even the finest landscape in which we live for three months is no longer certain of our love, and any kind of more distant coast excites our covetousness: the possession for the most part becomes smaller through possessing. Our pleasure in ourselves seeks to maintain itself, by always transforming something new into ourselves,—that is just possessing. To become satiated with a possession, that is to become satiated with ourselves.
paras.uz: Biz asta-sekin eski, ishonchli egalik qilinayotgan narsadan to'yamiz va yana qo'llarimizni cho'zamiz; hatto uch oy yashaydigan eng go'zal manzara ham endi sevgimizga ishonchli emas va qandaydir uzoqroq qirg'oq ochko'zligimizni qo'zg'atadi: mulk ko'pincha egalik qilish orqali kichrayadi. O'zimizdan zavqlanishimiz doimo yangi nimanidir o'zimizga aylantirish orqali o'zini saqlashga intiladi, — aynan shu egalik qilishdir. Mulkdan to'yish — o'zimizdan to'yish demakdir.

paras.en: (One can also suffer from excess,—even the desire to cast away, to share out, can assume the honourable name of "love.") When we see any one suffering, we willingly utilise the opportunity then afforded to take possession of him; the beneficent and sympathetic man, for example, does this; he also calls the desire for new possession awakened in him, by the name of "love," and has enjoyment in it, as in a new acquisition suggesting itself to him. The love of the sexes, however, betrays itself most plainly as the striving after possession: the lover wants the unconditioned, sole possession of the person longed for by him; he wants just as absolute power over her soul as over her body; he wants to be loved solely, and to dwell and rule in the other soul as what is highest and most to be desired.
paras.uz: (Odam ortiqchalikdan ham azob chekishi mumkin, — hatto tashlab yuborish, bo'lishish istagi ham «sevgi» degan sharafli nomni olishi mumkin.) Kimningdir azob chekayotganini ko'rganimizda, uni egallab olish uchun o'shanda berilgan imkoniyatdan bajonidil foydalanamiz; masalan, xayrixoh va hamdard odam shunday qiladi; u ham o'zida uyg'ongan yangi mulkka bo'lgan istakni «sevgi» deb ataydi va undan o'ziga taklif qilinayotgan yangi orttirmadan zavqlangandek zavqlanadi. Biroq jinslar sevgisi o'zini eng aniq egalikka intilish sifatida oshkor qiladi: oshiq o'zi orzu qilgan odamga shartsiz, yagona egalik qilishni istaydi; u uning tanasi ustidan bo'lgani kabi ruhi ustidan ham mutlaq hokimiyatni istaydi; u faqat o'zi sevilishni va boshqa ruhda eng oliy va eng orzu qilinadigan narsa sifatida yashashni va hukmronlik qilishni istaydi.

paras.en: When one considers that this means precisely to exclude all the world from a precious possession, a happiness, and an enjoyment; when one considers that the lover has in view the impoverishment and privation of all other rivals, and would like to become the dragon of his golden hoard, as the most inconsiderate and selfish of all "conquerors" and exploiters; when one considers finally that to the lover himself, the whole world besides appears indifferent, colourless, and worthless, and that he is ready to make every sacrifice, disturb every arrangement, and put every other interest behind his own,—one is verily surprised that this ferocious lust of property and injustice of sexual love should have been glorified and deified to such an extent at all times; yea, that out of this love the conception of love as the antithesis of egoism should have been derived, when it is perhaps precisely the most unqualified expression of egoism.
paras.uz: Bu aynan butun dunyoni qimmatli mulkdan, baxtdan va zavqdan chetlatish ekanini o'ylaganda; oshiq barcha boshqa raqiblarning qashshoqlashishi va mahrumligini ko'zda tutishini va barcha «bosqinchilar» va ekspluatatorlarning eng beparvo va eng xudbini sifatida o'z oltin xazinasining ajdahosi bo'lishni xohlashini o'ylaganda; nihoyat, oshiqning o'ziga butun boshqa dunyo befarq, rangsiz va qadrsiz ko'rinishini va u har qanday qurbonlik qilishga, har qanday tartibni buzishga va har qanday boshqa manfaatni o'zinikidan keyin qo'yishga tayyor ekanini o'ylaganda, — mulkka bo'lgan bu yirtqich hirs va jinsiy sevgining bu adolatsizligi barcha zamonlarda bunchalik ulug'lanib, ilohiylashtirilganidan haqiqatan ham hayron qolasan; ha, bu sevgidan sevgi xudbinlikning qarama-qarshisi degan tushuncha kelib chiqqan, holbuki u balki aynan xudbinlikning eng shartsiz ifodasidir.

paras.en: Here, evidently, the non-possessors and desirers have determined the usage of language,—there were, of course, always too many of them. Those who have been favoured with much possession and satiety, have, to be sure, dropped a word now and then about the "raging demon," as, for instance, the most lovable and most beloved of all the Athenians—Sophocles; but Eros always laughed at such revilers,—they were always his greatest favourites.—There is, of course, here and there on this terrestrial sphere a kind of sequel to love, in which that covetous longing of two persons for one another has yielded to a new desire and covetousness, to a common, higher thirst for a superior ideal standing above them: but who knows this love? Who has experienced it? Its right name is friendship.
paras.uz: Bu yerda, aftidan, egalik qilmaydiganlar va istovchilar til qo'llanilishini belgilagan, — albatta, ular doimo haddan tashqari ko'p bo'lgan. Ko'p mulk va to'qlik nasib etganlar, albatta, vaqti-vaqti bilan «quturgan iblis» haqida bir so'z aytib o'tishgan, masalan, barcha afinaliklarning eng yoqimtoyi va eng sevimlisi — Sofokl; lekin Eros doimo bunday so'kuvchilar ustidan kulgan, — ular doimo uning eng sevimli erkatoylari bo'lgan. — Albatta, bu yer kurrasida u yer-bu yerda sevgining qandaydir davomi bor, unda ikki kishining bir-biriga bo'lgan o'sha ochko'z sog'inchi yangi istak va ochko'zlikka, ulardan yuqorida turgan oliy idealga bo'lgan umumiy, yuksakroq tashnalikka o'rin bergan: lekin bu sevgini kim biladi? Kim uni boshdan kechirgan? Uning to'g'ri nomi — do'stlik.

paras.en: 15. Out of the Distance. — This mountain makes the whole district which it dominates charming in every way, and full of significance: after we have said this to ourselves for the hundredth time, we are so irrationally and so gratefully disposed towards it, as the giver of this charm, that we fancy it must itself be the most charming thing in the district—and so we climb it, and are undeceived. All of a sudden, it itself, and the whole landscape around and under us, is as it were disenchanted; we had forgotten that many a greatness, like many a goodness, wants only to be seen at a certain distance, and entirely from below, not from above,—it is thus only that it operates. Perhaps you know men in your neighbourhood who can only look at themselves from a certain distance to find themselves at all endurable, or attractive and enlivening; they are to be dissuaded from self-knowledge.
paras.uz: 15. Uzoqdan. — Bu tog' o'zi hukmronlik qiladigan butun o'lkani har jihatdan maftunkor va ma'noga to'la qiladi: buni o'zimizga yuzinchi marta aytganimizdan keyin, biz unga, bu jozibani beruvchi sifatida, shunchalik aqlsiz va shunchalik minnatdorlik bilan munosabatda bo'lamizki, uning o'zi o'lkadagi eng maftunkor narsa bo'lsa kerak deb xayol qilamiz — shuning uchun unga chiqamiz va hafsalamiz pir bo'ladi. To'satdan uning o'zi ham, atrofimiz va ostimizdagi butun manzara ham go'yo sehridan mahrum bo'ladi; biz ko'p buyuklik, ko'p yaxshilik kabi, faqat ma'lum masofadan va butunlay pastdan, yuqoridan emas, ko'rilishini istashini unutgan edik, — faqat shundagina u ta'sir qiladi. Balki atrofingizda o'zlarini umuman chidab bo'ladigan, yoki jozibali va jonlantiruvchi deb topish uchun o'zlariga faqat ma'lum masofadan qaray oladigan odamlarni bilarsiz; ularni o'zini bilishdan qaytarish kerak.

paras.en: 16. Across the Plank. — One must be able to dissimulate in intercourse with persons who are ashamed of their feelings; they experience a sudden aversion towards anyone who surprises them in a state of tender, or enthusiastic and high-running feeling, as if he had seen their secrets. If one wants to be kind to them in such moments one should make them laugh, or say some kind of cold, playful wickedness:—their feeling thereby congeals, and they are again self-possessed. But I give the moral before the story.—We were once on a time so near one another in the course of our lives, that nothing more seemed to hinder our friendship and fraternity, and there was merely a small plank between us. While you were just about to step on it, I asked you:
paras.uz: 16. Taxta orqali. — O'z tuyg'ularidan uyaladigan odamlar bilan munosabatda o'zini boshqacha ko'rsata bilish kerak; ularni mayin, yoki ishtiyoqli va jo'shqin tuyg'u holatida tutib olgan har qanday odamga, go'yo u ularning sirlarini ko'rgandek, to'satdan nafrat paydo bo'ladi. Agar bunday lahzalarda ularga mehribonlik qilmoqchi bo'lsang, ularni kuldirishing yoki qandaydir sovuq, o'yinqaroq yovuzlik aytishing kerak: — shunda ularning tuyg'usi qotib qoladi va ular yana o'zini qo'lga oladi. Lekin men ibratni hikoyadan oldin beryapman. — Bir paytlar biz hayot yo'limizda bir-birimizga shunchalik yaqin edikki, do'stligimiz va birodarligimizga boshqa hech narsa to'sqinlik qilmayotgandek tuyulardi va oramizda faqat kichkina bir taxta bor edi. Sen endigina unga qadam qo'ymoqchi bo'lganingda, men sendan so'radim:

paras.en: "Do you want to come across the plank to me?" But then you did not want to come any longer; and when I again entreated, you were silent. Since then mountains and torrents, and whatever separates and alienates, have interposed between us, and even if we wanted to come to one another, we could no longer do so! When, however, you now remember that small plank, you have no longer words,—but merely sobs and amazement.
paras.uz: «Taxta orqali menga o'tmoqchimisan?» Lekin keyin sen endi o'tishni istamading; va men yana yolvorganimda, sen jim qolding. O'shandan beri oramizga tog'lar va sel oqimlari, ajratadigan va begonalashtiradigan hamma narsa tushdi va hatto bir-birimizga kelmoqchi bo'lsak ham, endi kela olmaymiz! Biroq endi o'sha kichkina taxtani eslaganingda, so'zing qolmaydi, — faqat o'ksik va hayrat.

paras.en: 17. Motivation of Poverty. — We cannot, to be sure, by any artifice make a rich and richly-flowing virtue out of a poor one, but we can gracefully enough reinterpret its poverty into necessity, so that its aspect no longer gives pain to us, and we do not make any reproachful faces at fate on account of it. It is thus that the wise gardener does, who puts the tiny streamlet of his garden into the arms of a fountain-nymph, and thus motivates the poverty:—and who would not like him need the nymphs!
paras.uz: 17. Qashshoqlikni asoslash. — Albatta, hech qanday hiyla bilan kambag'al fazilatdan boy va mo'l oqadigan fazilat yasay olmaymiz, lekin uning qashshoqligini yetarlicha nafis tarzda zaruratga aylantirib talqin qila olamiz, shunda uning ko'rinishi endi bizga og'riq bermaydi va shu tufayli taqdirga ta'na bilan qaramaymiz. Dono bog'bon shunday qiladi: u bog'idagi kichkina jilg'ani favvora parisining qo'llariga topshiradi va shu tariqa qashshoqlikni asoslaydi: — va kim unga o'xshab parilarga muhtoj bo'lmasdi!

paras.en: 18. Ancient Pride. — The ancient savour of nobility is lacking in us, because the ancient slave is lacking in our sentiment. A Greek of noble descent found such immense intermediate stages, and such a distance betwixt his elevation and that ultimate baseness, that he could hardly even see the slave plainly: even Plato no longer saw him entirely. It is otherwise with us, accustomed as we are to the doctrine of the equality of men, although not to the equality itself.
paras.uz: 18. Qadimiy g'urur. — Bizda qadimiy zodagonlik ta'mi yetishmaydi, chunki tuyg'umizda qadimiy qul yetishmaydi. Zodagon nasldan bo'lgan yunon o'zining yuksakligi va o'sha so'nggi pastkashlik o'rtasida shunday ulkan oraliq bosqichlar va shunday masofani topardiki, qulni hatto aniq ko'ra olmasdi: hatto Platon ham uni endi butunlay ko'rmagan. Biz bilan boshqacha, chunki biz odamlar tengligi ta'limotiga o'rganganmiz, garchi tenglikning o'ziga o'rganmagan bo'lsak ham.

paras.en: A being who has not the free disposal of himself and has not got leisure,—that is not regarded by us as anything contemptible; there is perhaps too much of this kind of slavishness in each of us, in accordance with the conditions of our social order and activity, which are fundamentally different from those of the ancients.—The Greek philosopher went through life with the secret feeling that there were many more slaves than people supposed—that is to say, that every one was a slave who was not a philosopher. His pride was puffed up when he considered that even the mightiest of the earth were thus to be looked upon as slaves. This pride is also unfamiliar to us, and impossible; the word "slave" has not its full force for us even in simile.
paras.uz: O'zini erkin tasarruf eta olmaydigan va bo'sh vaqti yo'q mavjudot — biz uni jirkanch narsa deb hisoblamaymiz; ijtimoiy tartibimiz va faoliyatimiz shartlariga ko'ra, ular qadimgilarnikidan tubdan farq qiladi, har birimizda bunday qullikdan balki haddan tashqari ko'p bor. — Yunon faylasufi hayot bo'ylab odamlar o'ylaganidan ancha ko'p qullar bor degan yashirin tuyg'u bilan yurgan — ya'ni faylasuf bo'lmagan har kim qul. Hatto yer yuzining eng qudratlilariga ham shu tariqa qul sifatida qarash kerakligini o'ylaganda uning g'ururi ko'pchirdi. Bu g'urur bizga ham notanish va imkonsiz; «qul» so'zi biz uchun hatto o'xshatishda ham to'liq kuchiga ega emas.

paras.en: 19. Evil. — Test the life of the best and most productive men and nations, and ask yourselves whether a tree which is to grow proudly heavenward can dispense with bad weather and tempests: whether disfavour and opposition from without, whether every kind of hatred, jealousy, stubbornness, distrust, severity, greed, and violence do not belong to the favouring circumstances without which a great growth even in virtue is hardly possible? The poison by which the weaker nature is destroyed is strengthening to the strong individual—and he does not call it poison.
paras.uz: 19. Yovuzlik. — Eng yaxshi va eng samarali odamlar va xalqlarning hayotini sinab ko'ring va o'zingizdan so'rang: osmonga mag'rur o'sishi kerak bo'lgan daraxt yomon ob-havo va bo'ronlarsiz yashay oladimi; tashqaridan bo'lgan noxushlik va qarshilik, har qanday nafrat, rashk, qaysarlik, ishonchsizlik, qattiqqo'llik, ochko'zlik va zo'ravonlik — ularsiz hatto fazilatda ham buyuk o'sish deyarli imkonsiz bo'lgan qulay sharoitlarga kirmaydimi? Zaif tabiatni halok qiladigan zahar kuchli shaxsni kuchaytiradi — va u uni zahar deb atamaydi.

quiz.why_uz: Nitsshe sevgini mulkka bo'lgan hirsga o'xshatadi.

chapters.recap_uz: Lazzat va og'riq chambarchas bog'liq bo'lishi mumkin. Biz boshqalarga yaxshilik yoki yomonlik qilib qudratimizni his qilamiz. Sevgi ko'pincha egalik qilish istagi; uning yuksak shakli — do'stlik. Kuchli odamga zahar kuch beradi.

chapters.title: The dignity of folly

paras.en: 20. Dignity of Folly. — Several millenniums further on in the path of the last century!—and in everything that man does the highest prudence will be exhibited: but just thereby prudence will have lost all its dignity. It will then, sure enough, be necessary to be prudent, but it will also be so usual and common, that a more fastidious taste will feel this necessity as vulgarity. And just as a tyranny of truth and science would be in a position to raise the value of falsehood, a tyranny of prudence could force into prominence a new species of nobleness. To be noble—that might then mean, perhaps, to be capable of follies.
paras.uz: 20. Ahmoqlikning qadr-qimmati. — O'tgan asr yo'lida yana bir necha ming yil oldinga! — va insonning har bir ishida eng oliy ehtiyotkorlik namoyon bo'ladi: lekin aynan shu bilan ehtiyotkorlik butun qadr-qimmatini yo'qotadi. O'shanda, albatta, ehtiyotkor bo'lish zarur bo'ladi, lekin u shunchalik odatiy va oddiy bo'lib qoladiki, nozikroq did bu zaruratni qo'pollik deb his qiladi. Va xuddi haqiqat va ilm zulmi yolg'onning qadrini oshirishga qodir bo'lgani kabi, ehtiyotkorlik zulmi ham olijanoblikning yangi turini oldinga chiqarishi mumkin. Olijanob bo'lish — o'shanda, ehtimol, ahmoqliklarga qodir bo'lishni anglatar.

paras.en: 21. To the Teachers of Unselfishness. — The virtues of a man are called good, not in respect of the results they have for himself, but in respect of the results which we expect therefrom for ourselves and for society:—we have all along had very little unselfishness, very little "non-egoism" in our praise of the virtues! For otherwise it could not but have been seen that the virtues (such as diligence, obedience, chastity, piety, justice) are mostly injurious to their possessors, as impulses which rule in them too vehemently and ardently, and do not want to be kept in co-ordination with the other impulses by the reason. If you have a virtue, an actual, perfect virtue (and not merely a kind of impulse towards virtue!)—you are its victim! But your neighbour praises your virtue precisely on that account!
paras.uz: 21. Fidoyilik o'qituvchilariga. — Insonning fazilatlari uning o'zi uchun keltiradigan natijalar nuqtai nazaridan emas, balki biz ulardan o'zimiz va jamiyat uchun kutadigan natijalar nuqtai nazaridan yaxshi deb ataladi: — fazilatlarni maqtashimizda doimo juda oz fidoyilik, juda oz «xudbin emaslik» bo'lgan! Aks holda, fazilatlar (masalan, tirishqoqlik, itoatkorlik, iffat, taqvo, adolat) ko'pincha o'z egalariga zarar keltirishini ko'rmaslik mumkin emas edi, chunki ular ularda haddan tashqari shiddatli va qizg'in hukmronlik qiladigan va aql tomonidan boshqa mayllar bilan muvofiqlashtirilishni istamaydigan mayllardir. Agar sizda fazilat bo'lsa, haqiqiy, mukammal fazilat (va shunchaki fazilatga qandaydir mayl emas!) — siz uning qurbonisiz! Lekin qo'shningiz aynan shuning uchun fazilatingizni maqtaydi!

paras.en: One praises the diligent man though he injures his sight, or the originality and freshness of his spirit, by his diligence; the youth is honoured and regretted who has "worn himself out by work," because one passes the judgment that "for society as a whole the loss of the best individual is only a small sacrifice! A pity that this sacrifice should be necessary! A much greater pity, it is true, if the individual should think differently, and regard his preservation and development as more important than his work in the service of society!" And so one regrets this youth, not on his own account, but because a devoted instrument, regardless of self—a so-called "good man," has been lost to society by his death.
paras.uz: Tirishqoq odamni, garchi tirishqoqligi bilan ko'zini yoki ruhining o'ziga xosligi va tazeligini buzsa ham, maqtashadi; «ishdan charchab ado bo'lgan» yigitni hurmat qilishadi va unga achinishadi, chunki shunday hukm chiqariladi: «butun jamiyat uchun eng yaxshi shaxsni yo'qotish kichkina qurbonlik, xolos! Bu qurbonlik zarurligi achinarli! To'g'ri, agar shaxs boshqacha o'ylasa va o'zini saqlash va rivojlantirishni jamiyat xizmatidagi ishidan muhimroq deb bilsa, bu ancha achinarliroq bo'lardi!» Shunday qilib, bu yigitga uning o'zi uchun emas, balki o'zini ayamaydigan sadoqatli qurol — «yaxshi odam» deb ataladigan kishi uning o'limi bilan jamiyat uchun yo'qolgani uchun achinishadi.

paras.en: Perhaps one further considers the question, whether it would not have been more advantageous for the interests of society if he had laboured with less disregard of himself, and had preserved himself longer,—indeed, one readily admits an advantage therefrom, but one esteems the other advantage, namely, that a sacrifice has been made, and that the disposition of the sacrificial animal has once more been obviously endorsed—as higher and more enduring. It is accordingly, on the one part, the instrumental character in the virtues which is praised when the virtues are praised, and on the other part, the blind, ruling impulse in every virtue, which refuses to let itself be kept within bounds by the general advantage to the individual; in short, what is praised is the unreason in the virtues, in consequence of which the individual allows himself to be transformed into a function of the whole.
paras.uz: Balki yana, agar u o'zini kamroq ayamay ishlaganida va o'zini uzoqroq saqlaganida jamiyat manfaatlari uchun foydaliroq bo'lmasmidi, degan savolni ham ko'rib chiqishar, — haqiqatan ham, bundan foyda borligini osongina tan olishadi, lekin boshqa foydani — ya'ni qurbonlik qilingani va qurbonlik hayvonining moyilligi yana bir bor ochiq tasdiqlangani — yuqoriroq va bardoshliroq deb baholashadi. Demak, fazilatlar maqtalganda, bir tomondan, fazilatlardagi qurol xarakteri maqtaladi, boshqa tomondan esa, har bir fazilatdagi shaxs uchun umumiy foyda bilan chegaralanishni rad etadigan ko'r, hukmron mayl; qisqasi, maqtalgan narsa — fazilatlardagi aqlsizlik, uning natijasida shaxs o'zini butunning funksiyasiga aylantirishga yo'l qo'yadi.

paras.en: The praise of the virtues is the praise of something which is privately injurious to the individual; it is praise of impulses which deprive man of his noblest self-love, and the power to take the best care of himself. To be sure, for the teaching and embodying of virtuous habits a series of effects of virtue are displayed, which make it appear that virtue and private advantage are closely related,—and there is in fact such a relationship! Blindly furious diligence, for example, the typical virtue of an instrument, is represented as the way to riches and honour, and as the most beneficial antidote to tedium and passion: but people are silent concerning its danger, its greatest dangerousness.
paras.uz: Fazilatlarni maqtash — shaxs uchun shaxsan zararli bo'lgan narsani maqtashdir; bu insonni eng olijanob o'zini sevishidan va o'ziga eng yaxshi g'amxo'rlik qilish kuchidan mahrum qiladigan mayllarni maqtashdir. Albatta, fazilatli odatlarni o'rgatish va singdirish uchun fazilatning qator ta'sirlari ko'rsatiladi, ular fazilat va shaxsiy foyda chambarchas bog'liqdek ko'rsatadi, — va haqiqatan ham shunday bog'liqlik bor! Masalan, ko'r-ko'rona quturgan tirishqoqlik, qurolning tipik fazilati, boylik va sharafga yo'l, zerikish va ehtirosga qarshi eng foydali dori sifatida tasvirlanadi: lekin uning xavfi, eng katta xavfliligi haqida odamlar jim turishadi.

paras.en: Education proceeds in this manner throughout: it endeavours, by a series of enticements and advantages, to determine the individual to a certain mode of thinking and acting, which, when it has become habit, impulse and passion, rules in him and over him, in opposition to his ultimate advantage, but "for the general good." How often do I see that blindly furious diligence does indeed create riches and honours, but at the same time deprives the organs of the refinement by virtue of which alone an enjoyment of riches and honours is possible; so that really the main expedient for combating tedium and passion, simultaneously blunts the senses and makes the spirit refractory towards new stimuli!
paras.uz: Tarbiya butunlay shu tarzda olib boriladi: u qator vasvasalar va foydalar orqali shaxsni ma'lum fikrlash va harakat qilish usuliga yo'naltirishga intiladi, u odat, mayl va ehtirosga aylanganda, unda va uning ustidan uning oliy foydasiga zid ravishda, lekin «umumiy farovonlik uchun» hukmronlik qiladi. Necha marta ko'raman: ko'r-ko'rona quturgan tirishqoqlik haqiqatan ham boylik va sharaf yaratadi, lekin bir vaqtning o'zida a'zolarni faqat ular tufayli boylik va sharafdan zavq olish mumkin bo'lgan nozikligidan mahrum qiladi; shunday qilib, aslida zerikish va ehtirosga qarshi kurashning asosiy vositasi bir vaqtning o'zida sezgilarni o'tmaslashtiradi va ruhni yangi qo'zg'atuvchilarga nisbatan qaysar qiladi!

paras.en: (The busiest of all ages—our age—does not know how to make anything out of its great diligence and wealth, except always more and more wealth, and more and more diligence; there is even more genius needed for laying out wealth than for acquiring it!—Well, we shall have our "grandchildren"!) If the education succeeds, every virtue of the individual is a public utility, and a private disadvantage in respect to the highest private end,—probably some psycho-æsthetic stunting, or even premature dissolution. One should consider successively from the same standpoint the virtues of obedience, chastity, piety, and justice.
paras.uz: (Barcha davrlarning eng band davri — bizning davrimiz — o'zining katta tirishqoqligi va boyligidan doimo tobora ko'proq boylik va tobora ko'proq tirishqoqlikdan boshqa hech narsa yasashni bilmaydi; boylikni sarflash uchun uni orttirishdan ham ko'proq daho kerak! — Mayli, bizning «nevaralarimiz» bo'ladi!) Agar tarbiya muvaffaqiyatli bo'lsa, shaxsning har bir fazilati jamoat foydasi va oliy shaxsiy maqsad nuqtai nazaridan shaxsiy zarar bo'ladi, — ehtimol, qandaydir ruhiy-estetik o'sishdan qolish, yoki hatto muddatidan oldin yemirilish. Itoatkorlik, iffat, taqvo va adolat fazilatlarini ham ketma-ket xuddi shu nuqtai nazardan ko'rib chiqish kerak.

paras.en: The praise of the unselfish, self-sacrificing, virtuous person—he, consequently, who does not expend his whole energy and reason for his own conservation, development, elevation, furtherance and augmentation of power, but lives as regards himself unassumingly and thoughtlessly, perhaps even indifferently or ironically,—this praise has in any case not originated out of the spirit of unselfishness! The "neighbour" praises unselfishness because he profits by it! If the neighbour were "unselfishly" disposed himself, he would reject that destruction of power, that injury for his advantage, he would thwart such inclinations in their origin, and above all he would manifest his unselfishness just by not giving it a good name! The fundamental contradiction in that morality which at present stands in high honour is here indicated: the motives to such a morality are in antithesis to its principle!
paras.uz: Fidoyi, o'zini qurbon qiladigan, fazilatli odamni maqtash — ya'ni butun kuchi va aqlini o'zini saqlash, rivojlantirish, yuksaltirish, qo'llab-quvvatlash va qudratini oshirishga sarflamaydigan, balki o'ziga nisbatan kamtarona va beparvo, balki hatto befarq yoki kinoya bilan yashaydigan odamni maqtash, — bu maqtov har holda fidoyilik ruhidan kelib chiqmagan! «Qo'shni» fidoyilikni undan foyda ko'rgani uchun maqtaydi! Agar qo'shnining o'zi «fidoyi» moyillikka ega bo'lganida, u o'z foydasi uchun qudratning bunday yo'q qilinishini, bunday zararni rad etgan, bunday moyilliklarni boshidayoq to'xtatgan bo'lardi va eng avvalo, o'z fidoyiligini aynan unga yaxshi nom bermaslik bilan namoyon qilgan bo'lardi! Hozir yuksak hurmatda turgan axloqdagi asosiy qarama-qarshilik shu yerda ko'rsatilgan: bunday axloqning motivlari uning tamoyiliga ziddir!

paras.en: That with which this morality wishes to prove itself, refutes it out of its criterion of what is moral! The maxim, "Thou shalt renounce thyself and offer thyself as a sacrifice," in order not to be inconsistent with its own morality, could only be decreed by a being who himself renounced his own advantage thereby, and who perhaps in the required self-sacrifice of individuals brought about his own dissolution. As soon, however, as the neighbour (or society) recommended altruism on account of its utility, the precisely antithetical proposition, "Thou shalt seek thy advantage even at the expense of everybody else," was brought into use: accordingly, "thou shalt," and "thou shalt not," are preached in one breath!
paras.uz: Bu axloq o'zini isbotlamoqchi bo'lgan narsa uni axloqiylik mezonidan kelib chiqib rad etadi! «Sen o'zingdan voz kechishing va o'zingni qurbon qilishing kerak» degan qoidani, o'z axloqiga zid kelmaslik uchun, faqat bu bilan o'z foydasidan voz kechgan va balki shaxslardan talab qilingan fidoyilikda o'zining yemirilishiga sabab bo'lgan mavjudotgina e'lon qila olardi. Biroq qo'shni (yoki jamiyat) altruizmni foydasi uchun tavsiya qilishi bilanoq, aynan qarama-qarshi qoida — «Sen hatto boshqa hammaning hisobiga bo'lsa ham o'z foydangni izlashing kerak» — qo'llanila boshlandi: shunday qilib, «kerak» va «kerak emas» bir nafasda va'z qilinadi!

paras.en: 22. L'Ordre du Jour pour le Roi. — The day commences: let us begin to arrange for this day the business and fêtes of our most gracious lord, who at present is still pleased to repose. His Majesty has bad weather to-day: we shall be careful not to call it bad; we shall not speak of the weather,—but we shall go through to-day's business somewhat more ceremoniously and make the fêtes somewhat more festive than would otherwise be necessary. His Majesty may perhaps even be sick: we shall give the last good news of the evening at breakfast, the arrival of M. Montaigne, who knows how to joke so pleasantly about his sickness,—he suffers from stone. We shall receive several persons (persons!—what would that old inflated frog, who will be among them, say, if he heard this word!
paras.uz: 22. L'Ordre du Jour pour le Roi — Qirol uchun kun tartibi. — Kun boshlanmoqda: hozircha hali dam olishni ma'qul ko'rayotgan eng mehribon hukmdorimizning bu kungi ishlari va bayramlarini tartibga sola boshlaylik. Janobi oliylarining bugun ob-havosi yomon: biz uni yomon demaslikka ehtiyot bo'lamiz; ob-havo haqida gapirmaymiz, — lekin bugungi ishlarni biroz tantanaliroq o'tkazamiz va bayramlarni aks holda zarur bo'lganidan biroz bayramonaroq qilamiz. Janobi oliylari balki hatto kasaldirlar: nonushtada kechqurungi oxirgi yaxshi xabarni beramiz — o'z kasalligi haqida shunchalik yoqimli hazil qila oladigan janob Monten keldi, — u tosh kasalligidan aziyat chekadi. Bir nechta shaxslarni qabul qilamiz (shaxslar! — ular orasida bo'ladigan o'sha keksa, ko'pchigan qurbaqa bu so'zni eshitsa nima derdi!

paras.en: "I am no person," he would say, "but always the thing itself")—and the reception will last longer than is pleasant to anybody; a sufficient reason for telling about the poet who wrote over his door, "He who enters here will do me an honour; he who does not—a favour."—That is, forsooth, saying a discourteous thing in a courteous manner! And perhaps this poet is quite justified on his part in being discourteous; they say that the rhymes are better than the rhymester. Well, let him still make many of them, and withdraw himself as much as possible from the world: and that is doubtless the significance of his well-bred rudeness! A prince, on the other hand, is always of more value than his "verse," even when—but what are we about?
paras.uz: «Men shaxs emasman, — derdi u, — balki doimo narsaning o'ziman») — va qabul hammaga yoqimli bo'lganidan uzoqroq davom etadi; eshigi ustiga: «Bu yerga kirgan menga sharaf keltiradi; kirmagan — iltifot» deb yozgan shoir haqida gapirib berishga yetarli sabab. — Bu, haqiqatan ham, xushmuomala tarzda qo'pol gap aytish! Balki bu shoir o'z tomonidan qo'pol bo'lishga butunlay haqlidir; aytishlaricha, uning qofiyalari qofiyaboz o'zidan yaxshiroq ekan. Mayli, ulardan yana ko'p yozsin va dunyodan iloji boricha ko'proq chetlansin: shubhasiz, uning tarbiyali qo'polligining ma'nosi shu! Shahzoda esa, aksincha, doimo o'z «she'ri»dan qimmatliroq, hatto qachonki — lekin biz nima qilyapmiz?

paras.en: We gossip, and the whole court believes that we have already been at work and racked our brains: there is no light to be seen earlier than that which burns in our window.—Hark! Was that not the bell? The devil! The day and the dance commence, and we do not know our rounds! We must then improvise,—all the world improvises its day. To-day, let us for once do like all the world!—And therewith vanished my wonderful morning dream, probably owing to the violent strokes of the tower-clock, which just then announced the fifth hour with all the importance which is peculiar to it.
paras.uz: Biz g'iybat qilyapmiz, butun saroy esa biz allaqachon ishlab, miyamizni qotirdik deb o'ylaydi: bizning derazamizda yonayotgan chiroqdan oldin hech qanday chiroq ko'rinmaydi. — Quloq soling! Bu qo'ng'iroq emasmidi? La'nati! Kun va raqs boshlanmoqda, biz esa o'z aylanishlarimizni bilmaymiz! Demak, bado'ha qilishimiz kerak, — butun dunyo o'z kunini bado'ha qiladi. Bugun bir marta butun dunyo kabi qilaylik! — Va shu bilan mening ajoyib tongi tushim g'oyib bo'ldi, ehtimol, aynan o'sha paytda o'ziga xos butun salobati bilan beshinchi soatni e'lon qilgan minora soatining kuchli zarbalari tufayli.

paras.en: It seems to me that, on this occasion, the God of dreams wanted to make merry over my habits,—it is my habit to commence the day by arranging it properly, to make it endurable for myself, and it is possible that I may often have done this too formally, and too much like a prince.
paras.uz: Menimcha, bu safar tushlar Xudosi mening odatlarim ustidan kulmoqchi bo'lgan, — mening odatim kunni to'g'ri tartibga solish, uni o'zim uchun chidab bo'ladigan qilish bilan boshlash, va ehtimol men buni ko'pincha haddan tashqari rasmiy, haddan tashqari shahzodalarcha qilgandirman.
