…r otherwise it could not but have been seen that the virtues (such as diligence, obedience, chastity, piety, justice) are mostly injurious to their possessors,…
21. To the Teachers of Unselfishness. — The virtues of a man are called good, not in respect of the results they…
…or society as a whole the loss of the best individual is only a small sacrifice! A pity that this sacrifice should be necessary! A much greater pity, it is true…
…erely a kind of impulse towards virtue!)—you are its victim! But your neighbour praises your virtue precisely on that account!

quiz.q: Why does the 'neighbour' praise unselfishness?
quiz.why_uz: «Qo'shni fidoyilikni undan foyda ko'rgani uchun maqtaydi».

quiz.q: What might being noble mean in the future?
quiz.why_uz: Ehtiyotkorlik hamma uchun oddiy bo'lsa, ahmoqlik olijanoblik belgisiga aylanadi.

chapters.recap_uz: Kelajakda ehtiyotkorlik oddiy bo'lib qolsa, olijanoblik ahmoqlikka qodir bo'lishni anglatishi mumkin. Fazilatlar ko'pincha o'z egasiga zarar keltiradi, ularni esa jamiyat foydasi uchun maqtashadi. Oxirida — qirol kuni haqidagi tush.

chapters.title: Corruption and the individual

paras.en: 23. The Characteristics of Corruption. — Let us observe the following characteristics in that condition of society from time to time necessary, which is designated by the word "corruption." Immediately upon the appearance of corruption anywhere, a motley superstition gets the upper hand, and the hitherto universal belief of a people becomes colourless and impotent in comparison with it; for superstition is freethinking of the second rank,—he who gives himself over to it selects certain forms and formulæ which appeal to him, and permits himself a right of choice. The superstitious man is always much more of a "person," in comparison with the religious man, and a superstitious society will be one in which there are many individuals, and a delight in individuality. Seen from this standpoint superstition always appears as a progress in comparison with belief, and as a sign that the intellect becomes more independent and claims to have its rights.
paras.uz: 23. Buzilishning belgilari. — Jamiyatning vaqti-vaqti bilan zarur bo'ladigan, «buzilish» so'zi bilan ataladigan holatidagi quyidagi belgilarni kuzataylik. Qayerdadir buzilish paydo bo'lishi bilanoq, rang-barang xurofot ustunlikka erishadi va xalqning shu paytgacha umumiy bo'lgan e'tiqodi u bilan solishtirganda rangsiz va kuchsiz bo'lib qoladi; chunki xurofot — ikkinchi darajali erkin fikrlash, — unga berilgan odam o'ziga yoqadigan ma'lum shakl va formulalarni tanlaydi va o'ziga tanlash huquqini beradi. Xurofotchi odam dindor odamga nisbatan doimo ko'proq «shaxs» bo'ladi va xurofotchi jamiyat ko'plab shaxslar va o'ziga xoslikdan zavqlanish bo'lgan jamiyat bo'ladi. Shu nuqtai nazardan qaraganda, xurofot e'tiqodga nisbatan doimo taraqqiyot sifatida va aql mustaqilroq bo'lib, o'z huquqlarini talab qilayotganining belgisi sifatida ko'rinadi.

paras.en: Those who reverence the old religion and the religious disposition then complain of corruption,—they have hitherto also determined the usage of language, and have given a bad repute to superstition, even among the freest spirits. Let us learn that it is a symptom of enlightenment.—Secondly, a society in which corruption takes a hold is blamed for effeminacy: for the appreciation of war, and the delight in war perceptibly diminish in such a society, and the conveniences of life are now just as eagerly sought after as were military and gymnastic honours formerly.
paras.uz: O'shanda eski din va diniy moyillikni hurmat qiladiganlar buzilishdan shikoyat qilishadi, — ular shu paytgacha til qo'llanilishini ham belgilab kelgan va hatto eng erkin ruhlar orasida ham xurofotga yomon nom berishgan. Bu ma'rifatning alomati ekanini o'rganaylik. — Ikkinchidan, buzilish o'rnashgan jamiyat xotinchalishlikda ayblanadi: chunki bunday jamiyatda urushni qadrlash va urushdan zavqlanish sezilarli kamayadi va hayot qulayliklari endi ilgari harbiy va gimnastik sharaflar qanday qizg'in izlangan bo'lsa, xuddi shunday izlanadi.

paras.en: But one is accustomed to overlook the fact that the old national energy and national passion, which acquired a magnificent splendour in war and in the tourney, has now transferred itself into innumerable private passions, and has merely become less visible; indeed in periods of "corruption" the quantity and quality of the expended energy of a people is probably greater than ever, and the individual spends it lavishly, to such an extent as could not be done formerly—he was not then rich enough to do so!
paras.uz: Lekin urushda va turnirda ajoyib ulug'vorlikka erishgan eski milliy kuch va milliy ehtiros endi son-sanoqsiz shaxsiy ehtiroslarga o'tganini va shunchaki kamroq ko'rinadigan bo'lib qolganini e'tibordan chetda qoldirishga odatlanishgan; haqiqatan ham, «buzilish» davrlarida xalqning sarflagan kuchining miqdori va sifati, ehtimol, har qachongidan ham ko'proq bo'ladi va shaxs uni ilgari mumkin bo'lmagan darajada saxiylik bilan sarflaydi — u o'shanda buning uchun yetarlicha boy emas edi!

paras.en: And thus it is precisely in times of "effeminacy" that tragedy runs at large in and out of doors, it is then that ardent love and ardent hatred are born, and the flame of knowledge flashes heavenward in full blaze.—Thirdly, as if in amends for the reproach of superstition and effeminacy, it is customary to say of such periods of corruption that they are milder, and that cruelty has then greatly diminished in comparison with the older, more credulous, and stronger period. But to this praise I am just as little able to assent as to that reproach: I only grant so much—namely, that cruelty now becomes more refined, and its older forms are henceforth counter to the taste; but the wounding and torturing by word and look reaches its highest development in times of corruption,—it is now only that wickedness is created, and the delight in wickedness.
paras.uz: Va aynan «xotinchalishlik» davrlarida tragediya eshik ichkarisida ham, tashqarisida ham erkin yuradi, aynan o'shanda qizg'in sevgi va qizg'in nafrat tug'iladi va bilim alangasi to'liq lovullab osmonga chaqnaydi. — Uchinchidan, go'yo xurofot va xotinchalishlik ta'nasini qoplash uchun, bunday buzilish davrlari haqida ular yumshoqroq va shafqatsizlik eski, ishonuvchanroq va kuchliroq davrga nisbatan ancha kamaygan, deyish odat. Lekin men bu maqtovga ham o'sha ta'naga qo'shilmaganim kabi qo'shila olmayman: faqat shuncha narsani tan olaman — ya'ni shafqatsizlik endi nozikroq bo'ladi va uning eski shakllari bundan buyon didga zid keladi; lekin so'z va nigoh bilan yaralash va qiynash buzilish davrlarida eng yuqori rivojiga yetadi, — faqat endigina yovuzlik va yovuzlikdan zavqlanish yaratiladi.

paras.en: The men of the period of corruption are witty and calumnious; they know that there are yet other ways of murdering than by the dagger and the ambush—they know also that all that is well said is believed in.—Fourthly, it is when "morals decay" that those beings whom one calls tyrants first make their appearance; they are the forerunners of the individual, and as it were early matured firstlings. Yet a little while, and this fruit of fruits hangs ripe and yellow on the tree of a people,—and only for the sake of such fruit did this tree exist! When the decay has reached its worst, and likewise the conflict of all sorts of tyrants, there always arises the Cæsar, the final tyrant, who puts an end to the exhausted struggle for sovereignty, by making the exhaustedness work for him.
paras.uz: Buzilish davri odamlari o'tkir so'zli va tuhmatchi; ular xanjar va pistirmadan boshqa o'ldirish yo'llari ham borligini bilishadi — ular yana yaxshi aytilgan hamma narsaga ishonilishini ham bilishadi. — To'rtinchidan, aynan «axloq buzilganda» zolim deb ataladigan mavjudotlar birinchi marta paydo bo'ladi; ular shaxsning darakchilari, go'yo erta pishgan birinchi mevalari. Yana ozgina vaqt o'tadi va bu mevalar mevasi xalq daraxtida pishib, sarg'ayib osilib turadi, — va bu daraxt faqat shunday meva uchungina mavjud bo'lgan! Yemirilish eng yomon holatiga yetganda, shuningdek, har xil zolimlar o'rtasidagi kurash ham, doimo Sezar, oxirgi zolim paydo bo'ladi, u holdan toygan hukmronlik uchun kurashga chek qo'yadi, holsizlikni o'zi uchun ishlatib.

paras.en: In his time the individual is usually most mature, and consequently the "culture" is highest and most fruitful, but not on his account nor through him: although the men of highest culture love to flatter their Cæsar by pretending that they are his creation. The truth, however, is that they need quietness externally, because internally they have disquietude and labour. In these times bribery and treason are at their height: for the love of the ego, then first discovered, is much more powerful than the love of the old, used-up, hackneyed "fatherland"; and the need to be secure in one way or other against the frightful fluctuations of fortune, opens even the nobler hands, as soon as a richer and more powerful person shows himself ready to put gold into them.
paras.uz: Uning davrida shaxs odatda eng yetuk bo'ladi va shuning uchun «madaniyat» eng yuqori va eng samarali bo'ladi, lekin uning tufayli ham, u orqali ham emas: garchi eng yuksak madaniyatli odamlar o'zlarini uning ijodi deb ko'rsatib, o'z Sezariga xushomad qilishni yaxshi ko'rsalar ham. Haqiqat esa shundaki, ularga tashqaridan sokinlik kerak, chunki ichkaridan bezovtalik va mehnat bor. Bu davrlarda poraxo'rlik va xoinlik avjiga chiqadi: chunki endigina kashf etilgan «men»ga bo'lgan sevgi eski, eskirgan, siyqasi chiqqan «vatan»ga bo'lgan sevgidan ancha kuchliroq; va omadning dahshatli tebranishlaridan qandaydir tarzda himoyalanish ehtiyoji hatto olijanobroq qo'llarni ham ochadi, boyroq va qudratliroq odam ularga oltin solishga tayyor ekanini ko'rsatishi bilanoq.

paras.en: There is then so little certainty with regard to the future; people live only for the day: a condition of mind which enables every deceiver to play an easy game,—people of course only let themselves be misled and bribed "for the present," and reserve for themselves futurity and virtue.
paras.uz: O'shanda kelajakka nisbatan shunchalik oz ishonch bo'ladi; odamlar faqat bugun uchun yashaydi: bunday ruhiy holat har bir aldamchiga oson o'yin o'ynash imkonini beradi, — odamlar, albatta, faqat «hozircha» o'zlarini yo'ldan urishga va pora berishga yo'l qo'yishadi va kelajak va fazilatni o'zlariga saqlab qolishadi.

paras.en: The individuals, as is well known, the men who only live for themselves, provide for the moment more than do their opposites, the gregarious men, because they consider themselves just as incalculable as the future; and similarly they attach themselves willingly to despots, because they believe themselves capable of activities and expedients, which can neither reckon on being understood by the multitude, nor on finding favour with them,—but the tyrant or the Cæsar understands the rights of the Individual even in his excesses, and has an interest in speaking on behalf of a bolder private morality, and even in giving his hand to it. For he thinks of himself, and wishes people to think of him what Napoleon once uttered in his classical style—"I have the right to answer by an eternal 'thus I am' to everything about which complaint is brought against me.
paras.uz: Ma'lumki, shaxslar, faqat o'zlari uchun yashaydigan odamlar, o'zlarining qarama-qarshilari — podaviy odamlardan ko'ra lahza haqida ko'proq qayg'urishadi, chunki ular o'zlarini kelajak kabi oldindan hisoblab bo'lmaydigan deb bilishadi; xuddi shunday, ular despotlarga bajonidil qo'shilishadi, chunki o'zlarini olomon tomonidan tushunilishiga ham, uning marhamatiga ham umid qila olmaydigan faoliyat va choralarga qodir deb hisoblashadi, — lekin zolim yoki Sezar shaxsning huquqlarini hatto uning haddan oshishlarida ham tushunadi va dadilroq shaxsiy axloq tarafida gapirishdan, hatto unga qo'l cho'zishdan manfaatdor. Chunki u o'zi haqida Napoleon bir marta o'zining klassik uslubida aytgan narsani o'ylaydi va odamlar ham shunday o'ylashini istaydi: «Menga qarshi qilinadigan har qanday shikoyatga abadiy "men shundayman" deb javob berishga haqqim bor.

paras.en: I am apart from all the world, I accept conditions from nobody. I wish people also to submit to my fancies, and to take it quite as a simple matter, if I should indulge in this or that diversion." Thus spoke Napoleon once to his wife, when she had reasons for calling in question the fidelity of her husband.—The times of corruption are the seasons when the apples fall from the tree: I mean the individuals, the seed-bearers of the future, the pioneers of the spiritual colonisation and of a new construction of national and social unions. Corruption is only an abusive term for the harvest time of a people.
paras.uz: Men butun dunyodan alohidaman, hech kimdan shart qabul qilmayman. Men odamlarning ham mening injiqliklarimga bo'ysunishini va agar men u yoki bu ermakka berilsam, buni oddiy narsa deb qabul qilishini istayman». Napoleon bir marta xotiniga shunday degan, o'shanda u erining sadoqatiga shubha qilish uchun sabablarga ega edi. — Buzilish davrlari — olmalar daraxtdan tushadigan fasllar: men shaxslarni, kelajakning urug' tashuvchilarini, ruhiy mustamlakachilikning va milliy va ijtimoiy ittifoqlarning yangi qurilishining kashshoflarini nazarda tutyapman. Buzilish — xalqning hosil yig'im vaqti uchun shunchaki haqoratli atama.

paras.en: 24. Different Dissatisfactions. — The feeble and as it were feminine dissatisfied people have ingenuity for beautifying and deepening life; the strong dissatisfied people—the masculine persons among them, to continue the metaphor—have the ingenuity for improving and safeguarding life. The former show their weakness and feminine character by willingly letting themselves be temporarily deceived, and perhaps even by putting up with a little ecstasy and enthusiasm on a time, but on the whole they are never to be satisfied, and suffer from the incurability of their dissatisfaction; moreover they are the patrons of all those who manage to concoct opiate and narcotic comforts, and just on that account averse to those who value the physician higher than the priest,—they thereby encourage the continuance of actual distress!
paras.uz: 24. Turli noroziliklar. — Zaif va go'yo ayolona norozi odamlarda hayotni go'zallashtirish va chuqurlashtirish uchun zukkolik bor; kuchli norozi odamlar — o'xshatishni davom ettirsak, ular orasidagi erkakona shaxslar — hayotni yaxshilash va himoya qilish uchun zukkolikka ega. Birinchilari o'zlarini vaqtincha aldashga bajonidil yo'l qo'yish, balki hatto ba'zan ozgina vajd va ishtiyoqqa ham chidash bilan zaiflik va ayolona xarakterini ko'rsatadi, lekin umuman olganda ular hech qachon qoniqmaydi va noroziliklarining davosizligidan azob chekadi; bundan tashqari, ular afyun va giyohvand tasallilarni tayyorlay oladiganlarning homiylari va aynan shuning uchun shifokorni ruhoniydan yuqori qo'yadiganlarga qarshi, — shu bilan ular haqiqiy qayg'uning davom etishini rag'batlantiradi!

paras.en: If there had not been a surplus of dissatisfied persons of this kind in Europe since the time of the Middle Ages, the remarkable capacity of Europeans for constant transformation would perhaps not have originated at all; for the claims of the strong dissatisfied persons are too gross, and really too modest to resist being finally quieted down. China is an instance of a country in which dissatisfaction on a grand scale and the capacity for transformation have died out for many centuries; and the Socialists and state-idolaters of Europe could easily bring things to Chinese conditions and to a Chinese "happiness," with their measures for the amelioration and security of life, provided that they could first of all root out the sicklier, tenderer, more feminine dissatisfaction and Romanticism which are still very abundant among us.
paras.uz: Agar O'rta asrlardan beri Yevropada bunday norozi odamlarning ortiqchasi bo'lmaganida, yevropaliklarning doimiy o'zgarishga bo'lgan ajoyib qobiliyati, ehtimol, umuman paydo bo'lmagan bo'lardi; chunki kuchli norozi odamlarning talablari haddan tashqari qo'pol va aslida oxir-oqibat tinchlantirilishga qarshi tura olmaydigan darajada kamtar. Xitoy — katta miqyosdagi norozilik va o'zgarish qobiliyati ko'p asrlar davomida so'nib ketgan mamlakatga misol; Yevropa sotsialistlari va davlatga sig'inuvchilari esa hayotni yaxshilash va xavfsizligini ta'minlash choralari bilan ishlarni osongina Xitoy sharoitlariga va Xitoy «baxti»ga olib kelishlari mumkin edi, agar ular avvalo oramizda hali juda ko'p bo'lgan kasalmandroq, nozikroq, ayolonaroq norozilik va romantizmni ildizi bilan sug'urib tashlay olsalar.

paras.en: Europe is an invalid who owes her best thanks to her incurability and the eternal transformations of her sufferings; these constant new situations, these equally constant new dangers, pains, and make-shifts, have at last generated an intellectual sensitiveness which is almost equal to genius, and is in any case the mother of all genius.
paras.uz: Yevropa — o'zining eng katta minnatdorligini davosizligi va azoblarining abadiy o'zgarishlariga qarzdor bo'lgan bemor; bu doimiy yangi vaziyatlar, xuddi shunday doimiy yangi xavflar, og'riqlar va vaqtinchalik choralar oxir-oqibat deyarli dahoga teng bo'lgan va har holda barcha dahoning onasi bo'lgan aqliy sezgirlikni tug'dirgan.

paras.en: 25. Not Pre-ordained to Knowledge. — There is a purblind humility not at all rare, and when a person is afflicted with it, he is once for all unqualified for being a disciple of knowledge. It is this in fact: the moment a man of this kind perceives anything striking, he turns as it were on his heel, and says to himself: "You have deceived yourself! Where have your wits been! This cannot be the truth!"—and then, instead of looking at it and listening to it with more attention, he runs out of the way of the striking object as if intimidated, and seeks to get it out of his head as quickly as possible. For his fundamental rule runs thus: "I want to see nothing that contradicts the usual opinion concerning things! Am I created for the purpose of discovering new truths? There are already too many of the old ones."
paras.uz: 25. Bilimga oldindan tayinlanmagan. — Umuman kam uchramaydigan ko'r kamtarlik bor va odam unga mubtalo bo'lsa, bir yo'la bilim shogirdi bo'lishga yaroqsiz bo'ladi. U aslida shunday: bunday odam biror ajoyib narsani payqashi bilanoq, go'yo tovonida aylanib, o'ziga aytadi: «Sen o'zingni aldading! Aqling qayerda edi! Bu haqiqat bo'lishi mumkin emas!» — va keyin unga ko'proq diqqat bilan qarash va quloq solish o'rniga, go'yo qo'rqib ketgandek, ajoyib narsaning yo'lidan qochib ketadi va uni iloji boricha tezroq boshidan chiqarishga intiladi. Chunki uning asosiy qoidasi shunday: «Men narsalar haqidagi odatiy fikrga zid keladigan hech narsani ko'rishni istamayman! Men yangi haqiqatlarni kashf etish uchun yaratilganmanmi? Eskilari ham allaqachon haddan tashqari ko'p».

paras.en: 26. What is Living?. — Living—that is to continually eliminate from ourselves what is about to die; Living—that is to be cruel and inexorable towards all that becomes weak and old in ourselves, and not only in ourselves. Living—that means, therefore, to be without piety toward the dying, the wretched and the old? To be continually a murderer?—And yet old Moses said: "Thou shalt not kill!"
paras.uz: 26. Yashash nima? — Yashash — bu o'zimizdan o'lishga yaqin qolgan narsani doimo chiqarib tashlash; yashash — bu o'zimizda, va nafaqat o'zimizda, zaif va qari bo'layotgan hamma narsaga nisbatan shafqatsiz va murosasiz bo'lish. Demak, yashash — o'layotganlarga, bechoralarga va qarilarga nisbatan hurmatsiz bo'lish demakmi? Doimo qotil bo'lishmi? — Va shunga qaramay keksa Muso: «Odam o'ldirma!» degan.

paras.en: 27. The Self-Renouncer. — What does the self-renouncer do? He strives after a higher world, he wants to fly longer and further and higher than all men of affirmation—he throws away many things that would burden his flight, and several things among them that are not valueless, that are not unpleasant to him: he sacrifices them to his desire for elevation. Now this sacrificing, this casting away, is the very thing which becomes visible in him: on that account one calls him the self-renouncer, and as such he stands before us, enveloped in his cowl, and as the soul of a hair-shirt. With this effect, however, which he makes upon us he is well content: he wants to keep concealed from us his desire, his pride, his intention of flying above us.—Yes! He is wiser than we thought, and so courteous towards us—this affirmer! For that is what he is, like us, even in his self-renunciation.
paras.uz: 27. O'zidan voz kechuvchi. — O'zidan voz kechuvchi nima qiladi? U oliyroq dunyoga intiladi, u barcha tasdiqlovchi odamlardan ko'ra uzoqroq, nariroq va balandroq uchmoqchi — u parvoziga og'irlik qiladigan ko'p narsalarni tashlab yuboradi, ular orasida qadrsiz bo'lmagan, unga yoqimsiz bo'lmagan bir nechta narsalarni ham: u ularni yuksalish istagi uchun qurbon qiladi. Endi aynan shu qurbon qilish, shu tashlab yuborish unda ko'rinadigan narsa bo'ladi: shuning uchun uni o'zidan voz kechuvchi deb atashadi va u shunday sifatda bizning oldimizda turadi, qalpog'iga o'ralgan va jun ko'ylakning ruhi kabi. Biroq u bizda qoldiradigan bu taassurotdan juda mamnun: u bizdan o'z istagini, g'ururini, bizdan yuqori uchish niyatini yashirmoqchi. — Ha! U biz o'ylaganimizdan donoroq va bizga nisbatan shunchalik xushmuomala — bu tasdiqlovchi! Chunki u aynan shunday, biz kabi, hatto o'zidan voz kechishida ham.

paras.en: 28. Injuring with one's best Qualities. — Our strong points sometimes drive us so far forward that we cannot any longer endure our weaknesses, and we perish by them: we also perhaps see this result beforehand, but nevertheless do not want it to be otherwise. We then become hard towards that which would fain be spared in us, and our pitilessness is also our greatness. Such an experience, which must in the end cost us our life, is a symbol of the collective effect of great men upon others and upon their epoch:—it is just with their best abilities, with that which only they can do, that they destroy much that is weak, uncertain, evolving, and willing, and are thereby injurious. Indeed, the case may happen in which, taken on the whole, they only do injury, because their best is accepted and drunk up as it were solely by those who lose their understanding and their egoism by it, as by too strong a beverage; they become so intoxicated that they go breaking their limbs on all the wrong roads where their drunkenness drives them.
paras.uz: 28. Eng yaxshi xususiyatlari bilan zarar yetkazish. — Kuchli tomonlarimiz ba'zan bizni shunchalik oldinga haydaydiki, biz endi zaif tomonlarimizga chiday olmaymiz va ular tufayli halok bo'lamiz: biz balki bu natijani oldindan ko'ramiz ham, lekin baribir boshqacha bo'lishini istamaymiz. O'shanda biz o'zimizdagi ayalishni istaydigan narsaga nisbatan qattiqqo'l bo'lamiz va shafqatsizligimiz bizning buyukligimiz hamdir. Oxir-oqibat hayotimizga tushishi kerak bo'lgan bunday tajriba buyuk odamlarning boshqalarga va o'z davriga umumiy ta'sirining ramzi: — aynan eng yaxshi qobiliyatlari bilan, faqat ular qila oladigan narsa bilan ular ko'p zaif, noaniq, rivojlanayotgan va xohlayotgan narsalarni vayron qiladi va shu bilan zarar keltiradi. Haqiqatan ham, shunday holat bo'lishi mumkinki, umuman olganda ular faqat zarar keltiradi, chunki ularning eng yaxshisi faqat undan aqli va xudbinligini yo'qotadiganlar tomonidan qabul qilinadi va go'yo ichib yuboriladi, xuddi haddan tashqari kuchli ichimlikdan kabi; ular shunchalik mast bo'lishadiki, mastliklari ularni haydaydigan barcha noto'g'ri yo'llarda oyoq-qo'llarini sindirib yurishadi.

paras.en: 29. Adventitious Liars. — When people began to combat the unity of Aristotle in France, and consequently also to defend it, there was once more to be seen that which has been seen so often, but seen so unwillingly:—people imposed false reasons on themselves on account of which those laws ought to exist, merely for the sake of not acknowledging to themselves that they had accustomed themselves to the authority of those laws, and did not want any longer to have things otherwise. And people do so in every prevailing morality and religion, and have always done so: the reasons and intentions behind the habit, are only added surreptitiously when people begin to combat the habit, and ask for reasons and intentions. It is here that the great dishonesty of the conservatives of all times hides:—they are adventitious liars.
paras.uz: 29. Tasodifiy yolg'onchilar. — Fransiyada Aristotel birligiga qarshi kurasha boshlaganlarida va shuning uchun uni himoya qila boshlaganlarida, yana ko'p marta ko'rilgan, lekin juda istamay ko'rilgan narsani ko'rish mumkin edi: — odamlar o'zlariga o'sha qonunlar nima uchun mavjud bo'lishi kerakligi haqida soxta sabablar o'ylab topishdi, faqat o'zlari o'sha qonunlarning obro'siga o'rganib qolganlarini va endi boshqacha bo'lishini istamasliklarini o'zlariga tan olmaslik uchun. Odamlar har bir hukmron axloq va dinda shunday qilishadi va doimo shunday qilishgan: odat ortidagi sabablar va niyatlar faqat odamlar odatga qarshi kurasha boshlab, sabablar va niyatlarni so'ray boshlaganda yashirincha qo'shiladi. Barcha zamonlar konservatorlarining buyuk nohalolligi shu yerda yashiringan: — ular tasodifiy yolg'onchilar.

paras.en: 30. The Comedy of Celebrated Men. — Celebrated men who need their fame, as, for instance, all politicians, no longer select their associates and friends without after-thoughts: from the one they want a portion of the splendour and reflection of his virtues; from the other they want the fear-inspiring power of certain dubious qualities in him, of which everybody is aware; from another they steal his reputation for idleness and basking in the sun, because it is advantageous for their own ends to be regarded temporarily as heedless and lazy:—it conceals the fact that they lie in ambush; they now use the visionaries, now the experts, now the brooders, now the pedants in their neighbourhood, as their actual selves for the time, but very soon they do not need them any longer!
paras.uz: 30. Mashhur odamlarning komediyasi. — Shon-shuhratiga muhtoj bo'lgan mashhur odamlar, masalan, barcha siyosatchilar, endi o'z hamrohlari va do'stlarini orqa fikrsiz tanlashmaydi: biridan uning fazilatlarining ulug'vorligi va aksidan bir ulush istashadi; boshqasidan undagi hamma biladigan ba'zi shubhali xususiyatlarning qo'rqinch soladigan kuchini istashadi; yana boshqasidan uning dangasalik va quyoshda isinish obro'sini o'g'irlashadi, chunki o'z maqsadlari uchun vaqtincha beparvo va dangasa deb hisoblanish foydali: — bu ularning pistirmada yotganini yashiradi; ular atrofidagi goh xayolparastlardan, goh mutaxassislardan, goh o'ychanlardan, goh mayda-chuyda bilimdonlardan vaqtincha o'zlarining haqiqiy o'zlari sifatida foydalanishadi, lekin tez orada ular endi kerak bo'lmaydi!

paras.en: And thus while their environment and outside die off continually, everything seems to crowd into this environment, and wants to become a "character" of it; they are like great cities in this respect. Their repute is continually in process of mutation, like their character, for their changing methods require this change, and they show and exhibit sometimes this and sometimes that actual or fictitious quality on the stage; their friends and associates, as we have said, belong to these stage properties. On the other hand, that which they aim at must remain so much the more steadfast, and burnished and resplendent in the distance,—and this also sometimes needs its comedy and its stage-play.
paras.uz: Va shunday qilib, atroflari va tashqi qiyofalari doimo so'nib borar ekan, hamma narsa bu atrofga yopirilayotgandek va uning «xarakter»i bo'lmoqchidek ko'rinadi; bu jihatdan ular katta shaharlarga o'xshaydi. Ularning obro'si xarakterlari kabi doimo o'zgarish jarayonida, chunki ularning o'zgaruvchan usullari bu o'zgarishni talab qiladi va ular sahnada goh bu, goh u haqiqiy yoki to'qima xususiyatni ko'rsatib, namoyish qilishadi; aytganimizdek, ularning do'stlari va hamrohlari ana shu sahna jihozlariga tegishli. Boshqa tomondan, ular ko'zlagan narsa shunchalik qat'iyroq, uzoqda sayqallangan va porloq qolishi kerak, — va buning ham ba'zan o'z komediyasi va sahna o'yini kerak bo'ladi.

quiz.q: What is 'corruption' really, according to Nietzsche?
o: The harvest time of a people
quiz.why_uz: Buzilish davrida olmalar — shaxslar daraxtdan tushadi.

quiz.q: Why is Europe called an invalid?
o: It owes its genius to incurable dissatisfaction
quiz.why_uz: Doimiy azob va o'zgarish aqliy sezgirlikni tug'dirgan.

chapters.recap_uz: «Buzilish» davrlari aslida xalqning hosil yig'ish vaqti: shaxslar, zolimlar va Sezarlar paydo bo'ladi. Yevropa — davosiz kasalligi tufayli dahoga ega bo'lgan bemor. Yashash — o'layotgan narsani o'zingdan chiqarib tashlash.

chapters.title: Commerce, heresy and last words

paras.en: 31. Commerce and Nobility. — Buying and selling is now regarded as something ordinary, like the art of reading and writing; everyone is now trained to it even when he is not a tradesman, exercising himself daily in the art; precisely as formerly in the period of uncivilised humanity, everyone was a hunter and exercised himself day by day in the art of hunting. Hunting was then something common: but just as this finally became a privilege of the powerful and noble, and thereby lost the character of the commonplace and the ordinary—by ceasing to be necessary and by becoming an affair of fancy and luxury:—so it might become the same some day with buying and selling.
paras.uz: 31. Savdo va zodagonlik. — Oldi-sotdi endi o'qish va yozish san'ati kabi oddiy narsa hisoblanadi; endi har kim, hatto savdogar bo'lmasa ham, unga o'rgatilgan va har kuni bu san'atda mashq qiladi; xuddi ilgari, insoniyatning madaniyatsiz davrida, har kim ovchi bo'lgani va kunma-kun ov san'atida mashq qilgani kabi. O'shanda ov oddiy narsa edi: lekin xuddi u oxir-oqibat qudratli va zodagonlarning imtiyoziga aylangani va shu bilan oddiylik va odatiylik xarakterini yo'qotgani kabi — zarur bo'lishdan to'xtab, injiqlik va hashamat ishiga aylanib, — bir kun kelib oldi-sotdi bilan ham shunday bo'lishi mumkin.

paras.en: Conditions of society are imaginable in which there will be no selling and buying, and in which the necessity for this art will become quite lost; perhaps it may then happen that individuals who are less subjected to the law of the prevailing condition of things will indulge in buying and selling as a luxury of sentiment. It is then only that commerce would acquire nobility, and the noble would then perhaps occupy themselves just as readily with commerce as they have done hitherto with war and politics: while on the other hand the valuation of politics might then have entirely altered. Already even politics ceases to be the business of a gentleman; and it is possible that one day it may be found to be so vulgar as to be brought, like all party literature and daily literature, under the rubric: "Prostitution of the intellect."
paras.uz: Oldi-sotdi bo'lmaydigan va bu san'atga ehtiyoj butunlay yo'qoladigan jamiyat sharoitlarini tasavvur qilish mumkin; balki o'shanda hukmron narsalar tartibi qonuniga kamroq bo'ysunadigan shaxslar oldi-sotdiga tuyg'u hashamati sifatida berilishar. Faqat o'shandagina savdo zodagonlikka ega bo'lardi va zodagonlar o'shanda, balki, shu paytgacha urush va siyosat bilan shug'ullanganlaridek bajonidil savdo bilan shug'ullanishar: boshqa tomondan esa siyosatning bahosi o'shanda butunlay o'zgargan bo'lishi mumkin. Allaqachon siyosat ham janobning ishi bo'lishdan to'xtamoqda; va bir kun kelib u shunchalik qo'pol deb topilishi mumkinki, barcha partiya adabiyoti va kundalik adabiyot kabi «Aqlning fohishaligi» rukniga kiritiladi.

paras.en: 32. Undesirable Disciples. — What shall I do with these two youths! called out a philosopher dejectedly, who "corrupted" youths, as Socrates had once corrupted them,—they are unwelcome disciples to me. One of them cannot say "Nay," and the other says "Half and half" to everything. Provided they grasped my doctrine, the former would suffer too much, for my mode of thinking requires a martial soul, willingness to cause pain, delight in denying, and a hard skin,—he would succumb by open wounds and internal injuries. And the other will choose the mediocre in everything he represents, and thus make a mediocrity of the whole,—I should like my enemy to have such a disciple.
paras.uz: 32. Nomaqbul shogirdlar. — Bu ikki yigit bilan nima qilay! — deb tushkun qichqirdi bir faylasuf, u yigitlarni bir paytlar Sokrat ularni «buzgani» kabi «buzardi», — ular menga nomaqbul shogirdlar. Ulardan biri «Yo'q» deya olmaydi, ikkinchisi esa hamma narsaga «Yarim-yarti» deydi. Agar ular ta'limotimni tushunishsa, birinchisi haddan tashqari ko'p azob chekardi, chunki mening fikrlash tarzim jangovar ruhni, og'riq berishga tayyorlikni, inkor etishdan zavqlanishni va qalin terini talab qiladi, — u ochiq yaralar va ichki shikastlardan halok bo'lardi. Ikkinchisi esa o'zi ifodalaydigan hamma narsada o'rtamiyonani tanlaydi va shu tariqa butun narsani o'rtamiyonalikka aylantiradi, — dushmanimning shunday shogirdi bo'lishini istardim.

paras.en: 33. Outside the Lecture-room. — "In order to prove that man after all belongs to the good-natured animals, I would remind you how credulous he has been for so long a time. It is now only, quite late, and after an immense self-conquest, that he has become a distrustful animal,—yes! man is now more wicked than ever."—I do not understand this; why should man now be more distrustful and more wicked?—"Because he now has science,—because he needs to have it!"—
paras.uz: 33. Ma'ruza zalidan tashqarida. — «Inson oxir-oqibat mehribon hayvonlarga tegishli ekanini isbotlash uchun sizga u qancha uzoq vaqt qanchalik ishonuvchan bo'lganini eslatgan bo'lardim. Faqat endigina, juda kech va ulkan o'zini yengishdan keyin u ishonchsiz hayvonga aylandi, — ha! inson endi har qachongidan yovuzroq». — Men buni tushunmayman; nega inson endi ishonchsizroq va yovuzroq bo'lishi kerak? — «Chunki endi unda ilm bor, — chunki unga u kerak!» —

paras.en: 34. Historia abscondita. — Every great man has a power which operates backward; all history is again placed on the scales on his account, and a thousand secrets of the past crawl out of their lurking-places—into his sunlight. There is absolutely no knowing what history may be some day. The past is still perhaps undiscovered in its essence! There are yet so many retroactive powers needed!
paras.uz: 34. Historia abscondita — Yashirin tarix. — Har bir buyuk odamda orqaga ta'sir qiladigan kuch bor; uning tufayli butun tarix yana tarozi pallasiga qo'yiladi va o'tmishning ming siri o'z yashirin joylaridan — uning quyosh nuriga o'rmalab chiqadi. Tarix bir kun kelib nima bo'lishini mutlaqo bilib bo'lmaydi. O'tmish mohiyatan, ehtimol, hali kashf etilmagandir! Yana shunchalik ko'p orqaga ta'sir qiluvchi kuchlar kerak!

paras.en: 35. Heresy and Witchcraft. — To think otherwise than is customary—that is by no means so much the activity of a better intellect, as the activity of strong, wicked inclinations,—severing, isolating, refractory, mischief-loving, malicious inclinations. Heresy is the counterpart of witchcraft, and is certainly just as little a merely harmless affair, or a thing worthy of honour in itself. Heretics and sorcerers are two kinds of bad men; they have it in common that they also feel themselves wicked; their unconquerable delight is to attack and injure whatever rules,—whether it be men or opinions. The Reformation, a kind of duplication of the spirit of the Middle Ages at a time when it had no longer a good conscience, produced both of these kinds of people in the greatest profusion.
paras.uz: 35. Bid'at va jodugarlik. — Odatdagidan boshqacha o'ylash — bu aslo yaxshiroq aqlning faoliyati emas, balki kuchli, yovuz moyilliklarning — ajratuvchi, yolg'izlatuvchi, qaysar, yomonlikni sevuvchi, g'arazli moyilliklarning faoliyatidir. Bid'at — jodugarlikning aksi va albatta xuddi shunday kam zararsiz ish yoki o'z-o'zidan hurmatga loyiq narsadir. Bid'atchilar va sehrgarlar — yomon odamlarning ikki turi; ularning umumiy jihati shundaki, ular ham o'zlarini yovuz his qilishadi; ularning yengib bo'lmas zavqi — hukmronlik qilayotgan narsaga, xoh odamlar, xoh fikrlar bo'lsin, hujum qilish va zarar yetkazish. Islohot, O'rta asrlar ruhining endi vijdoni toza bo'lmagan paytdagi bir xil takrori, bu ikki turdagi odamlarni eng ko'p miqdorda yetishtirdi.

paras.en: 36. Last Words. — It will be recollected that the Emperor Augustus, that terrible man, who had himself as much in his own power, and who could be silent as well as any wise Socrates, became indiscreet about himself in his last words; for the first time he let his mask fall, when he gave to understand that he had carried a mask and played a comedy,—he had played the father of his country and wisdom on the throne well, even to the point of illusion! Plaudite amici, comoedia finita est!—The thought of the dying Nero: qualis artifex pereo! was also the thought of the dying Augustus: histrionic conceit! histrionic loquacity! And the very counterpart to the dying Socrates!—But Tiberius died silently, that most tortured of all self-torturers,—he was genuine and not a stage-player! What may have passed through his head in the end! Perhaps this: "Life—that is a long death.
paras.uz: 36. So'nggi so'zlar. — Esingizda bo'lsa, o'zini shunchalik qo'lda tutgan va har qanday dono Sokrat kabi jim tura oladigan o'sha dahshatli odam imperator Avgust so'nggi so'zlarida o'zi haqida ehtiyotsizlik qildi; u birinchi marta niqobini tushirdi, niqob kiyib, komediya o'ynaganini tushuntirganda, — u taxtda vatan otasi va donolikni yaxshi, hatto xayol darajasigacha o'ynagan edi! Plaudite amici, comoedia finita est! — Qarsak chalinglar, do'stlar, komediya tugadi! — O'layotgan Neronning fikri: qualis artifex pereo! — qanday san'atkor halok bo'lmoqda! — o'layotgan Avgustning ham fikri edi: aktyorona takabburlik! aktyorona ezmalik! Va o'layotgan Sokratning aynan aksi! — Lekin Tiberiy jimgina o'ldi, barcha o'zini qiynovchilarning eng qiynalgani, — u haqiqiy edi, aktyor emas! Oxirida uning boshidan nimalar o'tgan bo'lishi mumkin! Balki shudir: «Hayot — bu uzoq o'lim.

paras.en: I am a fool, who shortened the lives of so many! Was I created for the purpose of being a benefactor? I should have given them eternal life: and then I could have seen them dying eternally. I had such good eyes for that: qualis spectator pereo!" When he seemed once more to regain his powers after a long death-struggle, it was considered advisable to smother him with pillows,—he died a double death.
paras.uz: Men ahmoqman, shuncha odamning umrini qisqartirdim! Men xayrixoh bo'lish uchun yaratilganmidim? Ularga abadiy hayot berishim kerak edi: shunda men ularning abadiy o'layotganini ko'ra olardim. Mening bunga shunday yaxshi ko'zlarim bor edi: qualis spectator pereo! — qanday tomoshabin halok bo'lmoqda!» Uzoq jon talashishdan keyin u yana kuchini tiklayotgandek ko'ringanida, uni yostiqlar bilan bo'g'ish maqsadga muvofiq deb topildi, — u ikki karra o'lim bilan o'ldi.

paras.en: 37. Owing to three Errors. — Science has been furthered during recent centuries, partly because it was hoped that God's goodness and wisdom would be best understood therewith and thereby—the principal motive in the soul of great Englishmen (like Newton); partly because the absolute utility of knowledge was believed in, and especially the most intimate connection of morality, knowledge, and happiness—the principal motive in the soul of great Frenchmen (like Voltaire); and partly because it was thought that in science there was something unselfish, harmless, self-sufficing, lovable, and truly innocent to be had, in which the evil human impulses did not at all participate—the principal motive in the soul of Spinoza, who felt himself divine, as a knowing being:—it is consequently owing to three errors that science has been furthered.
paras.uz: 37. Uch xato tufayli. — So'nggi asrlarda ilm rivojlantirildi, qisman chunki u bilan va u orqali Xudoning yaxshiligi va donoligi eng yaxshi tushuniladi deb umid qilingan — buyuk inglizlar (Nyuton kabi) qalbidagi asosiy motiv; qisman chunki bilimning mutlaq foydaliligiga, ayniqsa axloq, bilim va baxtning eng yaqin bog'liqligiga ishonilgan — buyuk fransuzlar (Volter kabi) qalbidagi asosiy motiv; va qisman chunki ilmda fidoyi, zararsiz, o'zi-o'ziga yetarli, sevimli va chinakam beg'ubor, yovuz inson mayllari umuman ishtirok etmaydigan nimadir topish mumkin deb o'ylangan — o'zini bilim egasi sifatida ilohiy his qilgan Spinoza qalbidagi asosiy motiv: — demak, ilm uch xato tufayli rivojlantirilgan.

paras.en: 38. Explosive People. — When one considers how ready are the forces of young men for discharge, one does not wonder at seeing them decide so unfastidiously and with so little selection for this or that cause: that which attracts them is the sight of eagerness about any cause, as it were the sight of the burning match—not the cause itself. The more ingenious seducers on that account operate by holding out the prospect of an explosion to such persons, and do not urge their cause by means of reasons; these powder-barrels are not won over by means of reasons!
paras.uz: 38. Portlovchi odamlar. — Yigitlarning kuchlari otilib chiqishga qanchalik tayyor ekanini o'ylaganda, ularning u yoki bu ish uchun shunchalik injiqlanmay va shunchalik oz tanlab qaror qilishlariga hayron bo'lmaysan: ularni jalb qiladigan narsa — biror ish atrofidagi ishtiyoqni ko'rish, go'yo yonayotgan gugurtni ko'rish — ishning o'zi emas. Shuning uchun mohirroq yo'ldan uruvchilar bunday odamlarga portlash istiqbolini ko'rsatish orqali harakat qilishadi va o'z ishlarini dalillar bilan targ'ib qilishmaydi; bu porox bochkalarini dalillar bilan qozonib bo'lmaydi!

paras.en: 39. Altered Taste. — The alteration of the general taste is more important than the alteration of opinions; opinions, with all their proving, refuting, and intellectual masquerade, are merely symptoms of altered taste, and are certainly not what they are still so often claimed to be, the causes of the altered taste. How does the general taste alter? By the fact of individuals, the powerful and influential persons, expressing and tyrannically enforcing without any feeling of shame, their hoc est ridiculum, hoc est absurdum; the decisions, therefore, of their taste and their disrelish:—they thereby lay a constraint upon many people, out of which there gradually grows a habituation for still more, and finally a necessity for all. The fact, however, that these individuals feel and "taste" differently, has usually its origin in a peculiarity of their mode of life, nourishment, or digestion, perhaps in a surplus or deficiency of the inorganic salts in their blood and brain, in short in their physis; they have, however, the courage to avow their physical constitution, and to lend an ear even to the most delicate tones of its requirements: their æsthetic and moral judgments are those "most delicate tones" of their physis.
paras.uz: 39. O'zgargan did. — Umumiy didning o'zgarishi fikrlarning o'zgarishidan muhimroq; fikrlar barcha isbotlashlari, rad etishlari va aqliy maskaradlari bilan shunchaki o'zgargan didning alomatlari, va albatta ular hali ko'pincha da'vo qilinganidek o'zgargan didning sabablari emas. Umumiy did qanday o'zgaradi? Shaxslar, qudratli va ta'sirli odamlar hech qanday uyat tuyg'usisiz o'zlarining hoc est ridiculum, hoc est absurdum — bu kulgili, bu bema'ni — degan hukmlarini, ya'ni didlari va jirkanishlari qarorlarini ifodalab, zolimlarcha majburlashlari orqali: — shu bilan ular ko'p odamlarga majburlov yuklaydi, undan asta-sekin yana ham ko'proq odamlar uchun odat va oxir-oqibat hamma uchun zarurat o'sib chiqadi. Biroq bu shaxslar boshqacha his qilishi va «tatishi» odatda ularning turmush tarzi, ovqatlanishi yoki hazmidagi o'ziga xoslikdan, balki qon va miyalaridagi noorganik tuzlarning ortiqchaligi yoki yetishmasligidan, qisqasi, ularning fizisidan kelib chiqadi; biroq ularda o'z jismoniy tuzilishini tan olish va hatto uning ehtiyojlarining eng nozik ohanglariga quloq solish jasorati bor: ularning estetik va axloqiy hukmlari fizisining ana shu «eng nozik ohanglari»dir.

paras.en: 40. The Lack of a noble Presence. — Soldiers and their leaders have always a much higher mode of comportment toward one another than workmen and their employers. At present at least, all militarily established civilisation still stands high above all so-called industrial civilisation; the latter, in its present form, is in general the meanest mode of existence that has ever been. It is simply the law of necessity that operates here: people want to live, and have to sell themselves; but they despise him who exploits their necessity, and purchases the workman.
paras.uz: 40. Olijanob qiyofaning yo'qligi. — Askarlar va ularning boshliqlari bir-biriga nisbatan doimo ishchilar va ularning ish beruvchilariga qaraganda ancha yuksakroq munosabatda bo'lishadi. Hech bo'lmasa hozircha harbiy asosda qurilgan har qanday tsivilizatsiya hali ham industrial deb ataladigan har qanday tsivilizatsiyadan ancha yuqori turadi; ikkinchisi hozirgi shaklida umuman olganda shu paytgacha bo'lgan eng pastkash yashash tarzidir. Bu yerda shunchaki zarurat qonuni amal qiladi: odamlar yashashni istaydi va o'zlarini sotishga majbur; lekin ular zaruratidan foydalanib, ishchini sotib oladigan odamni mensimaydi.

paras.en: It is curious that the subjection to powerful, fear-inspiring, and even dreadful individuals, to tyrants and leaders of armies, is not at all felt so painfully as the subjection to such undistinguished and uninteresting persons as the captains of industry; in the employer the workman usually sees merely a crafty, blood-sucking dog of a man, speculating on every necessity, whose name, form, character, and reputation are altogether indifferent to him. It is probable that the manufacturers and great magnates of commerce have hitherto lacked too much all those forms and attributes of a superior race, which alone make persons interesting; if they had had the nobility of the nobly-born in their looks and bearing, there would perhaps have been no socialism in the masses of the people.
paras.uz: Qizig'i shundaki, qudratli, qo'rquv soladigan va hatto dahshatli shaxslarga, zolimlar va qo'shin boshliqlariga bo'ysunish sanoat sardorlari kabi ko'zga tashlanmaydigan va qiziqarsiz shaxslarga bo'ysunish kabi og'riqli his qilinmaydi; ish beruvchida ishchi odatda shunchaki har bir zaruratdan foydalanib chayqovchilik qiladigan, ismi, qiyofasi, xarakteri va obro'si unga butunlay befarq bo'lgan ayyor, qonxo'r it odamni ko'radi. Ehtimol, fabrikantlar va savdoning buyuk magnatlarida shu paytgacha shaxslarni qiziqarli qiladigan oliy zotning barcha shakl va sifatlari haddan tashqari yetishmagan; agar ularning qiyofasi va xatti-harakatida olijanob tug'ilganlarning zodagonligi bo'lganida, balki xalq ommasida sotsializm bo'lmasdi.

paras.en: For these are really ready for slavery of every kind, provided that the superior class above them constantly shows itself legitimately superior, and born to command—by its noble presence! The commonest man feels that nobility is not to be improvised, and that it is his part to honour it as the fruit of protracted race-culture,—but the absence of superior presence, and the notorious vulgarity of manufacturers with red, fat hands, brings up the thought to him that it is only chance and fortune that has here elevated the one above the other; well then—so he reasons with himself—let us in our turn tempt chance and fortune! Let us in our turn throw the dice!—and socialism commences.
paras.uz: Chunki ular aslida har qanday qullikka tayyor, faqat ularning ustidagi oliy tabaqa o'zini doimo qonuniy ravishda oliy va buyurish uchun tug'ilgan ekanini ko'rsatib tursa — olijanob qiyofasi bilan! Eng oddiy odam ham zodagonlikni bado'ha qilib bo'lmasligini va uni uzoq zot tarbiyasining mevasi sifatida hurmat qilish o'zining burchi ekanini his qiladi, — lekin oliy qiyofaning yo'qligi va qizil, semiz qo'lli fabrikantlarning hammaga ma'lum qo'polligi unda bu yerda birini boshqasidan yuqori ko'targan narsa faqat tasodif va omad degan fikrni uyg'otadi; unday bo'lsa — deb o'zi bilan mulohaza qiladi u — endi biz ham navbatimiz bilan tasodif va omadni sinab ko'raylik! Endi biz ham navbatimiz bilan zar tashlaylik! — va sotsializm boshlanadi.

paras.en: 41. Against Remorse. — The thinker sees in his own actions attempts and questionings to obtain information about something or other; success and failure are answers to him first and foremost. To vex himself, however, because something does not succeed, or to feel remorse at all—he leaves that to those who act because they are commanded to do so, and expect to get a beating when their gracious master is not satisfied with the result.
paras.uz: 41. Pushaymonlikka qarshi. — Mutafakkir o'z harakatlarida nima haqidadir ma'lumot olish uchun urinishlar va so'rovlarni ko'radi; muvaffaqiyat va muvaffaqiyatsizlik — uning uchun eng avvalo javoblar. Biroq biror narsa muvaffaqiyatli bo'lmagani uchun o'zini qiynash yoki umuman pushaymon bo'lish — buni u buyurilgani uchun harakat qiladigan va mehribon xo'jayinlari natijadan mamnun bo'lmasa kaltak yeyishni kutadiganlarga qoldiradi.

paras.en: 42. Work and Ennui. — In respect to seeking work for the sake of the pay, almost all men are alike at present in civilised countries; to all of them work is a means, and not itself the end; on which account they are not very select in the choice of the work, provided it yields an abundant profit. But still there are rarer men who would rather perish than work without delight in their labour: the fastidious people, difficult to satisfy, whose object is not served by an abundant profit, unless the work itself be the reward of all rewards. Artists and contemplative men of all kinds belong to this rare species of human beings; and also the idlers who spend their life in hunting and travelling, or in love affairs and adventures.
paras.uz: 42. Ish va zerikish. — Maosh uchun ish izlash borasida hozir madaniyatli mamlakatlarda deyarli barcha odamlar bir xil; ularning hammasi uchun ish vosita, maqsadning o'zi emas; shuning uchun ular ish tanlashda unchalik injiq emas, faqat u mo'l foyda keltirsa bas. Lekin hali ham mehnatidan zavq olmay ishlashdan ko'ra halok bo'lishni afzal ko'radigan kamyob odamlar bor: injiq, qoniqtirish qiyin odamlar, agar ishning o'zi barcha mukofotlarning mukofoti bo'lmasa, mo'l foyda ularning maqsadiga xizmat qilmaydi. Barcha turdagi san'atkorlar va mulohazakor odamlar insonlarning shu kamyob turiga kiradi; shuningdek, hayotini ov va sayohatda yoki ishqiy munosabatlar va sarguzashtlarda o'tkazadigan bekorchilar ham.

paras.en: They all seek toil and trouble in so far as these are associated with pleasure, and they want the severest and hardest labour, if it be necessary. In other respects, however, they have a resolute indolence, even should impoverishment, dishonour, and danger to health and life be associated therewith. They are not so much afraid of ennui as of labour without pleasure; indeed they require much ennui, if their work is to succeed with them. For the thinker and for all inventive spirits ennui is the unpleasant "calm" of the soul which precedes the happy voyage and the dancing breezes; he must endure it, he must await the effect it has on him:—it is precisely this which lesser natures cannot at all experience! It is common to scare away ennui in every way, just as it is common to labour without pleasure. It perhaps distinguishes the Asiatics above the Europeans, that they are capable of a longer and profounder repose; even their narcotics operate slowly and require patience, in contrast to the obnoxious suddenness of the European poison, alcohol.
paras.uz: Ularning hammasi mehnat va mashaqqatni lazzat bilan bog'liq bo'lgan darajada izlaydi va agar kerak bo'lsa, eng og'ir va eng qattiq mehnatni istaydi. Biroq boshqa jihatlarda ularda qat'iy dangasalik bor, hatto bunga qashshoqlik, sharmandalik va sog'liq va hayot uchun xavf bog'liq bo'lsa ham. Ular zerikishdan ko'ra lazzatsiz mehnatdan qo'rqishadi; haqiqatan ham, agar ishlari muvaffaqiyatli bo'lishi kerak bo'lsa, ularga ko'p zerikish kerak. Mutafakkir va barcha ixtirochi ruhlar uchun zerikish — baxtli sayohat va raqsga tushayotgan shabadalardan oldingi ruhning yoqimsiz «shtil»i; u unga chidashi, uning o'ziga ta'sirini kutishi kerak: — aynan buni kichikroq tabiatlar umuman boshdan kechira olmaydi! Zerikishni har qanday yo'l bilan quvib chiqarish odatiy, xuddi lazzatsiz mehnat qilish odatiy bo'lgani kabi. Balki osiyoliklarni yevropaliklardan ustun qiladigan narsa shuki, ular uzoqroq va chuqurroq osoyishtalikka qodir; hatto ularning giyohvand moddalari ham sekin ta'sir qiladi va sabr talab qiladi, Yevropa zahri — alkogolning jirkanch to'satdanligidan farqli ravishda.

paras.en: 43. What the Laws Betray. — One makes a great mistake when one studies the penal laws of a people, as if they were an expression of its character; the laws do not betray what a people is, but what appears to them foreign, strange, monstrous, and outlandish. The laws concern themselves with the exceptions to the morality of custom; and the severest punishments fall on acts which conform to the customs of the neighbouring peoples. Thus among the Wahabites, there are only two mortal sins: having another God than the Wahabite God, and—smoking (it is designated by them as "the disgraceful kind of drinking"). "And how is it with regard to murder and adultery?"—asked the Englishman with astonishment on learning these things.
paras.uz: 43. Qonunlar nimani oshkor qiladi. — Xalqning jinoyat qonunlarini go'yo ular uning xarakterining ifodasidek o'rganish katta xato; qonunlar xalq nima ekanini emas, balki unga nima begona, g'alati, dahshatli va yot ko'rinishini oshkor qiladi. Qonunlar urf-odat axloqidan istisnolar bilan shug'ullanadi; va eng og'ir jazolar qo'shni xalqlarning urf-odatlariga mos keladigan harakatlarga tushadi. Masalan, vahhobiylarda faqat ikkita o'limga loyiq gunoh bor: vahhobiy Xudosidan boshqa Xudoga ega bo'lish va — chekish (ular uni «ichishning sharmandali turi» deb atashadi). «Qotillik va zino haqida-chi?» — deb so'radi hayron bo'lgan ingliz bularni bilib olgach.

paras.en: "Well, God is gracious and pitiful!" answered the old chief.—Thus among the ancient Romans there was the idea that a woman could only sin mortally in two ways: by adultery on the one hand, and—by wine-drinking on the other. Old Cato pretended that kissing among relatives had only been made a custom in order to keep women in control on this point; a kiss meant: did her breath smell of wine?
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, Xudo mehribon va rahmli!» — deb javob berdi keksa boshliq. — Xuddi shunday, qadimgi rimliklarda ayol faqat ikki yo'l bilan o'limga loyiq gunoh qilishi mumkin degan g'oya bor edi: bir tomondan zino, boshqa tomondan esa — sharob ichish. Keksa Katon qarindoshlar orasida o'pishish faqat ayollarni shu jihatdan nazorat ostida tutish uchun odat qilingan deb da'vo qilgan; o'pich shuni anglatardi: uning nafasidan sharob hidi keladimi?

paras.en: Wives had actually been punished by death who were surprised taking wine: and certainly not merely because women under the influence of wine sometimes unlearn altogether the art of saying No; the Romans were afraid above all things of the orgiastic and Dionysian spirit with which the women of Southern Europe at that time (when wine was still new in Europe) were sometimes visited, as by a monstrous foreignness which subverted the basis of Roman sentiments; it seemed to them treason against Rome, as the embodiment of foreignness.
paras.uz: Sharob ichayotganda qo'lga tushgan xotinlar haqiqatan ham o'lim bilan jazolangan: va albatta faqat sharob ta'sirida ayollar ba'zan «Yo'q» deyish san'atini butunlay unutib qo'yishlari uchun emas; rimliklar eng ko'p o'sha paytda (sharob Yevropada hali yangi bo'lgan paytda) Janubiy Yevropa ayollariga ba'zan Rim tuyg'ularining asosini ag'daradigan dahshatli yotlik kabi kelib turgan orgiastik va Dionisiy ruhdan qo'rqishgan; bu ularga yotlikning timsoli sifatida Rimga xiyonat bo'lib tuyulgan.
