quiz.q: What were Augustus's last words about?
o: Life as a comedy he had played
quiz.why_uz: «Qarsak chalinglar, do'stlar, komediya tugadi!»

quiz.q: What does the thinker think about ennui?
o: It is the calm before a happy voyage
quiz.why_uz: Zerikish ijodkor ruh uchun zarur «shtil».

chapters.recap_uz: Nitsshe savdo bir kun zodagonlarning hashamatiga aylanishini tasavvur qiladi. Bid'at va jodugarlik yovuz mayllardan kelib chiqadi. Imperatorlarning so'nggi so'zlari, ilmni rivojlantirgan uch xato va ish bilan zerikish haqida yozadi.

chapters.title: Epicurus and the knowledge of pain

paras.en: 44. The Believed Motive. — However important it may be to know the motives according to which mankind has really acted hitherto, perhaps the belief in this or that motive, and therefore that which mankind has assumed and imagined to be the actual mainspring of its activity hitherto, is something still more essential for the thinker to know. For the internal happiness and misery of men have always come to them through their belief in this or that motive,—not however, through that which was actually the motive! All about the latter has an interest of secondary rank.
paras.uz: 44. Ishonilgan motiv. — Insoniyat shu paytgacha haqiqatda qaysi motivlarga ko'ra harakat qilganini bilish qanchalik muhim bo'lmasin, balki u yoki bu motivga bo'lgan ishonch, ya'ni insoniyat shu paytgacha o'z faoliyatining haqiqiy harakatlantiruvchi kuchi deb faraz qilgan va tasavvur qilgan narsani bilish mutafakkir uchun yana ham muhimroqdir. Chunki odamlarning ichki baxti va baxtsizligi doimo ularga u yoki bu motivga bo'lgan ishonchi orqali kelgan, — lekin haqiqatda motiv bo'lgan narsa orqali emas! Ikkinchisi haqidagi hamma narsa ikkinchi darajali qiziqishga ega.

paras.en: 45. Epicurus. — Yes, I am proud of perceiving the character of Epicurus differently from anyone else perhaps, and of enjoying the happiness of the afternoon of antiquity in all that I hear and read of him:—I see his eye gazing out on a broad whitish sea, over the shore-rocks on which the sunshine rests, while great and small creatures play in its light, secure and calm like this light and that eye itself. Such happiness could only have been devised by a chronic sufferer, the happiness of an eye before which the sea of existence has become calm, and which can no longer tire of gazing at the surface and at the variegated, tender, tremulous skin of this sea. Never previously was there such a moderation of voluptuousness.
paras.uz: 45. Epikur. — Ha, men Epikurning xarakterini, ehtimol, boshqa hammadan boshqacha his qilishimdan va u haqida eshitgan va o'qigan hamma narsamda antik davr tushdan keyingi baxtidan zavqlanishimdan faxrlanaman: — men uning ko'zini keng, oqish dengizga, quyosh nuri yotgan qirg'oq qoyalari osha tikilib turganini ko'raman, bu nurda katta-kichik jonzotlar o'ynaydi, xuddi shu nur va o'sha ko'zning o'zidek xotirjam va osoyishta. Bunday baxtni faqat surunkali azob chekuvchigina o'ylab topa olardi, oldida hayot dengizi tinchlangan va bu dengizning yuzasiga va rang-barang, nozik, titroq terisiga tikilishdan endi charchay olmaydigan ko'zning baxti. Ilgari hech qachon rohatning bunday mo'tadilligi bo'lmagan.

paras.en: 46. Our Astonishment. — There is a profound and fundamental satisfaction in the fact that science ascertains things that hold their ground, and again furnish the basis for new researches:—it could certainly be otherwise. Indeed, we are so much convinced of all the uncertainty and caprice of our judgments, and of the everlasting change of all human laws and conceptions, that we are really astonished how persistently the results of science hold their ground! In earlier times people knew nothing of this changeability of all human things; the custom of morality maintained the belief that the whole inner life of man was bound to iron necessity by eternal fetters:—perhaps people then felt a similar voluptuousness of astonishment when they listened to tales and fairy stories. The wonderful did so much good to those men, who might well get tired sometimes of the regular and the eternal. To leave the ground for once! To soar! To stray! To be mad!—that belonged to the paradise and the revelry of earlier times; while our felicity is like that of the shipwrecked man who has gone ashore, and places himself with both feet on the old, firm ground—in astonishment that it does not rock.
paras.uz: 46. Bizning hayratimiz. — Ilm o'z o'rnida turadigan va yana yangi tadqiqotlar uchun asos beradigan narsalarni aniqlashida chuqur va tubdan qoniqish bor: — albatta, boshqacha bo'lishi ham mumkin edi. Haqiqatan ham, biz hukmlarimizning barcha noaniqligi va injiqligiga, barcha inson qonunlari va tushunchalarining abadiy o'zgarishiga shunchalik aminmizki, ilm natijalari qanchalik qat'iy o'z o'rnida turishidan haqiqatan ham hayron qolamiz! Ilgarigi zamonlarda odamlar barcha inson narsalarining bu o'zgaruvchanligi haqida hech narsa bilishmagan; axloq odati insonning butun ichki hayoti abadiy kishanlar bilan temir zaruratga bog'langan degan ishonchni saqlab turgan: — balki odamlar o'shanda ertak va afsonalarni tinglaganlarida hayratning shunga o'xshash rohatini his qilishgandir. Ajoyib narsa muntazamlik va abadiylikdan ba'zan charchashi mumkin bo'lgan o'sha odamlarga shunchalik foyda bergan. Bir marta yerdan uzilish! Parvoz qilish! Adashib yurish! Telba bo'lish! — bu ilgarigi zamonlarning jannati va bazmiga tegishli edi; bizning saodatimiz esa qirg'oqqa chiqqan va ikkala oyog'i bilan eski, mustahkam yerga turgan kema halokatiga uchragan odamning saodatiga o'xshaydi — u chayqalmayotganidan hayratda.

paras.en: 47. The Suppression of the Passions. — When one continually prohibits the expression of the passions as something to be left to the "vulgar," to coarser, bourgeois, and peasant natures—that is, when one does not want to suppress the passions themselves, but only their language and demeanour, one nevertheless realises therewith just what one does not want: the suppression of the passions themselves, or at least their weakening and alteration,—as the court of Louis XIV. (to cite the most instructive instance), and all that was dependent on it, experienced. The generation that followed, trained in suppressing their expression, no longer possessed the passions themselves, but had a pleasant, superficial, playful disposition in their place,—a generation which was so permeated with the incapacity to be ill-mannered, that even an injury was not taken and retaliated, except with courteous words. Perhaps our own time furnishes the most remarkable counterpart to this period:
paras.uz: 47. Ehtiroslarni bostirish. — Ehtiroslarni ifodalashni doimo «oddiy xalq»ga, qo'polroq, burjua va dehqon tabiatlarga qoldirilishi kerak bo'lgan narsa sifatida taqiqlaganda — ya'ni ehtiroslarning o'zini emas, faqat ularning tili va xatti-harakatini bostirmoqchi bo'lganda, baribir aynan istamagan narsani amalga oshirasan: ehtiroslarning o'zini bostirish, yoki hech bo'lmasa ularni zaiflashtirish va o'zgartirish, — Lyudovik XIV saroyi (eng ibratli misolni keltirsak) va unga qaram bo'lgan hamma narsa buni boshdan kechirgan. Ularning ifodasini bostirishga o'rgatilgan keyingi avlodda endi ehtiroslarning o'zi yo'q edi, balki ularning o'rnida yoqimli, yuzaki, o'yinqaroq fe'l bor edi, — odobsiz bo'lishga qodir emaslik bilan shunchalik sug'orilgan avlodki, hatto haqoratni ham xushmuomala so'zlardan boshqacha qabul qilmas va javob qaytarmasdi. Balki bizning davrimiz bu davrning eng ajoyib aksini beradi:

paras.en: I see everywhere (in life, in the theatre, and not least in all that is written) satisfaction at all the coarser outbursts and gestures of passion; a certain convention of passionateness is now desired,—only not the passion itself! Nevertheless it will thereby be at last reached, and our posterity will have a genuine savagery, and not merely a formal savagery and unmannerliness.
paras.uz: Men hamma joyda (hayotda, teatrda va yozilgan hamma narsada oz emas) ehtirosning har qanday qo'polroq otilishlari va imo-ishoralaridan mamnunlikni ko'raman; endi ehtiroslilikning ma'lum bir konvensiyasi istaladi, — faqat ehtirosning o'zi emas! Shunga qaramay, u shu bilan oxir-oqibat erishiladi va avlodlarimizda shunchaki rasmiy vahshiylik va odobsizlik emas, haqiqiy vahshiylik bo'ladi.

paras.en: 48. Knowledge of Distress. — Perhaps there is nothing by which men and periods are so much separated from one another, as by the different degrees of knowledge of distress which they possess; distress of the soul as well as of the body. With respect to the latter, owing to lack of sufficient self-experience, we men of the present day (in spite of our deficiencies and infirmities), are perhaps all of us blunderers and visionaries in comparison with the men of the age of fear—the longest of all ages,—when the individual had to protect himself against violence, and for that purpose had to be a man of violence himself.
paras.uz: 48. Qayg'uni bilish. — Balki odamlar va davrlarni bir-biridan ular ega bo'lgan qayg'uni bilishning turli darajalari kabi hech narsa ajratmaydi; ruh qayg'usi ham, tana qayg'usi ham. Ikkinchisiga kelsak, o'z tajribamiz yetarli bo'lmagani tufayli, biz hozirgi zamon odamlari (kamchilik va zaifliklarimizga qaramay), ehtimol, qo'rquv davri — barcha davrlarning eng uzuni — odamlari bilan solishtirganda hammamiz bo'shang va xayolparastmiz; o'shanda shaxs o'zini zo'ravonlikdan himoya qilishi kerak edi va buning uchun o'zi zo'ravon odam bo'lishi kerak edi.

paras.en: At that time a man went through a long schooling of corporeal tortures and privations, and found even in a certain kind of cruelty toward himself, in a voluntary use of pain, a necessary means for his preservation; at that time a person trained his environment to the endurance of pain; at that time a person willingly inflicted pain, and saw the most frightful things of this kind happen to others, without having any other feeling than for his own security.
paras.uz: O'shanda inson jismoniy qiynoqlar va mahrumliklarning uzoq maktabidan o'tardi va hatto o'ziga nisbatan qandaydir shafqatsizlikda, og'riqni ixtiyoriy qo'llashda o'zini saqlashning zarur vositasini topardi; o'shanda odam atrofidagilarni og'riqqa chidashga o'rgatardi; o'shanda odam bajonidil og'riq berardi va bunday narsalarning eng dahshatlilarini boshqalarga sodir bo'layotganini ko'rardi, o'z xavfsizligi tuyg'usidan boshqa hech qanday tuyg'usiz.

paras.en: As regards the distress of the soul, however, I now look at every man with respect to whether he knows it by experience or by description; whether he still regards it as necessary to simulate this knowledge, perhaps as an indication of more refined culture; or whether, at the bottom of his heart, he does not at all believe in great sorrows of soul, and at the naming of them has in his mind a similar experience as at the naming of great corporeal sufferings, such as tooth-aches, and stomach-aches. It is thus, however, that it seems to be with most people at present.
paras.uz: Biroq ruh qayg'usiga kelsak, men endi har bir odamga u uni tajribadan biladimi yoki tasvirdanmi, degan nuqtai nazardan qarayman; u hali ham bu bilimni, balki nozikroq madaniyat belgisi sifatida, o'zini bilgandek ko'rsatishni zarur deb hisoblaydimi; yoki qalbining tubida buyuk ruhiy qayg'ularga umuman ishonmaydimi va ular tilga olinganda xayolida tish og'rig'i va oshqozon og'rig'i kabi buyuk jismoniy azoblar tilga olingandagi kabi tajribaga egami. Biroq hozir ko'pchilik odamlar bilan shunday bo'lib tuyuladi.

paras.en: Owing to the universal inexperience of both kinds of pain, and the comparative rarity of the spectacle of a sufferer, an important consequence results: people now hate pain far more than earlier man did, and calumniate it worse than ever; indeed people nowadays can hardly endure the thought of pain, and make out of it an affair of conscience and a reproach to collective existence.
paras.uz: Ikkala turdagi og'riqda umumiy tajribasizlik va azob chekuvchini ko'rishning nisbatan kamyobligi tufayli muhim oqibat kelib chiqadi: odamlar endi og'riqdan ilgarigi insonga qaraganda ancha ko'proq nafratlanadi va unga har qachongidan yomonroq tuhmat qiladi; haqiqatan ham, hozirgi odamlar og'riq haqidagi fikrga zo'rg'a chiday oladi va undan vijdon masalasi va butun hayotga ta'na yasaydi.

paras.en: The appearance of pessimistic philosophies is not at all the sign of great and dreadful miseries; for these interrogative marks regarding the worth of life appear in periods when the refinement and alleviation of existence already deem the unavoidable gnat-stings of the soul and body as altogether too bloody and wicked; and in the poverty of actual experiences of pain, would now like to make painful general ideas appear as suffering of the worst kind.—There might indeed be a remedy for pessimistic philosophies and the excessive sensibility which seems to me the real "distress of the present":—but perhaps this remedy already sounds too cruel, and would itself be reckoned among the symptoms owing to which people at present conclude that "existence is something evil." Well! the remedy for "the distress" is distress.
paras.uz: Pessimistik falsafalarning paydo bo'lishi aslo buyuk va dahshatli baxtsizliklarning belgisi emas; chunki hayot qadri haqidagi bu so'roq belgilari hayotning nafisligi va yengillashuvi ruh va tananing muqarrar chivin chaqishlarini ham haddan tashqari qonli va yovuz deb hisoblaydigan davrlarda paydo bo'ladi va og'riqning haqiqiy tajribalari kambag'alligida endi og'riqli umumiy g'oyalarni eng yomon turdagi azob sifatida ko'rsatmoqchi bo'ladi. — Haqiqatan ham, pessimistik falsafalar va menga haqiqiy «hozirgi zamon qayg'usi» bo'lib ko'rinadigan haddan tashqari sezgirlik uchun davo bo'lishi mumkin edi: — lekin balki bu davo allaqachon haddan tashqari shafqatsiz eshitilar va o'zi ham hozir odamlar «hayot yomon narsa» degan xulosaga keladigan alomatlar qatoriga kiritilar. Xo'sh! «Qayg'u»ning davosi — qayg'u.

paras.en: 49. Magnanimity and allied Qualities. — Those paradoxical phenomena, such as the sudden coldness in the demeanour of good-natured men, the humour of the melancholy, and above all magnanimity, as a sudden renunciation of revenge or of the gratification of envy—appear in men in whom there is a powerful inner impulsiveness, in men of sudden satiety and sudden disgust. Their satisfactions are so rapid and violent that satiety, aversion, and flight into the antithetical taste, immediately follow upon them: in this contrast the convulsion of feeling liberates itself, in one person by sudden coldness, in another by laughter, and in a third by tears and self-sacrifice.
paras.uz: 49. Saxiylik va unga yaqin xususiyatlar. — O'sha paradoksal hodisalar — masalan, xushfe'l odamlarning xatti-harakatidagi to'satdan sovuqlik, g'amginlarning hazili va eng avvalo saxiylik, qasos yoki hasadni qondirishdan to'satdan voz kechish sifatida — ichida kuchli ichki shiddatkorlik bo'lgan odamlarda, to'satdan to'yish va to'satdan jirkanish odamlarida paydo bo'ladi. Ularning qoniqishlari shunchalik tez va shiddatliki, ulardan keyin darhol to'yish, nafrat va qarama-qarshi didga qochish keladi: bu qarama-qarshilikda tuyg'u talvasasi o'zini ozod qiladi, birida to'satdan sovuqlik bilan, boshqasida kulgi bilan, uchinchisida ko'z yoshlari va fidoyilik bilan.

paras.en: The magnanimous person appears to me—at least that kind of magnanimous person who has always made most impression—as a man with the strongest thirst for vengeance, to whom a gratification presents itself close at hand, and who already drinks it off in imagination so copiously, thoroughly, and to the last drop, that an excessive, rapid disgust follows this rapid licentiousness;—he now elevates himself "above himself," as one says, and forgives his enemy, yea, blesses and honours him. With this violence done to himself, however, with this mockery of his impulse to revenge, even still so powerful, he merely yields to the new impulse, the disgust which has become powerful, and does this just as impatiently and licentiously, as a short time previously he forestalled, and as it were exhausted, the joy of revenge with his fantasy. In magnanimity there is the same amount of egoism as in revenge, but a different quality of egoism.
paras.uz: Saxiy odam menga — hech bo'lmasa doimo eng ko'p taassurot qoldirgan saxiy odamning o'sha turi — qasosga eng kuchli tashnalikka ega bo'lgan odam bo'lib ko'rinadi, unga qoniqish yaqin qo'l ostida taqdim etiladi va u uni xayolida shunchalik mo'l, puxta va oxirgi tomchisigacha ichib yuboradiki, bu tez buzuqlikdan keyin haddan tashqari, tez jirkanish keladi; — endi u aytilganidek «o'zidan yuqori» ko'tariladi va dushmanini kechiradi, ha, uni duo qiladi va hurmat qiladi. Biroq o'ziga nisbatan bu zo'ravonlik bilan, hali ham shunchalik kuchli bo'lgan qasos mayli ustidan bu masxara bilan u shunchaki yangi maylga, kuchli bo'lib qolgan jirkanishga taslim bo'ladi va buni xuddi qisqa vaqt oldin qasos quvonchini fantaziyasi bilan oldindan qo'lga kiritib, go'yo tugatganidek sabrsiz va buzuqlik bilan qiladi. Saxiylikda qasosdagidek miqdorda xudbinlik bor, lekin boshqacha sifatdagi xudbinlik.

paras.en: 50. The Argument of Isolation. — The reproach of conscience, even in the most conscientious, is weak against the feeling: "This and that are contrary to the good morals of your society." A cold glance or a wry mouth, on the part of those among whom and for whom one has been educated, is still feared even by the strongest. What is really feared there? Isolation! as the argument which demolishes even the best arguments for a person or cause!—It is thus that the gregarious instinct speaks in us.
paras.uz: 50. Yolg'izlik dalili. — Vijdon ta'nasi, hatto eng vijdonlilarda ham, «Bu va u sening jamiyatingning yaxshi axloqiga zid» degan tuyg'u oldida zaif. O'zi orasida va o'zi uchun tarbiyalangan odamlarning sovuq nigohi yoki qiyshaygan og'zidan hatto eng kuchlilar ham hali qo'rqadi. U yerda aslida nimadan qo'rqiladi? Yolg'izlikdan! — shaxs yoki ish uchun hatto eng yaxshi dalillarni ham vayron qiladigan dalil sifatida! — Bizda podaviy instinkt shunday gapiradi.

paras.en: 51. Sense for Truth. — Commend me to all scepticism where I am permitted to answer: "Let us put it to the test!" But I don't wish to hear anything more of things and questions which do not admit of being tested. That is the limit of my "sense for truth": for bravery has there lost its right.
paras.uz: 51. Haqiqat tuyg'usi. — Menga «Keling, sinab ko'raylik!» deb javob berishga ruxsat berilgan har qanday skeptitsizmni ma'qullayman. Lekin sinab ko'rishga imkon bermaydigan narsalar va savollar haqida boshqa hech narsa eshitishni istamayman. Bu mening «haqiqat tuyg'usi»ning chegarasi: chunki u yerda jasorat o'z huquqini yo'qotgan.

paras.en: 52. What others Know of us. — That which we know of ourselves and have in our memory is not so decisive for the happiness of our life as is generally believed. One day it flashes upon our mind what others know of us (or think they know)—and then we acknowledge that it is the more powerful. We get on with our bad conscience more easily than with our bad reputation.
paras.uz: 52. Boshqalar biz haqimizda nima biladi. — O'zimiz haqimizda biladigan va xotiramizda saqlaydigan narsa hayotimiz baxti uchun odatda ishonilganidek hal qiluvchi emas. Bir kun xayolimizga boshqalar biz haqimizda nima bilishi (yoki bilaman deb o'ylashi) chaqnab keladi — va o'shanda biz buning kuchliroq ekanini tan olamiz. Biz yomon vijdonimiz bilan yomon obro'yimizdan ko'ra osonroq kelishamiz.

paras.en: 53. Where Goodness Begins. — Where bad eyesight can no longer see the evil impulse as such, on account of its refinement,—there man sets up the kingdom of goodness; and the feeling of having now gone over into the kingdom of goodness brings all those impulses (such as the feelings of security, of comfortableness, of benevolence) into simultaneous activity, which were threatened and confined by the evil impulses. Consequently, the duller the eye so much the further does goodness extend! Hence the eternal cheerfulness of the populace and of children! Hence the gloominess and grief (allied to the bad conscience) of great thinkers.
paras.uz: 53. Yaxshilik qayerdan boshlanadi. — Zaif ko'z nozikligi tufayli yovuz maylni endi o'shandayligicha ko'ra olmaydigan joyda — inson o'sha yerda yaxshilik saltanatini o'rnatadi; va endi yaxshilik saltanatiga o'tgan degan tuyg'u yovuz mayllar tahdid qilgan va cheklagan barcha mayllarni (masalan, xavfsizlik, qulaylik, xayrixohlik tuyg'ularini) bir vaqtda faoliyatga keltiradi. Demak, ko'z qanchalik xira bo'lsa, yaxshilik shunchalik uzoqqa yoyiladi! Oddiy xalq va bolalarning abadiy quvnoqligi shundan! Buyuk mutafakkirlarning ma'yusligi va qayg'usi (yomon vijdonga yaqin) shundan.

paras.en: 54. The Consciousness of Appearance. — How wonderfully and novelly, and at the same time how awfully and ironically, do I feel myself situated with respect to collective existence, with my knowledge! I have discovered for myself that the old humanity and animality, yea, the collective primeval age, and the past of all sentient being, continues to meditate, love, hate, and reason in me,—I have suddenly awoke in the midst of this dream, but merely to the consciousness that I just dream, and that I must dream on in order not to perish; just as the sleep-walker must dream on in order not to tumble down. What is it that is now "appearance" to me! Verily, not the antithesis of any kind of essence,—what knowledge can I assert of any kind of essence whatsoever, except merely the predicates of its appearance!
paras.uz: 54. Ko'rinish haqidagi ong. — Bilimim bilan butun hayotga nisbatan o'zimni qanchalik ajoyib va yangi, shu bilan birga qanchalik dahshatli va kinoyali holatda his qilaman! Men o'zim uchun kashf etdimki, eski insoniylik va hayvoniylik, ha, butun ibtidoiy davr va barcha sezuvchi mavjudotning o'tmishi menda o'ylashda, sevishda, nafratlanishda va mulohaza qilishda davom etadi, — men to'satdan bu tushning o'rtasida uyg'ondim, lekin faqat shunchaki tush ko'rayotganimni va halok bo'lmaslik uchun tush ko'rishda davom etishim kerakligini anglash uchun; xuddi uyquda yuruvchi yiqilmaslik uchun tush ko'rishda davom etishi kerak bo'lgani kabi. Endi men uchun «ko'rinish» nima! Haqiqatan ham, qandaydir mohiyatning qarama-qarshisi emas, — men har qanday mohiyat haqida uning ko'rinishining predikatlaridan boshqa qanday bilimni da'vo qila olaman!

paras.en: Verily not a dead mask which one could put upon an unknown X, and which to be sure one could also remove! Appearance is for me the operating and living thing itself; which goes so far in its self-mockery as to make me feel that here there is appearance, and Will o' the Wisp, and spirit-dance, and nothing more,—that among all these dreamers, I also, the "thinker," dance my dance, that the thinker is a means of prolonging further the terrestrial dance, and in so far is one of the masters of ceremony of existence, and that the sublime consistency and connectedness of all branches of knowledge is perhaps, and will perhaps, be the best means for maintaining the universality of the dreaming, the complete, mutual understandability of all those dreamers, and thereby the duration of the dream.
paras.uz: Haqiqatan ham noma'lum X ga kiydirish mumkin bo'lgan va albatta yechib olish ham mumkin bo'lgan o'lik niqob emas! Ko'rinish men uchun ta'sir qiluvchi va tirik narsaning o'zi; u o'zini masxara qilishda shunchalik uzoqqa boradiki, menga bu yerda ko'rinish, adashtiruvchi chiroq va arvohlar raqsi va boshqa hech narsa yo'q ekanini his qildiradi, — bu barcha tush ko'ruvchilar orasida men ham, «mutafakkir», o'z raqsimni tushaman, mutafakkir yerdagi raqsni yana uzaytirish vositasi va shu jihatdan hayotning marosim ustalaridan biri, va bilimning barcha sohalarining yuksak izchilligi va bog'liqligi, ehtimol, tush ko'rishning umumiyligini, barcha tush ko'ruvchilarning to'liq, o'zaro tushunarliligini va shu bilan tushning davomiyligini saqlashning eng yaxshi vositasi va balki shunday bo'lib qoladi.

paras.en: 55. The Ultimate Nobility of Character. — What then makes a person "noble"? Certainly not that he makes sacrifices; even the frantic libertine makes sacrifices. Certainly not that he generally follows his passions; there are contemptible passions. Certainly not that he does something for others and without selfishness; perhaps the effect of selfishness is precisely at its greatest in the noblest persons.—But that the passion which seizes the noble man is a peculiarity, without his knowing that it is so: the use of a rare and singular measuring-rod, almost a frenzy: the feeling of heat in things which feel cold to all other persons: a divining of values for which scales have not yet been invented: a sacrificing on altars which are consecrated to an unknown God: a bravery without the desire for honour: a self-sufficiency which has superabundance, and imparts to men and things.
paras.uz: 55. Xarakterning eng oliy olijanobligi. — Xo'sh, odamni nima «olijanob» qiladi? Albatta, qurbonlik qilishi emas; hatto quturgan buzuq ham qurbonlik qiladi. Albatta, umuman ehtiroslariga ergashishi emas; jirkanch ehtiroslar ham bor. Albatta, boshqalar uchun va xudbinliksiz nimadir qilishi emas; balki xudbinlikning ta'siri aynan eng olijanob odamlarda eng katta bo'ladi. — Balki olijanob odamni egallab olgan ehtiros o'ziga xoslik ekani, u buni bilmasa ham: kamyob va yagona o'lchov tayog'ini qo'llash, deyarli telbalik: boshqa hamma odamlarga sovuq tuyuladigan narsalarda issiqlikni his qilish: tarozilar hali ixtiro qilinmagan qadriyatlarni sezish: noma'lum Xudoga bag'ishlangan qurbongohlarda qurbonlik qilish: sharafga intilishsiz jasorat: ortiqcha mo'lligi bo'lgan va uni odamlar va narsalarga ulashadigan o'ziga yetarlilik.

paras.en: Hitherto, therefore, it has been the rare in man, and the unconsciousness of this rareness, that has made men noble. Here, however, let us consider that everything ordinary, immediate, and indispensable, in short, what has been most preservative of the species, and generally the rule in mankind hitherto, has been judged unreasonable and calumniated in its entirety by this standard, in favour of the exceptions. To become the advocate of the rule—that may perhaps be the ultimate form and refinement in which nobility of character will reveal itself on earth.
paras.uz: Demak, shu paytgacha odamlarni olijanob qilgan narsa insondagi kamyoblik va bu kamyoblikni anglamaslik bo'lgan. Biroq bu yerda shuni o'ylaylikki, barcha oddiy, bevosita va zarur narsalar, qisqasi, turni eng ko'p saqlagan va shu paytgacha insoniyatda umuman qoida bo'lgan narsa bu o'lchov bilan istisnolar foydasiga butunlay aqlsiz deb hukm qilingan va tuhmat qilingan. Qoidaning himoyachisi bo'lish — balki xarakter olijanobligi yer yuzida o'zini namoyon qiladigan so'nggi shakl va nafislik shudir.

paras.en: 56. The Desire for Suffering. — When I think of the desire to do something, how it continually tickles and stimulates millions of young Europeans, who cannot endure themselves and all their ennui,—I conceive that there must be a desire in them to suffer something, in order to derive from their suffering a worthy motive for acting, for doing something. Distress is necessary! Hence the cry of the politicians, hence the many false, trumped-up, exaggerated "states of distress" of all possible kinds, and the blind readiness to believe in them. This young world desires that there should arrive or appear from the outside—not happiness—but misfortune; and their imagination is already busy beforehand to form a monster out of it, so that they may afterwards be able to fight with a monster.
paras.uz: 56. Azob chekish istagi. — Nimadir qilish istagi o'zlariga va barcha zerikishlariga chiday olmaydigan millionlab yosh yevropaliklarni qanday doimo qitiqlab, qo'zg'atib turishini o'ylaganimda, — tushunamanki, ularda harakat qilish, nimadir qilish uchun azoblaridan munosib motiv olish maqsadida nimadir azob chekish istagi bo'lsa kerak. Qayg'u zarur! Siyosatchilarning qichqirig'i shundan, har xil yolg'on, to'qilgan, bo'rttirilgan «qayg'u holatlari» va ularga ishonishga ko'r-ko'rona tayyorlik shundan. Bu yosh dunyo tashqaridan baxt emas — baxtsizlik kelishini yoki paydo bo'lishini istaydi; va ularning xayoli undan oldindan mahluq yasash bilan band, toki keyin mahluq bilan jang qila olishsin.

paras.en: If these distress-seekers felt the power to benefit themselves, to do something for themselves from internal sources, they would also understand how to create a distress of their own, specially their own, from internal sources. Their inventions might then be more refined, and their gratifications might sound like good music: while at present they fill the world with their cries of distress, and consequently too often with the feeling of distress in the first place! They do not know what to make of themselves—and so they paint the misfortune of others on the wall; they always need others! And always again other others!—Pardon me, my friends, I have ventured to paint my happiness on the wall.
paras.uz: Agar bu qayg'u izlovchilar o'zlariga foyda keltirish, ichki manbalardan o'zlari uchun nimadir qilish kuchini his qilganlarida, ular ichki manbalardan o'zlarining shaxsiy, alohida o'zlariga xos qayg'usini yaratishni ham tushunishardi. O'shanda ularning ixtirolari nozikroq bo'lishi va qoniqishlari yaxshi musiqadek yangrashi mumkin edi: hozir esa ular dunyoni qayg'u qichqiriqlari va shuning uchun juda ko'pincha birinchi navbatda qayg'u tuyg'usi bilan to'ldiradi! Ular o'zlari bilan nima qilishni bilishmaydi — shuning uchun boshqalarning baxtsizligini devorga chizishadi; ularga doimo boshqalar kerak! Va doimo yana boshqa boshqalar! — Kechiringlar, do'stlarim, men o'z baxtimni devorga chizishga jur'at etdim.

chapters.recap_uz: Epikurning sokin dengizga qaragan baxti; ilm natijalari mustahkam qolishidan hayrat. Hozirgi odamlar og'riqni kam biladi, shuning uchun undan ko'proq nafratlanadi. Saxiylik, yolg'izlik qo'rquvi va haqiqiy olijanoblik haqida.

chapters.title: Realists and artists

paras.en: 57. To the Realists. — Ye sober beings, who feel yourselves armed against passion and fantasy, and would gladly make a pride and an ornament out of your emptiness, ye call yourselves realists and give to understand that the world is actually constituted as it appears to you; before you alone reality stands unveiled, and ye yourselves would perhaps be the best part of it,—oh, ye dear images of Sais! But are not ye also in your unveiled condition still extremely passionate and dusky beings compared with the fish, and still all too like an enamoured artist?—and what is "reality" to an enamoured artist! Ye still carry about with you the valuations of things which had their origin in the passions and infatuations of earlier centuries! There is still a secret and ineffaceable drunkenness embodied in your sobriety! Your love of "reality," for example—oh, that is an old, primitive "love"!
paras.uz: 57. Realistlarga. — Siz, o'zingizni ehtiros va fantaziyaga qarshi qurollangan deb his qiladigan va bo'shligingizdan g'urur va bezak yasashni xohlaydigan hushyor mavjudotlar, o'zingizni realist deb ataysiz va dunyo haqiqatda sizga qanday ko'rinsa, shunday tuzilgan deb tushuntirasiz; faqat sizning oldingizda haqiqat pardasiz turadi va balki siz o'zingiz uning eng yaxshi qismi bo'lardingiz, — oh, siz, Saisning aziz haykallari! Lekin siz ham pardasiz holatingizda baliq bilan solishtirganda hali ham nihoyatda ehtirosli va qorong'i mavjudotlar emasmisiz, hali ham oshiq san'atkorga haddan tashqari o'xshash emasmisiz? — oshiq san'atkor uchun esa «haqiqat» nima! Siz hali ham o'zingiz bilan oldingi asrlarning ehtiroslari va maftunliklarida kelib chiqqan narsalar baholarini olib yurasiz! Hushyorligingizda hali ham yashirin va o'chmas mastlik mujassam! Masalan, sizning «haqiqat»ga bo'lgan sevgingiz — oh, bu eski, ibtidoiy «sevgi»!

paras.en: In every feeling, in every sense-impression, there is a portion of this old love: and similarly also some kind of fantasy, prejudice, irrationality, ignorance, fear, and whatever else has become mingled and woven into it. There is that mountain! There is that cloud! What is "real" in them? Remove the phantasm and the whole human element therefrom, ye sober ones! Yes, if ye could do that! If ye could forget your origin, your past, your preparatory schooling,—your whole history as man and beast! There is no "reality" for us—nor for you either, ye sober ones,—we are far from being so alien to one another as ye suppose, and perhaps our good-will to get beyond drunkenness is just as respectable as your belief that ye are altogether incapable of drunkenness.
paras.uz: Har bir tuyg'uda, har bir sezgi taassurotida bu eski sevgining bir ulushi bor: shuningdek, unga aralashib, to'qilib ketgan qandaydir fantaziya, xurofot, aqlsizlik, johillik, qo'rquv va boshqa narsalar ham. Mana o'sha tog'! Mana o'sha bulut! Ulardagi «haqiqiy» nima? Ulardan sarobni va butun insoniy unsurni olib tashlang, ey hushyorlar! Ha, agar buni qila olsangiz! Agar kelib chiqishingizni, o'tmishingizni, tayyorlov maktabingizni — inson va hayvon sifatidagi butun tarixingizni unuta olsangiz! Biz uchun «haqiqat» yo'q — siz uchun ham yo'q, ey hushyorlar, — biz bir-birimizga siz o'ylagandek begona emasmiz va balki mastlikdan narida o'tishga bo'lgan yaxshi niyatimiz siz mastlikka butunlay qodir emasman degan ishonchingiz kabi hurmatga loyiqdir.

paras.en: 58. Only as Creators!. — It has caused me the greatest trouble, and for ever causes me the greatest trouble, to perceive that unspeakably more depends upon what things are called, than on what they are. The reputation, the name and appearance, the importance, the usual measure and weight of things—each being in origin most frequently an error and arbitrariness thrown over the things like a garment, and quite alien to their essence and even to their exterior—have gradually, by the belief therein and its continuous growth from generation to generation, grown as it were on-and-into things and become their very body; the appearance at the very beginning becomes almost always the essence in the end, and operates as the essence! What a fool he would be who would think it enough to refer here to this origin and this nebulous veil of illusion, in order to annihilate that which virtually passes for the world—namely, so-called "reality"! It is only as creators that we can annihilate!—But let us not forget this: it suffices to create new names and valuations and probabilities, in order in the long run to create new "things."
paras.uz: 58. Faqat yaratuvchilar sifatida! — Narsalar nima ekaniga qaraganda ular qanday atalishiga beqiyos ko'proq narsa bog'liq ekanini ko'rish menga eng katta mashaqqat keltirgan va doimo keltiradi. Narsalarning obro'si, nomi va ko'rinishi, ahamiyati, odatiy o'lchovi va og'irligi — ularning har biri kelib chiqishida ko'pincha narsalar ustiga kiyimdek tashlangan va ularning mohiyatiga, hatto tashqi ko'rinishiga ham butunlay begona bo'lgan xato va o'zboshimchalik — asta-sekin, ularga bo'lgan ishonch va uning avloddan avlodga uzluksiz o'sishi tufayli go'yo narsalarga yopishib, ichiga o'sib kirgan va ularning tanasining o'ziga aylangan; boshidagi ko'rinish oxirida deyarli doimo mohiyatga aylanadi va mohiyat sifatida ta'sir qiladi! Amalda dunyo deb hisoblanadigan narsani — ya'ni «haqiqat» deb ataladigan narsani yo'q qilish uchun bu kelib chiqishga va bu xayolning tumanli pardasiga ishora qilish kifoya deb o'ylagan odam qanday ahmoq bo'lardi! Biz faqat yaratuvchilar sifatidagina yo'q qila olamiz! — Lekin buni unutmaylik: uzoq muddatda yangi «narsalar» yaratish uchun yangi nomlar, baholar va ehtimolliklar yaratish kifoya.

paras.en: 59. We Artists!. — When we love a woman we have readily a hatred against nature, on recollecting all the disagreeable natural functions to which every woman is subject; we prefer not to think of them at all, but if once our soul touches on these things it twitches impatiently, and glances, as we have said, contemptuously at nature:—we are hurt; nature seems to encroach upon our possessions, and with the profanest hands.
paras.uz: 59. Biz san'atkorlar! — Biz ayolni sevganimizda, har bir ayol bo'ysunadigan barcha yoqimsiz tabiiy funksiyalarni eslab, tabiatga nisbatan osongina nafrat his qilamiz; biz ular haqida umuman o'ylamaslikni afzal ko'ramiz, lekin agar ruhimiz bu narsalarga bir marta tegib ketsa, u sabrsiz pirpiraydi va aytganimizdek, tabiatga nafrat bilan qaraydi: — bizga og'ir botadi; tabiat bizning mulkimizga, va eng nopok qo'llar bilan, tajovuz qilayotgandek tuyuladi.

paras.en: We then shut our ears against all physiology, and we decree in secret that "we will hear nothing of the fact that man is something else than soul and form!" "The man under the skin" is an abomination and monstrosity, a blasphemy of God and of love to all lovers.—Well, just as the lover still feels with respect to nature and natural functions, so did every worshipper of God and his "holy omnipotence" formerly feel: in all that was said of nature by astronomers, geologists, physiologists, and physicians, he saw an encroachment on his most precious possession, and consequently an attack,—and moreover also an impertinence of the assailant!
paras.uz: O'shanda biz barcha fiziologiyaga qulog'imizni yopamiz va yashirincha hukm chiqaramiz: «biz inson ruh va shakldan boshqa narsa ekani haqida hech narsa eshitmaymiz!» «Teri ostidagi inson» barcha oshiqlar uchun jirkanchlik va mahluq, Xudoga va sevgiga kufrdir. — Xo'sh, oshiq hali ham tabiat va tabiiy funksiyalarga nisbatan qanday his qilsa, Xudoga va uning «muqaddas qudrati»ga sig'inuvchi har bir kishi ilgari xuddi shunday his qilgan: astronomlar, geologlar, fiziologlar va shifokorlar tabiat haqida aytgan hamma narsada u o'zining eng qimmatli mulkiga tajovuzni va shuning uchun hujumni ko'rgan, — bundan tashqari, hujumchining surbetligini ham!

paras.en: The "law of nature" sounded to him as blasphemy against God; in truth he would too willingly have seen the whole of mechanics traced back to moral acts of volition and arbitrariness:—but because nobody could render him this service, he concealed nature and mechanism from himself as best he could, and lived in a dream. Oh, those men of former times understood how to dream, and did not need first to go to sleep!—and we men of the present day also still understand it too well, with all our good-will for wakefulness and daylight!
paras.uz: «Tabiat qonuni» unga Xudoga kufrdek eshitilgan; haqiqatda u butun mexanikani axloqiy iroda va o'zboshimchalik harakatlariga olib borilganini juda bajonidil ko'rgan bo'lardi: — lekin hech kim unga bu xizmatni qila olmagani uchun, u tabiat va mexanizmni o'zidan iloji boricha yashirdi va tushda yashadi. Oh, o'sha ilgarigi zamon odamlari tush ko'rishni bilishgan va buning uchun avval uxlashlari shart emas edi! — biz hozirgi zamon odamlari ham uyg'oqlik va kunduzga bo'lgan barcha yaxshi niyatimizga qaramay buni hali haddan tashqari yaxshi bilamiz!

paras.en: It suffices to love, to hate, to desire, and in general to feel,—immediately the spirit and the power of the dream come over us, and we ascend, with open eyes and indifferent to all danger, the most dangerous paths, to the roofs and towers of fantasy, and without any giddiness, as persons born for climbing—we the night-walkers by day! We artists! We concealers of naturalness! We moon-struck and God-struck ones! We dead-silent, untiring wanderers on heights which we do not see as heights, but as our plains, as our places of safety!
paras.uz: Sevish, nafratlanish, istash va umuman his qilish kifoya, — darhol tushning ruhi va kuchi bizni chulg'ab oladi va biz ochiq ko'zlar bilan va har qanday xavfga befarq holda eng xavfli yo'llardan, fantaziyaning tomlari va minoralariga, hech qanday bosh aylanishsiz, tirmashish uchun tug'ilgan odamlardek ko'tarilamiz — biz kunduzgi tunda yuruvchilar! Biz san'atkorlar! Biz tabiiylikni yashiruvchilar! Biz oy urgan va Xudo urganlar! Biz o'likdek jim, charchamas sayyohlar, balandliklarda, ularni balandlik deb emas, o'z tekisligimiz, o'z xavfsiz joylarimiz deb ko'radigan!

paras.en: 60. Women and their Effect in the Distance. — Have I still ears? Am I only ear, and nothing else besides? Here I stand in the midst of the surging of the breakers, whose white flames fork up to my feet;—from all sides there is howling, threatening, crying, and screaming at me, while in the lowest depths the old earth-shaker sings his aria, hollow like a roaring bull; he beats such an earth-shaker's measure thereto, that even the hearts of these weathered rock-monsters tremble at the sound. Then, suddenly, as if born out of nothingness, there appears before the portal of this hellish labyrinth, only a few fathoms distant,—a great sailing-ship gliding silently along like a ghost. Oh, this ghostly beauty! With what enchantment it seizes me! What? Has all the repose and silence in the world embarked here? Does my happiness itself sit in this quiet place, my happier ego, my second immortalised self?
paras.uz: 60. Ayollar va ularning uzoqdan ta'siri. — Menda hali quloq bormi? Men faqat quloqmanmi, boshqa hech narsa emasmi? Mana men to'lqinlarning qaynashi o'rtasida turibman, ularning oq alangalari oyoqlarimgacha ayri bo'lib otiladi; — har tomondan menga uvillash, tahdid, qichqiriq va chinqiriq, eng chuqur qa'rda esa keksa yer silkituvchi bo'kirayotgan buqadek bo'g'iq ariyasini kuylaydi; u bunga shunday yer silkituvchi takt uradiki, hatto bu shamol yegan qoya mahluqlarining yuraklari ham tovushdan titraydi. Keyin to'satdan, go'yo hech narsalikdan tug'ilgandek, bu do'zaxiy labirintning darvozasi oldida, atigi bir necha quloch narida, — arvohdek jimgina sirpanib o'tayotgan katta yelkanli kema paydo bo'ladi. Oh, bu arvohona go'zallik! Meni qanday sehr bilan ushlab oladi! Nima? Dunyodagi barcha osoyishtalik va sukunat bu yerga chiqib olganmi? Mening baxtimning o'zi bu sokin joyda o'tiribdimi, mening baxtliroq «men»im, ikkinchi abadiylashgan o'zim?

paras.en: Still not dead, yet also no longer living? As a ghost-like, calm, gazing, gliding, sweeping, neutral being? Similar to the ship, which, with its white sails, like an immense butterfly, passes over the dark sea! Yes! Passing over existence! That is it! That would be it!——It seems that the noise here has made me a visionary? All great noise causes one to place happiness in the calm and the distance. When a man is in the midst of his hubbub, in the midst of the breakers of his plots and plans, he there sees perhaps calm, enchanting beings glide past him, for whose happiness and retirement he longs—they are women. He almost thinks that there with the women dwells his better self; that in these calm places even the loudest breakers become still as death, and life itself a dream of life. But still! But still!
paras.uz: Hali o'lik emas, lekin endi tirik ham emasmi? Arvohdek, sokin, tikilib turuvchi, sirpanuvchi, suzuvchi, betaraf mavjudot sifatida? Oq yelkanlari bilan ulkan kapalakdek qorong'i dengiz ustidan o'tib ketayotgan kemaga o'xshab! Ha! Hayot ustidan o'tib ketish! Gap shunda! Shunday bo'lardi! —— Bu yerdagi shovqin meni xayolparast qilib qo'ydi shekilli? Har qanday katta shovqin odamni baxtni sokinlik va uzoqlikda deb bilishga undaydi. Inson o'z g'ala-g'ovurining o'rtasida, rejalari va niyatlarining to'lqinlari o'rtasida bo'lganda, u yerda balki yonidan sirpanib o'tayotgan sokin, maftunkor mavjudotlarni ko'radi va ularning baxti va xilvatini sog'inadi — bular ayollar. U deyarli o'ylaydiki, u yerda, ayollar bilan uning yaxshiroq o'zi yashaydi; bu sokin joylarda hatto eng shovqinli to'lqinlar ham o'likdek tinchiydi va hayotning o'zi hayot haqidagi tushga aylanadi. Lekin baribir! Lekin baribir!

paras.en: My noble enthusiast, there is also in the most beautiful sailing-ship so much noise and bustling, and alas, so much petty, pitiable bustling! The enchantment and the most powerful effect of women is, to use the language of philosophers, an effect at a distance, an actio in distans; there belongs thereto, however, primarily and above all,—distance!
paras.uz: Mening olijanob ishqibozim, eng go'zal yelkanli kemada ham shunchalik ko'p shovqin va tashvish bor, afsus, shunchalik ko'p mayda, ayanchli tashvish! Ayollarning sehri va eng kuchli ta'siri, faylasuflar tili bilan aytganda, uzoqdan ta'sir, actio in distans; biroq buning uchun birinchi navbatda va eng avvalo — masofa kerak!

paras.en: 61. In Honour of Friendship. — That the sentiment of friendship was regarded by antiquity as the highest sentiment, higher even than the most vaunted pride of the self-sufficient and wise, yea as it were its sole and still holier brotherhood, is very well expressed by the story of the Macedonian king who made the present of a talent to a cynical Athenian philosopher from whom he received it back again. "What?" said the king, "has he then no friend?" He therewith meant to say, "I honour this pride of the wise and independent man, but I should have honoured his humanity still higher if the friend in him had gained the victory over his pride. The philosopher has lowered himself in my estimation, for he showed that he did not know one of the two highest sentiments—and in fact the higher of them!"
paras.uz: 61. Do'stlik sharafiga. — Do'stlik tuyg'usi antik davrda eng oliy tuyg'u, hatto o'ziga yetarli va donolarning eng ko'p maqtalgan g'ururidan ham oliyroq, ha, go'yo uning yagona va yana ham muqaddasroq birodarligi deb hisoblangani makedoniyalik podshoh kinik afinalik faylasufga bir talant sovg'a qilgani va undan uni qaytarib olgani haqidagi hikoyada juda yaxshi ifodalangan. «Nima? — dedi podshoh, — demak, uning do'sti yo'qmi?» U bu bilan demoqchi bo'ldi: «Men dono va mustaqil odamning bu g'ururini hurmat qilaman, lekin agar undagi do'st g'ururi ustidan g'alaba qozonganida, uning insoniyligini yana ham yuqoriroq hurmat qilgan bo'lardim. Faylasuf mening nazarimda o'zini pasaytirdi, chunki u ikki oliy tuyg'udan birini — va aslida ularning oliyrog'ini bilmasligini ko'rsatdi!»

paras.en: 62. Love. — Love pardons even the passion of the beloved.
paras.uz: 62. Sevgi. — Sevgi hatto sevganining ehtirosini ham kechiradi.

paras.en: 63. Woman in Music. — How does it happen that warm and rainy winds bring the musical mood and the inventive delight in melody with them? Are they not the same winds that fill the churches and give women amorous thoughts?
paras.uz: 63. Musiqadagi ayol. — Qanday qilib iliq va yomg'irli shamollar o'zlari bilan musiqiy kayfiyat va kuy ixtiro qilish zavqini olib keladi? Ular cherkovlarni to'ldiradigan va ayollarga ishqiy fikrlar beradigan o'sha shamollar emasmi?

paras.en: 64. Sceptics. — I fear women who have become old are more sceptical in the secret recesses of their hearts than any of the men are; they believe in the superficiality of existence as in its essence, and all virtue and profundity is to them only the disguising of this "truth," the very desirable disguising of a pudendum,—an affair, therefore, of decency and of modesty, and nothing more!
paras.uz: 64. Skeptiklar. — Qo'rqamanki, qarib qolgan ayollar qalblarining yashirin burchaklarida har qanday erkakdan ko'ra ko'proq skeptik; ular hayotning yuzakiligiga uning mohiyatiga ishongandek ishonishadi va ular uchun barcha fazilat va chuqurlik bu «haqiqat»ni niqoblash, uyatli narsaning juda istalgan niqobi, — demak, odob va hayo masalasi, boshqa hech narsa emas!

paras.en: 65. Devotedness. — There are noble women with a certain poverty of spirit, who, in order to express their profoundest devotedness, have no other alternative but to offer their virtue and modesty: it is the highest thing they have. And this present is often accepted without putting the recipient under such deep obligation as the giver supposed,—a very melancholy story!
paras.uz: 65. Sadoqat. — Ruhda qandaydir kambag'allik bo'lgan olijanob ayollar bor, ular o'zlarining eng chuqur sadoqatini ifodalash uchun fazilati va hayosini taqdim etishdan boshqa chorasi yo'q: bu ularda bor eng oliy narsa. Va bu sovg'a ko'pincha oluvchini beruvchi o'ylagandek chuqur minnatdorlik majburiyati ostiga qo'ymasdan qabul qilinadi, — juda g'amgin hikoya!

paras.en: 66. The Strength of the Weak. — Women are all skilful in exaggerating their weaknesses, indeed they are inventive in weaknesses, so as to seem quite fragile ornaments to which even a grain of dust does harm; their existence is meant to bring home to man's mind his coarseness, and to appeal to his conscience. They thus defend themselves against the strong and all "rights of might."
paras.uz: 66. Zaiflarning kuchi. — Ayollarning hammasi zaifliklarini bo'rttirishda mohir, haqiqatan ham, ular zaifliklarda ixtirochi, toki ularga hatto chang zarrasi ham zarar keltiradigan juda mo'rt bezaklar bo'lib ko'rinishsin; ularning mavjudligi erkakning ongiga uning qo'polligini yetkazish va vijdoniga murojaat qilish uchun. Ular shu tariqa o'zlarini kuchlilardan va barcha «kuch huquqlari»dan himoya qilishadi.

paras.en: 67. Self-dissembling. — She loves him now and has since been looking forth with as quiet confidence as a cow; but alas! It was precisely his delight that she seemed so fitful and absolutely incomprehensible! He had rather too much steady weather in himself already! Would she not do well to feign her old character? to feign indifference? Does not—love itself advise her to do so? Vivat comœdia!
paras.uz: 67. O'zini niqoblash. — U endi uni sevadi va o'shandan beri sigirdek sokin ishonch bilan qaraydi; lekin afsus! Aynan uning injiq va mutlaqo tushunarsiz ko'rinishi uni zavqlantirgan edi! Uning o'zida allaqachon haddan tashqari ko'p barqaror ob-havo bor edi! Ayol o'zining eski xarakterini ko'rsatsa yaxshi qilmasmidi? Befarqlikni ko'rsatsa? Unga buni — sevgining o'zi maslahat bermaydimi? Vivat comoedia! — Komediya yashasin!

paras.en: 68. Will and Willingness. — Some one brought a youth to a wise man and said, "See, this is one who is being corrupted by women!" The wise man shook his head and smiled. "It is men," he called out, "who corrupt women; and everything that women lack should be atoned for and improved in men,—for man creates for himself the ideal of woman, and woman moulds herself according to this ideal."—"You are too tender-hearted towards women," said one of the bystanders, "you do not know them!" The wise man answered: "Man's attribute is will, woman's attribute is willingness,—such is the law of the sexes, verily! a hard law for woman! All human beings are innocent of their existence, women, however, are doubly innocent; who could have enough of salve and gentleness for them!"—"What about salve! What about gentleness!" called out another person in the crowd, "we must educate women better!"—"We must educate men better," said the wise man, and made a sign to the youth to follow him.—The youth, however, did not follow him.
paras.uz: 68. Iroda va tayyorlik. — Kimdir bir yigitni donishmandning oldiga olib kelib dedi: «Mana, buni ayollar buzyapti!» Donishmand boshini chayqab, jilmaydi. «Ayollarni erkaklar buzadi, — deb xitob qildi u, — va ayollarda yetishmaydigan hamma narsa erkaklarda to'lanishi va tuzatilishi kerak, — chunki erkak o'zi uchun ayol idealini yaratadi, ayol esa o'zini shu idealga ko'ra shakllantiradi». — «Siz ayollarga nisbatan haddan tashqari ko'ngilchansiz, — dedi atrofda turganlardan biri, — siz ularni bilmaysiz!» Donishmand javob berdi: «Erkakning sifati — iroda, ayolning sifati — tayyorlik, — jinslar qonuni shunday, haqiqatan! ayol uchun og'ir qonun! Barcha insonlar o'z mavjudligida aybsiz, ayollar esa ikki karra aybsiz; ular uchun kim yetarlicha malham va muloyimlik topa olardi!» — «Malham nima! Muloyimlik nima! — deb qichqirdi olomondan yana bir kishi, — biz ayollarni yaxshiroq tarbiyalashimiz kerak!» — «Biz erkaklarni yaxshiroq tarbiyalashimiz kerak», — dedi donishmand va yigitga orqasidan yurishni ishora qildi. — Biroq yigit uning orqasidan bormadi.

paras.en: 69. Capacity for Revenge. — That a person cannot and consequently will not defend himself, does not yet cast disgrace upon him in our eyes; but we despise the person who has neither the ability nor the good-will for revenge—whether it be a man or a woman. Would a woman be able to captivate us (or, as people say, to "fetter" us) whom we did not credit with knowing how to employ the dagger (any kind of dagger) skilfully against us under certain circumstances? Or against herself; which in a certain case might be the severest revenge (the Chinese revenge).
paras.uz: 69. Qasos olish qobiliyati. — Odam o'zini himoya qila olmasligi va shuning uchun himoya qilishni istamasligi bizning nazarimizda unga hali sharmandalik keltirmaydi; lekin biz qasos olishga na qobiliyati, na yaxshi niyati bo'lmagan odamni mensimaymiz — xoh erkak, xoh ayol bo'lsin. Ma'lum sharoitlarda bizga qarshi xanjarni (har qanday xanjarni) mohirona ishlata olishiga ishonmagan ayol bizni maftun eta olarmidi (yoki odamlar aytganidek, bizni «kishanlay» olarmidi)? Yoki o'ziga qarshi; bu ma'lum holatda eng og'ir qasos bo'lishi mumkin (xitoycha qasos).

paras.en: 70. The Mistresses of the Masters. — A powerful contralto voice, as we occasionally hear it in the theatre, raises suddenly for us the curtain on possibilities in which we usually do not believe; all at once we are convinced that somewhere in the world there may be women with high, heroic, royal souls, capable and prepared for magnificent remonstrances, resolutions, and self-sacrifices, capable and prepared for domination over men, because in them the best in man, superior to sex, has become a corporeal ideal. To be sure, it is not the intention of the theatre that such voices should give such a conception of women; they are usually intended to represent the ideal male lover, for example, a Romeo; but, to judge by my experience, the theatre regularly miscalculates here, and the musician also, who expects such effects from such a voice. People do not believe in these lovers; these voices still contain a tinge of the motherly and housewifely character, and most of all when love is in their tone.
paras.uz: 70. Xo'jayinlarning xo'jayinlari. — Teatrda ba'zan eshitadigan kuchli kontralto ovozi biz uchun to'satdan odatda ishonmaydigan imkoniyatlar pardasini ko'taradi; birdaniga biz dunyoning qayerdadir yuksak, qahramonona, shohona qalbli, ulug'vor e'tirozlar, qarorlar va fidoyiliklarga qodir va tayyor, erkaklar ustidan hukmronlikka qodir va tayyor ayollar bo'lishi mumkinligiga ishonamiz, chunki ularda erkakdagi eng yaxshi narsa, jinsdan yuqori turgan narsa jismoniy idealga aylangan. Albatta, bunday ovozlar ayollar haqida bunday tasavvur berishi teatrning niyati emas; ular odatda ideal erkak oshiqni, masalan, Romeoni tasvirlash uchun mo'ljallangan; lekin tajribamga ko'ra, teatr bu yerda muntazam ravishda xato hisob qiladi, bunday ovozdan bunday ta'sir kutadigan musiqachi ham. Odamlar bu oshiqlarga ishonishmaydi; bu ovozlarda hali ham onalik va uy bekasi xarakterining bir tusi bor, ayniqsa ularning ohangida sevgi bo'lganda.

chapters.recap_uz: Nitsshe «realistlar»ni masxara qiladi: haqiqat ham eski sevgi va fantaziya bilan aralashgan. Narsalar nomi ularning mohiyatidan muhimroq; faqat yaratuvchi yo'q qila oladi. Ayollar, sevgi va do'stlik haqida qisqa aforizmlar.

chapters.title: The greatest danger

paras.en: 71. On Female Chastity. — There is something quite astonishing and extraordinary in the education of women of the higher class; indeed, there is perhaps nothing more paradoxical. All the world is agreed to educate them with as much ignorance as possible in eroticis, and to inspire their soul with a profound shame of such things, and the extremest impatience and horror at the suggestion of them. It is really here only that all the "honour" of woman is at stake; what would one not forgive them in other respects! But here they are intended to remain ignorant to the very backbone:—they are intended to have neither eyes, ears, words, nor thoughts for this, their "wickedness"; indeed knowledge here is already evil. And then!
paras.uz: 71. Ayollar iffati haqida. — Yuqori tabaqa ayollarining tarbiyasida butunlay hayratlanarli va g'ayrioddiy nimadir bor; haqiqatan ham, balki bundan ko'ra paradoksalroq narsa yo'qdir. Butun dunyo ularni eroticis — ishqiy narsalarda iloji boricha johil qilib tarbiyalashga va ruhlariga bunday narsalardan chuqur uyat, ular haqida ishora qilinganda esa o'ta sabrsizlik va dahshat singdirishga kelishib olgan. Ayolning butun «sha'ni» haqiqatan ham faqat shu yerda xavf ostida; boshqa jihatlarda ularga nimani kechirishmaydi! Lekin bu yerda ular umurtqasigacha johil qolishi mo'ljallangan: — ularning bu «yovuzlik»ka na ko'zi, na qulog'i, na so'zi, na fikri bo'lmasligi kerak; haqiqatan ham, bu yerda bilimning o'zi allaqachon yomonlik. Keyin esa!

paras.en: To be hurled as with an awful thunderbolt into reality and knowledge with marriage—and indeed by him whom they most love and esteem: to have to encounter love and shame in contradiction, yea, to have to feel rapture, abandonment, duty, sympathy, and fright at the unexpected proximity of God and animal, and whatever else besides! all at once!—There, in fact, a psychic entanglement has been effected which is quite unequalled!
paras.uz: Nikoh bilan dahshatli chaqmoq urgandek haqiqat va bilimga uloqtirilish — va aynan o'zlari eng ko'p sevadigan va hurmat qiladigan odam tomonidan: sevgi va uyatga qarama-qarshilikda duch kelish, ha, Xudo va hayvonning kutilmagan yaqinligidan vajd, o'zini topshirish, burch, hamdardlik va qo'rquvni, va yana boshqa narsalarni ham his qilishga majbur bo'lish! birdaniga! — U yerda haqiqatan ham mutlaqo tengsiz ruhiy chigallik hosil qilingan!

paras.en: Even the sympathetic curiosity of the wisest discerner of men does not suffice to divine how this or that woman gets along with the solution of this enigma and the enigma of this solution; what dreadful, far-reaching suspicions must awaken thereby in the poor unhinged soul; and forsooth, how the ultimate philosophy and scepticism of the woman casts anchor at this point!—Afterwards the same profound silence as before: and often even a silence to herself, a shutting of her eyes to herself.—Young wives on that account make great efforts to appear superficial and thoughtless; the most ingenious of them simulate a kind of impudence.—Wives easily feel their husbands as a question-mark to their honour, and their children as an apology or atonement,—they require children, and wish for them in quite another spirit than a husband wishes for them.—In short, one cannot be gentle enough towards women!
paras.uz: Hatto odamlarni eng dono tanuvchining hamdard qiziquvchanligi ham u yoki bu ayol bu jumboqning yechimi va bu yechimning jumboqi bilan qanday kelishishini sezish uchun yetarli emas; bu bilan bechora, muvozanatidan chiqqan ruhda qanday dahshatli, uzoqqa boradigan shubhalar uyg'onishi kerak; va haqiqatan ham, ayolning so'nggi falsafasi va skeptitsizmi aynan shu nuqtada langar tashlaydi! — Keyin xuddi avvalgidek chuqur sukunat: va ko'pincha hatto o'ziga nisbatan ham sukunat, o'ziga nisbatan ko'zlarini yumish. — Shuning uchun yosh xotinlar yuzaki va beparvo ko'rinish uchun katta harakat qilishadi; ularning eng zukkolari qandaydir surbetlikni o'ynashadi. — Xotinlar erlarini osongina o'z sha'nlariga so'roq belgisi deb, farzandlarini esa uzr yoki kafforat deb his qilishadi, — ularga farzandlar kerak va ularni er istaganidan butunlay boshqa ruhda istashadi. — Qisqasi, ayollarga nisbatan yetarlicha muloyim bo'lish mumkin emas!

paras.en: 72. Mothers. — Animals think differently from men with respect to females; with them the female is regarded as the productive being. There is no paternal love among them, but there is such a thing as love of the children of a beloved, and habituation to them. In the young, the females find gratification for their lust of dominion; the young are a property, an occupation, something quite comprehensible to them, with which they can chatter: all this conjointly is maternal love,—it is to be compared to the love of the artist for his work. Pregnancy has made the females gentler, more expectant, more timid, more submissively inclined; and similarly intellectual pregnancy engenders the character of the contemplative, who are allied to women in character:—they are the masculine mothers.—Among animals the masculine sex is regarded as the beautiful sex.
paras.uz: 72. Onalar. — Hayvonlar urg'ochilarga nisbatan odamlardan boshqacha o'ylaydi; ularda urg'ochi samarali mavjudot deb hisoblanadi. Ularda otalik sevgisi yo'q, lekin sevgan jufti bolalariga bo'lgan sevgi va ularga o'rganish degan narsa bor. Bolalarda urg'ochilar hukmronlik hirsini qondiradi; bolalar — mulk, mashg'ulot, ular uchun butunlay tushunarli narsa, u bilan vaysashlari mumkin: bularning hammasi birgalikda onalik sevgisi, — uni san'atkorning o'z asariga bo'lgan sevgisiga qiyoslash mumkin. Homiladorlik urg'ochilarni muloyimroq, kutuvchanroq, qo'rqoqroq, itoatkorroq qilgan; xuddi shunday, aqliy homiladorlik xarakterda ayollarga yaqin bo'lgan mulohazakorlarning xarakterini tug'diradi: — ular erkak onalar. — Hayvonlar orasida erkak jinsi go'zal jins deb hisoblanadi.

paras.en: 73. Saintly Cruelty. — A man holding a newly born child in his hands came to a saint. "What should I do with the child," he asked, "it is wretched, deformed, and has not even enough of life to die." "Kill it," cried the saint with a dreadful voice, "kill it, and then hold it in thy arms for three days and three nights to brand it on thy memory:—thus wilt thou never again beget a child when it is not the time for thee to beget."—When the man had heard this he went away disappointed; and many found fault with the saint because he had advised cruelty, for he had advised to kill the child. "But is it not more cruel to let it live?" asked the saint.
paras.uz: 73. Avliyolarcha shafqatsizlik. — Qo'lida yangi tug'ilgan bolani ushlagan bir odam avliyoning oldiga keldi. «Bola bilan nima qilay, — deb so'radi u, — u bechora, majruh va hatto o'lish uchun ham yetarlicha hayoti yo'q». «Uni o'ldir, — deb qichqirdi avliyo dahshatli ovoz bilan, — uni o'ldir, keyin xotirangga muhrlash uchun uch kecha-kunduz quchog'ingda tut: — shunda sen hech qachon tug'dirish vaqting bo'lmaganda boshqa bola tug'dirmaysan». — Odam buni eshitib, hafsalasi pir bo'lib ketdi; va ko'pchilik avliyoni shafqatsizlik maslahat bergani uchun aybladi, chunki u bolani o'ldirishni maslahat bergan edi. «Lekin uni yashashga qo'yib berish shafqatsizroq emasmi?» — deb so'radi avliyo.

paras.en: 74. The Unsuccessful. — Those poor women always fail of success who become agitated and uncertain, and talk too much in presence of him whom they love; for men are most successfully seduced by a certain subtle and phlegmatic tenderness.
paras.uz: 74. Muvaffaqiyatsizlar. — Sevgan odamining oldida hayajonlanib, ikkilanib, haddan tashqari ko'p gapiradigan o'sha bechora ayollar doimo muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchraydi; chunki erkaklarni ma'lum bir nozik va sovuqqon muloyimlik eng muvaffaqiyatli yo'ldan uradi.

paras.en: 75. The Third Sex. — "A small man is a paradox, but still a man,—but the small woman seems to me to be of another sex in comparison with well-grown ones"—said an old dancing-master. A small woman is never beautiful—said old Aristotle.
paras.uz: 75. Uchinchi jins. — «Kichkina erkak — paradoks, lekin baribir erkak, — kichkina ayol esa menga yaxshi o'sganlar bilan solishtirganda boshqa jinsdandek tuyuladi», — dedi keksa raqs ustasi. Kichkina ayol hech qachon go'zal emas — degan keksa Aristotel.

paras.en: 76. The greatest Danger. — Had there not at all times been a larger number of men who regarded the cultivation of their mind—their "rationality"—as their pride, their obligation, their virtue, and were injured or shamed by all play of fancy and extravagance of thinking—as lovers of "sound common sense":—mankind would long ago have perished! Incipient insanity has hovered, and hovers continually over mankind as its greatest danger: that is precisely the breaking out of inclination in feeling, seeing, and hearing; the enjoyment of the unruliness of the mind; the delight in human unreason. It is not truth and certainty that is the antithesis of the world of the insane, but the universality and all-obligatoriness of a belief, in short, non-voluntariness in forming opinions.
paras.uz: 76. Eng katta xavf. — Agar barcha zamonlarda o'z aqlini — o'zining «aqlliligini» — g'ururi, majburiyati, fazilati deb bilgan va fantaziyaning har qanday o'yini va fikrlashning haddan oshishidan zarar ko'rgan yoki uyalgan — «sog'lom aql» ishqibozlari sifatida — ko'proq erkaklar bo'lmaganida, insoniyat allaqachon halok bo'lgan bo'lardi! Boshlanayotgan telbalik insoniyat ustida uning eng katta xavfi sifatida aylanib yurgan va doimo aylanib yuradi: bu aynan his qilish, ko'rish va eshitishda moyillikning otilib chiqishi; aqlning bebaoshligidan zavqlanish; inson aqlsizligidan lazzatlanish. Telbalar dunyosining qarama-qarshisi haqiqat va ishonchlilik emas, balki e'tiqodning umumiyligi va hamma uchun majburiyligi, qisqasi, fikr shakllantirishdagi ixtiyorsizlik.

paras.en: And the greatest labour of human beings hitherto has been to agree with one another regarding a great many things, and to impose upon themselves a law of agreement—indifferent whether these things are true or false. This is the discipline of the mind which has preserved mankind;—but the counter-impulses are still so powerful that one can really speak of the future of mankind with little confidence. The ideas of things still continually shift and move, and will perhaps alter more than ever in the future; it is continually the most select spirits themselves who strive against universal obligatoriness—the investigators of truth above all!
paras.uz: Va shu paytgacha insonlarning eng katta mehnati juda ko'p narsalar haqida bir-biri bilan kelishish va o'zlariga kelishuv qonunini yuklash bo'lgan — bu narsalar to'g'rimi yoki noto'g'rimi, farqi yo'q. Bu insoniyatni saqlab kelgan aql intizomi; — lekin qarshi mayllar hali shunchalik kuchliki, insoniyat kelajagi haqida haqiqatan ham kam ishonch bilan gapirish mumkin. Narsalar haqidagi g'oyalar hali ham doimo siljib, harakatlanib turadi va balki kelajakda har qachongidan ko'proq o'zgarar; umumiy majburiylikka qarshi doimo eng tanlangan ruhlarning o'zlari kurashadi — eng avvalo haqiqat tadqiqotchilari!

paras.en: The accepted belief, as the belief of all the world, continually engenders a disgust and a new longing in the more ingenious minds; and already the slow tempo which it demands for all intellectual processes (the imitation of the tortoise, which is here recognised as the rule) makes the artists and poets runaways:—it is in these impatient spirits that a downright delight in delirium breaks out, because delirium has such a joyful tempo! Virtuous intellects, therefore, are needed—ah! I want to use the least ambiguous word,—virtuous stupidity is needed, imperturbable conductors of the slow spirits are needed, in order that the faithful of the great collective belief may remain with one another and dance their dance further: it is a necessity of the first importance that here enjoins and demands. We others are the exceptions and the danger,—we eternally need protection!—Well, there can actually be something said in favour of the exceptions provided that they never want to become the rule.
paras.uz: Qabul qilingan e'tiqod, butun dunyoning e'tiqodi sifatida, zukkoroq aqllarda doimo jirkanish va yangi sog'inch tug'diradi; va u barcha aqliy jarayonlar uchun talab qiladigan sekin tempning o'zi (bu yerda qoida deb tan olingan toshbaqaga taqlid) san'atkorlar va shoirlarni qochoqqa aylantiradi: — aynan shu sabrsiz ruhlarda alahsirashdan chinakam zavq otilib chiqadi, chunki alahsirashning tempi shunchalik quvnoq! Shuning uchun fazilatli aqllar kerak — oh! men eng kam ikki ma'noli so'zni ishlatmoqchiman, — fazilatli ahmoqlik kerak, sekin ruhlarning sarosimaga tushmas yo'lboshchilari kerak, toki buyuk umumiy e'tiqod ahli bir-biri bilan qolib, o'z raqsini davom ettirsin: bu yerda buyuradigan va talab qiladigan narsa birinchi darajali zarurat. Biz boshqalar — istisnolar va xavfmiz, — bizga abadiy himoya kerak! — Xo'sh, agar istisnolar hech qachon qoidaga aylanishni istamasa, ular foydasiga haqiqatan ham nimadir aytish mumkin.

paras.en: 77. The Animal with good Conscience. — It is not unknown to me that there is vulgarity in everything that pleases Southern Europe—whether it be Italian opera (for example, Rossini's and Bellini's), or the Spanish adventure-romance (most readily accessible to us in the French garb of Gil Blas)—but it does not offend me, any more than the vulgarity which one encounters in a walk through Pompeii, or even in the reading of every ancient book: what is the reason of this? Is it because shame is lacking here, and because the vulgar always comes forward just as sure and certain of itself as anything noble, lovely, and passionate in the same kind of music or romance? "The animal has its rights like man, so let it run about freely; and you, my dear fellow-man, are still this animal, in spite of all!"—that seems to me the moral of the case, and the peculiarity of southern humanity.
paras.uz: 77. Vijdoni toza hayvon. — Menga Janubiy Yevropani zavqlantiradigan hamma narsada qo'pollik borligi noma'lum emas — xoh italyan operasi (masalan, Rossini va Bellinining operalari), xoh ispan sarguzasht romani (biz uchun eng oson fransuzcha «Jil Blaz» kiyimida) — lekin u meni Pompeyda sayr qilganda yoki hatto har bir antik kitobni o'qiganda uchraydigan qo'pollikdan ko'ra ko'proq ranjitmaydi: buning sababi nima? Bu yerda uyat yo'qligi va qo'pol narsa doimo o'sha turdagi musiqa yoki romandagi har qanday olijanob, yoqimli va ehtirosli narsa kabi o'ziga ishonchli va amin bo'lib oldinga chiqqani uchunmi? «Hayvonning ham inson kabi huquqlari bor, shuning uchun erkin yugursin; sen esa, aziz birodarim, hamma narsaga qaramay hali ham shu hayvonsan!» — menimcha, bu holatning ibrati va janubiy insoniyatning o'ziga xosligi shu.

paras.en: Bad taste has its rights like good taste, and even a prerogative over the latter when it is the great requisite, the sure satisfaction, and as it were a universal language, an immediately intelligible mask and attitude; the excellent, select taste on the other hand has always something of a seeking, tentative character, not fully certain that it understands,—it is never, and has never been popular! The masque is and remains popular! So let all this masquerade run along in the melodies and cadences, in the leaps and merriment of the rhythm of these operas! Quite the ancient life! What does one understand of it, if one does not understand the delight in the masque, the good conscience of all masquerade!
paras.uz: Yomon didning ham yaxshi did kabi huquqlari bor, hatto u katta ehtiyoj, ishonchli qoniqish va go'yo umumiy til, darhol tushunarli niqob va holat bo'lganda, ikkinchisidan ustunlikka ham ega; ajoyib, tanlangan did esa aksincha doimo qandaydir izlanuvchan, sinovchan xarakterga ega, tushunganiga to'liq ishonmaydi, — u hech qachon ommabop emas va hech qachon bo'lmagan! Niqob ommabop va shunday qoladi! Shuning uchun bu operalar ritmining kuylarida va kadanslarida, sakrashlari va quvnoqligida bu butun maskarad yugurib yuraversin! Xuddi antik hayot! Agar niqobdan zavqlanishni, har qanday maskaradning toza vijdonini tushunmasa, odam undan nimani tushunadi!

paras.en: Here is the bath and the refreshment of the ancient spirit:—and perhaps this bath was still more necessary for the rare and sublime natures of the ancient world than for the vulgar.—On the other hand, a vulgar turn in northern works, for example in German music, offends me unutterably. There is shame in it, the artist has lowered himself in his own sight, and could not even avoid blushing: we are ashamed with him, and are so hurt because we surmise that he believed he had to lower himself on our account.
paras.uz: Mana antik ruhning hammomi va yangilanishi: — va balki bu hammom antik dunyoning kamyob va yuksak tabiatlari uchun qo'pollardan ko'ra ham zarurroq bo'lgandir. — Boshqa tomondan, shimoliy asarlardagi qo'pol burilish, masalan, nemis musiqasida, meni so'z bilan aytib bo'lmas darajada ranjitadi. Unda uyat bor, san'atkor o'z nazarida o'zini pasaytirgan va hatto qizarishdan ham qochib qutula olmagan: biz u bilan birga uyalamiz va shunchalik ranjiymizki, u biz uchun o'zini pasaytirishi kerak deb ishonganini taxmin qilamiz.

paras.en: 78. What we should be Grateful for. — It is only the artists, and especially the theatrical artists who have furnished men with eyes and ears to hear and see with some pleasure what everyone is in himself, what he experiences and aims at: it is only they who have taught us how to estimate the hero that is concealed in each of these common-place men, and the art of looking at ourselves from a distance as heroes, and as it were simplified and transfigured,—the art of "putting ourselves on the stage" before ourselves. It is thus only that we get beyond some of the paltry details in ourselves! Without that art we should be nothing but fore-ground, and would live absolutely under the spell of the perspective which makes the closest and the commonest seem immensely large and like reality in itself.—Perhaps there is merit of a similar kind in the religion which commanded us to look at the sinfulness of every individual man with a magnifying-glass, and to make a great, immortal criminal out of the sinner; in that it put eternal perspectives around man, it taught him to see himself from a distance, and as something past, something entire.
paras.uz: 78. Biz nima uchun minnatdor bo'lishimiz kerak. — Faqat san'atkorlar, ayniqsa teatr san'atkorlari odamlarga har kim o'zida nima ekanini, nimani boshdan kechirishi va nimaga intilishini qandaydir zavq bilan eshitish va ko'rish uchun ko'z va quloq berishgan: faqat ular bizga bu oddiy odamlarning har birida yashiringan qahramonni qanday baholashni va o'zimizga uzoqdan qahramon sifatida, go'yo soddalashtirilgan va qiyofasi o'zgargan holda qarash san'atini — o'zimizni o'zimiz oldida «sahnaga qo'yish» san'atini o'rgatishgan. Faqat shu tariqa biz o'zimizdagi ba'zi arzimas tafsilotlardan narida o'tamiz! Bu san'atsiz biz faqat oldingi plandan iborat bo'lardik va eng yaqin va eng oddiy narsani ulkan katta va o'z-o'zidan haqiqatdek ko'rsatadigan istiqbol sehri ostida mutlaqo yashardik. — Balki bizga har bir alohida odamning gunohkorligiga lupa bilan qarashni va gunohkordan buyuk, o'lmas jinoyatchi yasashni buyurgan dinda ham shunga o'xshash xizmat bordir; u inson atrofiga abadiy istiqbollar qo'yib, unga o'zini uzoqdan va o'tib ketgan narsa, butun narsa sifatida ko'rishni o'rgatdi.

paras.en: 79. The Charm of Imperfection. — I see here a poet, who, like so many men, exercises a higher charm by his imperfections than by all that is rounded off and takes perfect shape under his hands,—indeed, he derives his advantage and reputation far more from his actual limitations than from his abundant powers. His work never expresses altogether what he would really like to express, what he would like to have seen: he appears to have had the foretaste of a vision and never the vision itself:—but an extraordinary longing for this vision has remained in his soul; and from this he derives his equally extraordinary eloquence of longing and craving.
paras.uz: 79. Nomukammallikning jozibasi. — Men bu yerda bir shoirni ko'raman, u ko'p odamlar kabi o'z nomukammalliklari bilan qo'llari ostida yumaloqlanib, mukammal shakl olgan hamma narsadan ko'ra yuksakroq jozibaga ega, — haqiqatan ham, u o'z foydasi va obro'sini mo'l kuchlaridan ko'ra haqiqiy cheklanganliklaridan ancha ko'proq oladi. Uning asari hech qachon u aslida ifodalamoqchi bo'lgan narsani, ko'rmoqchi bo'lgan narsani butunlay ifodalamaydi: u go'yo vahiyning oldindan ta'mini tatib ko'rgan, lekin hech qachon vahiyning o'zini emas: — lekin uning qalbida bu vahiyga g'ayrioddiy sog'inch qolgan; va u xuddi shunday g'ayrioddiy sog'inch va tashnalik notiqligini shundan oladi.

paras.en: With this he raises those who listen to him above his work and above all "works," and gives them wings to rise higher than hearers have ever risen before, thus making them poets and seers themselves; they then show an admiration for the originator of their happiness, as if he had led them immediately to the vision of his holiest and ultimate verities, as if he had reached his goal, and had actually seen and communicated his vision. It is to the advantage of his reputation that he has not really arrived at his goal.
paras.uz: Shu bilan u o'zini tinglayotganlarni o'z asaridan va barcha «asarlar»dan yuqori ko'taradi va ularga tinglovchilar hech qachon ko'tarilmagan darajadan yuqoriroq ko'tarilish uchun qanot beradi, shu tariqa ularning o'zlarini shoir va ko'regon qiladi; o'shanda ular baxtlarining yaratuvchisiga, go'yo u ularni bevosita o'zining eng muqaddas va so'nggi haqiqatlarini ko'rishga olib borgandek, go'yo u maqsadiga yetgan va vahiyini haqiqatan ko'rib, yetkazgandek hayrat bildiradi. U aslida maqsadiga yetmaganligi uning obro'si foydasiga.
