chapters.recap_uz: Ayollar tarbiyasining paradokslari, onalik va «avliyolarcha shafqatsizlik». Insoniyat uchun eng katta xavf — telbalik; uni umumiy e'tiqod va «fazilatli ahmoqlik» saqlab turadi. San'at bizga o'zimizni qahramon sifatida ko'rishni o'rgatgan.

chapters.title: Art and nature

paras.en: 80. Art and Nature. — The Greeks (or at least the Athenians) liked to hear good talking: indeed they had an eager inclination for it, which distinguished them more than anything else from non-Greeks. And so they required good talking even from passion on the stage, and submitted to the unnaturalness of dramatic verse with delight:—in nature, forsooth, passion is so sparing of words! so dumb and confused! Or if it finds words, so embarrassed and irrational and a shame to itself!
paras.uz: 80. San'at va tabiat. — Yunonlar (yoki hech bo'lmasa afinaliklar) yaxshi gapni eshitishni yaxshi ko'rishardi: haqiqatan ham, ularda bunga qizg'in moyillik bor edi va bu ularni yunon bo'lmaganlardan hamma narsadan ko'proq ajratib turardi. Shuning uchun ular sahnadagi ehtirosdan ham yaxshi gapni talab qilishgan va dramatik she'rning g'ayritabiiyligiga zavq bilan bo'ysunishgan: — tabiatda esa, haqiqatan, ehtiros so'zga shunchalik xasis! shunchalik soqov va chalkash! Yoki so'z topsa, shunchalik xijolatli, aqlsiz va o'zi uchun sharmandali!

paras.en: We have now, all of us, thanks to the Greeks, accustomed ourselves to this unnaturalness on the stage, as we endure that other unnaturalness, the singing passion, and willingly endure it, thanks to the Italians.—It has become a necessity to us, which we cannot satisfy out of the resources of actuality, to hear men talk well and in full detail in the most trying situations: it enraptures us at present when the tragic hero still finds words, reasons, eloquent gestures, and on the whole a bright spirituality, where life approaches the abysses, and where the actual man mostly loses his head, and certainly his fine language. This kind of deviation from nature is perhaps the most agreeable repast for man's pride: he loves art generally on account of it, as the expression of high, heroic unnaturalness and convention.
paras.uz: Endi hammamiz, yunonlar tufayli, sahnadagi bu g'ayritabiiylikka o'rganib qolganmiz, xuddi italyanlar tufayli o'sha boshqa g'ayritabiiylikka — kuylaydigan ehtirosga chidaganimiz va bajonidil chidaganimiz kabi. — Eng og'ir vaziyatlarda odamlarning yaxshi va batafsil gapirishini eshitish bizga ehtiyojga aylangan, uni haqiqatning manbalaridan qondira olmaymiz: hayot tubsizliklarga yaqinlashgan va haqiqiy odam ko'pincha boshini, albatta esa chiroyli tilini yo'qotadigan joyda tragik qahramon hali so'z, dalil, notiq imo-ishoralar va umuman yorqin ruhiylik topishi hozir bizni hayratga soladi. Tabiatdan bunday chetga chiqish, ehtimol, inson g'ururi uchun eng yoqimli taom: u umuman san'atni shu uchun, yuksak, qahramonona g'ayritabiiylik va shartlilikning ifodasi sifatida sevadi.

paras.en: One rightly objects to the dramatic poet when he does not transform everything into reason and speech, but always retains a remnant of silence:—just as one is dissatisfied with an operatic musician who cannot find a melody for the highest emotion, but only an emotional, "natural" stammering and crying. Here nature has to be contradicted! Here the common charm of illusion has to give place to a higher charm! The Greeks go far, far in this direction—frightfully far!
paras.uz: Dramatik shoir hamma narsani aql va nutqqa aylantirmay, doimo jimlikning bir qoldig'ini saqlab qolganda unga haqli ravishda e'tiroz bildiriladi: — xuddi eng yuksak tuyg'u uchun kuy topa olmay, faqat hissiy, «tabiiy» duduqlanish va qichqiriq topadigan opera musiqachisidan norozi bo'lganidek. Bu yerda tabiatga qarshi chiqish kerak! Bu yerda xayolning oddiy jozibasi yuksakroq jozibaga o'rin berishi kerak! Yunonlar bu yo'nalishda uzoqqa, uzoqqa boradi — dahshatli darajada uzoqqa!

paras.en: As they constructed the stage as narrow as possible and dispensed with all the effect of deep backgrounds, as they made pantomime and easy motion impossible to the actor, and transformed him into a solemn, stiff, masked bogey, so they have also deprived passion itself of its deep background, and have dictated to it a law of fine talk; indeed, they have really done everything to counteract the elementary effect of representations that inspire pity and terror: they did not want pity and terror,—with due deference, with the highest deference to Aristotle! but he certainly did not hit the nail, to say nothing of the head of the nail, when he spoke about the final aim of Greek tragedy!
paras.uz: Ular sahnani iloji boricha tor qurib, chuqur orqa fonning barcha ta'siridan voz kechganlari, aktyorga pantomima va yengil harakatni imkonsiz qilib, uni tantanali, qotib qolgan, niqobli qo'rqinchli qo'g'irchoqqa aylantirganlari kabi, ehtirosning o'zini ham chuqur orqa fonidan mahrum qilib, unga chiroyli gap qonunini buyurishgan; haqiqatan ham, ular achinish va qo'rquv uyg'otadigan tasvirlarning elementar ta'siriga qarshi turish uchun hamma narsani qilishgan: ular achinish va qo'rquvni istamagan, — Aristotelga tegishli hurmat bilan, eng yuksak hurmat bilan! lekin u yunon tragediyasining oxirgi maqsadi haqida gapirganda, mixning boshiga u yoqda tursin, mixning o'ziga ham urmagani aniq!

paras.en: Let us but look at the Grecian tragic poets with respect to what most excited their diligence, their inventiveness, and their emulation,—certainly it was not the intention of subjugating the spectators by emotion! The Athenian went to the theatre to hear fine talking! And fine talking was arrived at by Sophocles!—pardon me this heresy!—It is very different with serious opera: all its masters make it their business to prevent their personages being understood. "An occasional word picked up may come to the assistance of the inattentive listener; but on the whole the situation must be self-explanatory,—the talking is of no account!"—so they all think, and so they have all made fun of the words.
paras.uz: Keling, yunon tragik shoirlariga ularning tirishqoqligini, ixtirochiligini va raqobatini eng ko'p qo'zg'atgan narsa nuqtai nazaridan qaraylik, — albatta bu tomoshabinlarni his-tuyg'u bilan bo'ysundirish niyati emas edi! Afinalik teatrga chiroyli gap eshitish uchun borardi! Chiroyli gapga esa Sofokl erishgan edi! — bu bid'atimni kechiringlar! — Jiddiy opera bilan butunlay boshqacha: uning barcha ustalari o'z qahramonlarining tushunilishiga yo'l qo'ymaslikni o'z ishi qilib olgan. «Ba'zan ilib olingan bir so'z diqqatsiz tinglovchiga yordamga kelishi mumkin; lekin umuman olganda vaziyat o'zini o'zi tushuntirishi kerak, — gapning ahamiyati yo'q!» — ularning hammasi shunday o'ylaydi va shuning uchun hammasi so'zlar ustidan kulgan.

paras.en: Perhaps they have only lacked courage to express fully their extreme contempt for words: a little additional insolence in Rossini, and he would have allowed la-la-la-la to be sung throughout—and it might have been the rational course! The personages of the opera are not meant to be believed "in their words," but in their tones! That is the difference, that is the fine unnaturalness on account of which people go to the opera!
paras.uz: Balki ularga so'zlarga bo'lgan o'ta nafratlarini to'liq ifodalash uchun faqat jasorat yetishmagandir: Rossinida ozgina qo'shimcha surbetlik bo'lganida, u boshdan-oxir la-la-la-la kuylashga ruxsat bergan bo'lardi — va bu aqlli yo'l bo'lishi mumkin edi! Opera qahramonlariga «so'zlarida» emas, balki ohanglarida ishonish kerak! Farq shunda, odamlar operaga aynan shu nozik g'ayritabiiylik uchun boradi!

paras.en: Even the recitativo secco is not really intended to be heard as words and text: this kind of half-music is meant rather in the first place to give the musical ear a little repose (the repose from melody, as from the sublimest, and on that account the most straining enjoyment of this art),—but very soon something different results, namely, an increasing impatience, an increasing resistance, a new longing for entire music, for melody.—How is it with the art of Richard Wagner as seen from this standpoint? Is it perhaps the same? Perhaps otherwise? It would often seem to me as if one needed to have learned by heart both the words and the music of his creations before the performances; for without that—so it seemed to me—one may hear neither the words, nor even the music.
paras.uz: Hatto recitativo secco ham aslida so'z va matn sifatida eshitilishi uchun mo'ljallanmagan: bu yarim musiqa ko'proq birinchi navbatda musiqiy qulog'iga ozgina dam berish uchun mo'ljallangan (kuydan dam — bu san'atning eng yuksak va shuning uchun eng zo'riqtiradigan zavqidan dam), — lekin tez orada boshqa narsa kelib chiqadi, ya'ni ortib boradigan sabrsizlik, ortib boradigan qarshilik, to'liq musiqaga, kuyga yangi sog'inch. — Rixard Vagner san'ati bu nuqtai nazardan qanday? Balki xuddi shundaydir? Balki boshqachadir? Menga ko'pincha shunday tuyulardiki, uning asarlarining so'zlarini ham, musiqasini ham tomoshadan oldin yod olish kerak; chunki busiz — menga shunday tuyulgan — na so'zlarni, na hatto musiqani eshitish mumkin.

paras.en: 81. Grecian Taste. — "What is beautiful in it?"—asked a certain geometrician, after a performance of the Iphigenia—"there is nothing proved in it!" Could the Greeks have been so far from this taste? In Sophocles at least "everything is proved."
paras.uz: 81. Yunon didi. — «Bunda nima go'zal? — deb so'radi bir geometr «Ifigeniya» tomoshasidan keyin, — bunda hech narsa isbotlanmagan!» Yunonlar bu diddan shunchalik uzoq bo'lganmidi? Hech bo'lmasa Sofoklda «hamma narsa isbotlangan».

paras.en: 82. Esprit Un-Grecian. — The Greeks were exceedingly logical and plain in all their thinking; they did not get tired of it, at least during their long flourishing period, as is so often the case with the French; who too willingly made a little excursion into the opposite, and in fact endure the spirit of logic only when it betrays its sociable courtesy, its sociable self-renunciation, by a multitude of such little excursions into its opposite. Logic appears to them as necessary as bread and water, but also like these as a kind of prison-fare, as soon as it is to be taken pure and by itself. In good society one must never want to be in the right absolutely and solely, as all pure logic requires; hence, the little dose of irrationality in all French esprit.—The social sense of the Greeks was far less developed than that of the French in the present and the past; hence, so little esprit in their cleverest men, hence, so little wit, even in their wags, hence—alas! But people will not readily believe these tenets of mine, and how much of the kind I have still on my soul!—Est res magna tacere—says Martial, like all garrulous people.
paras.uz: 82. Yunoncha bo'lmagan esprit. — Yunonlar barcha fikrlashlarida nihoyatda mantiqiy va oddiy edi; ular bundan charchashmagan, hech bo'lmasa uzoq gullagan davrida, fransuzlarda ko'pincha bo'lgani kabi emas; fransuzlar qarama-qarshi tomonga kichkina sayohatga juda bajonidil chiqishgan va aslida mantiq ruhiga faqat u o'zining ijtimoiy xushmuomalaligini, ijtimoiy o'zidan voz kechishini qarama-qarshi tomonga bunday ko'plab kichkina sayohatlar bilan oshkor qilgandagina chidashadi. Mantiq ularga non va suvdek zarur ko'rinadi, lekin ular kabi sof va yolg'iz holda qabul qilinishi kerak bo'lishi bilanoq, qamoqxona taomidek ham. Yaxshi jamiyatda hech qachon har qanday sof mantiq talab qilganidek mutlaq va yolg'iz haq bo'lishni istamaslik kerak; shuning uchun har qanday fransuz espritida — zakovatida kichkina aqlsizlik dozasi bor. — Yunonlarning ijtimoiy tuyg'usi hozirgi va o'tmishdagi fransuzlarnikidan ancha kam rivojlangan edi; shuning uchun ularning eng aqlli odamlarida shunchalik oz esprit, hatto hazilkashlarida shunchalik oz zakovat, shuning uchun — afsus! Lekin odamlar bu fikrlarimga osongina ishonmaydi va qalbimda bunday narsalardan yana qanchasi bor! — Est res magna tacere — Jim turish buyuk ishdir — deydi Martsial, barcha vaysaqilar kabi.

paras.en: 83. Translations. — One can estimate the amount of the historical sense which an age possesses by the way in which it makes translations and seeks to embody in itself past periods and literatures. The French of Corneille, and even the French of the Revolution, appropriated Roman antiquity in a manner for which we would no longer have the courage—owing to our superior historical sense. And Roman antiquity itself: how violently, and at the same time how naïvely, did it lay its hand on everything excellent and elevated belonging to the older Grecian antiquity! How they translated these writings into the Roman present! How they wiped away intentionally and unconcernedly the wing-dust of the butterfly moment!
paras.uz: 83. Tarjimalar. — Davrning tarixiy tuyg'usi miqdorini u qanday tarjima qilishi va o'tmish davrlar va adabiyotlarni o'ziga qanday singdirishga intilishiga qarab baholash mumkin. Kornel davridagi fransuzlar, hatto Inqilob davridagi fransuzlar ham Rim antik davrini shunday tarzda o'zlashtirishganki, bizda endi — yuksakroq tarixiy tuyg'umiz tufayli — bunga jasorat yetmasdi. Rim antik davrining o'zi esa: u eski yunon antik davriga tegishli barcha ajoyib va yuksak narsalarga qanchalik zo'ravonlik bilan va shu bilan birga qanchalik sodda qo'l qo'ydi! Ular bu asarlarni Rim hozirgi zamoniga qanday tarjima qilishdi! Kapalak lahzasining qanot changini qanday qasddan va beparvo artib tashlashdi!

paras.en: It is thus that Horace now and then translated Alcæus or Archilochus, it is thus that Propertius translated Callimachus and Philetas (poets of equal rank with Theocritus, if we be allowed to judge): of what consequence was it to them that the actual creator experienced this and that, and had inscribed the indication thereof in his poem!—as poets they were averse to the antiquarian, inquisitive spirit which precedes the historical sense; as poets they did not respect those essentially personal traits and names, nor anything peculiar to city, coast, or century, such as its costume and mask, but at once put the present and the Roman in its place. They seem to us to ask: "Should we not make the old new for ourselves, and adjust ourselves to it?
paras.uz: Goratsiy ba'zan Alkey yoki Arxiloxni shunday tarjima qilgan, Propertsiy Kallimax va Filetni (agar hukm chiqarishga ruxsat berilsa, Teokrit bilan teng darajadagi shoirlar) shunday tarjima qilgan: haqiqiy ijodkor u yoki bu narsani boshdan kechirgani va uning belgisini she'riga yozgani ularga nima ahamiyatga ega edi! — shoir sifatida ular tarixiy tuyg'udan oldin keladigan antikvar, qiziquvchan ruhni yoqtirmasdi; shoir sifatida ular o'sha mohiyatan shaxsiy xususiyatlar va nomlarni, shahar, qirg'oq yoki asrga xos hech narsani, masalan, uning kiyimi va niqobini hurmat qilmasdi, balki darhol uning o'rniga hozirgi va Rimga xos narsani qo'yardi. Ular bizdan go'yo so'rayotgandek: «Eskini o'zimiz uchun yangi qilmasligimiz va unga moslashmasligimiz kerakmi?

paras.en: Should we not be allowed to inspire this dead body with our soul? for it is dead indeed: how loathsome is everything dead!"—They did not know the pleasure of the historical sense; the past and the alien was painful to them, and as Romans it was an incitement to a Roman conquest. In fact, they conquered when they translated,—not only in that they omitted the historical: no, they added also allusions to the present; above all, they struck out the name of the poet and put their own in its place—not with the feeling of theft, but with the very best conscience of the imperium Romanum.
paras.uz: Bu o'lik tanaga o'z ruhimizni puflashga ruxsat berilmasligi kerakmi? axir u haqiqatan ham o'lik: o'lik narsaning hammasi qanchalik jirkanch!» — Ular tarixiy tuyg'u lazzatini bilishmagan; o'tmish va yot narsa ularga og'riqli edi va rimliklar sifatida Rim istilosiga undov edi. Haqiqatan ham, ular tarjima qilganda istilo qilishgan, — nafaqat tarixiylikni tushirib qoldirganlari bilan: yo'q, ular hozirgi zamonga ishoralar ham qo'shishgan; eng avvalo, shoirning ismini o'chirib, o'rniga o'zlarinikini qo'yishgan — o'g'irlik tuyg'usi bilan emas, balki imperium Romanum — Rim imperiyasining eng toza vijdoni bilan.

chapters.recap_uz: Yunonlar sahnada ham chiroyli gapni istashgan: san'at tabiatdan ataylab chetga chiqadi. Opera esa so'zlarga ahamiyat bermaydi. Rimliklar yunon asarlarini tarjima qilganda ularni zabt etgan — o'z davriga moslab, shoir ismini o'chirib.

chapters.title: The origin of poetry

paras.en: 84. The Origin of Poetry. — The lovers of the fantastic in man, who at the same time represent the doctrine of instinctive morality, draw this conclusion: "Granted that utility has been honoured at all times as the highest divinity, where then in all the world has poetry come from?—this rhythmising of speech which thwarts rather than furthers plainness of communication, and which, nevertheless, has sprung up everywhere on the earth, and still springs up, as a mockery of all useful purpose! The wildly beautiful irrationality of poetry refutes you, ye utilitarians! The wish to get rid of utility in some way—that is precisely what has elevated man, that is what has inspired him to morality and art!" Well, I must here speak for once to please the utilitarians,—they are so seldom in the right that it is pitiful!
paras.uz: 84. She'riyatning kelib chiqishi. — Insondagi fantastik narsaning ishqibozlari, bir vaqtning o'zida instinktiv axloq ta'limotini ifodalaydiganlar, shunday xulosa chiqarishadi: «Faraz qilaylik, foydalilik barcha zamonlarda eng oliy ilohiyat sifatida hurmat qilingan, unda butun dunyoda she'riyat qayerdan kelgan? — nutqning bu ritmlanishi aloqaning ravshanligiga yordam berishdan ko'ra to'sqinlik qiladi va shunga qaramay butun yer yuzida, har qanday foydali maqsadni masxara qilib, paydo bo'lgan va hali ham paydo bo'lmoqda! She'riyatning yovvoyi go'zal aqlsizligi sizni rad etadi, ey utilitaristlar! Qandaydir tarzda foydalilikdan qutulish istagi — insonni aynan shu yuksaltirgan, uni axloq va san'atga aynan shu ilhomlantirgan!» Xo'sh, bu yerda bir marta utilitaristlarni xursand qilish uchun gapirishim kerak, — ular shunchalik kamdan-kam haq bo'ladiki, achinarli!

paras.en: In the old times which called poetry into being, people had still utility in view with respect to it, and a very important utility—at the time when rhythm was introduced into speech, the force which arranges all the particles of the sentence anew, commands the choosing of the words, recolours the thought, and makes it more obscure, more foreign, and more distant: to be sure a superstitious utility! It was intended that a human entreaty should be more profoundly impressed upon the Gods by virtue of rhythm, after it had been observed that men could remember a verse better than an unmetrical speech. It was likewise thought that people could make themselves audible at greater distances by the rhythmical beat; the rhythmical prayer seemed to come nearer to the ear of the Gods.
paras.uz: She'riyatni dunyoga keltirgan qadim zamonlarda odamlar unga nisbatan hali foydalilikni ko'zda tutishgan, va juda muhim foydalilikni — nutqqa ritm kiritilgan paytda, gapning barcha zarrachalarini yangidan tartibga soladigan, so'zlarni tanlashni buyuradigan, fikrni qayta bo'yaydigan va uni qorong'iroq, begonaroq va uzoqroq qiladigan kuch: albatta, xurofiy foydalilik! Odamlar ritmsiz nutqdan ko'ra she'rni yaxshiroq eslab qolishini payqagach, inson iltijosi ritm tufayli xudolarga chuqurroq ta'sir qiladi deb mo'ljallangan. Shuningdek, odamlar ritmik zarba bilan o'zlarini uzoqroq masofalardan eshittira oladi deb o'ylashgan; ritmik ibodat xudolarning qulog'iga yaqinroq kelayotgandek tuyulgan.

paras.en: Above all, however, people wanted to have the advantage of the elementary conquest which man experiences in himself when he hears music: rhythm is a constraint; it produces an unconquerable desire to yield, to join in; not only the step of the foot, but also the soul itself follows the measure,—probably the soul of the Gods also, as people thought! They attempted, therefore, to constrain the Gods by rhythm and to exercise a power over them; they threw poetry around the Gods like a magic noose. There was a still more wonderful idea, and it has perhaps operated most powerfully of all in the originating of poetry.
paras.uz: Biroq eng avvalo, odamlar inson musiqa eshitganda o'zida boshdan kechiradigan elementar zabt etishdan foydalanishni istashgan: ritm — majburlov; u bo'ysunish, qo'shilish uchun yengib bo'lmas istak tug'diradi; nafaqat oyoq qadami, balki ruhning o'zi ham o'lchovga ergashadi, — ehtimol, xudolarning ruhi ham, deb o'ylashgan odamlar! Shuning uchun ular xudolarni ritm bilan majburlashga va ular ustidan hokimiyat o'rnatishga urinishgan; ular she'riyatni xudolar atrofiga sehrli sirtmoqdek tashlashgan. Yana ham ajoyibroq bir g'oya bor edi va u she'riyatning kelib chiqishida, ehtimol, hammadan kuchliroq ta'sir qilgan.

paras.en: Among the Pythagoreans it made its appearance as a philosophical doctrine and as an artifice of teaching: but long before there were philosophers music was acknowledged to possess the power of unburdening the emotions, of purifying the soul, of soothing the ferocia animi—and this was owing to the rhythmical element in music. When the proper tension and harmony of the soul were lost a person had to dance to the measure of the singer,—that was the recipe of this medical art. By means of it Terpander quieted a tumult, Empedocles calmed a maniac, Damon purged a love-sick youth; by means of it even the maddened, revengeful Gods were treated for the purpose of a cure.
paras.uz: Pifagorchilar orasida u falsafiy ta'limot va o'qitish usuli sifatida paydo bo'lgan: lekin faylasuflar bo'lishidan ancha oldin musiqa his-tuyg'ularni yengillatish, ruhni poklash, ferocia animi — ruhning yovvoyiligini tinchlantirish kuchiga ega deb tan olingan — va bu musiqadagi ritmik unsur tufayli edi. Ruhning to'g'ri tarangligi va uyg'unligi yo'qolganda, odam qo'shiqchining o'lchoviga raqs tushishi kerak edi, — bu tibbiy san'atning retsepti shu edi. Uning yordamida Terpandr g'alayonni tinchitgan, Empedokl telbani tinchlantirgan, Damon ishqdan kasal yigitni poklagan; uning yordamida hatto quturgan, qasoskor xudolar ham davolash maqsadida muolaja qilingan.

paras.en: First of all, it was by driving the frenzy and wantonness of their emotions to the highest pitch, by making the furious mad, and the revengeful intoxicated with vengeance:—all the orgiastic cults seek to discharge the ferocia of a deity all at once and thus make an orgy, so that the deity may feel freer and quieter afterwards, and leave man in peace. Melos, according to its root, signifies a soothing means, not because the song is gentle itself, but because its after-effect makes gentle.—And not only in the religious song, but also in the secular song of the most ancient times the prerequisite is that the rhythm should exercise a magical influence; for example, in drawing water, or in rowing: the song is for the enchanting of the spirits supposed to be active thereby; it makes them obliging, involuntary, and the instruments of man.
paras.uz: Avvalo, ularning his-tuyg'ularining jazavasi va sho'xligini eng yuqori darajaga yetkazib, g'azablanganni telba, qasoskorni qasosdan mast qilib: — barcha orgiastik kultlar xudoning ferociasini — yovvoyiligini birdaniga bo'shatib, orgiya qilishga intiladi, toki xudo keyin o'zini erkinroq va sokinroq his qilsin va insonni tinch qo'ysin. Melos o'zagiga ko'ra tinchlantiruvchi vositani anglatadi, qo'shiqning o'zi muloyim bo'lgani uchun emas, balki uning keyingi ta'siri muloyim qilgani uchun. — Va nafaqat diniy qo'shiqda, balki eng qadimgi zamonlarning dunyoviy qo'shig'ida ham ritm sehrli ta'sir ko'rsatishi shart; masalan, suv tortishda yoki eshkak eshishda: qo'shiq bunda faol deb taxmin qilingan ruhlarni sehrlash uchun; u ularni xushmuomala, ixtiyorsiz va inson quroliga aylantiradi.

paras.en: And as often as a person acts he has occasion to sing, every action is dependent on the assistance of spirits: magic song and incantation appear to be the original form of poetry. When verse also came to be used in oracles—the Greeks said that the hexameter was invented at Delphi,—the rhythm was here also intended to exercise a compulsory influence. To make a prophecy—that means originally (according to what seems to me the probable derivation of the Greek word) to determine something; people thought they could determine the future by winning Apollo over to their side: he who, according to the most ancient idea, is far more than a foreseeing deity.
paras.uz: Va odam har safar harakat qilganda kuylashga sabab bor, har bir harakat ruhlarning yordamiga bog'liq: sehrli qo'shiq va afsun she'riyatning asl shakli bo'lib ko'rinadi. She'r bashoratlarda ham ishlatila boshlaganda — yunonlar geksametr Delfida ixtiro qilingan deyishgan, — bu yerda ham ritm majburlovchi ta'sir ko'rsatishi uchun mo'ljallangan. Bashorat qilish — bu dastlab (menga yunon so'zining ehtimoliy kelib chiqishi shunday tuyuladi) nimanidir belgilash demak; odamlar Apollonni o'z tomonlariga og'dirib, kelajakni belgilay olamiz deb o'ylashgan: u eng qadimgi g'oyaga ko'ra oldindan ko'ruvchi xudodan ancha ko'proq narsa.

paras.en: According as the formula is pronounced with literal and rhythmical correctness, it determines the future: the formula, however, is the invention of Apollo, who as the God of rhythm, can also determine the goddesses of fate.—Looked at and investigated as a whole, was there ever anything more serviceable to the ancient superstitious species of human being than rhythm? People could do everything with it: they could make labour go on magically; they could compel a God to appear, to be near at hand, and listen to them; they could arrange the future for themselves according to their will; they could unburden their own souls of any kind of excess (of anxiety, of mania, of sympathy, of revenge), and not only their own soul, but the souls of the most evil spirits,—without verse a person was nothing, by means of verse a person became almost a God.
paras.uz: Formula so'zma-so'z va ritmik jihatdan to'g'ri talaffuz qilinishiga qarab, u kelajakni belgilaydi: biroq formula Apollonning ixtirosi, u ritm xudosi sifatida taqdir ma'budalarini ham belgilay oladi. — Butun holda qaralganda va tekshirilganda, qadimgi xurofiy inson turi uchun ritmdan ko'ra foydaliroq narsa bo'lganmi? Odamlar u bilan hamma narsani qila olardi: mehnatni sehrli tarzda davom ettira olardi; xudoni paydo bo'lishga, yaqinda bo'lishga va ularni tinglashga majbur qila olardi; kelajakni o'z irodasiga ko'ra o'zlari uchun tartibga sola olardi; o'z ruhlarini har qanday ortiqchalikdan (xavotir, jazava, hamdardlik, qasos) yengillata olardi, va nafaqat o'z ruhini, balki eng yovuz ruhlarning ruhini ham, — she'rsiz odam hech narsa emas edi, she'r orqali odam deyarli xudoga aylanardi.

paras.en: Such a fundamental feeling no longer allows itself to be fully eradicated,—and even now, after millenniums of long labour in combating such superstition, the very wisest of us occasionally becomes the fool of rhythm, be it only that one perceives a thought to be truer when it has a metrical form and approaches with a divine hopping. Is it not a very funny thing that the most serious philosophers, however anxious they are in other respects for strict certainty, still appeal to poetical sayings in order to give their thoughts force and credibility?—and yet it is more dangerous to a truth when the poet assents to it than when he contradicts it! For, as Homer says, "The singers speak much falsehood!"—
paras.uz: Bunday asosiy tuyg'u endi o'zini butunlay yo'q qilishga yo'l qo'ymaydi, — va hatto hozir ham, bunday xurofotga qarshi kurashning ming yillik uzoq mehnatidan keyin, eng dono odamimiz ham ba'zan ritmning ahmog'iga aylanadi, faqat fikr vaznli shaklga ega bo'lib, ilohiy sakrash bilan yaqinlashganda uni haqiqatroq deb his qilishi bilan bo'lsa ham. Eng jiddiy faylasuflar, boshqa jihatlarda qat'iy ishonchlilikka qanchalik intilmasin, o'z fikrlariga kuch va ishonchlilik berish uchun hali ham she'riy hikmatlarga murojaat qilishi juda kulgili narsa emasmi? — vaholanki shoir haqiqatga qo'shilganda unga qarshi chiqqanidan ko'ra xavfliroq! Chunki Gomer aytganidek: «Qo'shiqchilar ko'p yolg'on gapiradi!» —

paras.en: 85. The Good and the Beautiful. — Artists glorify continually—they do nothing else,—and indeed they glorify all those conditions and things that have a reputation, so that man may feel himself good or great, or intoxicated, or merry, or pleased and wise by it. Those select things and conditions whose value for human happiness is regarded as secure and determined, are the objects of artists: they are ever lying in wait to discover such things, to transfer them into the domain of art. I mean to say that they are not themselves the valuers of happiness and of the happy ones, but they always press close to these valuers with the greatest curiosity and longing, in order immediately to use their valuations advantageously. As besides their impatience, they have also the big lungs of heralds and the feet of runners, they are likewise always among the first to glorify the new excellency, and often seem to be those who first of all called it good and valued it as good. This, however, as we have said, is an error; they are only faster and louder than the actual valuers:—And who then are these?—They are the rich and the leisurely.
paras.uz: 85. Yaxshi va go'zal. — San'atkorlar doimo ulug'laydi — ular boshqa hech narsa qilmaydi, — va haqiqatan ham, ular inson o'zini yaxshi yoki buyuk, yoki mast, yoki quvnoq, yoki mamnun va dono his qilishi uchun obro'ga ega bo'lgan barcha holatlar va narsalarni ulug'laydi. Inson baxti uchun qadri ishonchli va aniqlangan deb hisoblangan o'sha tanlangan narsalar va holatlar san'atkorlarning obyektlaridir: ular bunday narsalarni topib, san'at sohasiga ko'chirish uchun doimo pistirmada yotishadi. Aytmoqchimanki, ularning o'zlari baxtni va baxtlilarni baholovchilar emas, lekin ular doimo bu baholovchilarga eng katta qiziquvchanlik va sog'inch bilan yaqin bosib turishadi, toki ularning baholaridan darhol foydali ravishda foydalanishsin. Sabrsizliklaridan tashqari, ularda jarchilarning katta o'pkasi va yuguruvchilarning oyoqlari ham bo'lgani uchun, ular yangi ajoyiblikni ulug'laydiganlarning ham doimo birinchilari orasida bo'lishadi va ko'pincha uni birinchi bo'lib yaxshi deb atagan va yaxshi deb baholaganlardek ko'rinishadi. Biroq aytganimizdek, bu xato; ular haqiqiy baholovchilardan faqat tezroq va balandroq: — Xo'sh, ular kimlar? — Boylar va bekorchilar.

paras.en: 86. The Theatre. — This day has given me once more strong and elevated sentiments, and if I could have music and art in the evening, I know well what music and art I should not like to have; namely, none of that which would fain intoxicate its hearers and excite them to a crisis of strong and high feeling,—those men with commonplace souls, who in the evening are not like victors on triumphal cars, but like tired mules to whom life has rather too often applied the whip. What would those men at all know of "higher moods," unless there were expedients for causing ecstasy and idealistic strokes of the whip!—and thus they have their inspirers as they have their wines. But what is their drink and their drunkenness to me! Does the inspired one need wine?
paras.uz: 86. Teatr. — Bu kun menga yana bir bor kuchli va yuksak tuyg'ular berdi va agar kechqurun musiqa va san'at bo'lsa, qanday musiqa va san'atni istamasligimni yaxshi bilaman; ya'ni o'z tinglovchilarini mast qilmoqchi va ularni kuchli va yuksak tuyg'u inqiroziga qo'zg'atmoqchi bo'lganlarining hech birini, — kechqurun g'alaba aravalaridagi g'oliblarga emas, balki hayot juda ko'p marta qamchi urgan charchagan xachirlarga o'xshagan oddiy qalbli odamlarni. Agar vajd uyg'otish vositalari va idealistik qamchi zarbalari bo'lmasa, bu odamlar «yuksak kayfiyatlar» haqida umuman nima bilardi! — shuning uchun ularning sharoblari bo'lgani kabi ilhomlantiruvchilari ham bor. Lekin ularning ichimligi va mastligi menga nima! Ilhomlangan odamga sharob kerakmi?

paras.en: He rather looks with a kind of disgust at the agency and the agent which are here intended to produce an effect without sufficient reason,—an imitation of the high tide of the soul! What? One gives the mole wings and proud fancies—before going to sleep, before he creeps into his hole? One sends him into the theatre and puts great magnifying-glasses to his blind and tired eyes? Men, whose life is not "action" but business, sit in front of the stage and look at strange beings to whom life is more than business? "This is proper," you say, "this is entertaining, this is what culture wants!"—Well then! culture is too often lacking in me, for this sight is too often disgusting to me.
paras.uz: U ko'proq bu yerda yetarli sababsiz ta'sir ko'rsatishga mo'ljallangan vosita va vositachiga qandaydir jirkanish bilan qaraydi, — ruhning yuksak to'lqiniga taqlid! Nima? Ko'rsichqonga qanot va mag'rur xayollar beriladimi — uxlashdan oldin, iniga emaklab kirishidan oldin? Uni teatrga yuborib, ko'r va charchagan ko'zlariga katta lupalar qo'yiladimi? Hayoti «harakat» emas, balki ish-yumush bo'lgan odamlar sahna oldida o'tirib, hayoti ish-yumushdan ko'proq bo'lgan g'alati mavjudotlarga qarashadimi? «Bu to'g'ri, — deysiz, — bu qiziqarli, madaniyat buni istaydi!» — Unday bo'lsa! menda madaniyat juda ko'p yetishmaydi, chunki bu manzara menga juda ko'p jirkanch.

paras.en: He who has enough of tragedy and comedy in himself surely prefers to remain away from the theatre; or, as the exception, the whole procedure—theatre and public and poet included—becomes for him a truly tragic and comic play, so that the performed piece counts for little in comparison. He who is something like Faust and Manfred, what does it matter to him about the Fausts and Manfreds of the theatre!—while it certainly gives him something to think about that such figures are brought into the theatre at all. The strongest thoughts and passions before those who are not capable of thought and passion—but of intoxication only! And those as a means to this end! And theatre and music the hashish-smoking and betel-chewing of Europeans! Oh, who will narrate to us the whole history of narcotics!—It is almost the history of "culture," the so-called higher culture!
paras.uz: O'zida tragediya va komediya yetarli bo'lgan odam, albatta, teatrdan uzoqda qolishni afzal ko'radi; yoki, istisno sifatida, butun jarayon — teatr, jamoatchilik va shoir ham — u uchun chinakam tragik va komik o'yinga aylanadi, shunda ijro etilgan asar u bilan solishtirganda kam ahamiyatga ega bo'ladi. Faust va Manfredga o'xshagan odamga teatrdagi Faustlar va Manfredlarning nima ahamiyati bor! — garchi bunday qiyofalar umuman teatrga olib kelinishi unga albatta o'ylash uchun nimadir bersa ham. Eng kuchli fikrlar va ehtiroslar fikr va ehtirosga qodir bo'lmagan — faqat mastlikka qodir bo'lganlar oldida! Va ular shu maqsadga vosita sifatida! Teatr va musiqa esa — yevropaliklarning nasha chekishi va betel chaynashi! Oh, bizga giyohvand moddalarning butun tarixini kim so'zlab beradi! — Bu deyarli «madaniyat», yuksak deb ataladigan madaniyat tarixi!

paras.en: 87. The Conceit of Artists. — I think artists often do not know what they can do best, because they are too conceited, and have set their minds on something loftier than those little plants appear to be, which can grow up to perfection on their soil, fresh, rare, and beautiful. The final value of their own garden and vineyard is superciliously underestimated by them, and their love and their insight are not of the same quality. Here is a musician, who, more than any one else, has the genius for discovering the tones peculiar to suffering, oppressed, tortured souls, and who can endow even dumb animals with speech.
paras.uz: 87. San'atkorlarning manmanligi. — Menimcha, san'atkorlar ko'pincha nimani eng yaxshi qila olishini bilishmaydi, chunki ular haddan tashqari manman va o'z tuproqlarida yangi, kamyob va go'zal holda mukammallikkacha o'sa oladigan o'sha kichkina o'simliklardan yuksakroq narsaga ko'ngil qo'ygan. O'z bog'i va tokzorining oxirgi qadrini ular kibr bilan past baholashadi va ularning sevgisi va tushunchasi bir xil sifatda emas. Mana bir musiqachi, u hammadan ko'ra azob chekayotgan, ezilgan, qiynalgan qalblarga xos ohanglarni kashf etish dahosiga ega va hatto soqov hayvonlarga ham nutq bera oladi.

paras.en: No one equals him in the colours of the late autumn, in the indescribably touching happiness of a last, a final, and all too short enjoyment; he knows a chord for those secret and weird midnights of the soul when cause and effect seem out of joint, and when every instant something may originate "out of nothing." He draws his resources best of all out of the lower depths of human happiness, and so to speak, out of its drained goblet, where the bitterest and most nauseous drops have ultimately, for good or for ill, commingled with the sweetest.
paras.uz: Kech kuz ranglarida, oxirgi, so'nggi va haddan tashqari qisqa zavqning ta'riflab bo'lmas ta'sirli baxtida hech kim unga teng kelmaydi; u sabab va oqibat bir-biridan uzilgandek tuyuladigan va har lahzada «hech narsadan» nimadir paydo bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan ruhning o'sha sirli va g'alati yarim tunlari uchun akkord biladi. U o'z manbalarini eng yaxshisi inson baxtining quyi qa'rlaridan, aytish mumkinki, uning ichib bo'lingan kosasidan oladi, u yerda eng achchiq va eng ko'ngil aynitadigan tomchilar oxir-oqibat, yaxshilikka yoki yomonlikka, eng shirinlari bilan aralashib ketgan.

paras.en: He knows the weary shuffling along of the soul which can no longer leap or fly, yea, not even walk; he has the shy glance of concealed pain, of understanding without comfort, of leave-taking without avowal; yea, as the Orpheus of all secret misery, he is greater than anyone; and in fact much has been added to art by him which was hitherto inexpressible and not even thought worthy of art, and which was only to be scared away, by words, and not grasped—many small and quite microscopic features of the soul: yes, he is the master of miniature. But he does not wish to be so! His character is more in love with large walls and daring frescoes!
paras.uz: U endi sakray olmaydigan yoki ucha olmaydigan, ha, hatto yura ham olmaydigan ruhning charchab oyoq sudrashini biladi; unda yashirin og'riqning, tasallisiz tushunishning, tan olmay xayrlashishning uyatchan nigohi bor; ha, barcha yashirin baxtsizliklarning Orfeyi sifatida u hammadan buyuk; va haqiqatan ham, u tufayli san'atga shu paytgacha ifodalab bo'lmaydigan va hatto san'atga munosib deb hisoblanmagan, faqat so'zlar bilan cho'chitib yuborilishi mumkin bo'lgan va ushlab bo'lmaydigan ko'p narsa — ruhning ko'plab kichik va mutlaqo mikroskopik xususiyatlari qo'shildi: ha, u miniatyura ustasi. Lekin u shunday bo'lishni istamaydi! Uning xarakteri katta devorlar va dadil freskalarni ko'proq sevadi!

paras.en: He fails to see that his spirit has a different taste and inclination, and prefers to sit quietly in the corners of ruined houses:—concealed in this way, concealed even from himself, he there paints his proper masterpieces, all of which are very short, often only one bar in length,—there only does he become quite good, great, and perfect, perhaps there only.—But he does not know it! He is too conceited to know it.
paras.uz: U o'z ruhining boshqacha did va moyilligi borligini va vayron bo'lgan uylarning burchaklarida jimgina o'tirishni afzal ko'rishini ko'rmaydi: — shu tarzda yashiringan, hatto o'zidan ham yashiringan holda u o'sha yerda o'zining haqiqiy shoh asarlarini chizadi, ularning hammasi juda qisqa, ko'pincha faqat bir takt uzunlikda, — faqat o'sha yerda u butunlay yaxshi, buyuk va mukammal bo'ladi, balki faqat o'sha yerda. — Lekin u buni bilmaydi! U buni bilish uchun haddan tashqari manman.

paras.en: 88. Earnestness for the Truth. — Earnest for the truth! What different things men understand by these words! Just the same opinions, and modes of demonstration and testing which a thinker regards as a frivolity in himself, to which he has succumbed with shame at one time or other,—just the same opinions may give to an artist, who comes in contact with them and accepts them temporarily, the consciousness that the profoundest earnestness for the truth has now taken hold of him, and that it is worthy of admiration that, although an artist, he at the same time exhibits the most ardent desire for the antithesis of the apparent. It is thus possible that a person may, just by his pathos of earnestness, betray how superficially and sparingly his intellect has hitherto operated in the domain of knowledge.—And is not everything that we consider important our betrayer? It shows where our motives lie, and where our motives are altogether lacking.
paras.uz: 88. Haqiqatga jiddiylik. — Haqiqatga jiddiy! Odamlar bu so'zlardan qanchalik turli narsalarni tushunadi! Mutafakkir o'zida yengiltaklik deb biladigan, qachondir uyat bilan taslim bo'lgan aynan o'sha fikrlar, isbot va sinov usullari, — aynan o'sha fikrlar ularga duch kelib, vaqtincha qabul qilgan san'atkorga endi haqiqatga eng chuqur jiddiylik uni chulg'ab olgani va u san'atkor bo'lsa ham, bir vaqtning o'zida ko'rinadigan narsaning qarama-qarshisiga eng qizg'in istakni namoyon qilishi hayratga loyiq ekanligi haqida ong berishi mumkin. Shunday qilib, odam aynan jiddiylik pafosi bilan uning aqli shu paytgacha bilim sohasida qanchalik yuzaki va xasislik bilan ishlaganini oshkor qilishi mumkin. — Biz muhim deb hisoblagan hamma narsa bizning sotqinimiz emasmi? U motivlarimiz qayerda yotganini va motivlarimiz qayerda butunlay yo'qligini ko'rsatadi.

paras.en: 89. Now and Formerly. — Of what consequence is all our art in artistic products, if that higher art, the art of the festival, be lost by us? Formerly all artistic products were exhibited on the great festive path of humanity, as tokens of remembrance, and monuments of high and happy moments. One now seeks to allure the exhausted and sickly from the great suffering path of humanity for a wanton moment by means of works of art; one furnishes them with a little ecstasy and insanity.
paras.uz: 89. Hozir va ilgari. — Agar o'sha yuksakroq san'at, bayram san'ati bizdan yo'qolgan bo'lsa, san'at asarlaridagi butun san'atimizning nima ahamiyati bor? Ilgari barcha san'at asarlari insoniyatning buyuk bayram yo'lida xotira belgilari va yuksak va baxtli lahzalarning yodgorliklari sifatida namoyish etilgan. Endi esa san'at asarlari yordamida holdan toygan va kasallarni insoniyatning buyuk azob yo'lidan sho'x bir lahzaga tortib olishga intiladi; ularga ozgina vajd va telbalik beriladi.

paras.en: 90. Lights and Shades. — Books and writings are different with different thinkers. One writer has collected together in his book all the rays of light which he could quickly plunder and carry home from an illuminating experience; while another gives only the shadows, and the grey and black replicas of that which on the previous day had towered up in his soul.
paras.uz: 90. Nurlar va soyalar. — Turli mutafakkirlarda kitoblar va asarlar turlicha. Bir yozuvchi kitobida yorituvchi tajribadan tezda talon-taroj qilib, uyiga olib keta olgan barcha nur tolalarini to'plagan; boshqasi esa faqat soyalarni, oldingi kuni uning qalbida yuksalib turgan narsaning kulrang va qora nusxalarini beradi.

chapters.recap_uz: She'riyat foydasiz emas: qadimda ritm xudolarni majburlash, ruhni davolash va kelajakni belgilash vositasi deb hisoblangan. San'atkorlar faqat boylar va bekorchilar baholagan narsani ulug'laydi. Teatr — Yevropaning giyohvand moddasi.

chapters.title: Prose, poetry and Shakespeare

paras.en: 91. Precaution. — Alfieri, as is well known, told a great many falsehoods when he narrated the history of his life to his astonished contemporaries. He told falsehoods owing to the despotism toward himself which he exhibited, for example, in the way in which he created his own language, and tyrannised himself into a poet:—he finally found a rigid form of sublimity into which he forced his life and his memory; he must have suffered much in the process.—I would also give no credit to a history of Plato's life written by himself, as little as to Rousseau's, or to the Vita nuova of Dante.
paras.uz: 91. Ehtiyot chorasi. — Ma'lumki, Alfyeri hayratga tushgan zamondoshlariga hayoti tarixini so'zlab berganida juda ko'p yolg'on gapirgan. U o'ziga nisbatan ko'rsatgan zulm tufayli yolg'on gapirgan, masalan, o'z tilini yaratgani va o'zini zo'rlab shoirga aylantirgani kabi: — u oxir-oqibat yuksaklikning qattiq shaklini topdi va hayoti va xotirasini unga majburan kiritdi; bu jarayonda u ko'p azob chekkan bo'lsa kerak. — Men Platonning o'zi yozgan hayoti tarixiga ham, Russoning hayot tarixiga yoki Dantening «Vita nuova»siga ishonmaganim kabi ishonmagan bo'lardim.

paras.en: 92. Prose and Poetry. — Let it be observed that the great masters of prose have almost always been poets as well, whether openly, or only in secret and for the "closet"; and in truth one only writes good prose in view of poetry!
paras.uz: 92. Nasr va nazm. — E'tibor beringki, nasrning buyuk ustalari deyarli doimo shoir ham bo'lgan, xoh ochiq, xoh faqat yashirincha va «xilvat» uchun; va haqiqatan ham, odam faqat nazmni ko'zda tutibgina yaxshi nasr yozadi!

paras.en: For prose is an uninterrupted, polite warfare with poetry; all its charm consists in the fact that poetry is constantly avoided, and contradicted; every abstraction wants to have a gibe at poetry, and wishes to be uttered with a mocking voice; all dryness and coolness is meant to bring the amiable goddess into an amiable despair; there are often approximations and reconciliations for the moment, and then a sudden recoil and a burst of laughter; the curtain is often drawn up and dazzling light let in just while the goddess is enjoying her twilights and dull colours; the word is often taken out of her mouth and chanted to a melody while she holds her fine hands before her delicate little ears—and so there are a thousand enjoyments of the warfare, the defeats included, of which the unpoetic, the so-called prose-men know nothing at all:—they consequently write and speak only bad prose!
paras.uz: Chunki nasr — nazm bilan uzluksiz, xushmuomala urush; uning butun jozibasi nazmdan doimo qochish va unga qarshi chiqishda; har bir abstraksiya nazm ustidan kulmoqchi va masxaraomuz ovoz bilan aytilishni istaydi; har qanday quruqlik va sovuqlik yoqimli ma'budani yoqimli umidsizlikka solish uchun mo'ljallangan; ko'pincha bir lahzalik yaqinlashishlar va yarashishlar bo'ladi, keyin esa to'satdan chekinish va kulgi portlashi; ma'buda o'zining g'ira-shiraligi va xira ranglaridan zavqlanayotgan paytda ko'pincha parda ko'tarilib, ko'zni qamashtiruvchi yorug'lik kiritiladi; ko'pincha so'z uning og'zidan olinib, u nozik qo'llarini nozik kichkina quloqlari oldida tutib turganida kuyga solib kuylanadi — va shunday qilib urushning, mag'lubiyatlar bilan birga, ming xil zavqi bor, nazmdan bexabarlar, nasr odamlari deb ataladiganlar ular haqida umuman hech narsa bilishmaydi: — shuning uchun ular faqat yomon nasr yozishadi va gapirishadi!

paras.en: Warfare is the father of all good things, it is also the father of good prose!—There have been four very singular and truly poetical men in this century who have arrived at mastership in prose, for which otherwise this century is not suited, owing to lack of poetry, as we have indicated. Not to take Goethe into account, for he is reasonably claimed by the century that produced him, I look only on Giacomo Leopardi, Prosper Mérimée, Ralph Waldo Emerson, and Walter Savage Landor, the author of Imaginary Conversations, as worthy to be called masters of prose.
paras.uz: Urush barcha yaxshi narsalarning otasi, u yaxshi nasrning ham otasi! — Bu asrda nasrda ustalikka erishgan to'rtta juda o'ziga xos va chinakam shoirona odam bo'lgan, aks holda bu asr, ko'rsatganimizdek, nazm yetishmasligi tufayli bunga mos emas. Gyoteni hisobga olmaganda, chunki uni o'zini yaratgan asr haqli ravishda da'vo qiladi, men faqat Jakomo Leopardi, Prosper Merime, Ralf Uoldo Emerson va «Xayoliy suhbatlar» muallifi Uolter Sevij Lendorni nasr ustalari deb atashga loyiq deb bilaman.

paras.en: 93. But why, then, do you Write?. — A: I do not belong to those who think with the wet pen in hand; and still less to those who yield themselves entirely to their passions before the open ink-bottle, sitting on their chair and staring at the paper. I am always vexed and abashed by writing; writing is a necessity for me,—even to speak of it in a simile is disagreeable. B: But why, then, do you write? A: Well, my dear Sir, to tell you in confidence, I have hitherto found no other means of getting rid of my thoughts. B: And why do you wish to get rid of them? A: Why I wish? Do I really wish! I must.—B: Enough! Enough!
paras.uz: 93. Unda nega yozasiz? — A: Men ho'l qalamni qo'lda ushlab o'ylaydiganlardan emasman; ochiq siyohdon oldida kursida o'tirib, qog'ozga tikilib, butunlay ehtiroslariga beriladiganlardan esa yana ham kamroq. Yozish meni doimo g'azablantiradi va xijolat qiladi; yozish men uchun zarurat, — hatto bu haqda o'xshatish bilan gapirish ham yoqimsiz. B: Unda nega yozasiz? A: Xo'sh, aziz janob, sizga sir qilib aytsam, men shu paytgacha fikrlarimdan qutulishning boshqa yo'lini topmadim. B: Ulardan nega qutulmoqchisiz? A: Nega xohlayman? Men haqiqatan xohlaymanmi! Men majburman. — B: Yetadi! Yetadi!

paras.en: 94. Growth after Death. — Those few daring words about moral matters which Fontenelle threw into his immortal Dialogues of the Dead, were regarded by his age as paradoxes and amusements of a not unscrupulous wit; even the highest judges of taste and intellect saw nothing more in them,—indeed, Fontenelle himself perhaps saw nothing more. Then something incredible takes place: these thoughts become truths! Science proves them! The game becomes serious! And we read those dialogues with a feeling different from that with which Voltaire and Helvetius read them, and we involuntarily raise their originator into another and much higher class of intellects than they did.—Rightly? Wrongly?
paras.uz: 94. O'limdan keyingi o'sish. — Fontenel o'zining o'lmas «O'liklar suhbatlari»ga tashlagan axloqiy masalalar haqidagi o'sha bir nechta dadil so'zlarni uning davri paradokslar va unchalik vijdonli bo'lmagan zakovatning ermagi deb hisoblagan; hatto did va aqlning eng oliy hakamlari ham ularda bundan ortiq narsani ko'rmagan, — haqiqatan ham, balki Fontenelning o'zi ham bundan ortiq narsani ko'rmagandir. Keyin aql bovar qilmas narsa yuz beradi: bu fikrlar haqiqatga aylanadi! Ilm ularni isbotlaydi! O'yin jiddiylashadi! Biz esa bu suhbatlarni Volter va Gelvetsiy o'qigandan boshqacha tuyg'u bilan o'qiymiz va beixtiyor ularning muallifini ular qilganidan boshqa va ancha yuksakroq aqllar sinfiga ko'taramiz. — To'g'rimi? Noto'g'rimi?

paras.en: 95. Chamfort. — That such a judge of men and of the multitude as Chamfort should side with the multitude, instead of standing apart in philosophical resignation and defence—I am at a loss to explain, except as follows:—There was an instinct in him stronger than his wisdom, and it had never been gratified: the hatred against all noblesse of blood; perhaps his mother's old and only too explicable hatred, which was consecrated in him by love of her,—an instinct of revenge from his boyhood, which waited for the hour to avenge his mother. But then the course of his life, his genius, and alas! most of all, perhaps, the paternal blood in his veins, had seduced him to rank and consider himself equal to the noblesse—for many, many years!
paras.uz: 95. Shamfor. — Shamfor kabi odamlar va olomonning bilimdoni falsafiy taslimlik va himoyada chetda turish o'rniga olomon tarafini olganini quyidagicha tushuntirishdan boshqa yo'l topa olmayman: — Unda donoligidan kuchliroq instinkt bor edi va u hech qachon qondirilmagan edi: barcha qon zodagonligiga nafrat; balki onasining eski va juda tushunarli nafrati, u onasiga bo'lgan sevgi bilan unda muqaddaslashgan edi, — bolaligidan qolgan qasos instinkti, onasining qasosini olish soatini kutgan. Lekin keyin hayot yo'li, dahosi va afsus! eng ko'p, ehtimol, tomirlaridagi ota qoni uni zodagonlar qatoriga kirishga va o'zini ularga teng deb hisoblashga yo'ldan urgan edi — ko'p, ko'p yillar davomida!

paras.en: In the end, however, he could not endure the sight of himself, the "old man" under the old régime, any longer; he got into a violent, penitential passion, and in this state he put on the raiment of the populace as his special kind of hair-shirt! His bad conscience was the neglect of revenge.—If Chamfort had then been a little more of the philosopher, the Revolution would not have had its tragic wit and its sharpest sting; it would have been regarded as a much more stupid affair, and would have had no such seductive influence on men's minds. But Chamfort's hatred and revenge educated an entire generation; and the most illustrious men passed through his school.
paras.uz: Biroq oxirida u o'zini, eski tuzum ostidagi «eski odam»ni boshqa ko'ra olmadi; u kuchli, tavbakor ehtirosga tushdi va bu holatda olomon kiyimini o'zining alohida jun ko'ylagi sifatida kiydi! Uning yomon vijdoni qasosni e'tiborsiz qoldirgani edi. — Agar Shamfor o'shanda biroz ko'proq faylasuf bo'lganida, Inqilobning tragik zakovati va eng o'tkir nayzasi bo'lmasdi; u ancha ahmoqona ish deb hisoblanardi va odamlarning aqliga bunday yo'ldan uruvchi ta'sir ko'rsatmasdi. Lekin Shamforning nafrati va qasosi butun bir avlodni tarbiyaladi; va eng mashhur odamlar uning maktabidan o'tdi.

paras.en: Let us but consider that Mirabeau looked up to Chamfort as to his higher and older self, from whom he expected (and endured) impulses, warnings, and condemnations,—Mirabeau, who as a man belongs to an entirely different order of greatness, as the very foremost among the statesman-geniuses of yesterday and to-day.—Strange, that in spite of such a friend and advocate—we possess Mirabeau's letters to Chamfort—this wittiest of all moralists has remained unfamiliar to the French, quite the same as Stendhal, who has perhaps had the most penetrating eyes and ears of any Frenchman of this century.
paras.uz: Mirabo Shamforga o'zining yuksakroq va kattaroq o'zidek qaraganini o'ylab ko'raylik, undan turtkilar, ogohlantirishlar va qoralashlarni kutgan (va ularga chidagan), — inson sifatida butunlay boshqa buyuklik tartibiga mansub, kecha va bugungi davlat arbobi-dahosi bo'lganlarning eng oldingisi bo'lgan Mirabo. — G'alati, shunday do'st va himoyachiga qaramay — bizda Miraboning Shamforga yozgan xatlari bor — barcha moralistlarning bu eng zakovatlisi fransuzlarga notanish qolgan, xuddi bu asrning har qanday fransuzidan, ehtimol, eng o'tkir ko'z va quloqqa ega bo'lgan Stendal kabi.

paras.en: Is it because the latter had really too much of the German and the Englishman in his nature for the Parisians to endure him?—while Chamfort, a man with ample knowledge of the profundities and secret motives of the soul, gloomy, suffering, ardent—a thinker who found laughter necessary as the remedy of life, and who almost gave himself up as lost every day that he had not laughed,—seems much more like an Italian, and related by blood to Dante and Leopardi, than like a Frenchman. One knows Chamfort's last words: "Ah! mon ami," he said to Sieyès, "je m'en vais enfin de ce monde, où il faut que le cœur se brise ou se bronze—." These were certainly not the words of a dying Frenchman.
paras.uz: Bu ikkinchisining tabiatida parijliklar chiday olmaydigan darajada haddan tashqari ko'p nemis va inglizlik bo'lgani uchunmi? — Shamfor esa, ruhning chuqurliklari va yashirin motivlarini keng biladigan, ma'yus, azob chekuvchi, otashin odam — kulgini hayotning davosi sifatida zarur deb bilgan va kulmagan har bir kunida o'zini deyarli yo'qolgan deb hisoblagan mutafakkir, — fransuzdan ko'ra ko'proq italyanga o'xshaydi va Dante va Leopardi bilan qon qarindoshdek. Shamforning so'nggi so'zlari ma'lum: «Ah! mon ami, — dedi u Syeyesga, — je m'en vais enfin de ce monde, où il faut que le coeur se brise ou se bronze —» (Oh, do'stim, men nihoyat bu dunyodan ketyapman, bu yerda yurak yo sinishi, yo bronzaga aylanishi kerak). Bu albatta o'layotgan fransuzning so'zlari emas edi.

paras.en: 96. Two Orators. — Of these two orators the one arrives at a full understanding of his case only when he yields himself to emotion; it is only this that pumps sufficient blood and heat into his brain to compel his high intellectuality to reveal itself. The other attempts, indeed, now and then to do the same: to state his case sonorously, vehemently, and spiritedly with the aid of emotion,—but usually with bad success. He then very soon speaks obscurely and confusedly; he exaggerates, makes omissions, and excites suspicion of the justice of his case: indeed, he himself feels this suspicion, and the sudden changes into the coldest and most repulsive tones (which raise a doubt in the hearer as to his passionateness being genuine) are thereby explicable. With him emotion always drowns the spirit; perhaps because it is stronger than in the former. But he is at the height of his power when he resists the impetuous storm of his feeling, and as it were scorns it; it is then only that his spirit emerges fully from its concealment, a spirit logical, mocking, and playful, but nevertheless awe-inspiring.
paras.uz: 96. Ikki notiq. — Bu ikki notiqdan biri o'z ishini faqat his-tuyg'uga berilgandagina to'liq tushunadi; faqat shu uning miyasiga yuksak aqlining o'zini namoyon qilishiga majbur qilish uchun yetarli qon va issiqlik haydaydi. Ikkinchisi ham haqiqatan vaqti-vaqti bilan xuddi shunday qilishga urinadi: his-tuyg'u yordamida o'z ishini jarangdor, shiddatli va jo'shqin bayon qilishga, — lekin odatda muvaffaqiyatsiz. O'shanda u tez orada qorong'i va chalkash gapiradi; bo'rttiradi, tushirib qoldiradi va ishining adolatliligiga shubha uyg'otadi: haqiqatan ham, uning o'zi bu shubhani his qiladi va eng sovuq va eng itaruvchi ohanglarga to'satdan o'tishlari (ular tinglovchida uning ehtirosliligi haqiqiyligiga shubha uyg'otadi) shu bilan tushuntiriladi. Unda his-tuyg'u doimo ruhni g'arq qiladi; balki u birinchisinikidan kuchliroq bo'lgani uchundir. Lekin u tuyg'usining shiddatli bo'roniga qarshi turib, go'yo uni mensimaganida kuchining cho'qqisida bo'ladi; faqat o'shanda uning ruhi yashiringan joyidan to'liq chiqadi, mantiqiy, masxaraomuz va o'yinqaroq, lekin shunga qaramay qo'rquv uyg'otadigan ruh.

paras.en: 97. The Loquacity of Authors. — There is a loquacity of anger—frequent in Luther, also in Schopenhauer. A loquacity which comes from too great a store of conceptual formulæ, as in Kant. A loquacity which comes from delight in ever new modifications of the same idea: one finds it in Montaigne. A loquacity of malicious natures: whoever reads writings of our period will recollect two authors in this connection. A loquacity which comes from delight in fine words and forms of speech: by no means rare in Goethe's prose. A loquacity which comes from pure satisfaction in noise and confusion of feelings: for example in Carlyle.
paras.uz: 97. Mualliflarning ezmaligi. — G'azab ezmaligi bor — Lyuterda tez-tez uchraydi, Shopengauerda ham. Tushuncha formulalarining haddan tashqari katta zaxirasidan keladigan ezmalik, Kantdagidek. Bir xil g'oyaning doimo yangi o'zgarishlaridan zavqlanishdan keladigan ezmalik: uni Montenda topasiz. G'arazli tabiatlarning ezmaligi: davrimiz asarlarini o'qigan kishi bu munosabat bilan ikki muallifni eslaydi. Chiroyli so'zlar va nutq shakllaridan zavqlanishdan keladigan ezmalik: Gyote nasrida aslo kam emas. Shovqin va tuyg'ular chalkashligidan sof mamnuniyatdan keladigan ezmalik: masalan, Karleylda.

paras.en: 98. In Honour of Shakespeare. — The best thing I could say in honour of Shakespeare, the man, is that he believed in Brutus and cast not a shadow of suspicion on the kind of virtue which Brutus represents! It is to him that Shakespeare consecrated his best tragedy—it is at present still called by a wrong name,—to him and to the most terrible essence of lofty morality. Independence of soul!—that is the question at issue! No sacrifice can be too great there: one must be able to sacrifice to it even one's dearest friend, though he be also the grandest of men, the ornament of the world, the genius without peer,—if one really loves freedom as the freedom of great souls, and if this freedom be threatened by him:—it is thus that Shakespeare must have felt!
paras.uz: 98. Shekspir sharafiga. — Inson Shekspir sharafiga ayta oladigan eng yaxshi gapim shuki, u Brutga ishongan va Brut ifodalaydigan fazilat turiga zarracha ham shubha soyasini tashlamagan! Shekspir o'zining eng yaxshi tragediyasini aynan unga bag'ishlagan — u hozir ham noto'g'ri nom bilan ataladi, — unga va yuksak axloqning eng dahshatli mohiyatiga. Ruh mustaqilligi! — masala shunda! U yerda hech qanday qurbonlik haddan tashqari katta bo'la olmaydi: unga hatto eng aziz do'stingni ham qurbon qila olishing kerak, garchi u eng buyuk inson, dunyoning bezagi, tengsiz daho bo'lsa ham, — agar sen erkinlikni haqiqatan ham buyuk qalblar erkinligi sifatida sevsang va bu erkinlikka u tahdid qilsa: — Shekspir shunday his qilgan bo'lsa kerak!

paras.en: The elevation in which he places Cæsar is the most exquisite honour he could confer upon Brutus; it is thus only that he lifts into vastness the inner problem of his hero, and similarly the strength of soul which could cut this knot!—And was it actually political freedom that impelled the poet to sympathy with Brutus,—and made him the accomplice of Brutus? Or was political freedom merely a symbol for something inexpressible? Do we perhaps stand before some sombre event or adventure of the poet's own soul, which has remained unknown, and of which he only cared to speak symbolically? What is all Hamlet-melancholy in comparison with the melancholy of Brutus!—and perhaps Shakespeare also knew this, as he knew the other, by experience!
paras.uz: U Sezarni qo'ygan yuksaklik Brutga bera oladigan eng nafis sharafdir; faqat shu tarzda u qahramonining ichki muammosini, xuddi shunday bu tugunni kesa olgan ruh kuchini ulkanlikka ko'taradi! — Va shoirni Brutga hamdardlikka undagan — va uni Brutning sherigiga aylantirgan narsa haqiqatan ham siyosiy erkinlikmidi? Yoki siyosiy erkinlik shunchaki ifodalab bo'lmas narsaning ramzimidi? Balki biz shoirning o'z ruhidagi noma'lum qolgan va u faqat ramziy gapirishni ma'qul ko'rgan qandaydir ma'yus voqea yoki sarguzasht oldida turgandirmiz? Brutning g'amginligi bilan solishtirganda butun Hamlet g'amginligi nima! — va balki Shekspir buni ham, boshqasini bilgani kabi, tajribadan bilgandir!

paras.en: Perhaps he also had his dark hour and his bad angel, just as Brutus had them!—But whatever similarities and secret relationships of that kind there may have been, Shakespeare cast himself on the ground and felt unworthy and alien in presence of the aspect and virtue of Brutus:—he has inscribed the testimony thereof in the tragedy itself. He has twice brought in a poet in it, and twice heaped upon him such an impatient and extreme contempt, that it sounds like a cry,—like the cry of self-contempt. Brutus, even Brutus loses patience when the poet appears, self-important, pathetic, and obtrusive, as poets usually are,—persons who seem to abound in the possibilities of greatness, even moral greatness, and nevertheless rarely attain even to ordinary uprightness in the philosophy of practice and of life. "He may know the times, but I know his temper,—away with the jigging fool!"—shouts Brutus. We may translate this back into the soul of the poet that composed it.
paras.uz: Balki uning ham xuddi Brutdagidek qorong'i soati va yomon farishtasi bo'lgandir! — Lekin bunday o'xshashliklar va yashirin qarindoshliklar qanday bo'lmasin, Shekspir Brutning qiyofasi va fazilati oldida o'zini yerga tashlagan va o'zini nomunosib va begona his qilgan: — u buning guvohligini tragediyaning o'ziga yozib qo'ygan. U unda ikki marta shoirni olib kirgan va ikki marta unga shunday sabrsiz va o'ta nafrat yog'dirganki, bu qichqiriqdek eshitiladi, — o'zidan nafratlanish qichqirig'idek. Brut, hatto Brut ham shoir paydo bo'lganda sabrini yo'qotadi, — shoirlar odatda bo'lgani kabi o'zini muhim sanagan, pafosli va surbet, — buyuklik, hatto axloqiy buyuklik imkoniyatlariga to'ladek ko'rinadigan, lekin shunga qaramay amaliyot va hayot falsafasida hatto oddiy halollikka ham kamdan-kam erishadigan odamlar. «U zamonni bilishi mumkin, lekin men uning fe'lini bilaman, — yo'qolsin bu sakrovchi ahmoq!» — deb qichqiradi Brut. Buni uni yozgan shoirning ruhiga qaytarib tarjima qilishimiz mumkin.
