chapters.recap_uz: Yaxshi nasr nazm bilan muloyim urushdan tug'iladi. «Unda nega yozasiz?» — fikrlardan qutulish uchun. Shamfor, ikki notiq va mualliflarning ezmaligi haqida; oxirida Shekspir va Brut — ruh mustaqilligi uchun eng aziz do'stni qurbon qilish.

chapters.title: Schopenhauer and Wagner

paras.en: 99. The Followers of Schopenhauer. — What one sees at the contact of civilized peoples with barbarians,—namely, that the lower civilization regularly accepts in the first place the vices, weaknesses, and excesses of the higher; then, from that point onward, feels the influence of a charm; and finally, by means of the appropriated vices and weaknesses, also allows something of the valuable influence of the higher culture to leaven it:—one can also see this close at hand and without journeys to barbarian peoples, to be sure, somewhat refined and spiritualised, and not so readily palpable. What are the German followers of Schopenhauer still accustomed to receive first of all from their master:—those who, when placed beside his superior culture, must deem themselves sufficiently barbarous to be first of all barbarously fascinated and seduced by him.
paras.uz: 99. Shopengauer izdoshlari. — Madaniyatli xalqlar vahshiylar bilan to'qnashganda ko'riladigan narsa — ya'ni quyi madaniyat muntazam ravishda avvalo yuksakroq madaniyatning illatlari, zaifliklari va haddan oshishlarini qabul qiladi; keyin shu nuqtadan boshlab jozibaning ta'sirini his qiladi; va nihoyat, o'zlashtirilgan illatlar va zaifliklar orqali yuksakroq madaniyatning qimmatli ta'siridan ham nimadir uni achitishiga yo'l qo'yadi: — buni yaqindan va vahshiy xalqlarga sayohat qilmasdan ham ko'rish mumkin, albatta, biroz nozikroq va ruhiylashgan, unchalik oson sezilmaydigan holda. Shopengauerning nemis izdoshlari hali ham o'z ustozidan eng avvalo nimani olishga odatlangan: — uning yuksakroq madaniyati yonida qo'yilganda o'zlarini avvalo vahshiylarcha maftun bo'lish va yo'ldan urilish uchun yetarlicha vahshiy deb hisoblashi kerak bo'lganlar.

paras.en: Is it his hard matter-of-fact sense, his inclination to clearness and rationality, which often makes him appear so English, and so unlike Germans? Or the strength of his intellectual conscience, which endured a life-long contradiction of "being" and "willing," and compelled him to contradict himself constantly even in his writings on almost every point? Or his purity in matters relating to the Church and the Christian God?—for here he was pure as no German philosopher had been hitherto, so that he lived and died "as a Voltairian." Or his immortal doctrines of the intellectuality of intuition, the apriority of the law of causality, the instrumental nature of the intellect, and the non-freedom of the will?
paras.uz: Uni ko'pincha shunchalik inglizcha va nemislarga shunchalik o'xshamaydigan qilib ko'rsatadigan qattiq amaliy aqlimi, ravshanlik va aqlliligiga moyilligimi? Yoki butun umr «mavjud bo'lish» va «istash» o'rtasidagi qarama-qarshilikka chidagan va uni hatto asarlarida ham deyarli har bir nuqtada doimo o'ziga qarshi chiqishga majbur qilgan aqliy vijdonining kuchimi? Yoki cherkov va nasroniy Xudosiga oid masalalarda pokligimi? — chunki bu yerda u shu paytgacha hech bir nemis faylasufi bo'lmagandek pok edi, shuning uchun «volterchi sifatida» yashadi va o'ldi. Yoki uning sezgining aqliyligi, sabablilik qonunining aprioriligi, aqlning quroliy tabiati va irodaning erkin emasligi haqidagi o'lmas ta'limotlarimi?

paras.en: No, nothing of this enchants, nor is felt as enchanting; but Schopenhauer's mystical embarrassments and shufflings in those passages where the matter-of-fact thinker allowed himself to be seduced and corrupted by the vain impulse to be the unraveller of the world's riddle: his undemonstrable doctrine of one will ("all causes are merely occasional causes of the phenomenon of the will at such a time and at such a place," "the will to live, whole and undivided, is present in every being, even in the smallest, as perfectly as in the sum of all that was, is, and will be"); his denial of the individual ("all lions are really only one lion," "plurality of individuals is an appearance," as also development is only an appearance: he calls the opinion of Lamarck "an ingenious, absurd error"); his fantasy about genius ("in æsthetic contemplation the individual is no longer an individual, but a pure, will-less, painless, timeless subject of knowledge," "the subject, in that it entirely merges in the contemplated object, has become this object itself"); his nonsense about sympathy, and about the outburst of the principium individuationis thus rendered possible, as the source of all morality; including also such assertions as, "dying is really the design of existence," "the possibility should not be absolutely denied that a magical effect could proceed from a person already dead":—these, and similar extravagances and vices of the philosopher, are always first accepted and made articles of faith; for vices and extravagances are always easiest to imitate, and do not require a long preliminary practice.
paras.uz: Yo'q, bularning hech biri maftun qilmaydi va maftunkor deb his qilinmaydi; balki Shopengauerning amaliy mutafakkir o'zini dunyo jumboqini yechuvchi bo'lish haqidagi bo'sh istak bilan yo'ldan urishga va buzishga yo'l qo'ygan joylardagi mistik chalkashliklari va hiylalari: uning bitta iroda haqidagi isbotlab bo'lmas ta'limoti («barcha sabablar irodaning shu vaqtda va shu joyda namoyon bo'lishining tasodifiy sabablari xolos», «yashash irodasi butun va bo'linmas holda har bir mavjudotda, hatto eng kichigida ham, bo'lgan, bor va bo'ladigan hamma narsaning yig'indisidagidek mukammal mavjud»); shaxsni inkor etishi («barcha sherlar aslida faqat bitta sher», «shaxslarning ko'pligi — ko'rinish», xuddi rivojlanish ham faqat ko'rinish bo'lgani kabi: u Lamark fikrini «zukko, bema'ni xato» deb ataydi); daho haqidagi fantaziyasi («estetik mulohazada shaxs endi shaxs emas, balki bilimning sof, irodasiz, og'riqsiz, vaqtsiz subyekti», «subyekt mulohaza qilinayotgan obyektga butunlay singib, shu obyektning o'ziga aylangan»); hamdardlik va shu tariqa mumkin bo'ladigan principium individuationis — shaxslanish tamoyilining yorilishi barcha axloqning manbai ekani haqidagi bema'ni gaplari; shuningdek, «o'lish aslida hayotning maqsadi», «allaqachon o'lgan odamdan sehrli ta'sir chiqishi mumkinligini mutlaqo inkor etmaslik kerak» kabi da'volari: — faylasufning bular va shunga o'xshash haddan oshishlari va illatlari doimo birinchi navbatda qabul qilinadi va e'tiqod moddalariga aylantiriladi; chunki illatlar va haddan oshishlarga taqlid qilish doimo eng oson va uzoq dastlabki mashqni talab qilmaydi.

paras.en: But let us speak of the most celebrated of the living Schopenhauerians, Richard Wagner.—It has happened to him as it has already happened to many an artist: he made a mistake in the interpretation of the characters he created, and misunderstood the unexpressed philosophy of the art peculiarly his own. Richard Wagner allowed himself to be misled by Hegel's influence till the middle of his life; and he did the same again when later on he read Schopenhauer's doctrine between the lines of his characters, and began to express himself with such terms as "will," "genius," and "sympathy." Nevertheless it will remain true that nothing is more counter to Schopenhauer's spirit than the essentially Wagnerian element in Wagner's heroes: I mean the innocence of the supremest selfishness, the belief in strong passion as the good in itself, in a word, the Siegfried trait in the countenances of his heroes.
paras.uz: Lekin keling, tirik shopengauerchilarning eng mashhuri — Rixard Vagner haqida gapiraylik. — Unga ko'p san'atkorlarga allaqachon bo'lgani kabi bo'ldi: u o'zi yaratgan qahramonlarni talqin qilishda xato qildi va o'ziga xos san'atining ifodalanmagan falsafasini noto'g'ri tushundi. Rixard Vagner hayotining o'rtasigacha Gegel ta'siri bilan o'zini adashtirishga yo'l qo'ydi; va keyinroq qahramonlarining satrlari orasidan Shopengauer ta'limotini o'qiganda va «iroda», «daho» va «hamdardlik» kabi atamalar bilan o'zini ifodalay boshlaganda yana xuddi shunday qildi. Shunga qaramay, Vagner qahramonlaridagi mohiyatan vagnercha unsurdan Shopengauer ruhiga zidroq narsa yo'qligi haqiqat bo'lib qoladi: men eng oliy xudbinlikning beg'uborligini, kuchli ehtirosga o'z-o'zidan yaxshilik sifatida ishonishni, bir so'z bilan aytganda, qahramonlari yuzlaridagi Zigfrid xususiyatini nazarda tutyapman.

paras.en: "All that still smacks more of Spinoza than of me,"—Schopenhauer would probably have said. Whatever good reasons, therefore, Wagner might have had to be on the outlook for other philosophers than Schopenhauer, the enchantment to which he succumbed in respect to this thinker, not only made him blind towards all other philosophers, but even towards science itself; his entire art is more and more inclined to become the counterpart and complement of the Schopenhauerian philosophy, and it always renounces more emphatically the higher ambition to become the counterpart and complement of human knowledge and science. And not only is he allured thereto by the whole mystic pomp of this philosophy (which would also have allured a Cagliostro), the peculiar airs and emotions of the philosopher have all along been seducing him as well!
paras.uz: «Bularning hammasidan hali ham mendan ko'ra Spinoza hidi ko'proq keladi», — degan bo'lardi ehtimol Shopengauer. Demak, Vagnerda Shopengauerdan boshqa faylasuflarni izlash uchun qanday yaxshi sabablar bo'lmasin, u bu mutafakkirga nisbatan berilgan sehr uni nafaqat boshqa barcha faylasuflarga, balki hatto ilmning o'ziga nisbatan ham ko'r qildi; uning butun san'ati tobora ko'proq Shopengauer falsafasining aksi va to'ldiruvchisi bo'lishga moyil bo'lib boradi va inson bilimi va ilmining aksi va to'ldiruvchisi bo'lish haqidagi yuksakroq shuhratparastlikdan doimo qat'iyroq voz kechadi. Va uni bunga nafaqat bu falsafaning butun mistik hashamati (u Kalyostroni ham jalb qilgan bo'lardi) jalb qiladi, faylasufning o'ziga xos qiliqlari va his-tuyg'ulari ham doimo uni yo'ldan urib kelgan!

paras.en: For example, Wagner's indignation about the corruption of the German language is Schopenhauerian; and if one should commend his imitation in this respect, it is nevertheless not to be denied that Wagner's style itself suffers in no small degree from all the tumours and turgidities, the sight of which made Schopenhauer so furious; and that, in respect to the German-writing Wagnerians, Wagneromania is beginning to be as dangerous as only some kinds of Hegelomania have been. Schopenhauerian is Wagner's hatred of the Jews, to whom he is unable to do justice, even in their greatest exploit: are not the Jews the inventors of Christianity! The attempt of Wagner to construe Christianity as a seed blown away from Buddhism, and his endeavour to initiate a Buddhistic era in Europe, under a temporary approximation to Catholic-Christian formulas and sentiments, are both Schopenhauerian.
paras.uz: Masalan, Vagnerning nemis tilining buzilishidan g'azabi shopengauercha; va agar uning bu jihatdagi taqlidini maqtash kerak bo'lsa ham, Vagnerning uslubining o'zi Shopengauerni shunchalik g'azablantirgan barcha shishlar va ko'pchishlardan oz darajada aziyat chekmasligini va nemischa yozadigan vagnerchilarga nisbatan vagnermaniya faqat gegelmaniyaning ba'zi turlari bo'lgandek xavfli bo'la boshlaganini inkor etib bo'lmaydi. Vagnerning yahudiylarga nafrati shopengauercha, u ularning eng buyuk ishida ham ularga adolat qila olmaydi: axir yahudiylar nasroniylikni ixtiro qilganlar emasmi! Vagnerning nasroniylikni buddizmdan uchib ketgan urug' deb talqin qilish urinishi va katolik-nasroniy formulalari va tuyg'ulariga vaqtincha yaqinlashish ostida Yevropada buddistik davrni boshlash harakati — ikkalasi ham shopengauercha.

paras.en: Wagner's preaching in favour of pity in dealing with animals is Schopenhauerian; Schopenhauer's predecessor here, as is well known, was Voltaire, who already perhaps, like his successors, knew how to disguise his hatred of certain men and things as pity towards animals. At least Wagner's hatred of science, which manifests itself in his preaching, has certainly not been inspired by the spirit of charitableness and kindness—nor by the spirit at all, as is sufficiently obvious.—Finally, it is of little importance what the philosophy of an artist is, provided it is only a supplementary philosophy, and does not do any injury to his art itself.
paras.uz: Vagnerning hayvonlarga muomala qilishda achinish foydasiga va'zi shopengauercha; bu yerda Shopengauerning o'tmishdoshi, ma'lumki, Volter bo'lgan, u ham balki o'z vorislari kabi ba'zi odamlar va narsalarga nafratini hayvonlarga achinish sifatida niqoblashni bilgan. Hech bo'lmasa Vagnerning va'zida namoyon bo'ladigan ilmga nafrati albatta xayrixohlik va mehribonlik ruhidan ilhomlanmagan — umuman ruhdan ham emas, bu yetarlicha ravshan. — Nihoyat, agar san'atkorning falsafasi faqat qo'shimcha falsafa bo'lsa va san'atining o'ziga hech qanday zarar keltirmasa, uning qanday ekani kam ahamiyatga ega.

paras.en: We cannot be sufficiently on our guard against taking a dislike to an artist on account of an occasional, perhaps very unfortunate and presumptuous masquerade; let us not forget that the dear artists are all of them something of actors—and must be so; it would be difficult for them to hold out in the long run without stage-playing. Let us be loyal to Wagner in that which is true and original in him,—and especially in this point, that we, his disciples, remain loyal to ourselves in that which is true and original in us. Let us allow him his intellectual humours and spasms, let us in fairness rather consider what strange nutriments and necessaries an art like his is entitled to, in order to be able to live and grow! It is of no account that he is often wrong as a thinker; justice and patience are not his affair.
paras.uz: San'atkorni vaqti-vaqti bilan, balki juda baxtsiz va takabburona niqob tufayli yoqtirmay qolishdan yetarlicha ehtiyot bo'la olmaymiz; aziz san'atkorlarning hammasi biroz aktyor ekanini va shunday bo'lishi kerakligini unutmaylik; sahna o'yinisiz uzoq muddatda bardosh berish ular uchun qiyin bo'lardi. Keling, Vagnerga undagi haqiqiy va o'ziga xos narsada sodiq qolaylik, — ayniqsa shu nuqtada: biz, uning shogirdlari, o'zimizdagi haqiqiy va o'ziga xos narsada o'zimizga sodiq qolaylik. Unga aqliy injiqliklari va talvasalarini qoldiraylik, adolat bilan ko'proq uning san'ati kabi san'at yashash va o'sish uchun qanday g'alati ozuqa va zaruratlarga haqli ekanini o'ylaylik! U mutafakkir sifatida ko'pincha xato qilishi ahamiyatsiz; adolat va sabr uning ishi emas.

paras.en: It is sufficient that his life is right in his own eyes, and maintains its right,—the life which calls to each of us: "Be a man, and do not follow me—but thyself! thyself!" Our life, also ought to maintain its right in our own eyes! We also are to grow and blossom out of ourselves, free and fearless, in innocent selfishness! And so, on the contemplation of such a man, these thoughts still ring in my ears to-day, as formerly:
paras.uz: Uning hayoti o'z nazarida haq ekani va o'z haqini saqlashi kifoya, — har birimizga chaqiradigan hayot: «Inson bo'l va menga ergashma — balki o'zingga! o'zingga!» Bizning hayotimiz ham o'z nazarimizda o'z haqini saqlashi kerak! Biz ham o'zimizdan erkin va qo'rqmay, beg'ubor xudbinlikda o'sishimiz va gullashimiz kerak! Shuning uchun bunday odamni mushohada qilganda, bu fikrlar ilgarigidek bugun ham qulog'imda jaranglaydi:

paras.en: "That passion is better than stoicism or hypocrisy; that straightforwardness, even in evil, is better than losing oneself in trying to observe traditional morality; that the free man is just as able to be good as evil, but that the unemancipated man is a disgrace to nature, and has no share in heavenly or earthly bliss; finally, that all who wish to be free must become so through themselves, and that freedom falls to nobody's lot as a gift from Heaven." (Richard Wagner in Bayreuth, Vol. I. of this Translation, pp. 199-200).
paras.uz: «Ehtiros stoitsizm yoki riyokorlikdan yaxshiroq; to'g'rilik, hatto yomonlikda ham, an'anaviy axloqqa rioya qilishga urinib o'zini yo'qotishdan yaxshiroq; erkin inson yaxshi bo'lishga ham, yomon bo'lishga ham qodir, lekin ozod bo'lmagan inson tabiat uchun sharmandalik va samoviy yoki yerdagi saodatdan ulushi yo'q; nihoyat, erkin bo'lishni istaganlarning hammasi o'zlari orqali erkin bo'lishi kerak va erkinlik hech kimga osmondan sovg'a sifatida tushmaydi». («Rixard Vagner Bayroytda», ushbu tarjimaning I jildi, 199–200-betlar).

paras.en: 100. Learning to do Homage. — One must learn the art of homage, as well as the art of contempt. Whoever goes in new paths and has led many persons therein, discovers with astonishment how awkward and incompetent all of them are in the expression of their gratitude, and indeed how rarely gratitude is able even to express itself. It is always as if something comes into people's throats when their gratitude wants to speak, so that it only hems and haws, and becomes silent again. The way in which a thinker succeeds in tracing the effect of his thoughts, and their transforming and convulsing power, is almost a comedy: it sometimes seems as if those who have been operated upon felt profoundly injured thereby, and could only assert their independence, which they suspect to be threatened, by all kinds of improprieties.
paras.uz: 100. Hurmat ko'rsatishni o'rganish. — Hurmat san'atini ham, nafrat san'atini ham o'rganish kerak. Yangi yo'llardan yurgan va ko'p odamlarni o'sha yo'llarga boshlagan har kim hayrat bilan ularning hammasi minnatdorligini ifodalashda qanchalik noqulay va qobiliyatsiz ekanini, haqiqatan ham minnatdorlik o'zini ifodalay olishi ham qanchalik kam ekanini kashf etadi. Go'yo minnatdorlik gapirmoqchi bo'lganda odamlarning tomog'iga doimo nimadir tiqiladi, shunda u faqat g'o'ng'illab, yana jim bo'ladi. Mutafakkir o'z fikrlarining ta'sirini va ularning o'zgartiruvchi va larzaga soluvchi kuchini qanday kuzatishga muvaffaq bo'lishi deyarli komediya: ba'zan go'yo operatsiya qilinganlar bundan chuqur ranjigandek va o'zlari tahdid ostida deb gumon qilgan mustaqilliklarini faqat har xil odobsizliklar bilan tasdiqlay oladigandek tuyuladi.

paras.en: It needs whole generations in order merely to devise a courteous convention of gratefulness; it is only very late that the period arrives when something of spirit and genius enters into gratitude. Then there is usually some one who is the great receiver of thanks, not only for the good he himself has done, but mostly for that which has been gradually accumulated by his predecessors, as a treasure of what is highest and best.
paras.uz: Minnatdorlikning xushmuomala odatini o'ylab topish uchun ham butun avlodlar kerak; minnatdorlikka qandaydir ruh va daho kiradigan davr faqat juda kech keladi. O'shanda odatda kimdir minnatdorlikning buyuk oluvchisi bo'ladi, nafaqat o'zi qilgan yaxshilik uchun, balki ko'pincha o'tmishdoshlari eng oliy va eng yaxshi narsaning xazinasi sifatida asta-sekin to'plagan narsa uchun.

paras.en: 101. Voltaire. — Wherever there has been a court, it has furnished the standard of good-speaking, and with this also the standard of style for writers. The court language, however, is the language of the courtier who has no profession, and who even in conversations on scientific subjects avoids all convenient, technical expressions, because they smack of the profession; on that account the technical expression, and everything that betrays the specialist, is a blemish of style in countries which have a court culture. At present, when all courts have become caricatures of past and present times, one is astonished to find even Voltaire unspeakably reserved and scrupulous on this point (for example, in his judgments concerning such stylists as Fontenelle and Montesquieu),—we are now, all of us, emancipated from court taste, while Voltaire was its perfecter!
paras.uz: 101. Volter. — Saroy bo'lgan har joyda u yaxshi gapirish me'yorini, u bilan birga yozuvchilar uchun uslub me'yorini ham bergan. Biroq saroy tili — kasbi yo'q va hatto ilmiy mavzulardagi suhbatlarda ham barcha qulay, texnik iboralardan qochadigan saroyning tili, chunki ulardan kasb hidi keladi; shuning uchun saroy madaniyati bo'lgan mamlakatlarda texnik ibora va mutaxassisni oshkor qiladigan hamma narsa uslub nuqsonidir. Hozir, barcha saroylar o'tmish va hozirgi zamonning karikaturasiga aylanganda, hatto Volterni ham bu masalada so'z bilan aytib bo'lmas darajada vazmin va sinchkov ekanini ko'rib hayron bo'lasan (masalan, Fontenel va Monteskye kabi uslubchilar haqidagi hukmlarida), — biz endi hammamiz saroy didiga bo'ysunishdan ozodmiz, Volter esa uni mukammallashtiruvchi edi!

paras.en: 102. A Word for Philologists. — It is thought that there are books so valuable and royal that whole generations of scholars are well employed when through their efforts these books are kept genuine and intelligible,—to confirm this belief again and again is the purpose of philology. It presupposes that the rare men are not lacking (though they may not be visible), who actually know how to use such valuable books:—those men perhaps who write such books themselves, or could write them. I mean to say that philology presupposes a noble belief,—that for the benefit of some few who are always "to come," and are not there, a very great amount of painful, and even dirty labour has to be done beforehand: it is all labour in usum Delphinorum.
paras.uz: 102. Filologlar uchun bir so'z. — Shunday qimmatli va shohona kitoblar bor deb o'ylanadiki, olimlarning butun avlodlari ularning sa'y-harakatlari bilan bu kitoblar asl va tushunarli saqlanganda yaxshi ish qilgan bo'ladi, — bu ishonchni qayta-qayta tasdiqlash filologiyaning maqsadi. U bunday qimmatli kitoblardan haqiqatan ham foydalanishni biladigan kamyob odamlar yo'q emasligini faraz qiladi (garchi ular ko'rinmasa ham): — balki bunday kitoblarni o'zlari yozadigan yoki yoza oladigan odamlar. Aytmoqchimanki, filologiya olijanob ishonchni nazarda tutadi, — doimo «kelajakda» bo'ladigan va hozir yo'q bo'lgan bir necha kishi foydasi uchun oldindan juda katta miqdorda og'riqli, hatto iflos mehnat qilinishi kerak: bularning hammasi in usum Delphinorum — valiahd foydasi uchun mehnat.

paras.en: 103. German Music. — German music, more than any other, has now become European music; because the changes which Europe experienced through the Revolution have therein alone found expression: it is only German music that knows how to express the agitation of popular masses, the tremendous artificial uproar, which does not even need to be very noisy,—while Italian opera, for example, knows only the choruses of domestics or soldiers, but not "the people." There is the additional fact that in all German music a profound bourgeois jealousy of the noblesse can be traced, especially a jealousy of esprit and élégance, as the expressions of a courtly, chivalrous, ancient, and self-confident society. It is not music like that of Goethe's musician at the gate, which was pleasing also "in the hall," and to the king as well; it is not here said:
paras.uz: 103. Nemis musiqasi. — Nemis musiqasi endi har qanday boshqa musiqadan ko'ra Yevropa musiqasiga aylandi; chunki Yevropa Inqilob orqali boshdan kechirgan o'zgarishlar faqat unda ifodasini topdi: faqat nemis musiqasi xalq ommasining hayajonini, hatto unchalik shovqinli bo'lishi shart bo'lmagan dahshatli sun'iy g'alayonni ifodalashni biladi, — masalan, italyan operasi esa faqat xizmatkorlar yoki askarlar xorlarini biladi, lekin «xalq»ni emas. Bunga qo'shimcha ravishda, barcha nemis musiqasida zodagonlarga chuqur burjua hasadi, ayniqsa saroy, ritsarlik, qadimiy va o'ziga ishongan jamiyatning ifodalari sifatida esprit va élégance — zakovat va nafislikka hasad kuzatiladi. Bu Gyotening darvoza oldidagi musiqachisining musiqasiga o'xshagan musiqa emas, u «zalda» ham, podshohga ham yoqqan; bu yerda shunday deyilmaydi:

paras.en: "The knights looked on with martial air; with bashful eyes the ladies." Even the Graces are not allowed in German music without a touch of remorse; it is only with Pleasantness, the country sister of the Graces that the German begins to feel morally at ease—and from this point up to his enthusiastic, learned, and often gruff "sublimity" (the Beethoven-like sublimity), he feels more and more so.
paras.uz: «Ritsarlar jangovar qiyofada qarardi; xonimlar uyatchan ko'zlar bilan». Hatto Graziyalarga ham nemis musiqasiga vijdon azobi tusisiz ruxsat berilmaydi; nemis faqat Yoqimtoylik, Graziyalarning qishloqlik singlisi bilan axloqan o'zini erkin his qila boshlaydi — va shu nuqtadan uning ishtiyoqli, olimona va ko'pincha qo'pol «yuksakligi»gacha (Betxovencha yuksaklik) u o'zini tobora shunday his qiladi.

paras.en: If we want to imagine the man of this music,—well, let us just imagine Beethoven as he appeared beside Goethe, say, at their meeting at Teplitz: as semi-barbarism beside culture, as the masses beside the nobility, as the good-natured man beside the good and more than "good" man, as the visionary beside the artist, as the man needing comfort beside the comforted, as the man given to exaggeration and distrust beside the man of reason, as the crank and self-tormenter, as the foolish, enraptured, blessedly unfortunate, sincerely immoderate man, as the pretentious and awkward man,—and altogether as the "untamed man": it was thus that Goethe conceived and characterised him, Goethe, the exceptional German, for whom a music of equal rank has not yet been found!—Finally, let us consider whether the present, continually extending contempt of melody and the stunting of the sense for melody among Germans should not be understood as a democratic impropriety and an after-effect of the Revolution?
paras.uz: Agar bu musiqaning odamini tasavvur qilmoqchi bo'lsak, — xo'sh, Betxovenni Gyote yonida, aytaylik, ularning Teplitsdagi uchrashuvida qanday ko'ringan bo'lsa, shunday tasavvur qilaylik: madaniyat yonidagi yarim vahshiylik, zodagonlar yonidagi omma, yaxshi va «yaxshi»dan ham ortiq odam yonidagi xushfe'l odam, san'atkor yonidagi xayolparast, tasalli topgan odam yonidagi tasalliga muhtoj odam, aql odami yonidagi bo'rttirish va ishonchsizlikka moyil odam, g'alati va o'zini qiynovchi, ahmoq, vajdga tushgan, saodatli baxtsiz, samimiy me'yorsiz odam, da'vogar va noqulay odam, — va umuman «qo'lga o'rgatilmagan odam» sifatida: Gyote, istisno nemis, uni shunday tushungan va shunday ta'riflagan, u uchun hali teng darajadagi musiqa topilmagan! — Nihoyat, keling, o'ylab ko'raylik: nemislar orasida kuyga bo'lgan hozirgi, doimo kengayib borayotgan nafrat va kuy tuyg'usining o'smay qolishi demokratik odobsizlik va Inqilobning keyingi ta'siri sifatida tushunilishi kerak emasmi?

paras.en: For melody has such an obvious delight in conformity to law, and such an aversion to everything evolving, unformed and arbitrary, that it sounds like a note out of the ancient European regime, and as a seduction and re-duction back to it.
paras.uz: Chunki kuy qonunga muvofiqlikdan shunchalik ochiq zavqlanadi va rivojlanayotgan, shakllanmagan va o'zboshimcha hamma narsadan shunchalik jirkanadiki, u qadimiy Yevropa tuzumidan bir nota kabi, unga qaytishga vasvasa va chaqiriq kabi yangraydi.

chapters.title: Our gratitude to art

paras.en: 104. The Tone of the German Language. — We know whence the German originated which for several centuries has been the universal, literary language of Germany. The Germans, with their reverence for everything that came from the court, intentionally took the chancery style as their pattern in all that they had to write, especially in their letters, records, wills, &c. To write in the chancery style, that was to write in court and government style,—that was regarded as something select compared with the language of the city in which a person lived. People gradually drew this inference, and spoke also as they wrote,—they thus became still more select in the forms of their words, in the choice of their terms and modes of expression, and finally also in their tones: they affected a court tone when they spoke, and the affectation at last became natural.
paras.uz: 104. Nemis tilining ohangi. — Bir necha asrdan beri Germaniyaning umumiy adabiy tili bo'lib kelgan nemis tili qayerdan kelib chiqqanini bilamiz. Saroydan kelgan hamma narsaga hurmati bilan nemislar yozishlari kerak bo'lgan hamma narsada, ayniqsa xatlari, hujjatlari, vasiyatnomalari va hokazolarda qasddan kantselyariya uslubini namuna qilib olishgan. Kantselyariya uslubida yozish — saroy va hukumat uslubida yozish edi, — bu odam yashaydigan shahar tiliga nisbatan tanlangan narsa deb hisoblangan. Odamlar asta-sekin shu xulosaga kelib, yozganlaridek gapira ham boshlashgan, — shu tariqa ular so'z shakllarida, atamalar va ifoda usullarini tanlashda va oxir-oqibat ohanglarida ham yana ham tanlanganroq bo'lishgan: ular gapirganda saroy ohangiga taqlid qilishgan va taqlid oxir-oqibat tabiiy bo'lib qolgan.

paras.en: Perhaps nothing quite similar has ever happened elsewhere:—the predominance of the literary style over the talk, and the formality and affectation of an entire people, becoming the basis of a common and no longer dialectical language. I believe that the sound of the German language in the Middle Ages, and especially after the Middle Ages, was extremely rustic and vulgar; it has ennobled itself somewhat during the last centuries, principally because it was found necessary to imitate so many French, Italian, and Spanish sounds, and particularly on the part of the German (and Austrian) nobility, who could not at all content themselves with their mother-tongue.
paras.uz: Balki boshqa joyda bunga butunlay o'xshash narsa hech qachon bo'lmagandir: — adabiy uslubning og'zaki nutq ustidan hukmronligi va butun bir xalqning rasmiyatchiligi va taqlidi umumiy va endi shevaga xos bo'lmagan tilning asosiga aylanishi. Ishonamanki, O'rta asrlarda, ayniqsa O'rta asrlardan keyin nemis tilining jarangi nihoyatda qishloqi va qo'pol bo'lgan; u so'nggi asrlarda biroz olijanoblashdi, asosan juda ko'p fransuz, italyan va ispan tovushlariga taqlid qilish zarur deb topilgani uchun, ayniqsa ona tili bilan umuman qanoatlana olmagan nemis (va avstriyalik) zodagonlari tomonidan.

paras.en: But notwithstanding this practice, German must have sounded intolerably vulgar to Montaigne, and even to Racine: even at present, in the mouths of travellers among the Italian populace, it still sounds very coarse, sylvan, and hoarse, as if it had originated in smoky rooms and outlandish districts.—Now I notice that at present a similar striving after selectness of tone is spreading among the former admirers of the chancery style, and that the Germans are beginning to accommodate themselves to a peculiar "witchery of sound," which might in the long run become an actual danger to the German language,—for one may seek in vain for more execrable sounds in Europe.
paras.uz: Lekin bu amaliyotga qaramay, nemis tili Monten va hatto Rasinga chidab bo'lmas darajada qo'pol eshitilgan bo'lsa kerak: hatto hozir ham italyan oddiy xalqi orasidagi sayyohlarning og'zida u hali ham juda qo'pol, o'rmoniy va bo'g'iq eshitiladi, go'yo tutunli xonalar va olis o'lkalarda paydo bo'lgandek. — Endi men payqaymanki, hozir kantselyariya uslubining sobiq muxlislari orasida ohangning tanlanganligiga shunga o'xshash intilish tarqalmoqda va nemislar o'ziga xos «tovush sehri»ga moslasha boshlashmoqda, bu uzoq muddatda nemis tili uchun haqiqiy xavfga aylanishi mumkin, — chunki Yevropada bundan jirkanchroq tovushlarni behuda izlash mumkin.

paras.en: Something mocking, cold, indifferent, and careless in the voice: that is what at present sounds "noble" to the Germans—and I hear the approval of this nobleness in the voices of young officials, teachers, women, and trades-people; indeed, even the little girls already imitate this German of the officers. For the officer, and in fact the Prussian officer is the inventor of these tones: this same officer, who, as soldier and professional man possesses that admirable tact for modesty which the Germans as a whole might well imitate (German professors and musicians included!). But as soon as he speaks and moves he is the most immodest and inelegant figure in old Europe—no doubt unconsciously to himself!
paras.uz: Ovozdagi qandaydir masxaraomuz, sovuq, befarq va beparvo narsa: hozir nemislarga «olijanob» eshitiladigan narsa shu — va men bu olijanoblikni ma'qullashni yosh amaldorlar, o'qituvchilar, ayollar va savdogarlarning ovozlarida eshitaman; haqiqatan ham, hatto kichkina qizlar ham allaqachon ofitserlarning bu nemis tiliga taqlid qilishadi. Chunki ofitser, aslida prussiyalik ofitser bu ohanglarning ixtirochisi: o'sha ofitser askar va kasb egasi sifatida nemislar umuman olganda taqlid qilsa arziydigan ajoyib kamtarlik odobiga ega (nemis professorlari va musiqachilari ham!). Lekin gapirishi va harakatlanishi bilanoq u eski Yevropadagi eng kamtarsiz va eng nafosatsiz qiyofaga aylanadi — shubhasiz, o'zi buni anglamagan holda!

paras.en: And unconsciously also to the good Germans, who gaze at him as the man of the foremost and most select society, and willingly let him "give them his tone." And indeed he gives it to them!—in the first place it is the sergeant-majors and non-commissioned officers that imitate his tone and coarsen it. One should note the roars of command, with which the German cities are absolutely surrounded at present, when there is drilling at all the gates: what presumption, furious imperiousness, and mocking coldness speaks in this uproar! Could the Germans actually be a musical people?—It is certain that the Germans martialise themselves at present in the tone of their language: it is probable that, being exercised to speak martially, they will finally write martially also.
paras.uz: Va unga eng oldingi va eng tanlangan jamiyat odami deb qaraydigan va unga bajonidil «o'z ohangini berishga» yo'l qo'yadigan yaxshi nemislar ham buni anglamagan holda. Va haqiqatan ham u ularga beradi! — birinchi navbatda uning ohangiga feldfebellar va unter-ofitserlar taqlid qilib, uni qo'pollashtiradi. Hozir barcha darvozalarda mashq bo'layotganda nemis shaharlarini butunlay o'rab olgan buyruq bo'kiriqlariga e'tibor bering: bu shovqinda qanday takabburlik, quturgan hukmronlik va masxaraomuz sovuqlik gapiradi! Nemislar haqiqatan ham musiqiy xalq bo'lishi mumkinmi? — Aniqki, nemislar hozir tilining ohangida o'zlarini harbiylashtirmoqda: ehtimol, harbiycha gapirishga o'rgatilgan holda, oxir-oqibat harbiycha yozishadi ham.

paras.en: For habituation to definite tones extends deeply into the character:—people soon have the words and modes of expression, and finally also the thoughts which just suit these tones! Perhaps they already write in the officers' style; perhaps I only read too little of what is at present written in Germany to know this. But one thing I know all the surer: the German public declarations which also reach places abroad, are not inspired by German music, but just by that new tone of tasteless arrogance. Almost in every speech of the foremost German statesman, and even when he makes himself heard through his imperial mouth-piece, there is an accent which the ear of a foreigner repudiates with aversion: but the Germans endure it,—they endure themselves.
paras.uz: Chunki ma'lum ohanglarga o'rganish xarakterga chuqur yoyiladi: — odamlarda tez orada aynan shu ohanglarga mos keladigan so'zlar va ifoda usullari, oxir-oqibat fikrlar ham paydo bo'ladi! Balki ular allaqachon ofitserlar uslubida yozishar; balki men buni bilish uchun hozir Germaniyada yozilayotgan narsalardan haddan tashqari kam o'qiyman. Lekin bir narsani yana ham aniqroq bilaman: chet elga ham yetib boradigan nemis jamoat bayonotlari nemis musiqasidan emas, balki aynan didsiz takabburlikning o'sha yangi ohangidan ilhomlangan. Eng oldingi nemis davlat arbobining deyarli har bir nutqida, hatto u o'zini imperator ruporu orqali eshittirganda ham, chet ellikning qulog'i jirkanish bilan rad etadigan urg'u bor: lekin nemislar unga chidashadi, — ular o'zlariga chidashadi.

paras.en: 105. The Germans as Artists. — When once a German actually experiences passion (and not only, as is usual, the mere inclination to it), he then behaves just as he must do in passion, and does not think further of his behaviour. The truth is, however, that he then behaves very awkwardly and uglily, and as if destitute of rhythm and melody; so that onlookers are pained or moved thereby, but nothing more—unless he elevate himself to the sublimity and enrapturedness of which certain passions are capable. Then even the German becomes beautiful. The perception of the height at which beauty begins to shed its charm even over Germans, raises German artists to the height, to the supreme height, and to the extravagances of passion: they have an actual, profound longing, therefore, to get beyond, or at least to look beyond the ugliness and awkwardness—into a better, easier, more southern, more sunny world. And thus their convulsions are often merely indications that they would like to dance: these poor bears in whom hidden nymphs and satyrs, and sometimes still higher divinities, carry on their game!
paras.uz: 105. Nemislar san'atkor sifatida. — Nemis bir marta haqiqatan ehtirosni boshdan kechirganda (va odatdagidek shunchaki unga moyillikni emas), u ehtirosda qanday harakat qilishi kerak bo'lsa, shunday harakat qiladi va o'z xatti-harakati haqida boshqa o'ylamaydi. Biroq haqiqat shundaki, u o'shanda juda noqulay va xunuk harakat qiladi, go'yo ritm va kuydan mahrumdek; shunda tomoshabinlar bundan og'riq his qiladi yoki ta'sirlanadi, lekin boshqa hech narsa — agar u ba'zi ehtiroslar qodir bo'lgan yuksaklik va vajdgacha ko'tarilmasa. O'shanda hatto nemis ham go'zal bo'ladi. Go'zallik hatto nemislar ustiga ham jozibasini yoya boshlaydigan balandlikni sezish nemis san'atkorlarini balandlikka, eng oliy balandlikka va ehtirosning haddan oshishlariga ko'taradi: shuning uchun ularda xunuklik va noqulaylikdan narida o'tishga yoki hech bo'lmasa naridan qarashga — yaxshiroq, yengilroq, janubiyroq, quyoshliroq dunyoga haqiqiy, chuqur sog'inch bor. Shunday qilib, ularning talvasalari ko'pincha shunchaki raqsga tushmoqchi ekanliklarining belgisi: bu bechora ayiqlar, ularda yashirin parilar va satirlar, ba'zan esa yana ham yuksakroq ilohlar o'z o'yinini o'ynaydi!

paras.en: 106. Music as Advocate. — "I have a longing for a master of the musical art," said an innovator to his disciple, "that he may learn from me my ideas and speak them more widely in his language: I shall thus be better able to reach men's ears and hearts. For by means of tones one can seduce men to every error and every truth: who could refute a tone?"—"You would, therefore, like to be regarded as irrefutable?" said his disciple. The innovator answered: "I should like the germ to become a tree. In order that a doctrine may become a tree, it must be believed in for a considerable period; in order that it may be believed in it must be regarded as irrefutable.
paras.uz: 106. Musiqa himoyachi sifatida. — «Menga musiqa san'ati ustasi kerak, — dedi bir yangilik kirituvchi shogirdiga, — u mendan g'oyalarimni o'rganib, ularni o'z tilida kengroq gapirsin: shunda men odamlarning quloqlari va yuraklariga yaxshiroq yeta olaman. Chunki ohanglar yordamida odamlarni har qanday xatoga va har qanday haqiqatga yo'ldan urish mumkin: ohangni kim rad eta olardi?» — «Demak, siz rad etib bo'lmaydigan deb hisoblanishni istaysizmi?» — dedi shogirdi. Yangilik kirituvchi javob berdi: «Men urug'ning daraxtga aylanishini istayman. Ta'limot daraxtga aylanishi uchun unga ancha uzoq vaqt ishonilishi kerak; unga ishonilishi uchun u rad etib bo'lmaydigan deb hisoblanishi kerak.

paras.en: Storms and doubts and worms and wickedness are necessary to the tree, that it may manifest its species and the strength of its germ; let it perish if it is not strong enough! But a germ is always merely annihilated,—not refuted!"—When he had said this, his disciple called out impetuously: "But I believe in your cause, and regard it as so strong that I will say everything against it, everything that I still have in my heart."—The innovator laughed to himself and threatened the disciple with his finger. "This kind of discipleship," said he then, "is the best, but it is dangerous, and not every kind of doctrine can stand it."
paras.uz: Daraxtga o'z turini va urug'ining kuchini namoyon qilishi uchun bo'ronlar, shubhalar, qurtlar va yovuzlik kerak; agar yetarlicha kuchli bo'lmasa, halok bo'lsin! Lekin urug' doimo faqat yo'q qilinadi, — rad etilmaydi!» — U buni aytgach, shogirdi shiddat bilan xitob qildi: «Lekin men sizning ishingizga ishonaman va uni shunchalik kuchli deb bilamanki, unga qarshi hamma narsani, yuragimda hali bor hamma narsani aytaman». — Yangilik kirituvchi ichida kulib, shogirdiga barmog'i bilan do'q qildi. «Shogirdlikning bu turi, — dedi u keyin, — eng yaxshisi, lekin xavfli va har qanday ta'limot ham unga bardosh bera olmaydi».

paras.en: 107. Our Ultimate Gratitude to Art. — If we had not approved of the Arts and invented this sort of cult of the untrue, the insight into the general untruth and falsity of things now given us by science—an insight into delusion and error as conditions of intelligent and sentient existence—would be quite unendurable. Honesty would have disgust and suicide in its train. Now, however, our honesty has a counterpoise which helps us to escape such consequences;—namely, Art, as the good-will to illusion. We do not always restrain our eyes from rounding off and perfecting in imagination: and then it is no longer the eternal imperfection that we carry over the river of Becoming—for we think we carry a goddess, and are proud and artless in rendering this service.
paras.uz: 107. San'atga so'nggi minnatdorligimiz. — Agar biz san'atlarni ma'qullamaganimizda va yolg'onga bunday sig'inishni ixtiro qilmaganimizda, ilm hozir bizga bergan narsalarning umumiy yolg'onligi va soxtaligi haqidagi tushuncha — aqlli va sezuvchi mavjudlikning shartlari sifatida xayol va xato haqidagi tushuncha — mutlaqo chidab bo'lmas bo'lardi. Halollik o'z ortidan jirkanish va o'z joniga qasd qilishni olib kelardi. Biroq endi halolligimizning muvozanatlovchisi bor, u bizga bunday oqibatlardan qochishga yordam beradi; — ya'ni san'at, xayolga bo'lgan yaxshi niyat sifatida. Biz ko'zlarimizni xayolda yumaloqlash va mukammallashtirishdan doimo tiymaymiz: va o'shanda biz Bo'lish daryosi ustidan olib o'tayotgan narsa endi abadiy nomukammallik emas — chunki biz ma'budani olib o'tyapmiz deb o'ylaymiz va bu xizmatni bajarishda mag'rur va sodda bo'lamiz.

paras.en: As an æsthetic phenomenon existence is still endurable to us; and by Art, eye and hand and above all the good conscience are given to us, to be able to make such a phenomenon out of ourselves. We must rest from ourselves occasionally by contemplating and looking down upon ourselves, and by laughing or weeping over ourselves from an artistic remoteness: we must discover the hero, and likewise the fool, that is hidden in our passion for knowledge; we must now and then be joyful in our folly, that we may continue to be joyful in our wisdom!
paras.uz: Estetik hodisa sifatida hayot bizga hali chidab bo'ladigan; va san'at orqali bizga o'zimizdan shunday hodisa yasay olish uchun ko'z, qo'l va eng avvalo toza vijdon beriladi. Biz vaqti-vaqti bilan o'zimizni mushohada qilib, o'zimizga yuqoridan qarab va badiiy uzoqlikdan o'zimiz ustidan kulib yoki yig'lab, o'zimizdan dam olishimiz kerak: biz bilimga bo'lgan ehtirosimizda yashiringan qahramonni, shuningdek, ahmoqni ham kashf etishimiz kerak; donoligimizda quvnoq bo'lishda davom etishimiz uchun vaqti-vaqti bilan ahmoqligimizda quvonishimiz kerak!

paras.en: And just because we are heavy and serious men in our ultimate depth, and are rather weights than men, there is nothing that does us so much good as the fool's cap and bells: we need them in presence of ourselves—we need all arrogant, soaring, dancing, mocking, childish and blessed Art, in order not to lose the free dominion over things which our ideal demands of us. It would be backsliding for us, with our susceptible integrity, to lapse entirely into morality, and actually become virtuous monsters and scarecrows, on account of the over-strict requirements which we here lay down for ourselves. We ought also to be able to stand above morality, and not only stand with the painful stiffness of one who every moment fears to slip and fall, but we should also be able to soar and play above it! How could we dispense with Art for that purpose, how could we dispense with the fool?—And as long as you are still ashamed of yourselves in any way, you still do not belong to us!
paras.uz: Va aynan eng chuqur qa'rimizda og'ir va jiddiy odamlar ekanimiz, odamlardan ko'ra ko'proq toshlar ekanimiz uchun, bizga masxarabozning qo'ng'iroqli qalpog'ichalik foyda keltiradigan narsa yo'q: ular bizga o'zimiz oldida kerak — idealimiz bizdan talab qiladigan narsalar ustidan erkin hukmronlikni yo'qotmaslik uchun bizga barcha takabbur, parvoz qiluvchi, raqsga tushuvchi, masxara qiluvchi, bolalarcha va saodatli san'at kerak. Sezgir halolligimiz bilan butunlay axloqqa tushib qolish va bu yerda o'zimizga qo'yadigan haddan tashqari qattiq talablar tufayli haqiqatan ham fazilatli mahluqlar va qo'rqinchli qo'g'irchoqlarga aylanish biz uchun orqaga qaytish bo'lardi. Biz axloqdan yuqorida ham tura olishimiz kerak, va nafaqat har lahza sirpanib yiqilishdan qo'rqadigan odamning og'riqli qotib qolishi bilan turish, balki uning ustida parvoz qilish va o'ynay olishimiz ham kerak! Buning uchun san'atsiz qanday qila olardik, ahmoqsiz qanday qila olardik? — Va hali ham o'zingizdan qandaydir tarzda uyalar ekansiz, siz hali bizga tegishli emassiz!

quiz.q: What would honesty lead to without art?
quiz.why_uz: San'at halollikning muvozanatlovchisi.

quiz.q: Why do serious people need the fool's cap?
o: To keep free dominion over things
quiz.why_uz: Axloqdan yuqorida ham tura olish uchun.

chapters.recap_uz: Nemis tilining «ofitser ohangi», nemislar san'atkor sifatida va musiqa ta'limot himoyachisi sifatida. Ikkinchi kitob xulosasi: ilm hamma narsaning yolg'onligini ko'rsatsa, san'at — xayolga bo'lgan yaxshi niyat — bizni qutqaradi. Ahmoq qalpog'i ham kerak.

chapters.title: God is dead — new struggles

paras.en: 108. New Struggles. — After Buddha was dead people showed his shadow for centuries afterwards in a cave,—an immense frightful shadow. God is dead: but as the human race is constituted, there will perhaps be caves for millenniums yet, in which people will show his shadow,—And we—we have still to overcome his shadow!
paras.uz: 108. Yangi kurashlar. — Budda vafot etgandan keyin odamlar asrlar davomida bir g'orda uning soyasini ko'rsatib yurishgan, — ulkan, dahshatli soyani. Xudo o'ldi: lekin inson zoti qanday tuzilgan bo'lsa, ehtimol, yana ming yillar davomida uning soyasini ko'rsatadigan g'orlar bo'lar, — Biz esa — biz hali uning soyasini ham yengishimiz kerak!

paras.en: 109. Let us be on our Guard. — Let us be on our guard against thinking that the world is a living being. Where could it extend itself? What could it nourish itself with? How could it grow and increase? We know tolerably well what the organic is; and we are to reinterpret the emphatically derivative, tardy, rare and accidental, which we only perceive on the crust of the earth, into the essential, universal and eternal, as those do who call the universe an organism? That disgusts me.
paras.uz: 109. Ehtiyot bo'laylik. — Dunyo tirik mavjudot deb o'ylashdan ehtiyot bo'laylik. U qayerga yoyilishi mumkin? Nima bilan oziqlanishi mumkin? Qanday o'sib, ko'payishi mumkin? Biz organik narsa nima ekanini yetarlicha yaxshi bilamiz; va biz faqat yer po'stida ko'radigan, ochiqdan-ochiq hosila, kechikkan, kamyob va tasodifiy narsani, koinotni organizm deb ataydiganlar kabi, mohiyatli, umumiy va abadiy narsa deb qayta talqin qilishimiz kerakmi? Bu meni jirkantiradi.

paras.en: Let us now be on our guard against believing that the universe is a machine; it is assuredly not constructed with a view to one end; we invest it with far too high an honour with the word "machine." Let us be on our guard against supposing that anything so methodical as the cyclic motions of our neighbouring stars obtains generally and throughout the universe; indeed a glance at the Milky Way induces doubt as to whether there are not many cruder and more contradictory motions there, and even stars with continuous, rectilinearly gravitating orbits, and the like. The astral arrangement in which we live is an exception; this arrangement, and the relatively long durability which is determined by it, has again made possible the exception of exceptions, the formation of organic life.
paras.uz: Endi koinot mashina deb ishonishdan ehtiyot bo'laylik; u albatta bir maqsadni ko'zlab qurilmagan; «mashina» so'zi bilan biz unga haddan tashqari yuksak sharaf beramiz. Qo'shni yulduzlarimizning siklik harakatlari kabi muntazam narsa umuman va butun koinotda amal qiladi deb faraz qilishdan ehtiyot bo'laylik; haqiqatan ham, Somon yo'liga bir qarash u yerda ko'plab qo'polroq va qarama-qarshiroq harakatlar, hatto uzluksiz, to'g'ri chiziqli tortiladigan orbitali yulduzlar va shunga o'xshashlar yo'qmi degan shubha uyg'otadi. Biz yashaydigan yulduzlar tartibi — istisno; bu tartib va u belgilaydigan nisbatan uzoq barqarorlik yana istisnolar istisnosi — organik hayotning shakllanishini mumkin qilgan.

paras.en: The general character of the world, on the other hand, is to all eternity chaos; not by the absence of necessity, but in the sense of the absence of order, structure, form, beauty, wisdom, and whatever else our æsthetic humanities are called. Judged by our reason, the unlucky casts are far oftenest the rule, the exceptions are not the secret purpose; and the whole musical box repeats eternally its air, which can never be called a melody,—and finally the very expression, "unlucky cast" is already an anthropomorphising which involves blame. But how could we presume to blame or praise the universe! Let us be on our guard against ascribing to it heartlessness and unreason, or their opposites; it is neither perfect, nor beautiful, nor noble; nor does it seek to be anything of the kind, it does not at all attempt to imitate man!
paras.uz: Boshqa tomondan, dunyoning umumiy xarakteri abadiy tartibsizlik — xaosdir; zaruratning yo'qligi bilan emas, balki tartib, tuzilish, shakl, go'zallik, donolik va bizning estetik insoniyliklarimiz qanday atalsa, ularning yo'qligi ma'nosida. Aqlimiz bilan baholaganda, omadsiz tashlashlar eng ko'p qoida bo'ladi, istisnolar yashirin maqsad emas; va butun musiqa qutisi abadiy o'z kuyini takrorlaydi, uni hech qachon melodiya deb atab bo'lmaydi, — va nihoyat, «omadsiz tashlash» iborasining o'zi ham allaqachon ayblashni o'z ichiga olgan insonlashtirish. Lekin qanday qilib koinotni ayblash yoki maqtashga jur'at eta olardik! Unga shafqatsizlik va aqlsizlikni yoki ularning qarama-qarshisini nisbat berishdan ehtiyot bo'laylik; u na mukammal, na go'zal, na olijanob; u shunday narsa bo'lishga ham intilmaydi, u insonga taqlid qilishga umuman urinmaydi!

paras.en: It is altogether unaffected by our æsthetic and moral judgments! Neither has it any self-preservative instinct, nor instinct at all; it also knows no law. Let us be on our guard against saying that there are laws in nature. There are only necessities: there is no one who commands, no one who obeys, no one who transgresses. When you know that there is no design, you know also that there is no chance: for it is only where there is a world of design that the word "chance" has a meaning. Let us be on our guard against saying that death is contrary to life. The living being is only a species of dead being, and a very rare species.—Let us be on our guard against thinking that the world eternally creates the new.
paras.uz: U bizning estetik va axloqiy hukmlarimizdan butunlay ta'sirlanmaydi! Unda na o'zini saqlash instinkti, na umuman instinkt bor; u qonunni ham bilmaydi. Tabiatda qonunlar bor deyishdan ehtiyot bo'laylik. Faqat zaruratlar bor: buyuradigan ham, bo'ysunadigan ham, buzadigan ham yo'q. Maqsad yo'qligini bilsangiz, tasodif ham yo'qligini bilasiz: chunki «tasodif» so'zi faqat maqsadlar dunyosi bo'lgan joydagina ma'noga ega. O'lim hayotga zid deyishdan ehtiyot bo'laylik. Tirik mavjudot faqat o'lik mavjudotning bir turi, va juda kamyob turi. — Dunyo abadiy yangilik yaratadi deb o'ylashdan ehtiyot bo'laylik.

paras.en: There are no eternally enduring substances; matter is just another such error as the God of the Eleatics. But when shall we be at an end with our foresight and precaution! When will all these shadows of God cease to obscure us? When shall we have nature entirely undeified! When shall we be permitted to naturalise ourselves by means of the pure, newly discovered, newly redeemed nature?
paras.uz: Abadiy barqaror substansiyalar yo'q; materiya eleatlarning Xudosi kabi yana bir xato. Lekin bu ehtiyotkorlik va hushyorligimiz qachon tugaydi! Xudoning bu soyalarining hammasi qachon bizni qoraytirishdan to'xtaydi! Tabiatni qachon butunlay ilohiylikdan xoli qilamiz! Sof, yangi kashf etilgan, yangi qutqarilgan tabiat yordamida o'zimizni tabiiylashtirishimizga qachon ruxsat beriladi?

paras.en: 110. Origin of Knowledge. — Throughout immense stretches of time the intellect has produced nothing but errors; some of them proved to be useful and preservative of the species: he who fell in with them, or inherited them, waged the battle for himself and his offspring with better success. Those erroneous articles of faith which were successively transmitted by inheritance, and have finally become almost the property and stock of the human species, are, for example, the following:—that there are enduring things, that there are equal things, that there are things, substances, and bodies, that a thing is what it appears, that our will is free, that what is good for me is also good absolutely. It was only very late that the deniers and doubters of such propositions came forward,—it was only very late that truth made its appearance as the most impotent form of knowledge.
paras.uz: 110. Bilimning kelib chiqishi. — Ulkan vaqt oraliqlari davomida aql xatolardan boshqa hech narsa yaratmagan; ulardan ba'zilari foydali va turni saqlovchi bo'lib chiqqan: ularga duch kelgan yoki ularni meros qilib olgan kishi o'zi va avlodi uchun kurashni yaxshiroq muvaffaqiyat bilan olib borgan. Ketma-ket meros orqali o'tib, oxir-oqibat deyarli inson turining mulki va boyligiga aylangan o'sha xato e'tiqod moddalari, masalan, quyidagilar: — barqaror narsalar bor, teng narsalar bor, narsalar, substansiyalar va jismlar bor, narsa qanday ko'rinsa shunday, irodamiz erkin, men uchun yaxshi bo'lgan narsa mutlaq yaxshi. Bunday da'volarni inkor etuvchilar va shubhalanuvchilar juda kech maydonga chiqqan, — haqiqat faqat juda kech bilimning eng kuchsiz shakli sifatida paydo bo'lgan.

paras.en: It seemed as if it were impossible to get along with truth, our organism was adapted for the very opposite; all its higher functions, the perceptions of the senses, and in general every kind of sensation co-operated with those primevally embodied, fundamental errors. Moreover, those propositions became the very standards of knowledge according to which the "true" and the "false" were determined—throughout the whole domain of pure logic. The strength of conceptions does not, therefore, depend on their degree of truth, but on their antiquity, their embodiment, their character as conditions of life. Where life and knowledge seemed to conflict, there has never been serious contention; denial and doubt have there been regarded as madness.
paras.uz: Go'yo haqiqat bilan yashab bo'lmaydigandek tuyulardi, organizmimiz aynan aksiga moslashgan edi; uning barcha yuksakroq funksiyalari, sezgi idroklari va umuman har qanday tuyg'u o'sha qadimdan singdirilgan asosiy xatolar bilan hamkorlik qilgan. Bundan tashqari, bu da'volar bilimning aynan o'lchovlariga aylangan, ularga ko'ra «to'g'ri» va «noto'g'ri» belgilangan — sof mantiqning butun sohasi bo'ylab. Demak, tushunchalarning kuchi ularning haqiqat darajasiga emas, balki qadimiyligiga, singdirilganligiga, hayot shartlari sifatidagi xarakteriga bog'liq. Hayot va bilim to'qnashayotgandek ko'ringan joyda hech qachon jiddiy bahs bo'lmagan; u yerda inkor va shubha telbalik deb hisoblangan.

paras.en: The exceptional thinkers like the Eleatics, who, in spite of this, advanced and maintained the antitheses of the natural errors, believed that it was possible also to live these counterparts: it was they who devised the sage as the man of immutability, impersonality and universality of intuition, as one and all at the same time, with a special faculty for that reverse kind of knowledge; they were of the belief that their knowledge was at the same time the principle of life.
paras.uz: Bunga qaramay tabiiy xatolarning qarama-qarshisini ilgari surgan va himoya qilgan eleatlar kabi istisno mutafakkirlar bu qarama-qarshiliklar bilan yashash ham mumkin deb ishonishgan: aynan ular donishmandni o'zgarmaslik, shaxssizlik va sezgining umumiyligi odami sifatida, bir vaqtning o'zida bitta va hamma sifatida, o'sha teskari bilim uchun alohida qobiliyatga ega odam sifatida o'ylab topishgan; ular o'z bilimlari bir vaqtning o'zida hayot tamoyili ham deb ishonishgan.

paras.en: To be able to affirm all this, however, they had to deceive themselves concerning their own condition: they had to attribute to themselves impersonality and unchanging permanence, they had to mistake the nature of the philosophic individual, deny the force of the impulses in cognition, and conceive of reason generally as an entirely free and self-originating activity; they kept their eyes shut to the fact that they also had reached their doctrines in contradiction to valid methods, or through their longing for repose or for exclusive possession or for domination.
paras.uz: Biroq bularning hammasini tasdiqlay olish uchun ular o'z holatlari haqida o'zlarini aldashlari kerak edi: ular o'zlariga shaxssizlik va o'zgarmas barqarorlik nisbat berishlari, faylasuf shaxsning tabiatini noto'g'ri tushunishlari, bilishdagi mayllarning kuchini inkor etishlari va aqlni umuman butunlay erkin va o'zidan kelib chiqadigan faoliyat deb tasavvur qilishlari kerak edi; ular o'zlari ham o'z ta'limotlariga to'g'ri usullarga zid ravishda yoki osoyishtalikka, yoki yagona egalikka, yoki hukmronlikka bo'lgan sog'inchlari orqali yetib kelganlariga ko'z yumishgan.

paras.en: The subtler development of sincerity and of scepticism finally made these men impossible; their life also and their judgments turned out to be dependent on the primeval impulses and fundamental errors of all sentient being.—The subtler sincerity and scepticism arose whenever two antithetical maxims appeared to be applicable to life, because both of them were compatible with the fundamental errors; where, therefore, there could be contention concerning a higher or lower degree of utility for life; and likewise where new maxims proved to be, not in fact useful, but at least not injurious, as expressions of an intellectual impulse to play a game that was, like all games, innocent and happy. The human brain was gradually filled with such judgments and convictions; and in this tangled skein there arose ferment, strife and lust for power.
paras.uz: Samimiyat va skeptitsizmning nozikroq rivojlanishi oxir-oqibat bu odamlarni imkonsiz qildi; ularning hayoti va hukmlari ham barcha sezuvchi mavjudotning qadimiy mayllari va asosiy xatolariga bog'liq bo'lib chiqdi. — Nozikroq samimiyat va skeptitsizm ikki qarama-qarshi qoida hayotga qo'llanilishi mumkin bo'lib ko'ringan har safar paydo bo'lgan, chunki ikkalasi ham asosiy xatolarga mos edi; demak, hayot uchun yuqoriroq yoki pastroq foydalilik darajasi haqida bahs bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan joyda; shuningdek, yangi qoidalar aslida foydali emas, lekin hech bo'lmasa zararsiz bo'lib chiqqan joyda, barcha o'yinlar kabi beg'ubor va baxtli o'yin o'ynashga bo'lgan aqliy maylning ifodasi sifatida. Inson miyasi asta-sekin bunday hukmlar va ishonchlar bilan to'ldi; va bu chigal kalavada achish, kurash va hokimiyatga hirs paydo bo'ldi.

paras.en: Not only utility and delight, but every kind of impulse took part in the struggle for "truths": the intellectual struggle became a business, an attraction, a calling, a duty, an honour—: cognizing and striving for the true finally arranged themselves as needs among other needs. From that moment, not only belief and conviction, but also examination, denial, distrust and contradiction became forces; all "evil" instincts were subordinated to knowledge, were placed in its service, and acquired the prestige of the permitted, the honoured, the useful, and finally the appearance and innocence of the good. Knowledge, thus became a portion of life itself, and as life it became a continually growing power: until finally the cognitions and those primeval, fundamental, errors clashed with each other, both as life, both as power, both in the same man.
paras.uz: «Haqiqatlar» uchun kurashda nafaqat foydalilik va zavq, balki har qanday mayl ishtirok etdi: aqliy kurash ish, jozibalilik, kasb, burch, sharafga aylandi —: bilish va haqiqatga intilish oxir-oqibat boshqa ehtiyojlar orasida ehtiyoj sifatida joylashdi. O'sha lahzadan boshlab nafaqat e'tiqod va ishonch, balki tekshirish, inkor, ishonchsizlik va qarama-qarshilik ham kuchga aylandi; barcha «yovuz» instinktlar bilimga bo'ysundirildi, uning xizmatiga qo'yildi va ruxsat etilgan, hurmatli, foydali narsaning obro'sini va oxir-oqibat yaxshilikning ko'rinishi va beg'uborligini oldi. Shunday qilib, bilim hayotning o'zining bir qismiga aylandi va hayot sifatida doimo o'sib boruvchi kuchga aylandi: toki oxir-oqibat bilimlar va o'sha qadimiy, asosiy xatolar bir-biri bilan to'qnashdi, ikkalasi ham hayot sifatida, ikkalasi ham kuch sifatida, ikkalasi ham bir odamda.

paras.en: The thinker is now the being in whom the impulse to truth and those life-preserving errors wage their first conflict, now that the impulse to truth has also proved itself to be a life-preserving power. In comparison with the importance of this conflict everything else is indifferent; the final question concerning the conditions of life is here raised, and the first attempt is here made to answer it by experiment. How far is truth susceptible of embodiment?—that is the question, that is the experiment.
paras.uz: Mutafakkir endi haqiqatga bo'lgan mayl va hayotni saqlovchi o'sha xatolar o'zlarining birinchi kurashini olib boradigan mavjudot, endi haqiqatga bo'lgan mayl ham hayotni saqlovchi kuch ekanini isbotlaganida. Bu kurashning ahamiyati bilan solishtirganda qolgan hamma narsa befarq; bu yerda hayot shartlari haqidagi oxirgi savol qo'yiladi va bu yerda unga tajriba bilan javob berishga birinchi urinish qilinadi. Haqiqat qanchalik singdirilishi mumkin? — savol shu, tajriba shu.

paras.en: 111. Origin of the Logical. — Where has logic originated in men's heads? Undoubtedly out of the illogical, the domain of which must originally have been immense. But numberless beings who reasoned otherwise than we do at present, perished; albeit that they may have come nearer to truth than we! Whoever, for example, could not discern the "like" often enough with regard to food, and with regard to animals dangerous to him, whoever, therefore, deduced too slowly, or was too circumspect in his deductions, had smaller probability of survival than he who in all similar things immediately divined the equality. The preponderating inclination, however, to deal with the similar as the equal—an illogical inclination, for there is nothing equal in itself—first created the whole basis of logic.
paras.uz: 111. Mantiqning kelib chiqishi. — Mantiq odamlarning boshida qayerdan paydo bo'lgan? Shubhasiz, mantiqsizlikdan, uning sohasi dastlab ulkan bo'lgan bo'lsa kerak. Lekin biz hozir fikrlagandan boshqacha fikrlagan son-sanoqsiz mavjudotlar halok bo'lgan; garchi ular haqiqatga bizdan yaqinroq kelgan bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa ham! Masalan, ovqatga nisbatan va o'zi uchun xavfli hayvonlarga nisbatan «o'xshash»ni yetarlicha tez-tez ajrata olmagan, demak, juda sekin xulosa chiqargan yoki xulosalarida haddan tashqari ehtiyotkor bo'lgan kishining omon qolish ehtimoli barcha o'xshash narsalarda darhol tenglikni sezgan kishinikidan kamroq bo'lgan. Biroq o'xshash narsaga teng narsa sifatida munosabatda bo'lishga ustun moyillik — mantiqsiz moyillik, chunki o'z-o'zidan teng narsa yo'q — mantiqning butun asosini birinchi bo'lib yaratgan.

paras.en: It was just so (in order that the conception of substance might originate, this being indispensable to logic, although in the strictest sense nothing actual corresponds to it) that for a long period the changing process in things had to be overlooked, and remain unperceived; the beings not seeing correctly had an advantage over those who saw everything "in flux." In itself every high degree of circumspection in conclusions, every sceptical inclination, is a great danger to life.
paras.uz: Xuddi shunday (mantiq uchun zarur bo'lgan, garchi eng qat'iy ma'noda hech qanday haqiqiy narsa unga mos kelmasa ham, substansiya tushunchasi paydo bo'lishi uchun) uzoq vaqt davomida narsalardagi o'zgarish jarayoni e'tiborsiz qolishi va sezilmasligi kerak edi; to'g'ri ko'rmaydigan mavjudotlar hamma narsani «oqimda» ko'radiganlardan ustun edi. O'z-o'zidan xulosalardagi har qanday yuqori ehtiyotkorlik darajasi, har qanday skeptik moyillik hayot uchun katta xavfdir.

paras.en: No living being would have been preserved unless the contrary inclination—to affirm rather than suspend judgment, to mistake and fabricate rather than wait, to assent rather than deny, to decide rather than be in the right—had been cultivated with extraordinary assiduity.—The course of logical thought and reasoning in our modern brain corresponds to a process and struggle of impulses, which singly and in themselves are all very illogical and unjust; we experience usually only the result of the struggle, so rapidly and secretly does this primitive mechanism now operate in us.
paras.uz: Agar qarama-qarshi moyillik — hukmni to'xtatishdan ko'ra tasdiqlash, kutishdan ko'ra xato qilish va to'qish, inkor etishdan ko'ra rozi bo'lish, haq bo'lishdan ko'ra qaror qilish — g'ayrioddiy tirishqoqlik bilan parvarish qilinmaganida, hech bir tirik mavjudot saqlanib qolmasdi. — Zamonaviy miyamizdagi mantiqiy fikr va mulohaza yo'li alohida va o'z-o'zidan juda mantiqsiz va adolatsiz bo'lgan mayllarning jarayoni va kurashiga mos keladi; biz odatda faqat kurash natijasini boshdan kechiramiz, bu ibtidoiy mexanizm endi bizda shunchalik tez va yashirin ishlaydi.

paras.en: 112. Cause and Effect. — We say it is "explanation"; but it is only in "description" that we are in advance of the older stages of knowledge and science. We describe better,—we explain just as little as our predecessors. We have discovered a manifold succession where the naïve man and investigator of older cultures saw only two things, "cause" and "effect," as it was said; we have perfected the conception of becoming, but have not got a knowledge of what is above and behind the conception. The series of "causes" stands before us much more complete in every case; we conclude that this and that must first precede in order that that other may follow—but we have not grasped anything thereby. The peculiarity, for example, in every chemical process seems a "miracle," the same as before, just like all locomotion; nobody has "explained" impulse. How could we ever explain!
paras.uz: 112. Sabab va oqibat. — Biz buni «tushuntirish» deymiz; lekin biz bilim va ilmning eski bosqichlaridan faqat «tasvirlash»da oldindamiz. Biz yaxshiroq tasvirlaymiz, — o'tmishdoshlarimiz kabi kam tushuntiramiz. Biz sodda odam va eski madaniyatlar tadqiqotchisi faqat ikki narsani, aytilganidek «sabab» va «oqibat»ni ko'rgan joyda ko'p qirrali ketma-ketlikni kashf etdik; biz bo'lish tushunchasini mukammallashtirdik, lekin tushunchadan yuqorida va orqada nima borligi haqida bilimga ega bo'lmadik. «Sabablar» qatori har bir holatda oldimizda ancha to'liqroq turadi; biz u boshqasi kelishi uchun avval bu va u oldin kelishi kerak degan xulosaga kelamiz — lekin shu bilan hech narsani tushunmadik. Masalan, har bir kimyoviy jarayondagi o'ziga xoslik avvalgidek «mo''jiza» bo'lib ko'rinadi, xuddi har qanday harakat kabi; hech kim turtkini «tushuntirmagan». Qanday qilib biz tushuntira olardik!

paras.en: We operate only with things which do not exist, with lines, surfaces, bodies, atoms, divisible times, divisible spaces—how can explanation ever be possible when we first make everything a conception, our conception! It is sufficient to regard science as the exactest humanising of things that is possible; we always learn to describe ourselves more accurately by describing things and their successions. Cause and effect: there is probably never any such duality; in fact there is a continuum before us, from which we isolate a few portions;—just as we always observe a motion as isolated points, and therefore do not properly see it, but infer it. The abruptness with which many effects take place leads us into error; it is however only an abruptness for us. There is an infinite multitude of processes in that abrupt moment which escape us.
paras.uz: Biz faqat mavjud bo'lmagan narsalar bilan ishlaymiz — chiziqlar, yuzalar, jismlar, atomlar, bo'linadigan vaqtlar, bo'linadigan fazolar bilan — avval hamma narsani tushunchaga, o'z tushunchamizga aylantirsak, tushuntirish qanday qilib mumkin bo'lsin! Ilmni narsalarni iloji boricha eng aniq insonlashtirish deb hisoblash kifoya; biz narsalarni va ularning ketma-ketligini tasvirlash orqali doimo o'zimizni aniqroq tasvirlashni o'rganamiz. Sabab va oqibat: ehtimol, hech qachon bunday ikkilik yo'q; aslida oldimizda uzluksizlik bor, undan biz bir nechta qismni ajratib olamiz; — xuddi harakatni doimo alohida nuqtalar sifatida kuzatganimiz va shuning uchun uni to'g'ri ko'rmay, balki xulosa qilganimiz kabi. Ko'p ta'sirlarning to'satdanligi bizni xatoga olib boradi; biroq bu faqat biz uchun to'satdanlik. O'sha to'satdan lahzada bizdan qochib ketadigan cheksiz ko'p jarayonlar bor.

paras.en: An intellect which could see cause and effect as a continuum, which could see the flux of events not according to our mode of perception, as things arbitrarily separated and broken—would throw aside the conception of cause and effect, and would deny all conditionality.
paras.uz: Sabab va oqibatni uzluksizlik sifatida ko'ra oladigan, voqealar oqimini bizning idrok tarzimiz bo'yicha o'zboshimcha ajratilgan va bo'lingan narsalar sifatida emas, balki shunday ko'ra oladigan aql — sabab va oqibat tushunchasini chetga uloqtirib, har qanday shartlanganlikni inkor etardi.

paras.en: 113. The Theory of Poisons. — So many things have to be united in order that scientific thinking may arise, and all the necessary powers must have been devised, exercised, and fostered singly! In their isolation, however, they have very often had quite a different effect than at present, when they are confined within the limits of scientific thinking and kept mutually in check:—they have operated as poisons; for example, the doubting impulse, the denying impulse, the waiting impulse, the collecting impulse, the disintegrating impulse. Many hecatombs of men were sacrificed ere these impulses learned to understand their juxtaposition and regard themselves as functions of one organising force in one man! And how far are we still from the point at which the artistic powers and the practical wisdom of life shall co-operate with scientific thinking, so that a higher organic system may be formed, in relation to which the scholar, the physician, the artist, and the lawgiver, as we know them at present, will seem sorry antiquities!
paras.uz: 113. Zaharlar nazariyasi. — Ilmiy fikrlash paydo bo'lishi uchun shunchalik ko'p narsalar birlashishi kerak va barcha zarur kuchlar alohida-alohida o'ylab topilgan, mashq qilingan va parvarish qilingan bo'lishi kerak! Biroq ular alohida holda ko'pincha hozirgidan, ilmiy fikrlash chegaralarida cheklangan va bir-birini nazorat ostida tutganidan butunlay boshqacha ta'sir ko'rsatgan: — ular zahar sifatida ta'sir qilgan; masalan, shubhalanish mayli, inkor etish mayli, kutish mayli, to'plash mayli, parchalash mayli. Bu mayllar o'zlarining yonma-yonligini tushunishni va o'zlarini bir odamdagi bitta tashkil etuvchi kuchning funksiyalari deb bilishni o'rganmasdan oldin odamlarning ko'p gekatombalari qurbon qilingan! Va biz badiiy kuchlar va hayotning amaliy donoligi ilmiy fikrlash bilan hamkorlik qiladigan nuqtadan hali qanchalik uzoqmiz, shunda yuksakroq organik tizim shakllanadi, unga nisbatan hozir biz biladigan olim, shifokor, san'atkor va qonun chiqaruvchi ayanchli antikvarlarga o'xshab ko'rinadi!

paras.en: 114. The Extent of the Moral. — We construct a new picture, which we see immediately with the aid of all the old experiences which we have had, always according to the degree of our honesty and justice. The only events are moral events, even in the domain of sense-perception.
paras.uz: 114. Axloqning ko'lami. — Biz yangi tasvirni quramiz, uni darhol boshimizdan kechirgan barcha eski tajribalar yordamida, doimo halolligimiz va adolatimiz darajasiga ko'ra ko'ramiz. Hatto sezgi idroki sohasida ham yagona voqealar — axloqiy voqealar.

quiz.why_uz: G'orlarda hali ming yillar Xudoning soyasi ko'rsatiladi.
