chapters.recap_uz: Uchinchi kitob «Xudo o'ldi, lekin uning soyasini ham yengishimiz kerak» bilan boshlanadi. Dunyo na organizm, na mashina — u xaos. Bilim foydali xatolardan kelib chiqqan; mantiq mantiqsizlikdan. Sabab va oqibat — faqat tasvir.

chapters.title: The herd instinct

paras.en: 115. The Four Errors. — Man has been reared by his errors: firstly, he saw himself always imperfect; secondly, he attributed to himself imaginary qualities; thirdly, he felt himself in a false position in relation to the animals and nature; fourthly, he always devised new tables of values, and accepted them for a time as eternal and unconditioned, so that at one time this, and at another time that human impulse or state stood first, and was ennobled in consequence. When one has deducted the effect of these four errors, one has also deducted humanity, humaneness, and "human dignity."
paras.uz: 115. To'rt xato. — Insonni uning xatolari tarbiyalagan: birinchidan, u o'zini doimo nomukammal ko'rgan; ikkinchidan, o'ziga xayoliy xususiyatlar nisbat bergan; uchinchidan, o'zini hayvonlar va tabiatga nisbatan noto'g'ri holatda his qilgan; to'rtinchidan, u doimo yangi qadriyatlar jadvallarini o'ylab topgan va ularni bir muddat abadiy va shartsiz deb qabul qilgan, shunda goh bu, goh u inson mayli yoki holati birinchi o'ringa chiqqan va shuning natijasida olijanoblashtirilgan. Bu to'rt xatoning ta'sirini ayirib tashlasangiz, insoniyatni, insonparvarlikni va «inson qadr-qimmati»ni ham ayirib tashlagan bo'lasiz.

paras.en: 116. Herd-Instinct. — Wherever we meet with a morality we find a valuation and order of rank of the human impulses and activities. These valuations and orders of rank are always the expression of the needs of a community or herd: that which is in the first place to its advantage—and in the second place and third place—is also the authoritative standard for the worth of every individual. By morality the individual is taught to become a function of the herd, and to ascribe to himself value only as a function. As the conditions for the maintenance of one community have been very different from those of another community, there have been very different moralities; and in respect to the future essential transformations of herds and communities, states and societies, one can prophesy that there will still be very divergent moralities. Morality is the herd-instinct in the individual.
paras.uz: 116. Poda instinkti. — Qayerda axloqqa duch kelsak, inson mayllari va faoliyatlarining bahosi va darajalar tartibini topamiz. Bu baholar va darajalar tartibi doimo jamoa yoki podaning ehtiyojlari ifodasi: unga birinchi navbatda — ikkinchi va uchinchi navbatda ham — foydali bo'lgan narsa har bir shaxs qadrining ham obro'li o'lchovi. Axloq orqali shaxsga podaning funksiyasi bo'lishni va o'ziga faqat funksiya sifatida qadr berishni o'rgatishadi. Bir jamoani saqlash shartlari boshqa jamoanikidan juda farq qilgani uchun, juda turli axloqlar bo'lgan; va podalar va jamoalar, davlatlar va jamiyatlarning kelajakdagi muhim o'zgarishlariga nisbatan hali juda turlicha axloqlar bo'lishini bashorat qilish mumkin. Axloq — shaxsdagi poda instinktidir.

paras.en: 117. The Herd's Sting of Conscience. — In the longest and remotest ages of the human race there was quite a different sting of conscience from that of the present day. At present one only feels responsible for what one intends and for what one does, and we have our pride in ourselves. All our professors of jurisprudence start with this sentiment of individual independence and pleasure, as if the source of right had taken its rise here from the beginning. But throughout the longest period in the life of mankind there was nothing more terrible to a person than to feel himself independent. To be alone, to feel independent, neither to obey nor to rule, to represent an individual—that was no pleasure to a person then, but a punishment; he was condemned "to be an individual." Freedom of thought was regarded as discomfort personified.
paras.uz: 117. Podaning vijdon azobi. — Insoniyatning eng uzoq va eng olis davrlarida vijdon azobi hozirgidan butunlay boshqacha bo'lgan. Hozir odam faqat niyat qilgan va qilgan ishi uchun mas'ul ekanini his qiladi va biz o'zimizdan faxrlanamiz. Barcha huquqshunoslik professorlarimiz shaxsiy mustaqillik va lazzatning shu tuyg'usidan boshlashadi, go'yo huquq manbai boshidanoq shu yerdan boshlangandek. Lekin insoniyat hayotining eng uzun davri davomida odam uchun o'zini mustaqil his qilishdan dahshatliroq narsa bo'lmagan. Yolg'iz bo'lish, o'zini mustaqil his qilish, na bo'ysunish, na hukmronlik qilish, shaxsni ifodalash — bu o'shanda odam uchun lazzat emas, jazo edi; u «shaxs bo'lishga» hukm qilingan. Fikr erkinligi noqulaylikning timsoli deb hisoblangan.

paras.en: While we feel law and regulation as constraint and loss, people formerly regarded egoism as a painful thing, and a veritable evil. For a person to be himself, to value himself according to his own measure and weight—that was then quite distasteful. The inclination to such a thing would have been regarded as madness; for all miseries and terrors were associated with being alone. At that time the "free will" had bad conscience in close proximity to it; and the less independently a person acted, the more the herd-instinct, and not his personal character, expressed itself in his conduct, so much the more moral did he esteem himself. All that did injury to the herd, whether the individual had intended it or not, then caused him a sting of conscience—and his neighbour likewise, indeed the whole herd!—It is in this respect that we have most changed our mode of thinking.
paras.uz: Biz qonun va tartibni majburlov va yo'qotish deb his qilsak, odamlar ilgari xudbinlikni og'riqli narsa va chinakam yomonlik deb bilishgan. Odamning o'zi bo'lishi, o'zini o'z o'lchovi va og'irligi bilan baholashi — bu o'shanda butunlay yoqimsiz edi. Bunday narsaga moyillik telbalik deb hisoblangan bo'lardi; chunki barcha baxtsizliklar va dahshatlar yolg'iz bo'lish bilan bog'liq edi. O'shanda «erkin iroda»ning yonginasida yomon vijdon turardi; va odam qanchalik kam mustaqil harakat qilsa, uning xulqida shaxsiy xarakteri emas, poda instinkti qanchalik ko'p namoyon bo'lsa, u o'zini shunchalik axloqliroq deb bilardi. Podaga zarar keltirgan hamma narsa, shaxs buni niyat qilganmi-yo'qmi, unga vijdon azobi berardi — qo'shnisiga ham, haqiqatan ham butun podaga! — Biz fikrlash tarzimizni eng ko'p aynan shu jihatdan o'zgartirdik.

paras.en: 118. Benevolence. — Is it virtuous when a cell transforms itself into the function of a stronger cell? It must do so. And is it wicked when the stronger one assimilates the other? It must do so likewise: it is necessary, for it has to have abundant indemnity and seeks to regenerate itself. One has therefore to distinguish the instinct of appropriation, and the instinct of submission, in benevolence, according as the stronger or the weaker feels benevolent. Gladness and covetousness are united in the stronger person, who wants to transform something to his function: gladness and desire-to-be-coveted in the weaker person, who would like to become a function.—The former case is essentially pity, a pleasant excitation of the instinct of appropriation at the sight of the weaker: it is to be remembered, however, that "strong" and "weak" are relative conceptions.
paras.uz: 118. Xayrixohlik. — Hujayra o'zini kuchliroq hujayraning funksiyasiga aylantirganda bu fazilatmi? U shunday qilishi kerak. Kuchlirog'i boshqasini o'zlashtirganda bu yovuzlikmi? U ham shunday qilishi kerak: bu zarur, chunki unga mo'l to'lov kerak va u o'zini qayta tiklashga intiladi. Shuning uchun xayrixohlikda kuchliroq yoki zaifroq xayrixohlik his qilishiga qarab o'zlashtirish instinkti va bo'ysunish instinktini ajratish kerak. Nimanidir o'z funksiyasiga aylantirmoqchi bo'lgan kuchliroq odamda quvonch va ochko'zlik birlashgan: funksiya bo'lishni xohlaydigan zaifroq odamda quvonch va istalish istagi. — Birinchi holat mohiyatan achinish, zaifroqni ko'rganda o'zlashtirish instinktining yoqimli qo'zg'alishi: biroq shuni yodda tutish kerakki, «kuchli» va «zaif» nisbiy tushunchalar.

paras.en: 119. No Altruism!. — I see in many men an excessive impulse and delight in wanting to be a function; they strive after it, and have the keenest scent for all those positions in which precisely they themselves can be functions. Among such persons are those women who transform themselves into just that function of a man that is but weakly developed in him, and then become his purse, or his politics, or his social intercourse. Such beings maintain themselves best when they insert themselves in an alien organism; if they do not succeed they become vexed, irritated, and eat themselves up.
paras.uz: 119. Altruizm yo'q! — Men ko'p odamlarda funksiya bo'lishni istashga haddan tashqari mayl va zavqni ko'raman; ular bunga intilishadi va aynan o'zlari funksiya bo'la oladigan barcha mavqelarni eng o'tkir hidlash qobiliyatiga ega. Bunday odamlar orasida o'zlarini erkakning undagi zaif rivojlangan aynan o'sha funksiyasiga aylantiradigan va keyin uning hamyoni, yoki siyosati, yoki ijtimoiy muloqotiga aylanadigan ayollar bor. Bunday mavjudotlar o'zlarini begona organizmga kiritganda eng yaxshi saqlanadi; agar muvaffaqiyatga erishmasalar, g'azablanadi, asabiylashadi va o'zlarini yeb qo'yishadi.

paras.en: 120. Health of the Soul. — The favourite medico-moral formula (whose originator was Ariston of Chios), "Virtue is the health of the soul," would, at least in order to be used, have to be altered to this: "Thy virtue is the health of thy soul." For there is no such thing as health in itself, and all attempts to define a thing in that way have lamentably failed. It is necessary to know thy aim, thy horizon, thy powers, thy impulses, thy errors, and especially the ideals and fantasies of thy soul, in order to determine what health implies even for thy body.
paras.uz: 120. Ruh sog'lig'i. — Sevimli tibbiy-axloqiy formula (uning muallifi Xioslik Ariston bo'lgan) «Fazilat — ruhning sog'lig'i», hech bo'lmasa foydalanish uchun quyidagicha o'zgartirilishi kerak edi: «Sening fazilating — sening ruhingning sog'lig'i». Chunki o'z-o'zidan sog'liq degan narsa yo'q va narsani shu tarzda ta'riflashga bo'lgan barcha urinishlar ayanchli muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchragan. Hatto tanang uchun ham sog'liq nimani anglatishini aniqlash uchun maqsadingni, ufqingni, kuchlaringni, mayllaringni, xatolaringni va ayniqsa ruhingning ideallari va fantaziyalarini bilish kerak.

paras.en: There are consequently innumerable kinds of physical health; and the more one again permits the unique and unparalleled to raise its head, the more one unlearns the dogma of the "Equality of men," so much the more also must the conception of a normal health, together with a normal diet and a normal course of disease, be abrogated by our physicians. And then only would it be time to turn our thoughts to the health and disease of the soul and make the special virtue of everyone consist in its health; but, to be sure, what appeared as health in one person might appear as the contrary of health in another.
paras.uz: Demak, jismoniy sog'liqning son-sanoqsiz turlari bor; va yagona va tengsiz narsaga qanchalik ko'proq bosh ko'tarishga yana ruxsat berilsa, «odamlar tengligi» aqidasini qanchalik ko'proq unutilsa, shifokorlarimiz tomonidan normal sog'liq tushunchasi, normal parhez va kasallikning normal kechishi bilan birga, shunchalik ko'proq bekor qilinishi kerak. Faqat o'shandagina fikrlarimizni ruhning sog'lig'i va kasalligiga qaratish va har kimning alohida fazilatini uning sog'lig'ida deb bilish vaqti kelardi; lekin, albatta, bir odamda sog'liq bo'lib ko'ringan narsa boshqasida sog'liqning aksi bo'lib ko'rinishi mumkin.

paras.en: In the end the great question might still remain open: whether we could do without sickness, even for the development of our virtue, and whether our thirst for knowledge and self-knowledge would not especially need the sickly soul as well as the sound one; in short, whether the mere will to health is not a prejudice, a cowardice, and perhaps an instance of the subtlest barbarism and unprogressiveness.
paras.uz: Oxirida buyuk savol hali ham ochiq qolishi mumkin: hatto fazilatimizni rivojlantirish uchun ham kasalliksiz qila olamizmi, bilimga va o'zini bilishga bo'lgan tashnaligimizga ayniqsa sog'lom ruh kabi kasal ruh ham kerak emasmi; qisqasi, sog'liqqa bo'lgan oddiy iroda xurofot, qo'rqoqlik va balki eng nozik vahshiylik va taraqqiyotsizlikning namunasi emasmi.

paras.en: 121. Life no Argument. — We have arranged for ourselves a world in which we can live—by the postulating of bodies, lines, surfaces, causes and effects, motion and rest, form and content: without these articles of faith no one could manage to live at present! But for all that they are still unproved. Life is no argument; error might be among the conditions of life.
paras.uz: 121. Hayot dalil emas. — Biz o'zimiz uchun yashay oladigan dunyoni tartibga solganmiz — jismlar, chiziqlar, yuzalar, sabablar va oqibatlar, harakat va osoyishtalik, shakl va mazmunni faraz qilish orqali: bu e'tiqod moddalarisiz hozir hech kim yashay olmasdi! Lekin shunga qaramay ular hali isbotlanmagan. Hayot dalil emas; xato hayot shartlari orasida bo'lishi mumkin.

paras.en: 122. The Element of Moral Scepticism in Christianity. — Christianity also has made a great contribution to enlightenment, and has taught moral scepticism in a very impressive and effective manner—accusing and embittering, but with untiring patience and subtlety; it annihilated in every individual the belief in his virtues: it made the great virtuous ones, of whom antiquity had no lack, vanish for ever from the earth, those popular men, who, in the belief in their perfection, walked about with the dignity of a hero of the bull-fight. When, trained in this Christian school of scepticism, we now read the moral books of the ancients, for example those of Seneca and Epictetus, we feel a pleasurable superiority, and are full of secret insight and penetration,—it seems to us as if a child talked before an old man, or a pretty, gushing girl before La Rochefoucauld:—we know better what virtue is!
paras.uz: 122. Nasroniylikdagi axloqiy skeptitsizm unsuri. — Nasroniylik ham ma'rifatga katta hissa qo'shgan va axloqiy skeptitsizmni juda ta'sirli va samarali tarzda o'rgatgan — ayblab va achchiqlantirib, lekin charchamas sabr va noziklik bilan; u har bir shaxsda uning fazilatlariga bo'lgan ishonchni yo'q qildi: u antik davrda kam bo'lmagan buyuk fazilatlilarni, o'z mukammalligiga ishonib, buqa jangi qahramonining viqori bilan yurgan o'sha ommabop odamlarni yer yuzidan abadiy yo'q qildi. Skeptitsizmning bu nasroniy maktabida tarbiyalangan holda endi qadimgilarning axloqiy kitoblarini, masalan, Seneka va Epiktetnikini o'qiganimizda, biz yoqimli ustunlikni his qilamiz va yashirin tushuncha va zukkolikka to'lamiz, — bizga go'yo bola qariya oldida, yoki go'zal, jo'shqin qiz La Roshfuko oldida gapirayotgandek tuyuladi: — biz fazilat nima ekanini yaxshiroq bilamiz!

paras.en: After all, however, we have applied the same scepticism to all religious states and processes, such as sin, repentance, grace, sanctification, &c., and have allowed the worm to burrow so well, that we have now the same feeling of subtle superiority and insight even in reading all Christian books:—we know also the religious feelings better! And it is time to know them well and describe them well, for the pious ones of the old belief die out also; let us save their likeness and type, at least for the sake of knowledge.
paras.uz: Biroq oxir-oqibat biz xuddi shu skeptitsizmni gunoh, tavba, inoyat, muqaddaslanish va hokazo kabi barcha diniy holatlar va jarayonlarga ham qo'lladik va qurtga shunchalik yaxshi kovlashga yo'l qo'ydikki, endi barcha nasroniy kitoblarini o'qiganda ham xuddi shunday nozik ustunlik va tushuncha tuyg'usiga egamiz: — biz diniy tuyg'ularni ham yaxshiroq bilamiz! Va ularni yaxshi bilish va yaxshi tasvirlash vaqti keldi, chunki eski e'tiqodning taqvodorlari ham qirilib ketmoqda; keling, hech bo'lmasa bilim uchun ularning qiyofasi va turini saqlab qolaylik.

paras.en: 123. Knowledge more than a Means. — Also without this passion—I refer to the passion for knowledge—science would be furthered: science has hitherto increased and grown up without it. The good faith in science, the prejudice in its favour, by which States are at present dominated (it was even the Church formerly), rests fundamentally on the fact that the absolute inclination and impulse has so rarely revealed itself in it, and that science is regarded not as a passion, but as a condition and an "ethos." Indeed, amour-plaisir of knowledge (curiosity) often enough suffices, amour-vanité suffices, and habituation to it, with the afterthought of obtaining honour and bread; it even suffices for many that they do not know what to do with a surplus of leisure, except to continue reading, collecting, arranging, observing and narrating; their "scientific impulse" is their ennui.
paras.uz: 123. Bilim vositadan ko'proq. — Bu ehtirossiz ham — men bilimga bo'lgan ehtirosni nazarda tutyapman — ilm rivojlanardi: ilm shu paytgacha usiz ko'payib, o'sib kelgan. Hozir davlatlar (ilgari hatto cherkov ham) hukmronlik qilinadigan ilmga bo'lgan yaxshi ishonch, uning foydasiga bo'lgan xurofot tubdan shunga asoslanadiki, unda mutlaq moyillik va mayl juda kamdan-kam namoyon bo'lgan va ilm ehtiros sifatida emas, balki holat va «etos» sifatida qaraladi. Haqiqatan ham, bilimning amour-plaisir'i — lazzat sevgisi (qiziquvchanlik) ko'pincha yetarli, amour-vanité — shuhrat sevgisi yetarli va sharaf va non olish orqa fikri bilan unga odatlanish; ko'pchilik uchun hatto ortiqcha bo'sh vaqt bilan o'qish, to'plash, tartiblash, kuzatish va hikoya qilishda davom etishdan boshqa nima qilishni bilmasliklari ham yetarli; ularning «ilmiy mayli» — ularning zerikishi.

paras.en: Pope Leo X. once (in the brief to Beroaldus) sang the praise of science; he designated it as the finest ornament and the greatest pride of our life, a noble employment in happiness and in misfortune; "without it," he says finally, "all human undertakings would be without a firm basis,—even with it they are still sufficiently mutable and insecure!" But this rather sceptical Pope, like all other ecclesiastical panegyrists of science, suppressed his ultimate judgment concerning it. If one may deduce from his words what is remarkable enough for such a lover of art, that he places science above art, it is after all, however, only from politeness that he omits to speak of that which he places high above all science: the "revealed truth," and the "eternal salvation of the soul,"—what are ornament, pride, entertainment and security of life to him, in comparison thereto?
paras.uz: Papa Leo X bir marta (Beroaldga yozgan xatida) ilmni maqtagan; u uni hayotimizning eng go'zal bezagi va eng katta g'ururi, baxtda ham, baxtsizlikda ham olijanob mashg'ulot deb atagan; «usiz, — deydi u oxirida, — barcha inson ishlari mustahkam asossiz bo'lardi, — u bilan ham ular hali yetarlicha o'zgaruvchan va ishonchsiz!» Lekin bu ancha skeptik Papa, ilmning boshqa barcha cherkov maqtovchilari kabi, u haqidagi oxirgi hukmini yashirdi. Agar uning so'zlaridan bunday san'at ishqibozi uchun yetarlicha diqqatga sazovor narsa — u ilmni san'atdan yuqori qo'yishini xulosa qilish mumkin bo'lsa ham, oxir-oqibat u barcha ilmdan baland qo'ygan narsa haqida faqat xushmuomalalik tufayli gapirmaydi: «vahiy qilingan haqiqat» va «ruhning abadiy najoti» — bezak, g'urur, ermak va hayot xavfsizligi unga bu bilan solishtirganda nima?

paras.en: "Science is something of secondary rank, nothing ultimate or unconditioned, no object of passion"—this judgment was kept back in Leo's soul: the truly Christian judgment concerning science! In antiquity its dignity and appreciation were lessened by the fact that, even among its most eager disciples, the striving after virtue stood foremost, and that people thought they had given the highest praise to knowledge when they celebrated it as the best means to virtue. It is something new in history that knowledge claims to be more than a means.
paras.uz: «Ilm — ikkinchi darajali narsa, oxirgi yoki shartsiz narsa emas, ehtiros obyekti emas» — bu hukm Leoning qalbida yashirin qoldi: ilm haqidagi chinakam nasroniy hukmi! Antik davrda uning qadr-qimmati va bahosi hatto uning eng qizg'in shogirdlari orasida ham fazilatga intilish birinchi o'rinda turgani va odamlar bilimni fazilatga eng yaxshi vosita deb ulug'laganda unga eng yuksak maqtovni bergan deb o'ylaganlari bilan kamaygan. Bilim vositadan ko'proq bo'lishni da'vo qilishi tarixda yangi narsa.

paras.en: 124. In the Horizon of the Infinite. — We have left the land and have gone aboard ship! We have broken down the bridge behind us,—nay, more, the land behind us! Well, little ship! look out! Beside thee is the ocean; it is true it does not always roar, and sometimes it spreads out like silk and gold and a gentle reverie. But times will come when thou wilt feel that it is infinite, and that there is nothing more frightful than infinity. Oh, the poor bird that felt itself free, and now strikes against the walls of this cage! Alas, if homesickness for the land should attack thee, as if there had been more freedom there,—and there is no "land" any longer!
paras.uz: 124. Cheksizlik ufqida. — Biz quruqlikni tark etib, kemaga chiqdik! Orqamizdagi ko'prikni buzib tashladik, — yo'q, bundan ham ko'proq, orqamizdagi quruqlikni! Xo'sh, kichkina kema! ehtiyot bo'l! Yoningda okean; to'g'ri, u doimo gumburlamaydi, ba'zan ipak va oltin va muloyim xayoldek yoyilib yotadi. Lekin shunday vaqtlar keladiki, uning cheksiz ekanini va cheksizlikdan dahshatliroq narsa yo'qligini his qilasan. Oh, o'zini erkin his qilgan va endi bu qafasning devorlariga urilayotgan bechora qush! Afsus, agar seni quruqlik sog'inchi qamrab olsa, go'yo u yerda ko'proq erkinlik bo'lgandek, — endi esa hech qanday «quruqlik» yo'q!

quiz.why_uz: Axloq shaxsni poda funksiyasiga aylantiradi.

quiz.q: In ancient times, what was the worst punishment?
quiz.why_uz: Odam «shaxs bo'lishga» hukm qilingan.

chapters.recap_uz: Axloq — shaxsdagi poda instinkti. Qadimda yolg'iz, mustaqil bo'lish jazo edi. Sog'liq har kimda boshqacha. Hayot dalil emas. Nasroniylik axloqiy skeptitsizmni o'rgatgan. Oxirida — cheksizlik okeanidagi kema.

chapters.title: The madman

paras.en: 125. The Madman. — Have you ever heard of the madman who on a bright morning lighted a lantern and ran to the market-place calling out unceasingly: "I seek God! I seek God!"—As there were many people standing about who did not believe in God, he caused a great deal of amusement. Why! is he lost? said one. Has he strayed away like a child? said another. Or does he keep himself hidden? Is he afraid of us? Has he taken a sea-voyage? Has he emigrated?—the people cried out laughingly, all in a hubbub. The insane man jumped into their midst and transfixed them with his glances. "Where is God gone?" he called out. "I mean to tell you! We have killed him,—you and I! We are all his murderers! But how have we done it? How were we able to drink up the sea?
paras.uz: 125. Telba odam. — Yorug' tongda chiroq yoqib, bozor maydoniga yugurib kelgan va tinimsiz: «Men Xudoni izlayapman! Men Xudoni izlayapman!» deb qichqirgan telba odam haqida hech eshitganmisiz? — U yerda Xudoga ishonmaydigan ko'p odamlar turgani uchun u katta kulgiga sabab bo'ldi. Nima! u adashib qoldimi? — dedi biri. Boladek yo'ldan adashdimi? — dedi boshqasi. Yoki yashirinib yuribdimi? Bizdan qo'rqadimi? Dengiz sayohatiga ketdimi? Ko'chib ketdimi? — odamlar g'ala-g'ovur bilan kulib qichqirishdi. Telba odam ularning o'rtasiga sakrab kirib, nigohlari bilan ularni teshib o'tdi. «Xudo qayerga ketdi? — deb xitob qildi u. — Sizga aytaman! Biz uni o'ldirdik, — siz va men! Biz hammamiz uning qotillarimiz! Lekin biz buni qanday qildik? Qanday qilib dengizni ichib yubora oldik?

paras.en: Who gave us the sponge to wipe away the whole horizon? What did we do when we loosened this earth from its sun? Whither does it now move? Whither do we move? Away from all suns? Do we not dash on unceasingly? Backwards, sideways, forwards, in all directions? Is there still an above and below? Do we not stray, as through infinite nothingness? Does not empty space breathe upon us? Has it not become colder? Does not night come on continually, darker and darker? Shall we not have to light lanterns in the morning? Do we not hear the noise of the grave-diggers who are burying God? Do we not smell the divine putrefaction?—for even Gods putrefy! God is dead! God remains dead! And we have killed him! How shall we console ourselves, the most murderous of all murderers?
paras.uz: Butun ufqni artib tashlash uchun bizga kim bulut bergan? Bu yerni quyoshidan ajratganimizda nima qildik? U endi qayerga harakatlanmoqda? Biz qayerga harakatlanyapmiz? Barcha quyoshlardan uzoqqami? Biz tinimsiz otilib ketayotgan emasmizmi? Orqaga, yonga, oldinga, har tomonga? Hali tepa va past bormi? Biz cheksiz hech narsalik ichidan adashib ketayotgan emasmizmi? Bo'sh fazo bizga nafas sepmayaptimi? Sovuqroq bo'lmadimi? Tun doimo, tobora qorong'iroq bo'lib kelmayaptimi? Ertalab chiroq yoqishimizga to'g'ri kelmaydimi? Xudoni ko'mayotgan go'rkovlarning shovqinini eshitmayapmizmi? Ilohiy chirish hidini sezmayapmizmi? — chunki xudolar ham chiriydi! Xudo o'ldi! Xudo o'likligicha qoladi! Va biz uni o'ldirdik! Biz, barcha qotillarning eng qotili, o'zimizga qanday tasalli beramiz?

paras.en: The holiest and the mightiest that the world has hitherto possessed, has bled to death under our knife,—who will wipe the blood from us? With what water could we cleanse ourselves? What lustrums, what sacred games shall we have to devise? Is not the magnitude of this deed too great for us? Shall we not ourselves have to become Gods, merely to seem worthy of it? There never was a greater event,—and on account of it, all who are born after us belong to a higher history than any history hitherto!"—Here the madman was silent and looked again at his hearers; they also were silent and looked at him in surprise. At last he threw his lantern on the ground, so that it broke in pieces and was extinguished. "I come too early," he then said, "I am not yet at the right time.
paras.uz: Dunyo shu paytgacha ega bo'lgan eng muqaddas va eng qudratli narsa bizning pichog'imiz ostida qon yo'qotib o'ldi, — bizdan qonni kim artadi? Qanday suv bilan poklana olamiz? Qanday poklanish marosimlarini, qanday muqaddas o'yinlarni o'ylab topishimizga to'g'ri keladi? Bu ishning ulkanligi biz uchun haddan tashqari katta emasmi? Faqat unga munosib ko'rinish uchun o'zimiz xudolarga aylanishimizga to'g'ri kelmaydimi? Bundan buyukroq voqea hech qachon bo'lmagan, — va u tufayli bizdan keyin tug'iladigan hamma shu paytgacha bo'lgan har qanday tarixdan yuksakroq tarixga tegishli!» — Shu yerda telba odam jim bo'lib, yana tinglovchilariga qaradi; ular ham jim bo'lib, unga hayrat bilan qarashdi. Nihoyat u chirog'ini yerga uloqtirdi, u parcha-parcha bo'lib, o'chdi. «Men juda erta keldim, — dedi u keyin, — mening vaqtim hali kelmagan.

paras.en: This prodigious event is still on its way, and is travelling,—it has not yet reached men's ears. Lightning and thunder need time, the light of the stars needs time, deeds need time, even after they are done, to be seen and heard. This deed is as yet further from them than the furthest star,—and yet they have done it!"—It is further stated that the madman made his way into different churches on the same day, and there intoned his Requiem aeternam deo. When led out and called to account, he always gave the reply: "What are these churches now, if they are not the tombs and monuments of God?"—
paras.uz: Bu dahshatli voqea hali yo'lda, u sayohat qilmoqda, — u hali odamlarning qulog'iga yetib bormagan. Chaqmoq va momaqaldiroqqa vaqt kerak, yulduzlar nuriga vaqt kerak, ishlarga, hatto qilinganidan keyin ham, ko'rilishi va eshitilishi uchun vaqt kerak. Bu ish ulardan hali eng uzoq yulduzdan ham uzoqroq, — va shunga qaramay ular uni qilishgan!» — Yana aytilishicha, telba odam o'sha kuni turli cherkovlarga kirib, u yerda Requiem aeternam deo — Xudoga abadiy marsiya kuylagan. Uni olib chiqib, javob berishni talab qilishganda, u doimo shunday javob bergan: «Bu cherkovlar endi Xudoning qabrlari va maqbaralari bo'lmasa, nima?» —

paras.en: 126. Mystical Explanations. — Mystical explanations are regarded as profound; the truth is that they do not even go the length of being superficial.
paras.uz: 126. Mistik tushuntirishlar. — Mistik tushuntirishlar chuqur deb hisoblanadi; haqiqat shundaki, ular hatto yuzaki bo'lishgacha ham yetmaydi.

paras.en: 127. After-Effect of the most Ancient Religiousness. — The thoughtless man thinks that the Will is the only thing that operates, that willing is something simple, manifestly given, underived, and comprehensible in itself. He is convinced that when he does anything, for example, when he delivers a blow, it is he who strikes, and he has struck because he willed to strike. He does not notice anything of a problem therein, but the feeling of willing suffices to him, not only for the acceptance of cause and effect, but also for the belief that he understands their relationship. Of the mechanism of the occurrence and of the manifold subtle operations that must be performed in order that the blow may result, and likewise of the incapacity of the Will in itself to effect even the smallest part of those operations—he knows nothing.
paras.uz: 127. Eng qadimiy dindorlikning keyingi ta'siri. — O'ylamas odam Iroda yagona ta'sir qiluvchi narsa, istash — oddiy, ochiq berilgan, hosila bo'lmagan va o'z-o'zidan tushunarli narsa deb o'ylaydi. U biror ish qilganda, masalan, zarba berganda, uradigan o'zi ekaniga va urmoqchi bo'lgani uchun urganiga amin. U bunda hech qanday muammoni payqamaydi, balki istash tuyg'usi unga nafaqat sabab va oqibatni qabul qilish uchun, balki ularning munosabatini tushunaman degan ishonch uchun ham yetarli. Hodisaning mexanizmi va zarba hosil bo'lishi uchun bajarilishi kerak bo'lgan ko'p qirrali nozik amallar haqida, shuningdek, Irodaning o'z-o'zidan bu amallarning eng kichik qismini ham bajara olmasligi haqida — u hech narsa bilmaydi.

paras.en: The Will is to him a magically operating force; the belief in the Will as the cause of effects is the belief in magically operating forces. In fact, whenever he saw anything happen, man originally believed in a Will as cause, and in personally willing beings operating in the background,—the conception of mechanism was very remote from him. Because, however, man for immense periods of time believed only in persons (and not in matter, forces, things, &c.), the belief in cause and effect has become a fundamental belief with him, which he applies everywhere when anything happens,—and even still uses instinctively as a piece of atavism of remotest origin.
paras.uz: Iroda uning uchun sehrli ta'sir qiluvchi kuch; Irodaga oqibatlarning sababi sifatida ishonish — sehrli ta'sir qiluvchi kuchlarga ishonishdir. Haqiqatan ham, inson dastlab biror narsa sodir bo'layotganini ko'rgan har safar sabab sifatida Irodaga va orqa fonda ta'sir qilayotgan shaxsan istovchi mavjudotlarga ishongan, — mexanizm tushunchasi unga juda uzoq edi. Biroq inson ulkan davrlar davomida faqat shaxslarga ishongani uchun (materiya, kuchlar, narsalar va hokazolarga emas), sabab va oqibatga ishonish unda asosiy ishonchga aylangan, u buni biror narsa sodir bo'lgan har joyda qo'llaydi, — va hali ham eng olis kelib chiqishli atavizm bo'lagi sifatida instinktiv ishlatadi.

paras.en: The propositions, "No effect without a cause," and "Every effect again implies a cause," appear as generalisations of several less general propositions:—"Where there is operation there has been willing," "Operating is only possible on willing beings." "There is never a pure, resultless experience of activity, but every experience involves stimulation of the Will" (to activity, defence, revenge or retaliation).
paras.uz: «Sababsiz oqibat yo'q» va «Har bir oqibat yana sababni nazarda tutadi» degan da'volar bir nechta kamroq umumiy da'volarning umumlashmasi bo'lib ko'rinadi: — «Ta'sir bo'lgan joyda istash bo'lgan», «Ta'sir faqat istovchi mavjudotlarga mumkin», «Faoliyatning hech qachon sof, natijasiz tajribasi bo'lmaydi, balki har bir tajriba Irodani qo'zg'atishni o'z ichiga oladi» (faoliyatga, himoyaga, qasos yoki javob qaytarishga).

paras.en: But in the primitive period of the human race, the latter and the former propositions were identical, the first were not generalisations of the second, but the second were explanations of the first.—Schopenhauer, with his assumption that all that exists is something volitional, has set a primitive mythology on the throne; he seems never to have attempted an analysis of the Will, because he believed like everybody in the simplicity and immediateness of all volition:—while volition is in fact such a cleverly practised mechanical process that it almost escapes the observing eye. I set the following propositions against those of Schopenhauer:—Firstly, in order that Will may arise, an idea of pleasure and pain is necessary.
paras.uz: Lekin insoniyatning ibtidoiy davrida keyingi va oldingi da'volar bir xil edi, birinchilari ikkinchilarining umumlashmasi emas, balki ikkinchilari birinchilarining tushuntirishi edi. — Shopengauer mavjud bo'lgan hamma narsa iroda bilan bog'liq narsa degan farazi bilan ibtidoiy mifologiyani taxtga o'tqazdi; u hech qachon Irodani tahlil qilishga urinmaganga o'xshaydi, chunki hamma kabi barcha istashning oddiyligi va bevositaligiga ishongan: — vaholanki istash aslida shunchalik mohirona mashq qilingan mexanik jarayonki, kuzatuvchi ko'zdan deyarli qochib ketadi. Men Shopengauerning da'volariga qarshi quyidagi da'volarni qo'yaman: — Birinchidan, Iroda paydo bo'lishi uchun lazzat va og'riq g'oyasi zarur.

paras.en: Secondly, that a vigorous excitation may be felt as pleasure or pain, is the affair of the interpreting intellect, which, to be sure, operates thereby for the most part unconsciously to us, and one and the same excitation may be interpreted as pleasure or pain. Thirdly, it is only in an intellectual being that there is pleasure, displeasure and Will; the immense majority of organisms have nothing of the kind.
paras.uz: Ikkinchidan, kuchli qo'zg'alish lazzat yoki og'riq sifatida his qilinishi talqin qiluvchi aqlning ishi, u albatta bunda ko'pincha bizga ongsiz ishlaydi va bitta va bir xil qo'zg'alish lazzat yoki og'riq sifatida talqin qilinishi mumkin. Uchinchidan, lazzat, norozilik va Iroda faqat aqlli mavjudotdagina bor; organizmlarning ulkan ko'pchiligida bunday narsa yo'q.

paras.en: 128. The Value of Prayer. — Prayer has been devised for such men as have never any thoughts of their own, and to whom an elevation of the soul is unknown, or passes unnoticed; what shall these people do in holy places and in all important situations in life which require repose and some kind of dignity? In order at least that they may not disturb, the wisdom of all the founders of religions, the small as well as the great, has commended to them the formula of prayer, as a long mechanical labour of the lips, united with an effort of the memory, and with a uniform, prescribed attitude of hands and feet—and eyes!
paras.uz: 128. Ibodatning qadri. — Ibodat hech qachon o'z fikri bo'lmagan va ruhning yuksalishi notanish yoki sezilmay qoladigan odamlar uchun o'ylab topilgan; bu odamlar muqaddas joylarda va osoyishtalik va qandaydir viqor talab qiladigan hayotdagi barcha muhim vaziyatlarda nima qilishsin? Hech bo'lmasa ular xalaqit bermasligi uchun barcha din asoschilarining, kichigi ham, kattasi ham, donoligi ularga ibodat formulasini tavsiya qilgan — lablarning uzoq mexanik mehnati, xotiraning harakati va qo'l, oyoq — va ko'zlarning bir xil, belgilangan holati bilan birlashtirilgan!

paras.en: They may then, like the Tibetans, chew the cud of their "om mane padme hum," innumerable times, or, as in Benares, count the name of God Ram-Ram-Ram (and so on, with or without grace) on their fingers; or honour Vishnu with his thousand names of invocation, Allah with his ninety-nine; or they may make use of the prayer-wheels and the rosary: the main thing is that they are settled down for a time at this work, and present a tolerable appearance; their mode of prayer is devised for the advantage of the pious who have thought and elevation of their own. But even these have their weary hours when a series of venerable words and sounds and a mechanical, pious ritual does them good.
paras.uz: O'shanda ular tibetliklar kabi o'zlarining «om mani padme hum»larini son-sanoqsiz marta kavshashlari, yoki Benaresdagidek Xudoning ismini Ram-Ram-Ram (va hokazo, inoyat bilan yoki usiz) barmoqlarida sanashlari mumkin; yoki Vishnuni ming chaqiriq nomi bilan, Allohni to'qson to'qqizta nomi bilan ulug'lashlari; yoki ibodat g'ildiraklari va tasbehdan foydalanishlari mumkin: asosiysi, ular bir muddat bu ishga o'tirishadi va chidab bo'ladigan ko'rinishda bo'lishadi; ularning ibodat usuli o'z fikri va yuksalishi bor taqvodorlar foydasi uchun o'ylab topilgan. Lekin hatto ularning ham charchagan soatlari bo'ladi, o'shanda bir qator muhtaram so'zlar va tovushlar va mexanik, taqvodor marosim ularga foyda beradi.

paras.en: But supposing that these rare men—in every religion the religious man is an exception—know how to help themselves, the poor in spirit do not know, and to forbid them the prayer-babbling would mean to take their religion from them, a fact which Protestantism brings more and more to light. All that religion wants with such persons is that they should keep still with their eyes, hands, legs, and all their organs: they thereby become temporarily beautified and—more human-looking!
paras.uz: Lekin bu kamyob odamlar — har bir dinda dindor odam istisno — o'zlariga yordam berishni bilishadi deb faraz qilsak, ruhan kambag'allar bilishmaydi va ularga ibodat vaysashini taqiqlash ulardan dinlarini tortib olish bo'lardi, protestantizm buni tobora ko'proq oshkor qilmoqda. Din bunday odamlardan istagan narsa faqat ular ko'zlari, qo'llari, oyoqlari va barcha a'zolari bilan jim turishi: shu bilan ular vaqtincha chiroyli va — insonga o'xshaganroq bo'lib qolishadi!

paras.en: 129. The Conditions for God. — "God himself cannot subsist without wise men," said Luther, and with good reason; but "God can still less subsist without unwise men,"—good Luther did not say that!
paras.uz: 129. Xudo uchun shartlar. — «Xudoning o'zi dono odamlarsiz mavjud bo'la olmaydi», — degan Lyuter va yaxshi asos bilan; lekin «Xudo nodon odamlarsiz yana ham kamroq mavjud bo'la oladi», — yaxshi Lyuter buni aytmagan!

paras.en: 130. A Dangerous Resolution. — The Christian resolution to find the world ugly and bad has made the world ugly and bad.
paras.uz: 130. Xavfli qaror. — Dunyoni xunuk va yomon deb topish haqidagi nasroniy qarori dunyoni xunuk va yomon qilib qo'ydi.

paras.en: 131. Christianity and Suicide. — Christianity made use of the excessive longing for suicide at the time of its origin as a lever for its power: it left only two forms of suicide, invested them with the highest dignity and the highest hopes, and forbade all others in a dreadful manner. But martyrdom and the slow self-annihilation of the ascetic were permitted.
paras.uz: 131. Nasroniylik va o'z joniga qasd qilish. — Nasroniylik o'zi paydo bo'lgan paytdagi o'z joniga qasd qilishga bo'lgan haddan tashqari sog'inchdan o'z qudrati uchun richag sifatida foydalangan: u o'z joniga qasd qilishning faqat ikki shaklini qoldirib, ularga eng yuksak viqor va eng yuksak umidlarni bergan va qolganlarining hammasini dahshatli tarzda taqiqlagan. Lekin shahidlik va zohidning sekin o'zini yo'q qilishi ruxsat etilgan.

paras.en: 132. Against Christianity. — It is now no longer our reason, but our taste that decides against Christianity.
paras.uz: 132. Nasroniylikka qarshi. — Endi nasroniylikka qarshi qaror chiqaradigan narsa bizning aqlimiz emas, balki didimiz.

paras.en: 133. Axioms. — An unavoidable hypothesis on which mankind must always fall back again, is, in the long run, more powerful than the most firmly believed belief in something untrue (like the Christian belief). In the long run: that means a hundred thousand years from now.
paras.uz: 133. Aksiomalar. — Insoniyat doimo yana qaytishi kerak bo'lgan muqarrar gipoteza uzoq muddatda biror yolg'on narsaga eng qat'iy ishonilgan e'tiqoddan (masalan, nasroniy e'tiqodidan) kuchliroq. Uzoq muddatda: bu hozirdan yuz ming yil keyin degani.

paras.en: 134. Pessimists as Victims. — When a profound dislike of existence gets the upper hand, the after-effect of a great error in diet of which a people has been long guilty comes to light. The spread of Buddhism (not its origin) is thus to a considerable extent dependent on the excessive and almost exclusive rice-fare of the Indians, and on the universal enervation that results therefrom. Perhaps the modern, European discontentedness is to be looked upon as caused by the fact that the world of our forefathers, the whole Middle Ages, was given to drink, owing to the influence of German tastes in Europe: the Middle Ages, that means the alcoholic poisoning of Europe.—The German dislike of life (including the influence of the cellar-air and stove-poison in German dwellings), is essentially a cold-weather complaint.
paras.uz: 134. Pessimistlar qurbon sifatida. — Hayotga chuqur nafrat ustunlikka erishganda, xalq uzoq vaqt aybdor bo'lgan ovqatlanishdagi katta xatoning keyingi ta'siri yuzaga chiqadi. Masalan, buddizmning tarqalishi (kelib chiqishi emas) ko'p jihatdan hindlarning haddan tashqari va deyarli faqat guruchdan iborat taomiga va undan kelib chiqadigan umumiy holsizlikka bog'liq. Balki zamonaviy Yevropa noroziligini ota-bobolarimizning dunyosi, butun O'rta asrlar Yevropadagi nemis didlari ta'sirida ichkilikka berilgani bilan bog'liq deb qarash kerakdir: O'rta asrlar — bu Yevropaning alkogoldan zaharlanishi demak. — Nemislarning hayotdan nafrati (nemis uylaridagi yerto'la havosi va pech zahri ta'sirini ham qo'shib) mohiyatan sovuq ob-havo kasalligi.

paras.en: 135. Origin of Sin. — Sin, as it is at present felt wherever Christianity prevails or has prevailed, is a Jewish feeling and a Jewish invention; and in respect to this background of all Christian morality, Christianity has in fact aimed at "Judaising" the whole world. To what an extent this has succeeded in Europe is traced most accurately in the extent of our alienness to Greek antiquity—a world without the feeling of sin—in our sentiments even at present; in spite of all the good will to approximation and assimilation, which whole generations and many distinguished individuals have not failed to display.
paras.uz: 135. Gunohning kelib chiqishi. — Nasroniylik hukmron bo'lgan yoki hukmron bo'lgan har joyda hozir his qilinadigan gunoh — yahudiy tuyg'usi va yahudiy ixtirosi; va barcha nasroniy axloqining bu orqa foniga nisbatan nasroniylik haqiqatan ham butun dunyoni «yahudiylashtirish»ni maqsad qilgan. Bu Yevropada qay darajada muvaffaqiyatli bo'lgani yunon antik davriga — gunoh tuyg'usisiz dunyoga — hozir ham tuyg'ularimizdagi begonaligimiz darajasida eng aniq kuzatiladi; butun avlodlar va ko'p taniqli shaxslar ko'rsatishdan to'xtamagan yaqinlashish va o'zlashtirishga bo'lgan barcha yaxshi niyatga qaramay.

paras.en: "Only when thou repentest is God gracious to thee"—that would arouse the laughter or the wrath of a Greek: he would say, "Slaves may have such sentiments." Here a mighty being, an almighty being, and yet a revengeful being, is presupposed; his power is so great that no injury whatever can be done to him, except in the point of honour. Every sin is an infringement of respect, a crimen læsæ majestatis divinæ—and nothing more! Contrition, degradation, rolling-in-the-dust,—these are the first and last conditions on which his favour depends: the restoration, therefore, of his divine honour!
paras.uz: «Faqat tavba qilgandagina Xudo senga rahm qiladi» — bu yunonning kulgisini yoki g'azabini qo'zg'atardi: u «Qullarda bunday tuyg'ular bo'lishi mumkin», derdi. Bu yerda qudratli mavjudot, hamma narsaga qodir mavjudot, lekin shunga qaramay qasoskor mavjudot nazarda tutiladi; uning qudrati shunchalik kattaki, unga sharaf masalasidan boshqa hech qanday zarar yetkazib bo'lmaydi. Har bir gunoh hurmatning buzilishi, crimen laesae majestatis divinae — ilohiy ulug'vorlikni haqoratlash jinoyati — va boshqa hech narsa emas! Tavba, o'zini xorlash, tuproqda yumalash — uning marhamati bog'liq bo'lgan birinchi va oxirgi shartlar shular: demak, uning ilohiy sharafini tiklash!

paras.en: If injury be caused otherwise by sin, if a profound, spreading evil be propagated by it, an evil which, like a disease, attacks and strangles one man after another—that does not trouble this honour-craving Oriental in heaven; sin is an offence against him, not against mankind!—to him on whom he has bestowed his favour he bestows also this indifference to the natural consequences of sin. God and mankind are here thought of as separated, as so antithetical that sin against the latter cannot be at all possible,—all deeds are to be looked upon solely with respect to their supernatural consequences, and not with respect to their natural results: it is thus that the Jewish feeling, to which all that is natural seems unworthy in itself, would have things.
paras.uz: Agar gunoh boshqa yo'l bilan zarar keltirsa, agar u orqali chuqur, tarqaluvchi yomonlik, kasallik kabi birin-ketin odamlarga hujum qilib, bo'g'ib o'ldiradigan yomonlik tarqalsa — bu osmondagi sharafga tashna sharqlikni bezovta qilmaydi; gunoh insoniyatga emas, unga qarshi haqorat! — u marhamat ko'rsatgan kishiga gunohning tabiiy oqibatlariga bu befarqlikni ham beradi. Bu yerda Xudo va insoniyat bir-biridan ajratilgan, shunchalik qarama-qarshi deb o'ylanadiki, ikkinchisiga qarshi gunoh umuman mumkin bo'lmaydi, — barcha ishlarga faqat ularning g'ayritabiiy oqibatlari nuqtai nazaridan qarash kerak, tabiiy natijalari nuqtai nazaridan emas: barcha tabiiy narsalar o'z-o'zidan nomunosib bo'lib ko'rinadigan yahudiy tuyg'usi narsalarni shunday ko'rishni istaydi.

paras.en: The Greeks, on the other hand, were more familiar with the thought that transgression also may have dignity,—even theft, as in the case of Prometheus, even the slaughtering of cattle as the expression of frantic jealousy, as in the case of Ajax; in their need to attribute dignity to transgression and embody it therein, they invented tragedy,—an art and a delight, which in its profoundest essence has remained alien to the Jew, in spite of all his poetic endowment and taste for the sublime.
paras.uz: Yunonlar esa, aksincha, qonunbuzarlikning ham viqori bo'lishi mumkin degan fikrga ko'proq tanish edi, — hatto o'g'irlikning ham, Prometey holatidagidek, hatto telbalarcha rashkning ifodasi sifatida mollarni so'yishning ham, Ayaks holatidagidek; qonunbuzarlikka viqor nisbat berish va uni unda mujassamlashtirish ehtiyojida ular tragediyani ixtiro qilishdi, — eng chuqur mohiyatida yahudiyga, uning barcha shoirona iste'dodi va yuksaklikka bo'lgan didiga qaramay, begona qolgan san'at va zavq.

paras.en: 136. The Chosen People. — The Jews, who regard themselves as the chosen people among the nations, and that too because they are the moral genius among the nations (in virtue of their capacity for despising the human in themselves more than any other people)—the Jews have a pleasure in their divine monarch and saint similar to that which the French nobility had in Louis XIV. This nobility had allowed its power and autocracy to be taken from it, and had become contemptible: in order not to feel this, in order to be able to forget it, an unequalled royal magnificence, royal authority and plenitude of power was needed, to which there was access only for the nobility. As in accordance with this privilege they raised themselves to the elevation of the court, and from that elevation saw everything under them,—saw everything contemptible,—they got beyond all uneasiness of conscience. They thus elevated intentionally the tower of the royal power more and more into the clouds, and set the final coping-stone of their own power thereon.
paras.uz: 136. Tanlangan xalq. — O'zlarini xalqlar orasida tanlangan xalq deb biladigan yahudiylar, va bu ham ular xalqlar orasida axloqiy daho bo'lgani uchun (o'zlaridagi insoniylikni har qanday boshqa xalqdan ko'ra ko'proq mensimaslik qobiliyati tufayli), — yahudiylar o'zlarining ilohiy monarxi va avliyosidan fransuz zodagonlari Lyudovik XIV dan olgan zavqqa o'xshash zavq olishadi. Bu zodagonlar o'zining qudrati va mustabidligini tortib olishga yo'l qo'ygan va jirkanch bo'lib qolgan edi: buni his qilmaslik uchun, buni unuta olish uchun tengsiz shohona ulug'vorlik, shohona obro' va qudrat to'liqligi kerak edi, unga faqat zodagonlarning kirish imkoni bor edi. Bu imtiyozga ko'ra ular o'zlarini saroy yuksakligiga ko'tarib, o'sha yuksaklikdan hamma narsani o'zlaridan pastda ko'rganlarida, — hamma narsani jirkanch ko'rganlarida, — ular vijdonning barcha bezovtaligidan narida o'tishdi. Shu tariqa ular shoh hokimiyati minorasini qasddan tobora bulutlarga ko'tarishdi va uning ustiga o'z qudratlarining oxirgi tomtoshini qo'yishdi.

chapters.title: Many gods, many ideals

paras.en: 137. Spoken in Parable. — A Jesus Christ was only possible in a Jewish landscape—I mean in one over which the gloomy and sublime thunder-cloud of the angry Jehovah hung continually. Here only was the rare, sudden flashing of a single sunbeam through the dreadful, universal and continuous nocturnal-day regarded as a miracle of "love," as a beam of the most unmerited "grace." Here only could Christ dream of his rainbow and celestial ladder on which God descended to man; everywhere else the clear weather and the sun were considered the rule and the commonplace.
paras.uz: 137. Masal bilan aytilgan. — Iso Masih faqat yahudiy manzarasida mumkin edi — men ustida g'azablangan Yahovaning ma'yus va yuksak momaqaldiroq buluti doimo osilib turgan manzarani nazarda tutyapman. Faqat shu yerdagina dahshatli, umumiy va uzluksiz tungi-kunduz orqali bitta quyosh nurining kamyob, to'satdan chaqnashi «sevgi» mo''jizasi, eng nohaq «inoyat» nuri deb hisoblangan. Faqat shu yerdagina Masih o'zining kamalagi va Xudo insonga tushadigan samoviy narvoni haqida orzu qila olardi; boshqa hamma joyda tiniq havo va quyosh qoida va oddiy narsa deb hisoblangan.

paras.en: 138. The Error of Christ. — The founder of Christianity thought there was nothing from which men suffered so much as from their sins:—it was his error, the error of him who felt himself without sin, to whom experience was lacking in this respect! It was thus that his soul filled with that marvellous, fantastic pity which had reference to a trouble that even among his own people, the inventors of sin, was rarely a great trouble! But Christians understood subsequently how to do justice to their master, and to sanctify his error into a "truth."
paras.uz: 138. Masihning xatosi. — Nasroniylik asoschisi odamlar gunohlaridan ko'ra ko'proq azob chekadigan narsa yo'q deb o'ylagan: — bu uning xatosi edi, o'zini gunohsiz his qilgan, bu jihatda tajribasi yetishmagan odamning xatosi! Shu tariqa uning qalbi hatto o'z xalqi, gunohni ixtiro qilganlar orasida ham kamdan-kam katta tashvish bo'lgan tashvishga taalluqli o'sha ajoyib, xayoliy achinish bilan to'ldi! Lekin nasroniylar keyinroq o'z ustozlariga adolat qilishni va uning xatosini «haqiqat»ga aylantirib muqaddaslashtirishni tushunishdi.

paras.en: 139. Colour of the Passions. — Natures such as the apostle Paul, have an evil eye for the passions; they learn to know only the filthy, the distorting, and the heart-breaking in them,—their ideal aim, therefore, is the annihilation of the passions; in the divine they see complete purification from passion. The Greeks, quite otherwise than Paul and the Jews, directed their ideal aim precisely to the passions, and loved, elevated, embellished and deified them: in passion they evidently not only felt themselves happier, but also purer and diviner than otherwise.—And now the Christians? Have they wished to become Jews in this respect? Have they perhaps become Jews!
paras.uz: 139. Ehtiroslarning rangi. — Havoriy Pavlus kabi tabiatlarning ehtiroslarga yomon ko'zi bor; ular ularda faqat iflos, buzuvchi va yurak sindiruvchi narsani bilishni o'rganishadi, — shuning uchun ularning ideal maqsadi ehtiroslarni yo'q qilish; ilohiylikda ular ehtirosdan to'liq poklanishni ko'rishadi. Yunonlar esa, Pavlus va yahudiylardan butunlay boshqacha, o'zlarining ideal maqsadini aynan ehtiroslarga qaratishgan va ularni sevishgan, yuksaltirishgan, bezashgan va ilohiylashtirishgan: ehtirosda ular aftidan o'zlarini nafaqat baxtliroq, balki boshqa paytlardagidan pokroq va ilohiyroq ham his qilishgan. — Endi nasroniylar-chi? Ular bu jihatdan yahudiy bo'lishni istashganmi? Balki ular yahudiy bo'lib qolishgandir!

paras.en: 140. Too Jewish. — If God had wanted to become an object of love, he would first of all have had to forgo judging and justice:—a judge, and even a gracious judge, is no object of love. The founder of Christianity showed too little of the finer feelings in this respect—being a Jew.
paras.uz: 140. Haddan tashqari yahudiycha. — Agar Xudo sevgi obyekti bo'lishni istaganida, u avvalo hukm qilish va adolatdan voz kechishi kerak edi: — hakam, hatto mehribon hakam ham sevgi obyekti emas. Nasroniylik asoschisi bu jihatda nozikroq tuyg'ulardan haddan tashqari kam ko'rsatgan — yahudiy bo'lgani uchun.

paras.en: 141. Too Oriental. — What? A God who loves men, provided that they believe in him, and who hurls frightful glances and threatenings at him who does not believe in this love! What? A conditioned love as the feeling of an almighty God! A love which has not even become master of the sentiment of honour and of the irritable desire for vengeance! How Oriental is all that! "If I love thee, what does it concern thee?" is already a sufficient criticism of the whole of Christianity.
paras.uz: 141. Haddan tashqari sharqona. — Nima? Odamlarni, agar ular unga ishonsa, sevadigan va bu sevgiga ishonmaganga dahshatli nigohlar va tahdidlar otadigan Xudo! Nima? Hamma narsaga qodir Xudoning tuyg'usi sifatida shartli sevgi! Hatto sharaf tuyg'usi va asabiy qasos istagi ustidan ham hukmron bo'lmagan sevgi! Bularning hammasi qanchalik sharqona! «Agar men seni sevsam, buning senga nima aloqasi bor?» — butun nasroniylikning yetarli tanqidi.

paras.en: 142. Frankincense. — Buddha says: "Do not flatter thy benefactor!" Let one repeat this saying in a Christian church:—it immediately purifies the air of all Christianity.
paras.uz: 142. Kundur. — Budda deydi: «Xayrixohingga xushomad qilma!» Bu so'zni nasroniy cherkovida takrorlab ko'ring: — u darhol havoni butun nasroniylikdan tozalaydi.

paras.en: 143. The Greatest Utility of Polytheism. — For the individual to set up his own ideal and derive from it his laws, his pleasures and his rights—that has perhaps been hitherto regarded as the most monstrous of all human aberrations, and as idolatry in itself; in fact, the few who have ventured to do this have always needed to apologise to themselves, usually in this wise: "Not I! not I! but a God, through my instrumentality!" It was in the marvellous art and capacity for creating Gods—in polytheism—that this impulse was permitted to discharge itself, it was here that it became purified, perfected, and ennobled; for it was originally a commonplace and unimportant impulse, akin to stubbornness, disobedience and envy. To be hostile to this impulse towards the individual ideal,—that was formerly the law of every morality. There was then only one norm, "the man"—and every people believed that it had this one and ultimate norm.
paras.uz: 143. Ko'pxudolikning eng katta foydasi. — Shaxsning o'z idealini o'rnatishi va undan o'z qonunlari, lazzatlari va huquqlarini chiqarishi — bu shu paytgacha, ehtimol, barcha inson adashishlarining eng dahshatlisi va o'z-o'zidan butparastlik deb hisoblangan; haqiqatan ham, bunga jur'at etgan ozchilik doimo o'zlariga uzr so'rashlari kerak bo'lgan, odatda shu tarzda: «Men emas! men emas! balki Xudo, men orqali!» Bu mayl o'zini bo'shatishiga xudolar yaratishning ajoyib san'ati va qobiliyatida — ko'pxudolikda ruxsat berilgan, aynan shu yerda u poklangan, mukammallashgan va olijanoblashgan; chunki u dastlab o'jarlik, itoatsizlik va hasadga yaqin oddiy va ahamiyatsiz mayl edi. Shaxsiy idealga bo'lgan bu maylga dushman bo'lish — bu ilgari har bir axloqning qonuni edi. O'shanda faqat bitta me'yor bor edi, «inson» — va har bir xalq bu bitta va oxirgi me'yorga o'zi ega deb ishongan.

paras.en: But above himself, and outside of himself, in a distant over-world, a person could see a multitude of norms: the one God was not the denial or blasphemy of the other Gods! It was here that individuals were first permitted, it was here that the right of individuals was first respected. The inventing of Gods, heroes and supermen of all kinds, as well as co-ordinate men and undermen—dwarfs, fairies, centaurs, satyrs, demons, devils—was the inestimable preliminary to the justification of the selfishness and sovereignty of the individual: the freedom which was granted to one God in respect to other Gods, was at last given to the individual himself in respect to laws, customs and neighbours.
paras.uz: Lekin o'zidan yuqorida va o'zidan tashqarida, uzoq yuqori dunyoda odam ko'plab me'yorlarni ko'ra olardi: bitta xudo boshqa xudolarni inkor etish yoki ularga kufr emas edi! Aynan shu yerda shaxslarga birinchi marta ruxsat berildi, aynan shu yerda shaxslarning huquqi birinchi marta hurmat qilindi. Xudolar, qahramonlar va har xil o'ta insonlarni, shuningdek, yonma-yon odamlar va quyi odamlarni — mittilar, parilar, kentavrlar, satirlar, jinlar, iblislarni ixtiro qilish shaxsning xudbinligi va hukmronligini oqlashning bebaho dastlabki bosqichi edi: bir xudoga boshqa xudolarga nisbatan berilgan erkinlik oxir-oqibat shaxsning o'ziga qonunlar, urf-odatlar va qo'shnilarga nisbatan berildi.

paras.en: Monotheism, on the contrary, the rigid consequence of the doctrine of one normal human being—consequently the belief in a normal God, beside whom there are only false, spurious Gods—has perhaps been the greatest danger of mankind in the past: man was then threatened by that premature state of inertia, which, so far as we can see, most of the other species of animals reached long ago, as creatures who all believe in one normal animal and ideal in their species, and definitely translated their morality of custom into flesh and blood. In polytheism man's free-thinking and many-sided thinking had a prototype set up: the power to create for himself new and individual eyes, always newer and more individualised: so that it is for man alone, of all the animals, that there are no eternal horizons and perspectives.
paras.uz: Yakkaxudolik esa, aksincha, bitta normal inson ta'limotining qat'iy oqibati — demak, normal Xudoga ishonish, uning yonida faqat soxta, yolg'on xudolar bor — o'tmishda, ehtimol, insoniyatning eng katta xavfi bo'lgan: inson o'shanda muddatidan oldingi inersiya holati bilan tahdid qilingan edi, bizga ko'rinib turishicha, boshqa hayvon turlarining ko'pchiligi unga allaqachon yetib kelgan, chunki ularning hammasi o'z turida bitta normal hayvon va idealga ishonadi va urf-odat axloqini qat'iy ravishda go'sht va qonga aylantirgan. Ko'pxudolikda insonning erkin fikrlashi va ko'p qirrali fikrlashi uchun namuna o'rnatilgan edi: o'zi uchun yangi va shaxsiy, doimo yangiroq va shaxsiyroq ko'zlar yaratish kuchi: shuning uchun barcha hayvonlar ichida faqat inson uchun abadiy ufqlar va istiqbollar yo'q.

paras.en: 144. Religious Wars. — The greatest advance of the masses hitherto has been religious war, for it proves that the masses have begun to deal reverently with conceptions of things. Religious wars only result, when human reason generally has been refined by the subtle disputes of sects; so that even the populace becomes punctilious and regards trifles as important, actually thinking it possible that the "eternal salvation of the soul" may depend upon minute distinctions of concepts.
paras.uz: 144. Diniy urushlar. — Ommaning shu paytgacha eng katta taraqqiyoti diniy urush bo'lgan, chunki u omma narsalar haqidagi tushunchalarga hurmat bilan munosabatda bo'la boshlaganini isbotlaydi. Diniy urushlar faqat inson aqli umuman sektalarning nozik bahslari bilan nozikroq bo'lganda kelib chiqadi; shunda hatto oddiy xalq ham sinchkov bo'lib, arzimas narsalarni muhim deb hisoblaydi, «ruhning abadiy najoti» tushunchalarning mayda farqlariga bog'liq bo'lishi mumkin deb haqiqatan o'ylaydi.

paras.en: 145. Danger of Vegetarians. — The immense prevalence of rice-eating impels to the use of opium and narcotics, in like manner as the immense prevalence of potato-eating impels to the use of brandy:—it also impels, however, in its more subtle after-effects to modes of thought and feeling which operate narcotically. This is in accord with the fact that those who promote narcotic modes of thought and feeling, like those Indian teachers, praise a purely vegetable diet, and would like to make it a law for the masses: they want thereby to call forth and augment the need which they are in a position to satisfy.
paras.uz: 145. Vegetarianlar xavfi. — Guruch yeyishning ulkan tarqalishi afyun va giyohvand moddalarni ishlatishga undaydi, xuddi kartoshka yeyishning ulkan tarqalishi aroq ichishga undagani kabi: — biroq u nozikroq keyingi ta'sirlarida giyohvanddek ta'sir qiladigan fikrlash va his qilish tarzlariga ham undaydi. Bu shunga mos keladiki, giyohvand fikrlash va his qilish tarzlarini targ'ib qiladiganlar, o'sha hind o'qituvchilari kabi, sof o'simlik taomini maqtashadi va uni omma uchun qonun qilishni istashadi: ular shu bilan o'zlari qondira oladigan ehtiyojni chaqirib, oshirmoqchi.

paras.en: 146. German Hopes. — Do not let us forget that the names of peoples are generally names of reproach. The Tartars, for example, according to their name, are "the dogs"; they were so christened by the Chinese. "Deutschen" (Germans) means originally "heathen": it is thus that the Goths after their conversion named the great mass of their unbaptized fellow-tribes, according to the indication in their translation of the Septuagint, in which the heathen are designated by the word which in Greek signifies "the nations." (See Ulfilas.)—It might still be possible for the Germans to make an honourable name ultimately out of their old name of reproach, by becoming the first non-Christian nation of Europe; for which purpose Schopenhauer, to their honour, regarded them as highly qualified. The work of Luther would thus be consummated,—he who taught them to be anti-Roman and to say: "Here I stand! I cannot do otherwise!"—
paras.uz: 146. Nemis umidlari. — Xalqlarning nomlari odatda haqoratli nomlar ekanini unutmaylik. Masalan, tatarlar nomiga ko'ra «itlar»; ularni xitoyliklar shunday nomlagan. «Deutschen» (nemislar) dastlab «majusiylar»ni anglatadi: gotlar o'zlari dinga kirgach, cho'qintirilmagan qabiladoshlarining katta qismini Septuaginta tarjimasidagi ko'rsatmaga ko'ra shunday atashgan, unda majusiylar yunoncha «xalqlar»ni anglatadigan so'z bilan belgilangan. (Qarang: Vulfila.) — Nemislar oxir-oqibat o'zlarining eski haqoratli nomidan sharafli nom yasashlari hali mumkin bo'lar, Yevropaning birinchi nasroniy bo'lmagan xalqiga aylanib; Shopengauer ularning sharafiga ularni bunga juda qodir deb hisoblagan. Shunda Lyuterning ishi yakunlanardi, — ularga Rimga qarshi bo'lishni va «Men shu yerda turibman! Boshqacha qila olmayman!» deyishni o'rgatgan odamning.

paras.en: 147. Question and Answer. — What do savage tribes at present accept first of all from Europeans? Brandy and Christianity, the European narcotics.—And by what means are they fastest ruined?—By the European narcotics.
paras.uz: 147. Savol va javob. — Yovvoyi qabilalar hozir yevropaliklardan eng avvalo nimani qabul qiladi? Aroq va nasroniylikni, Yevropa giyohvand moddalarini. — Va ular eng tez nima bilan halok bo'ladi? — Yevropa giyohvand moddalari bilan.

paras.en: 148. Where Reformations Originate. — At the time of the great corruption of the church it was least of all corrupt in Germany: it was on that account that the Reformation originated here, as a sign that even the beginnings of corruption were felt to be unendurable. For, comparatively speaking, no people was ever more Christian than the Germans at the time of Luther; their Christian culture was just about to burst into bloom with a hundred-fold splendour,—one night only was still lacking; but that night brought the storm which put an end to all.
paras.uz: 148. Islohotlar qayerdan kelib chiqadi. — Cherkovning buyuk buzilishi davrida u Germaniyada eng kam buzilgan edi: shuning uchun Islohot aynan shu yerda kelib chiqdi, hatto buzilishning boshlanishi ham chidab bo'lmas deb his qilinganining belgisi sifatida. Chunki nisbatan olganda, hech bir xalq Lyuter davridagi nemislardan ko'ra nasroniyroq bo'lmagan; ularning nasroniy madaniyati yuz baravar ulug'vorlik bilan gullashga endigina tayyor edi, — faqat bir kecha yetishmasdi; lekin o'sha kecha hamma narsaga chek qo'ygan bo'ronni olib keldi.

paras.en: 149. The Failure of Reformations. — It testifies to the higher culture of the Greeks, even in rather early ages, that attempts to establish new Grecian religions frequently failed; it testifies that quite early there must have been a multitude of dissimilar individuals in Greece, whose dissimilar troubles were not cured by a single recipe of faith and hope. Pythagoras and Plato, perhaps also Empedocles, and already much earlier the Orphic enthusiasts, aimed at founding new religions; and the two first-named were so endowed with the qualifications for founding religions, that one cannot be sufficiently astonished at their failure: they just reached the point of founding sects.
paras.uz: 149. Islohotlarning muvaffaqiyatsizligi. — Yangi yunon dinlarini o'rnatish urinishlarining tez-tez muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchragani yunonlarning hatto ancha erta davrlardagi ham yuksakroq madaniyatidan dalolat beradi; bu Yunonistonda juda erta ko'plab turli shaxslar bo'lgan bo'lishi kerakligidan, ularning turli tashvishlari bitta iymon va umid retsepti bilan davolanmaganidan dalolat beradi. Pifagor va Platon, balki Empedokl ham, va undan ancha oldin orfik ishqibozlar yangi dinlar asos solishni maqsad qilishgan; va birinchi ikkitasi din asos solish uchun shunchalik qobiliyatli ediki, ularning muvaffaqiyatsizligidan yetarlicha hayron bo'lib bo'lmaydi: ular faqat sekta asos solish nuqtasigacha yetishdi.

paras.en: Every time that the Reformation of an entire people fails and only sects raise their heads, one may conclude that the people already contains many types, and has begun to free itself from the gross herding instincts and the morality of custom,—a momentous state of suspense, which one is accustomed to disparage as decay of morals and corruption, while it announces the maturing of the egg and the early rupture of the shell. That Luther's Reformation succeeded in the north, is a sign that the north had remained backward in comparison with the south of Europe, and still had requirements tolerably uniform in colour and kind; and there would have been no Christianising of Europe at all, if the culture of the old world of the south had not been gradually barbarized by an excessive admixture of the blood of German barbarians, and thus lost its ascendency.
paras.uz: Har safar butun bir xalqning islohoti muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchrab, faqat sektalar bosh ko'targanda, xalqda allaqachon ko'p turlar borligi va u qo'pol poda instinktlari va urf-odat axloqidan ozod bo'la boshlagani haqida xulosa chiqarish mumkin, — muhim noaniqlik holati, uni axloqning tanazzuli va buzilish deb past baholashga odatlanishgan, holbuki u tuxumning pishishi va po'chog'ining erta yorilishini e'lon qiladi. Lyuter islohoti shimolda muvaffaqiyatli bo'lgani shimol Yevropa janubiga nisbatan orqada qolgani va hali rangi va turi jihatidan ancha bir xil ehtiyojlarga ega ekanining belgisi; va agar janubdagi eski dunyo madaniyati nemis vahshiylari qonining haddan tashqari aralashuvi bilan asta-sekin vahshiylashmaganida va shu tariqa ustunligini yo'qotmaganida, Yevropani nasroniylashtirish umuman bo'lmasdi.

paras.en: The more universally and unconditionally an individual, or the thought of an individual, can operate, so much more homogeneous and so much lower must be the mass that is there operated upon; while counter-strivings betray internal counter-requirements, which also want to gratify and realise themselves. Reversely, one may always conclude with regard to an actual elevation of culture, when powerful and ambitious natures only produce a limited and sectarian effect: this is true also for the separate arts, and for the provinces of knowledge. Where there is ruling there are masses: where there are masses there is need of slavery. Where there is slavery the individuals are but few, and have the instincts and conscience of the herd opposed to them.
paras.uz: Shaxs yoki shaxsning fikri qanchalik umumiyroq va shartsizroq ta'sir qila olsa, u yerda ta'sir qilinadigan omma shunchalik bir xilroq va shunchalik pastroq bo'lishi kerak; qarama-qarshi intilishlar esa o'zini qondirmoqchi va amalga oshirmoqchi bo'lgan ichki qarama-qarshi ehtiyojlarni oshkor qiladi. Aksincha, qudratli va shuhratparast tabiatlar faqat cheklangan va sektachilik ta'sirini ko'rsatganda doimo madaniyatning haqiqiy yuksalishi haqida xulosa chiqarish mumkin: bu alohida san'atlar va bilim sohalari uchun ham to'g'ri. Hukmronlik bor joyda omma bor: omma bor joyda qullikka ehtiyoj bor. Qullik bor joyda shaxslar juda oz va ularga podaning instinktlari va vijdoni qarshi turadi.

paras.en: 150. Criticism of Saints. — Must one then, in order to have a virtue, be desirous of having it precisely in its most brutal form?—as the Christian saints desired and needed;—those who only endured life with the thought that at the sight of their virtue self-contempt might seize every man. A virtue with such an effect I call brutal.
paras.uz: 150. Avliyolarni tanqid qilish. — Demak, fazilatga ega bo'lish uchun uni aynan eng qo'pol shaklida istash kerakmi? — nasroniy avliyolar istagan va ularga kerak bo'lganidek; — ular hayotga faqat ularning fazilatini ko'rganda har bir odamni o'zidan nafratlanish chulg'ab olishi mumkin degan fikr bilan chidashgan. Bunday ta'sirli fazilatni men qo'pol deb atayman.

paras.en: 151. The Origin of Religion. — The metaphysical requirement is not the origin of religions, as Schopenhauer claims, but only a later sprout from them. Under the dominance of religious thoughts we have accustomed ourselves to the idea of "another (back, under, or upper) world," and feel an uncomfortable void and privation through the annihilation of the religious illusion;—and then "another world" grows out of this feeling once more, but now it is only a metaphysical world, and no longer a religious one. That however which in general led to the assumption of "another world" in primitive times, was not an impulse or requirement, but an error in the interpretation of certain natural phenomena, a difficulty of the intellect.
paras.uz: 151. Dinning kelib chiqishi. — Metafizik ehtiyoj Shopengauer da'vo qilganidek dinlarning kelib chiqishi emas, balki faqat ulardan keyinroq o'sib chiqqan novda. Diniy fikrlar hukmronligi ostida biz «boshqa (orqa, quyi yoki yuqori) dunyo» g'oyasiga o'rganib qolganmiz va diniy xayolning yo'q qilinishi bilan noqulay bo'shliq va mahrumlikni his qilamiz; — keyin bu tuyg'udan yana «boshqa dunyo» o'sib chiqadi, lekin endi u faqat metafizik dunyo, endi diniy emas. Biroq ibtidoiy zamonlarda umuman «boshqa dunyo»ni faraz qilishga olib kelgan narsa mayl yoki ehtiyoj emas, balki ba'zi tabiat hodisalarini talqin qilishdagi xato, aqlning qiyinchiligi edi.

paras.en: 152. The greatest Change. — The lustre and the hues of all things have changed! We no longer quite understand how earlier men conceived of the most familiar and frequent things,—for example, of the day, and the awakening in the morning: owing to their belief in dreams the waking state seemed to them differently illuminated. And similarly of the whole of life, with its reflection of death and its significance: our "death" is an entirely different death. All events were of a different lustre, for a God shone forth in them; and similarly of all resolutions and peeps into the distant future: for people had oracles, and secret hints, and believed in prognostication. "Truth" was conceived in quite a different manner, for the insane could formerly be regarded as its mouthpiece—a thing which makes us shudder, or laugh.
paras.uz: 152. Eng katta o'zgarish. — Barcha narsalarning yaltirashi va ranglari o'zgardi! Biz ilgarigi odamlar eng tanish va eng tez-tez uchraydigan narsalarni, masalan, kunni va ertalab uyg'onishni qanday tasavvur qilganini endi butunlay tushunmaymiz: tushlarga bo'lgan ishonchlari tufayli uyg'oq holat ularga boshqacha yoritilgandek ko'rinardi. Xuddi shunday butun hayot haqida, o'limning aksi va uning ma'nosi bilan: bizning «o'lim»imiz butunlay boshqa o'lim. Barcha voqealar boshqacha yaltirardi, chunki ularda Xudo porlardi; xuddi shunday barcha qarorlar va uzoq kelajakka nazar tashlashlar haqida: chunki odamlarda bashoratlar va yashirin ishoralar bor edi va ular oldindan aytishga ishonishardi. «Haqiqat» butunlay boshqacha tasavvur qilingan, chunki ilgari telbalarni uning so'zlovchisi deb hisoblash mumkin edi — bu bizni titratadigan yoki kuldiradigan narsa.

paras.en: Injustice made a different impression on the feelings: for people were afraid of divine retribution, and not only of legal punishment and disgrace. What joy was there in an age when men believed in the devil and tempter! What passion was there when people saw demons lurking close at hand! What philosophy was there when doubt was regarded as sinfulness of the most dangerous kind, and in fact as an outrage on eternal love, as distrust of everything good, high, pure, and compassionate!—We have coloured things anew, we paint them over continually,—but what have we been able to do hitherto in comparison with the splendid colouring of that old master!—I mean ancient humanity.
paras.uz: Adolatsizlik tuyg'ularga boshqacha taassurot qoldirardi: chunki odamlar faqat qonuniy jazo va sharmandalikdan emas, ilohiy jazodan ham qo'rqishardi. Odamlar iblis va vasvasachiga ishongan davrda qanday quvonch bor edi! Odamlar jinlarni yaqin qo'l ostida pusib turganini ko'rganda qanday ehtiros bor edi! Shubha eng xavfli turdagi gunoh, haqiqatan ham abadiy sevgiga haqorat, barcha yaxshi, yuksak, pok va rahmdil narsaga ishonchsizlik deb hisoblanganda qanday falsafa bor edi! — Biz narsalarni yangidan bo'yadik, ularni doimo qayta bo'yayapmiz, — lekin o'sha keksa ustaning ajoyib bo'yog'i bilan solishtirganda biz shu paytgacha nima qila oldik! — men qadimgi insoniyatni nazarda tutyapman.

paras.en: 153. Homo poeta. — "I myself who have made this tragedy of tragedies altogether independently, in so far as it is completed; I who have first entwined the perplexities of morality about existence, and have tightened them so that only a God could unravel them—so Horace demands!—I have already in the fourth act killed all the Gods—for the sake of morality! What is now to be done about the fifth act? Where shall I get the tragic dénouement! Must I now think about a comic dénouement?"
paras.uz: 153. Homo poeta — Shoir inson. — «Men o'zim, bu tragediyalar tragediyasini, u tugallangan darajada, butunlay mustaqil yaratgan men; axloqning chigalliklarini birinchi bo'lib hayot atrofiga o'ragan va ularni faqat Xudogina yecha oladigan qilib tortgan men — Goratsiy shuni talab qiladi! — to'rtinchi pardadayoq barcha xudolarni o'ldirdim — axloq uchun! Endi beshinchi parda bilan nima qilish kerak? Tragik yechimni qayerdan olaman! Endi komik yechim haqida o'ylashim kerakmi?»

paras.en: 154. Differences in the Dangerousness of Life. — You don't know at all what you experience; you run through life as if intoxicated, and now and then fall down a stair. Thanks however to your intoxication you still do not break your limbs: your muscles are too languid and your head too confused to find the stones of the staircase as hard as we others do! For us life is a greater danger: we are made of glass—alas, if we should strike against anything! And all is lost if we should fall!
paras.uz: 154. Hayot xavfliligidagi farqlar. — Siz nimani boshdan kechirayotganingizni umuman bilmaysiz; hayot bo'ylab go'yo mastdek yugurasiz va vaqti-vaqti bilan zinapoyadan yiqilasiz. Biroq mastligingiz tufayli siz hali ham oyoq-qo'llaringizni sindirmaysiz: mushaklaringiz haddan tashqari bo'shashgan va boshingiz haddan tashqari chalkash, zinapoya toshlarini biz boshqalar kabi qattiq deb topish uchun! Biz uchun hayot kattaroq xavf: biz shishadan yasalganmiz — afsus, agar biror narsaga urilsak! Va agar yiqilsak, hammasi yo'qoladi!

paras.en: 155. What we Lack. — We love the grandeur of Nature and have discovered it; that is because human grandeur is lacking in our minds. It was the reverse with the Greeks: their feeling towards Nature was quite different from ours.
paras.uz: 155. Bizga nima yetishmaydi. — Biz tabiatning ulug'vorligini sevamiz va uni kashf etdik; buning sababi — aqlimizda inson ulug'vorligi yetishmaydi. Yunonlarda aksincha edi: ularning tabiatga bo'lgan tuyg'usi biznikidan butunlay boshqacha edi.
