chapters.recap_uz: Nitsshe nasroniylikni tanqid qiladi va ko'pxudolikni maqtaydi: u shaxsga o'z idealini yaratish huquqini bergan. Diniy urushlar, islohotlar va «eng katta o'zgarish» — o'tmish odamlari dunyoni butunlay boshqacha ranglarda ko'rgan.

chapters.title: Short arrows

paras.en: 156. The most Influential Person. — The fact that a person resists the whole spirit of his age, stops it at the door, and calls it to account, must exert an influence! It is indifferent whether he wishes to exert an influence; the point is that he can.
paras.uz: 156. Eng ta'sirli odam. — Odam o'z davrining butun ruhiga qarshi turishi, uni eshik oldida to'xtatib, javob berishga chaqirishi albatta ta'sir ko'rsatishi kerak! U ta'sir ko'rsatishni istaydimi, farqi yo'q; gap shundaki, u qila oladi.

paras.en: 157. Mentiri. — Take care!—he reflects: he will have a lie ready immediately. This is a stage in the civilisation of whole nations. Consider only what the Romans expressed by mentiri!
paras.uz: 157. Mentiri — Yolg'on gapirish. — Ehtiyot bo'l! — u o'ylayapti: hozir yolg'oni tayyor bo'ladi. Bu butun xalqlar tsivilizatsiyasidagi bir bosqich. Rimliklar mentiri bilan nimani ifodalaganini o'ylab ko'ring!

paras.en: 158. An Inconvenient Peculiarity. — To find everything deep is an inconvenient peculiarity: it makes one constantly strain one's eyes, so that in the end one always finds more than one wishes.
paras.uz: 158. Noqulay xususiyat. — Hamma narsani chuqur deb topish noqulay xususiyat: u odamni doimo ko'zini zo'riqtirishga majbur qiladi, shunda oxir-oqibat doimo istaganidan ko'proq narsa topadi.

paras.en: 159. Every Virtue has its Time. — The honesty of him who is at present inflexible often causes him remorse; for inflexibility is the virtue of a time different from that in which honesty prevails.
paras.uz: 159. Har bir fazilatning o'z vaqti bor. — Hozir murosasiz bo'lgan odamning halolligi unga ko'pincha pushaymonlik keltiradi; chunki murosasizlik halollik hukmron bo'lgan davrdan boshqa davrning fazilati.

paras.en: 160. In Intercourse with Virtues. — One can also be undignified and flattering towards a virtue.
paras.uz: 160. Fazilatlar bilan muomalada. — Fazilatga nisbatan ham qadrsiz va xushomadgo'y bo'lish mumkin.

paras.en: 161. To the Admirers of the Age. — The runaway priest and the liberated criminal are continually making grimaces; what they want is a look without a past.—But have you ever seen men who know that their looks reflect the future, and who are so courteous to you, the admirers of the "age," that they assume a look without a future.
paras.uz: 161. Zamon muxlislariga. — Qochqin ruhoniy va ozod qilingan jinoyatchi doimo turqini burishtirib turadi; ular o'tmishsiz qiyofani istashadi. — Lekin siz hech qachon qiyofasida kelajak aks etishini biladigan va sizga, «zamon» muxlislariga shunchalik xushmuomala bo'lgan, kelajaksiz qiyofaga kiradigan odamlarni ko'rganmisiz?

paras.en: 162. Egoism. — Egoism is the perspective law of our sentiment, according to which the near appears large and momentous, while in the distance the magnitude and importance of all things diminish.
paras.uz: 162. Xudbinlik. — Xudbinlik — tuyg'umizning istiqbol qonuni, unga ko'ra yaqin narsa katta va muhim ko'rinadi, uzoqda esa barcha narsalarning kattaligi va ahamiyati kamayadi.

paras.en: 163. After a Great Victory. — The best thing in a great victory is that it deprives the conqueror of the fear of defeat. "Why should I not be worsted for once?" he says to himself, "I am now rich enough to stand it."
paras.uz: 163. Buyuk g'alabadan keyin. — Buyuk g'alabadagi eng yaxshi narsa shuki, u g'olibni mag'lubiyat qo'rquvidan mahrum qiladi. «Nega bir marta yengilmasligim kerak? — deydi u o'ziga, — men endi bunga chidash uchun yetarlicha boyman».

paras.en: 164. Those who Seek Repose. — I recognise the minds that seek repose by the many dark objects with which they surround themselves: those who want to sleep darken their chambers, or creep into caverns. A hint to those who do not know what they really seek most, and would like to know!
paras.uz: 164. Osoyishtalik izlovchilar. — Men osoyishtalik izlayotgan aqllarni o'zlarini o'rab olgan ko'plab qorong'i narsalardan taniyman: uxlamoqchi bo'lganlar xonalarini qorong'ilatadi yoki g'orlarga emaklab kiradi. Aslida nimani eng ko'p izlayotganini bilmaydigan va bilishni istaydiganlarga ishora!

paras.en: 165. The Happiness of Renunciation. — He who has absolutely dispensed with something for a long time will almost imagine, when he accidentally meets with it again, that he has discovered it,—and what happiness every discoverer has! Let us be wiser than the serpents that lie too long in the same sunshine.
paras.uz: 165. Voz kechish baxti. — Biror narsadan uzoq vaqt butunlay voz kechgan odam unga tasodifan yana duch kelganda deyarli uni kashf etgandek tasavvur qiladi, — va har bir kashfiyotchida qanday baxt bor! Bir xil quyosh nurida haddan tashqari uzoq yotadigan ilonlardan donoroq bo'laylik.

paras.en: 166. Always in our own Society. — All that is akin to me in nature and history speaks to me, praises me, urges me forward and comforts me—: other things are unheard by me, or immediately forgotten. We are only in our own society always.
paras.uz: 166. Doimo o'z jamiyatimizda. — Tabiat va tarixdagi menga yaqin bo'lgan hamma narsa menga gapiradi, meni maqtaydi, oldinga undaydi va tasalli beradi —: boshqa narsalarni men eshitmayman yoki darhol unutaman. Biz doimo faqat o'z jamiyatimizdamiz.

paras.en: 167. Misanthropy and Philanthropy. — We only speak about being sick of men when we can no longer digest them, and yet have the stomach full of them. Misanthropy is the result of a far too eager philanthropy and "cannibalism,"—but who ever bade you swallow men like oysters, my Prince Hamlet!
paras.uz: 167. Odamlardan nafrat va insonparvarlik. — Biz odamlardan bezdik deb faqat ularni endi hazm qila olmaganimizda, lekin shunga qaramay qornimiz ular bilan to'la bo'lganda gapiramiz. Odamlardan nafrat — haddan tashqari ishtiyoqli insonparvarlik va «odamxo'rlik» natijasi, — lekin sizga odamlarni ustritsadek yutishni kim buyurgan, mening shahzodam Hamlet!

paras.en: 168. Concerning an Invalid. — "Things go badly with him!"—What is wrong?—"He suffers from the longing to be praised, and finds no sustenance for it."—Inconceivable! All the world does honour to him, and he is reverenced not only in deed but in word!—"Certainly, but he is dull of hearing for the praise. When a friend praises him it sounds to him as if the friend praised himself; when an enemy praises him, it sounds to him as if the enemy wanted to be praised for it; when, finally, some one else praises him—there are by no means so many of these, he is so famous!—he is offended because they neither want him for a friend nor for an enemy; he is accustomed to say: 'What do I care for those who can still pose as the all-righteous towards me!'"
paras.uz: 168. Bir bemor haqida. — «Uning ishlari yomon!» — Nima bo'ldi? — «U maqtalish istagidan azob chekmoqda va buning uchun ozuqa topa olmayapti». — Aql bovar qilmaydi! Butun dunyo uni hurmat qiladi va uni nafaqat amalda, balki so'zda ham ulug'lashadi! — «Albatta, lekin u maqtovga qulog'i og'ir. Do'sti uni maqtasa, unga go'yo do'st o'zini maqtayotgandek eshitiladi; dushmani uni maqtasa, unga go'yo dushman buning uchun maqtalishni istayotgandek eshitiladi; nihoyat, kimdir boshqa uni maqtasa — ular aslo unchalik ko'p emas, u shunchalik mashhur! — u xafa bo'ladi, chunki ular uni na do'st, na dushman qilib olishni istashadi; u odatda shunday deydi: "Menga nisbatan hali ham o'zini butunlay adolatli qilib ko'rsata oladiganlar menga nima!"»

paras.en: 169. Avowed Enemies. — Bravery in presence of an enemy is a thing by itself: a person may possess it and still be a coward and an irresolute numskull. That was Napoleon's opinion concerning the "bravest man" he knew, Murat:—whence it follows that avowed enemies are indispensable to some men, if they are to attain to their virtue, to their manliness, to their cheerfulness.
paras.uz: 169. Ochiq dushmanlar. — Dushman oldidagi jasorat — alohida narsa: odam unga ega bo'lib, shunga qaramay qo'rqoq va qatiyatsiz kallavaram bo'lishi mumkin. Napoleon o'zi bilgan «eng jasur odam» Myura haqida shunday fikrda edi: — bundan kelib chiqadiki, ba'zi odamlarga o'z fazilatiga, erkakligiga, quvnoqligiga erishish uchun ochiq dushmanlar zarur.

paras.en: 170. With the Multitude. — He has hitherto gone with the multitude and is its panegyrist; but one day he will be its opponent! For he follows it in the belief that his laziness will find its advantage thereby; he has not yet learned that the multitude is not lazy enough for him! that it always presses forward! that it does not allow any one to stand still!—And he likes so well to stand still!
paras.uz: 170. Olomon bilan. — U shu paytgacha olomon bilan yurgan va uning maqtovchisi; lekin bir kun kelib uning raqibi bo'ladi! Chunki u dangasaligi bundan foyda topadi degan ishonch bilan unga ergashadi; u hali olomon uning uchun yetarlicha dangasa emasligini o'rganmagan! u doimo oldinga intiladi! u hech kimga bir joyda turishga yo'l qo'ymaydi! — U esa bir joyda turishni shunchalik yaxshi ko'radi!

paras.en: 171. Fame. — When the gratitude of many to one casts aside all shame, then fame originates.
paras.uz: 171. Shon-shuhrat. — Ko'pchilikning bir kishiga minnatdorligi butun uyatni chetga tashlaganda, shon-shuhrat paydo bo'ladi.

paras.en: 172. The Perverter of Taste. — A: "You are a perverter of taste—they say so everywhere!" B: "Certainly! I pervert every one's taste for his party:—no party forgives me for that."
paras.uz: 172. Didni buzuvchi. — A: «Siz didni buzuvchisiz — hamma joyda shunday deyishyapti!» B: «Albatta! Men har kimning o'z partiyasiga bo'lgan didini buzaman: — buning uchun hech bir partiya meni kechirmaydi».

paras.en: 173. To be Profound and to Appear Profound. — He who knows that he is profound strives for clearness; he who would like to appear profound to the multitude strives for obscurity. The multitude thinks everything profound of which it cannot see the bottom; it is so timid and goes so unwillingly into the water.
paras.uz: 173. Chuqur bo'lish va chuqur ko'rinish. — O'zining chuqur ekanini biladigan odam ravshanlikka intiladi; olomonga chuqur ko'rinishni istagan odam qorong'ilikka intiladi. Olomon tubini ko'ra olmaydigan hamma narsani chuqur deb o'ylaydi; u shunchalik qo'rqoq va suvga shunchalik istamay kiradi.

paras.en: 174. Apart. — Parliamentarism, that is to say, the public permission to choose between five main political opinions, insinuates itself into the favour of the numerous class who would fain appear independent and individual, and like to fight for their opinions. After all, however, it is a matter of indifference whether one opinion is imposed upon the herd, or five opinions are permitted to it.—He who diverges from the five public opinions and goes apart, has always the whole herd against him.
paras.uz: 174. Chetda. — Parlamentarizm, ya'ni beshta asosiy siyosiy fikr o'rtasida tanlashga ommaviy ruxsat, o'zini mustaqil va alohida ko'rsatishni xohlaydigan va o'z fikrlari uchun kurashishni yaxshi ko'radigan ko'p sonli tabaqaning marhamatiga suqilib kiradi. Biroq oxir-oqibat, podaga bitta fikr majburlanadimi yoki unga beshta fikrga ruxsat beriladimi, farqi yo'q. — Beshta jamoat fikridan chetga chiqib, alohida yo'lga ketgan odamga doimo butun poda qarshi turadi.

paras.en: 175. Concerning Eloquence. — What has hitherto had the most convincing eloquence? The rolling of the drum: and as long as kings have this at their command, they will always be the best orators and popular leaders.
paras.uz: 175. Notiqlik haqida. — Shu paytgacha eng ishonarli notiqlik nimada bo'lgan? Barabanning gumburlashida: va podshohlar uni o'z ixtiyorida tutar ekan, ular doimo eng yaxshi notiqlar va xalq yetakchilari bo'lib qoladi.

paras.en: 176. Compassion. — The poor, ruling princes! All their rights now change unexpectedly into claims, and all these claims immediately sound like pretensions! And if they but say "we," or "my people," wicked old Europe begins laughing. Verily, a chief-master-of-ceremonies of the modern world would make little ceremony with them; perhaps he would decree that "les souverains rangent aux parvenus."
paras.uz: 176. Achinish. — Bechora, hukmron shahzodalar! Ularning barcha huquqlari endi kutilmaganda talablarga aylanadi va bu talablarning hammasi darhol da'volardek eshitiladi! Va ular faqat «biz» yoki «mening xalqim» deyishsa, yovuz keksa Yevropa kula boshlaydi. Haqiqatan ham, zamonaviy dunyoning bosh marosim ustasi ular bilan unchalik marosim qilmasdi; balki u «les souverains rangent aux parvenus» — hukmdorlar yangi boyib qolganlar qatoriga o'tadi — deb farmon chiqarar.

paras.en: 177. On "Educational Matters.". — In Germany an important educational means is lacking for higher men; namely, the laughter of higher men; these men do not laugh in Germany.
paras.uz: 177. «Tarbiya masalalari» haqida. — Germaniyada yuksakroq odamlar uchun muhim tarbiya vositasi yetishmaydi; ya'ni yuksakroq odamlarning kulgisi; bu odamlar Germaniyada kulmaydi.

paras.en: 178. For Moral Enlightenment. — The Germans must be talked out of their Mephistopheles—and out of their Faust also. These are two moral prejudices against the value of knowledge.
paras.uz: 178. Axloqiy ma'rifat uchun. — Nemislarni Mefistofeldan — va Faustdan ham gapirib qaytarish kerak. Bular bilimning qadriga qarshi ikkita axloqiy xurofot.

paras.en: 179. Thoughts. — Thoughts are the shadows of our sentiments—always, however, obscurer, emptier, and simpler.
paras.uz: 179. Fikrlar. — Fikrlar — tuyg'ularimizning soyalari, biroq doimo qorong'iroq, bo'shroq va oddiyroq.

paras.en: 180. The Good Time for Free Spirits. — Free Spirits take liberties even with regard to Science—and meanwhile they are allowed to do so,—while the Church still remains!—In so far they have now their good time.
paras.uz: 180. Erkin ruhlar uchun yaxshi vaqt. — Erkin ruhlar hatto ilmga nisbatan ham erkinlik qilishadi — va hozircha ularga bunga ruxsat beriladi, — cherkov hali qolar ekan! — Shu jihatdan ularning endi yaxshi vaqti.

paras.en: 181. Following and Leading. — A: "Of the two, the one will always follow, the other will always lead, whatever be the course of their destiny. And yet the former is superior to the other in virtue and intellect." B: "And yet? And yet? That is spoken for the others; not for me, not for us!—Fit secundum regulam."
paras.uz: 181. Ergashish va yetaklash. — A: «Ikkalasidan biri doimo ergashadi, ikkinchisi doimo yetaklaydi, taqdirlari qanday kechmasin. Lekin shunga qaramay birinchisi fazilat va aqlda ikkinchisidan ustun». B: «Lekin shunga qaramaymi? Lekin shunga qaramaymi? Bu boshqalar uchun aytilgan; men uchun emas, biz uchun emas! — Fit secundum regulam — Qoidaga ko'ra sodir bo'ladi».

paras.en: 182. In Solitude. — When one lives alone one does not speak too loudly, and one does not write too loudly either, for one fears the hollow reverberation—the criticism of the nymph Echo.—And all voices sound differently in solitude!
paras.uz: 182. Yolg'izlikda. — Yolg'iz yashaganda odam haddan tashqari baland gapirmaydi, haddan tashqari baland yozmaydi ham, chunki bo'sh aks-sadodan — Exo parisining tanqididan qo'rqadi. — Va yolg'izlikda barcha ovozlar boshqacha yangraydi!

paras.en: 183. The Music of the Best Future. — The first musician for me would be he who knew only the sorrow of the profoundest happiness, and no other sorrow: there has not hitherto been such a musician.
paras.uz: 183. Eng yaxshi kelajak musiqasi. — Men uchun birinchi musiqachi faqat eng chuqur baxtning qayg'usini bilgan va boshqa hech qanday qayg'uni bilmagan odam bo'lardi: shu paytgacha bunday musiqachi bo'lmagan.

paras.en: 184. Justice. — Better allow oneself to be robbed than have scarecrows around one—that is my taste. And under all circumstances it is just a matter of taste—and nothing more!
paras.uz: 184. Adolat. — Atrofingda qo'rqinchli qo'g'irchoqlar bo'lgandan ko'ra o'zingni talon-taroj qilishga yo'l qo'ygan yaxshiroq — mening didim shunday. Va har qanday sharoitda bu shunchaki did masalasi — va boshqa hech narsa emas!

paras.en: 185. Poor. — He is now poor, but not because everything has been taken from him, but because he has thrown everything away:—what does he care? He is accustomed to find new things.—It is the poor who misunderstand his voluntary poverty.
paras.uz: 185. Kambag'al. — U endi kambag'al, lekin undan hamma narsa tortib olingani uchun emas, balki u hamma narsani tashlab yuborgani uchun: — unga nima? U yangi narsalar topishga odatlangan. — Uning ixtiyoriy kambag'alligini kambag'allar noto'g'ri tushunadi.

paras.en: 186. Bad Conscience. — All that he now does is excellent and proper—and yet he has a bad conscience with it all. For the exceptional is his task.
paras.uz: 186. Yomon vijdon. — U endi qilayotgan hamma narsa ajoyib va to'g'ri — va shunga qaramay bularning hammasi bilan uning vijdoni yomon. Chunki uning vazifasi istisno narsa.

paras.en: 187. Offensiveness in Expression. — This artist offends me by the way in which he expresses his ideas, his very excellent ideas: so diffusely and forcibly, and with such gross rhetorical artifices, as if he were speaking to the mob. We feel always as if "in bad company" when devoting some time to his art.
paras.uz: 187. Ifodadagi haqoratlilik. — Bu san'atkor o'z g'oyalarini, juda ajoyib g'oyalarini ifodalash usuli bilan meni ranjitadi: shunchalik cho'zib va zo'rlab, shunday qo'pol ritorik hiylalar bilan, go'yo olomonga gapirayotgandek. Uning san'atiga biroz vaqt bag'ishlaganimizda doimo o'zimizni go'yo «yomon davrada»dek his qilamiz.

paras.en: 188. Work. — How close work and the workers now stand even to the most leisurely of us! The royal courtesy in the words: "We are all workers," would have been a cynicism and an indecency even under Louis XIV.
paras.uz: 188. Ish. — Ish va ishchilar endi hatto eng bekorchimizga ham qanchalik yaqin turadi! «Biz hammamiz ishchilarmiz» degan so'zlardagi shohona xushmuomalalik hatto Lyudovik XIV davrida ham kinizm va odobsizlik bo'lardi.

paras.en: 189. The Thinker. — He is a thinker: that is to say, he knows how to take things more simply than they are.
paras.uz: 189. Mutafakkir. — U mutafakkir: ya'ni u narsalarni ular qanday bo'lsa, shundan ko'ra soddaroq qabul qilishni biladi.

paras.en: 190. Against Eulogisers. — A: "One is only praised by one's equals!" B: "Yes! And he who praises you says: 'You are my equal!'"
paras.uz: 190. Maqtovchilarga qarshi. — A: «Odamni faqat o'ziga tenglar maqtaydi!» B: «Ha! Va sizni maqtagan odam: "Siz menga tengsiz!" deydi».

paras.en: 191. Against many a Vindication. — The most perfidious manner of injuring a cause is to vindicate it intentionally with fallacious arguments.
paras.uz: 191. Ko'p oqlashlarga qarshi. — Ishga zarar yetkazishning eng xoinona usuli — uni qasddan soxta dalillar bilan oqlash.

paras.en: 192. The Good-natured. — What is it that distinguishes the good-natured, whose countenances beam kindness, from other people? They feel quite at ease in presence of a new person, and are quickly enamoured of him; they therefore wish him well; their first opinion is: "He pleases me." With them there follow in succession the wish to appropriate (they make little scruple about the person's worth), rapid appropriation, joy in the possession, and actions in favour of the person possessed.
paras.uz: 192. Xushfe'llar. — Yuzlaridan mehribonlik porlab turadigan xushfe'llarni boshqa odamlardan nima ajratib turadi? Ular yangi odam oldida o'zlarini butunlay erkin his qilishadi va tez uni yoqtirib qolishadi; shuning uchun unga yaxshilik tilashadi; ularning birinchi fikri: «U menga yoqadi». Ularda ketma-ket o'zlashtirish istagi (ular odamning qadri haqida unchalik o'ylamaydi), tez o'zlashtirish, egalikdan quvonch va egalik qilingan odam foydasiga harakatlar keladi.

paras.en: 193. Kant's Joke. — Kant tried to prove, in a way that dismayed "everybody," that "everybody" was in the right:—that was his secret joke. He wrote against the learned, in favour of popular prejudice; he wrote, however, for the learned and not for the people.
paras.uz: 193. Kantning hazili. — Kant «hamma»ni dahshatga soladigan tarzda «hamma» haq ekanini isbotlashga urindi: — bu uning yashirin hazili edi. U olimlarga qarshi, xalq xurofoti foydasiga yozdi; biroq u xalq uchun emas, olimlar uchun yozdi.

paras.en: 194. The "Open-hearted" Man. — That man acts probably always from concealed motives; for he has always communicable motives on his tongue, and almost in his open hand.
paras.uz: 194. «Ochiq ko'ngilli» odam. — Bu odam ehtimol doimo yashirin motivlardan harakat qiladi; chunki uning tilida, deyarli ochiq kaftida doimo aytib bo'ladigan motivlar bor.

paras.en: 195. Laughable!. — See! See! He runs away from men—: they follow him, however, because he runs before them,—they are such a gregarious lot!
paras.uz: 195. Kulgili! — Qarang! Qarang! U odamlardan qochadi —: biroq ular uning orqasidan ergashadi, chunki u ularning oldida yuguradi, — ular shunchalik podaviy xalq!

paras.en: 196. The Limits of our Sense of Hearing. — We hear only the questions to which we are capable of finding an answer.
paras.uz: 196. Eshitishimiz chegaralari. — Biz faqat javob topishga qodir bo'lgan savollarnigina eshitamiz.

paras.en: 197. Caution therefore!. — There is nothing we are fonder of communicating to others than the seal of secrecy—together with what is under it.
paras.uz: 197. Shuning uchun ehtiyot bo'ling! — Boshqalarga sirlilik muhridan — uning ostidagi narsa bilan birga — yetkazishni yaxshi ko'radigan narsamiz yo'q.

paras.en: 198. Vexation of the Proud Man. — The proud man is vexed even with those who help him forward: he looks angrily at his carriage-horses!
paras.uz: 198. Mag'rur odamning g'azabi. — Mag'rur odam hatto uni oldinga yordam berayotganlardan ham g'azablanadi: u arava otlariga jahl bilan qaraydi!

paras.en: 199. Liberality. — Liberality is often only a form of timidity in the rich.
paras.uz: 199. Saxovat. — Saxovat ko'pincha boylardagi qo'rqoqlikning bir shakli, xolos.

paras.en: 200. Laughing. — To laugh means to love mischief, but with a good conscience.
paras.uz: 200. Kulish. — Kulish — yomonlikni sevish demak, lekin toza vijdon bilan.

paras.en: 201. In Applause. — In applause there is always some kind of noise: even in self-applause.
paras.uz: 201. Olqishda. — Olqishda doimo qandaydir shovqin bor: hatto o'zini olqishlashda ham.

paras.en: 202. A Spendthrift. — He has not yet the poverty of the rich man who has counted all his treasure,—he squanders his spirit with the irrationalness of the spendthrift Nature.
paras.uz: 202. Isrofgar. — Unda hali butun xazinasini sanab chiqqan boy odamning kambag'alligi yo'q, — u o'z ruhini isrofgar tabiatning aqlsizligi bilan sovuradi.

paras.en: 203. Hic niger est. — Usually he has no thoughts,—but in exceptional cases bad thoughts come to him.
paras.uz: 203. Hic niger est — Mana qora odam. — Odatda uning fikri yo'q, — lekin istisno hollarda unga yomon fikrlar keladi.

paras.en: 204. Beggars and Courtesy. — "One is not discourteous when one knocks at a door with a stone when the bell-pull is awanting"—so think all beggars and necessitous persons, but no one thinks they are in the right.
paras.uz: 204. Tilanchilar va xushmuomalalik. — «Qo'ng'iroq ipi yo'q bo'lganda eshikni tosh bilan taqillatgan odam qo'pol emas» — barcha tilanchilar va muhtojlar shunday o'ylaydi, lekin ularni haq deb hech kim o'ylamaydi.

paras.en: 205. Need. — Need is supposed to be the cause of things; but in truth it is often only the effect of the things themselves.
paras.uz: 205. Ehtiyoj. — Ehtiyoj narsalarning sababi deb hisoblanadi; lekin haqiqatda u ko'pincha narsalarning o'zining oqibati, xolos.

paras.en: 206. During the Rain. — It rains, and I think of the poor people who now crowd together with their many cares, which they are unaccustomed to conceal; all of them, therefore, ready and anxious to give pain to one another, and thus provide themselves with a pitiable kind of comfort, even in bad weather. This, this only, is the poverty of the poor!
paras.uz: 206. Yomg'ir paytida. — Yomg'ir yog'yapti va men endi o'zlarining ko'p tashvishlari bilan bir joyga to'planadigan kambag'al odamlar haqida o'ylayman, ular bu tashvishlarni yashirishga odatlanmagan; shuning uchun ularning hammasi bir-biriga og'riq berishga tayyor va intiladi va shu tariqa hatto yomon havoda ham o'zlariga ayanchli tasalli topadi. Mana shu, faqat shu — kambag'allarning kambag'alligi!

paras.en: 207. The Envious Man. — That is an envious man—it is not desirable that he should have children; he would be envious of them, because he can no longer be a child.
paras.uz: 207. Hasadgo'y odam. — Bu hasadgo'y odam — uning farzandlari bo'lishi maqsadga muvofiq emas; u ularga hasad qilardi, chunki o'zi endi bola bo'la olmaydi.

paras.en: 208. A Great Man!. — Because a person is "a great man," we are not authorised to infer that he is a man. Perhaps he is only a boy, or a chameleon of all ages, or a bewitched girl.
paras.uz: 208. Buyuk odam! — Odam «buyuk odam» bo'lgani uchun uning odam ekanini xulosa qilishga haqqimiz yo'q. Balki u faqat bola, yoki barcha yoshlarning xameleoni, yoki sehrlangan qizdir.

paras.en: 209. A Mode of Asking for Reasons. — There is a mode of asking for our reasons which not only makes us forget our best reasons, but also arouses in us a spite and repugnance against reason generally:—a very stupefying mode of questioning, and properly an artifice of tyrannical men!
paras.uz: 209. Sabab so'rashning bir usuli. — Bizdan sabablarimizni so'rashning shunday usuli borki, u nafaqat eng yaxshi sabablarimizni unuttiradi, balki bizda umuman aqlga qarshi g'azab va jirkanish uyg'otadi: — juda esankiratuvchi so'roq usuli va aslida zolim odamlarning hiylasi!

paras.en: 210. Moderation in Diligence. — One must not be anxious to surpass the diligence of one's father—that would make one ill.
paras.uz: 210. Tirishqoqlikda me'yor. — Otangning tirishqoqligidan o'zib ketishga intilmaslik kerak — bu kasal qiladi.

paras.en: 211. Secret Enemies. — To be able to keep a secret enemy—that is a luxury which the morality even of the highest-minded persons can rarely afford.
paras.uz: 211. Yashirin dushmanlar. — Yashirin dushman saqlay olish — bu hatto eng oliyjanob odamlarning axloqi ham kamdan-kam ko'tara oladigan hashamat.

paras.en: 212. Not Letting oneself be Deluded. — His spirit has bad manners, it is hasty and always stutters with impatience; so that one would hardly suspect the deep breathing and the large chest of the soul in which it resides.
paras.uz: 212. O'zini aldashga yo'l qo'ymaslik. — Uning ruhining odobi yomon, u shoshqaloq va sabrsizlikdan doimo duduqlanadi; shuning uchun u yashaydigan ruhning chuqur nafasi va keng ko'kragini deyarli gumon qilib bo'lmaydi.

paras.en: 213. The Way to Happiness. — A sage asked of a fool the way to happiness. The fool answered without delay, like one who had been asked the way to the next town: "Admire yourself, and live on the street!" "Hold," cried the sage, "you require too much; it suffices to admire oneself!" The fool replied: "But how can one constantly admire without constantly despising?"
paras.uz: 213. Baxtga yo'l. — Donishmand ahmoqdan baxtga yo'lni so'radi. Ahmoq, go'yo undan keyingi shaharga yo'lni so'ragandek, kechiktirmay javob berdi: «O'zingga qoyil qol va ko'chada yasha!» «To'xta, — deb qichqirdi donishmand, — sen haddan tashqari ko'p talab qilyapsan; o'zingga qoyil qolish kifoya!» Ahmoq javob berdi: «Lekin doimo mensimasdan doimo qanday qilib qoyil qolish mumkin?»

paras.en: 214. Faith Saves. — Virtue gives happiness and a state of blessedness only to those who have a strong faith in their virtue:—not, however, to the more refined souls whose virtue consists of a profound distrust of themselves and of all virtue. After all, therefore, it is "faith that saves" here also!—and be it well observed, not virtue!
paras.uz: 214. E'tiqod najot beradi. — Fazilat baxt va saodat holatini faqat o'z fazilatiga kuchli e'tiqodi bo'lganlargagina beradi: — biroq fazilati o'ziga va har qanday fazilatga chuqur ishonchsizlikdan iborat nozikroq qalblarga emas. Demak, oxir-oqibat bu yerda ham «najot beradigan narsa e'tiqod»! — va yaxshi e'tibor bering, fazilat emas!

paras.en: 215. The Ideal and the Material. — You have a noble ideal before your eyes: but are you also such a noble stone that such a divine image could be formed out of you? And without that—is not all your labour barbaric sculpturing? A blasphemy of your ideal!
paras.uz: 215. Ideal va material. — Ko'z oldingizda olijanob ideal bor: lekin siz ham sizdan shunday ilohiy tasvir yasash mumkin bo'lgan olijanob toshmisiz? Busiz esa — butun mehnatingiz vahshiyona haykaltaroshlik emasmi? Idealingizga kufr!

paras.en: 216. Danger in the Voice. — With a very loud voice a person is almost incapable of reflecting on subtle matters.
paras.uz: 216. Ovozdagi xavf. — Juda baland ovoz bilan odam nozik masalalar haqida mulohaza qilishga deyarli qodir emas.

paras.en: 217. Cause and Effect. — Before the effect one believes in other causes than after the effect.
paras.uz: 217. Sabab va oqibat. — Oqibatdan oldin odam oqibatdan keyingidan boshqa sabablarga ishonadi.

paras.en: 218. My Antipathy. — I do not like those people who, in order to produce an effect, have to burst like bombs, and in whose neighbourhood one is always in danger of suddenly losing one's hearing—or even something more.
paras.uz: 218. Mening nafratim. — Ta'sir ko'rsatish uchun bombadek portlashi kerak bo'lgan va ularning yonida doimo to'satdan eshitish qobiliyatingizni — yoki hatto undan ham ko'proq narsani yo'qotish xavfi ostida bo'ladigan odamlarni yoqtirmayman.

paras.en: 219. The Object of Punishment. — The object of punishment is to improve him who punishes,—that is the ultimate appeal of those who justify punishment.
paras.uz: 219. Jazoning maqsadi. — Jazoning maqsadi jazolovchini yaxshilash, — jazoni oqlaydiganlarning oxirgi dalili shu.

paras.en: 220. Sacrifice. — The victims think otherwise than the spectators about sacrifice and sacrificing: but they have never been allowed to express their opinion.
paras.uz: 220. Qurbonlik. — Qurbonlar qurbonlik va qurbon qilish haqida tomoshabinlardan boshqacha o'ylashadi: lekin ularga hech qachon o'z fikrini bildirishga ruxsat berilmagan.

paras.en: 221. Consideration. — Fathers and sons are much more considerate of one another than mothers and daughters.
paras.uz: 221. E'tiborlilik. — Otalar va o'g'illar bir-biriga onalar va qizlardan ko'ra ancha e'tiborliroq.

paras.en: 222. Poet and Liar. — The poet sees in the liar his foster-brother whose milk he has drunk up; the latter has thus remained wretched, and has not even attained to a good conscience.
paras.uz: 222. Shoir va yolg'onchi. — Shoir yolg'onchida sutini ichib qo'ygan emikdoshini ko'radi; shuning uchun ikkinchisi bechora bo'lib qolgan va hatto toza vijdonga ham erishmagan.

paras.en: 223. Vicariousness of the Senses. — "We have also eyes in order to hear with them,"—said an old confessor who had grown deaf; "and among the blind he that has the longest ears is king."
paras.uz: 223. Sezgilarning bir-birini almashtirishi. — «Bizda eshitish uchun ham ko'zlar bor», — dedi kar bo'lib qolgan keksa iqror oluvchi ruhoniy; «va ko'rlar orasida eng uzun quloqli podshoh».

quiz.q: How does one who wants to appear profound write?
quiz.why_uz: Olomon tubini ko'ra olmaydigan narsani chuqur deb o'ylaydi.

quiz.q: What does 'to laugh' mean in aphorism 200?
o: To love mischief with a good conscience
quiz.why_uz: «Kulish — yomonlikni sevish, lekin toza vijdon bilan».

chapters.recap_uz: Bir-ikki satrlik o'tkir aforizmlar to'plami: xudbinlik, shon-shuhrat, chuqur ko'rinish, parlamentarizm, kulgi, sabab va oqibat, baxtga yo'l. Har biri — alohida o'ylash uchun kichik o'q.

chapters.title: Become what you are

paras.en: 224. Animal Criticism. — I fear the animals regard man as a being like themselves, very seriously endangered by a loss of sound animal understanding;—they regard him perhaps as the absurd animal, the laughing animal, the crying animal, the unfortunate animal.
paras.uz: 224. Hayvonlar tanqidi. — Qo'rqamanki, hayvonlar insonni o'zlariga o'xshash, sog'lom hayvoniy aqlini yo'qotish xavfi ostida bo'lgan mavjudot deb bilishadi; — ular uni balki bema'ni hayvon, kuladigan hayvon, yig'laydigan hayvon, baxtsiz hayvon deb hisoblashar.

paras.en: 225. The Natural. — "Evil has always had the great effect! And Nature is evil! Let us therefore be natural!"—so reason secretly the great aspirants after effect, who are too often counted among great men.
paras.uz: 225. Tabiiy. — «Yovuzlik doimo katta ta'sir ko'rsatgan! Tabiat esa yovuz! Shuning uchun tabiiy bo'laylik!» — ta'sirga intiluvchi buyuklar, ko'pincha buyuk odamlar qatoriga qo'shiladiganlar, yashirincha shunday mulohaza qilishadi.

paras.en: 226. The Distrustful and their Style. — We say the strongest things simply, provided people are about us who believe in our strength:—such an environment educates to "simplicity of style." The distrustful, on the other hand, speak emphatically; they make things emphatic.
paras.uz: 226. Ishonchsizlar va ularning uslubi. — Biz eng kuchli gaplarni oddiy aytamiz, agar atrofimizda kuchimizga ishonadigan odamlar bo'lsa: — bunday muhit «uslub soddaligi»ga tarbiyalaydi. Ishonchsizlar esa urg'u bilan gapirishadi; ular narsalarni bo'rttirishadi.

paras.en: 227. Fallacy, Fallacy. — He cannot rule himself; therefore that woman concludes that it will be easy to rule him, and throws out her lines to catch him;—the poor creature, who in a short time will be his slave.
paras.uz: 227. Xato, xato. — U o'zini boshqara olmaydi; shuning uchun o'sha ayol uni boshqarish oson bo'ladi degan xulosaga kelib, uni ilintirish uchun qarmog'ini tashlaydi; — bechora, tez orada uning quli bo'ladi.

paras.en: 228. Against Mediators. — He who attempts to mediate between two decided thinkers is rightly called mediocre: he has not an eye for seeing the unique; similarising and equalising are signs of weak eyes.
paras.uz: 228. Vositachilarga qarshi. — Ikki qat'iy mutafakkir o'rtasida vositachilik qilishga urinadigan odam haqli ravishda o'rtamiyona deb ataladi: unda yagonani ko'radigan ko'z yo'q; o'xshatish va tenglashtirish — zaif ko'zlar belgisi.

paras.en: 229. Obstinacy and Loyalty. — Out of obstinacy he holds fast to a cause of which the questionableness has become obvious,—he calls that, however, his "loyalty."
paras.uz: 229. O'jarlik va sadoqat. — O'jarligi tufayli u shubhaliligi ayon bo'lgan ishni mahkam ushlab turadi, — biroq buni o'zining «sadoqati» deb ataydi.

paras.en: 230. Lack of Reserve. — His whole nature fails to convince—that results from the fact that he has never been reticent about a good action he has performed.
paras.uz: 230. Vazminlikning yo'qligi. — Uning butun tabiati ishontira olmaydi — bu u qilgan yaxshi ishi haqida hech qachon jim turmaganidan kelib chiqadi.

paras.en: 231. The "Plodders.". — Persons slow of apprehension think that slowness forms part of knowledge.
paras.uz: 231. «Sekin tushunadiganlar». — Sekin tushunadigan odamlar sekinlik bilimning bir qismi deb o'ylashadi.

paras.en: 232. Dreaming. — Either one does not dream at all, or one dreams in an interesting manner. One must learn to be awake in the same fashion:—either not at all, or in an interesting manner.
paras.uz: 232. Tush ko'rish. — Yo umuman tush ko'rmaysan, yoki qiziqarli tarzda tush ko'rasan. Xuddi shunday uyg'oq bo'lishni ham o'rganish kerak: — yo umuman emas, yoki qiziqarli tarzda.

paras.en: 233. The most Dangerous Point of View. — What I now do, or neglect to do, is as important for all that is to come, as the greatest event of the past: in this immense perspective of effects all actions are equally great and small.
paras.uz: 233. Eng xavfli nuqtai nazar. — Hozir nima qilsam yoki qilmay qo'ysam, kelajakdagi hamma narsa uchun o'tmishning eng buyuk voqeasi kabi muhim: ta'sirlarning bu ulkan istiqbolida barcha harakatlar bir xil katta va kichik.

paras.en: 234. Consolatory Words of a Musician. — "Your life does not sound into people's ears: for them you live a dumb life, and all refinements of melody, all fond resolutions in following or leading the way, are concealed from them. To be sure you do not parade the thoroughfares with regimental music,—but these good people have no right to say on that account that your life is lacking in music. He that hath ears let him hear."
paras.uz: 234. Musiqachining tasalli so'zlari. — «Hayoting odamlarning qulog'iga yetib bormaydi: ular uchun sen soqov hayot yashaysan va kuyning barcha nozikliklari, ergashish yoki yo'l boshlashdagi barcha mehrli qarorlar ulardan yashiringan. To'g'ri, sen ko'chalarda polk musiqasi bilan yurmaysan, — lekin bu yaxshi odamlarning shuning uchun hayotingda musiqa yo'q deyishga haqqi yo'q. Qulog'i borlar eshitsin».

paras.en: 235. Spirit and Character. — Many a one attains his full height of character, but his spirit is not adapted to the elevation,—and many a one reversely.
paras.uz: 235. Ruh va xarakter. — Ko'p odam xarakterining to'liq bo'yiga erishadi, lekin uning ruhi bu yuksaklikka moslashmagan, — ko'p odam esa aksincha.

paras.en: 236. To Move the Multitude. — Is it not necessary for him who wants to move the multitude to give a stage representation of himself? Has he not first to translate himself into the grotesquely obvious, and then set forth his whole personality and cause in that vulgarised and simplified fashion!
paras.uz: 236. Olomonni harakatga keltirish uchun. — Olomonni harakatga keltirmoqchi bo'lgan odam o'zini sahnada ko'rsatishi kerak emasmi? U avval o'zini kulgili darajada ayon narsaga tarjima qilib, keyin butun shaxsiyati va ishini o'sha qo'pollashtirilgan va soddalashtirilgan tarzda bayon qilishi kerak emasmi!

paras.en: 237. The Polite Man. — "He is so polite!"—Yes, he has always a sop for Cerberus with him, and is so timid that he takes everybody for Cerberus, even you and me,—that is his "politeness."
paras.uz: 237. Xushmuomala odam. — «U shunchalik xushmuomala!» — Ha, uning yonida doimo Serber uchun bir bo'lak non bor va u shunchalik qo'rqoqki, hammani, hatto sizni ham, meni ham Serber deb biladi, — uning «xushmuomalaligi» shu.

paras.en: 238. Without Envy. — He is wholly without envy, but there is no merit therein: for he wants to conquer a land which no one has yet possessed and hardly any one has even seen.
paras.uz: 238. Hasadsiz. — U butunlay hasadsiz, lekin bunda xizmat yo'q: chunki u hali hech kim egalik qilmagan va deyarli hech kim ko'rmagan yerni zabt etmoqchi.

paras.en: 239. The Joyless Person. — A single joyless person is enough to make constant displeasure and a clouded heaven in a household; and it is only by a miracle that such a person is lacking!—Happiness is not nearly such a contagious disease;—how is that!
paras.uz: 239. Quvonchsiz odam. — Uyda doimiy norozilik va bulutli osmon bo'lishi uchun bitta quvonchsiz odam kifoya; va faqat mo''jiza tufayligina bunday odam yo'q bo'ladi! — Baxt unchalik yuqumli kasallik emas; — bu qanday!

paras.en: 240. On the Sea-Shore. — I would not build myself a house (it is an element of my happiness not to be a house-owner!). If I had to do so, however, I should build it, like many of the Romans, right into the sea,—I should like to have some secrets in common with that beautiful monster.
paras.uz: 240. Dengiz qirg'og'ida. — Men o'zimga uy qurmagan bo'lardim (uy egasi bo'lmaslik baxtimning bir unsuri!). Biroq agar qurishim kerak bo'lsa, uni ko'p rimliklar kabi to'g'ri dengizning ichiga qurardim, — o'sha go'zal mahluq bilan ba'zi umumiy sirlarim bo'lishini istardim.

paras.en: 241. Work and Artist. — This artist is ambitious and nothing more; ultimately, however, his work is only a magnifying glass, which he offers to every one who looks in his direction.
paras.uz: 241. Asar va san'atkor. — Bu san'atkor shuhratparast va boshqa hech narsa emas; biroq oxir-oqibat uning asari faqat lupa, u uni o'z tomoniga qaragan har kimga taklif qiladi.

paras.en: 242. Suum cuique. — However great be my greed of knowledge, I cannot appropriate aught of things but what already belongs to me,—the property of others still remains in the things. How is it possible for a man to be a thief or a robber!
paras.uz: 242. Suum cuique — Har kimga o'ziniki. — Bilimga bo'lgan ochko'zligim qanchalik katta bo'lmasin, narsalardan allaqachon menga tegishli bo'lgan narsadan boshqasini o'zlashtira olmayman, — boshqalarning mulki narsalarda qoladi. Qanday qilib odam o'g'ri yoki qaroqchi bo'lishi mumkin!

paras.en: 243. Origin of "Good" and "Bad.". — He only will devise an improvement who can feel that "this is not good."
paras.uz: 243. «Yaxshi» va «yomon»ning kelib chiqishi. — Faqat «bu yaxshi emas» deb his qila oladigan odamgina yaxshilanish o'ylab topadi.

paras.en: 244. Thoughts and Words. — Even our thoughts we are unable to render completely in words.
paras.uz: 244. Fikrlar va so'zlar. — Hatto fikrlarimizni ham so'z bilan to'liq ifodalay olmaymiz.

paras.en: 245. Praise in Choice. — The artist chooses his subjects; that is his mode of praising.
paras.uz: 245. Tanlashdagi maqtov. — San'atkor o'z mavzularini tanlaydi; bu uning maqtash usuli.

paras.en: 246. Mathematics. — We want to carry the refinement and rigour of mathematics into all the sciences, as far as it is in any way possible, not in the belief that we shall apprehend things in this way, but in order thereby to assert our human relation to things. Mathematics is only a means to general and ultimate human knowledge.
paras.uz: 246. Matematika. — Biz matematikaning nozikligi va qat'iyligini iloji boricha barcha fanlarga olib kirmoqchimiz, shu tarzda narsalarni anglaymiz degan ishonch bilan emas, balki shu orqali narsalarga insoniy munosabatimizni tasdiqlash uchun. Matematika — umumiy va oxirgi inson bilimiga vosita, xolos.

paras.en: 247. Habits. — All habits make our hand wittier and our wit unhandier.
paras.uz: 247. Odatlar. — Barcha odatlar qo'limizni zukkoroq, zukkoligimizni esa qo'lsizroq qiladi.

paras.en: 248. Books. — Of what account is a book that never carries us away beyond all books!
paras.uz: 248. Kitoblar. — Bizni hech qachon barcha kitoblardan narida olib ketmaydigan kitobning nima qadri bor!

paras.en: 249. The Sigh of the Seeker of Knowledge. — "Oh, my covetousness! In this soul there is no disinterestedness—but an all-desiring self, which, by means of many individuals, would fain see as with its own eyes, and grasp as with its own hands—a self bringing back even the entire past, and wanting to lose nothing that could in any way belong to it! Oh, this flame of my covetousness! Oh, that I were reincarnated in a hundred individuals!"—He who does not know this sigh by experience, does not know the passion of the seeker of knowledge either.
paras.uz: 249. Bilim izlovchining xo'rsinishi. — «Oh, mening ochko'zligim! Bu ruhda manfaatsizlik yo'q — balki hamma narsani istovchi «men» bor, u ko'plab shaxslar orqali go'yo o'z ko'zlari bilan ko'rishni va o'z qo'llari bilan ushlashni xohlaydi — hatto butun o'tmishni qaytarib keladigan va qandaydir tarzda unga tegishli bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan hech narsani yo'qotishni istamaydigan «men»! Oh, ochko'zligimning bu alangasi! Oh, qaniydi yuzta shaxsda qayta tug'ilsam!» — Bu xo'rsinishni tajribadan bilmaydigan odam bilim izlovchining ehtirosini ham bilmaydi.

paras.en: 250. Guilt. — Although the most intelligent judges of the witches, and even the witches themselves, were convinced of the guilt of witchcraft, the guilt, nevertheless, was not there. So it is with all guilt.
paras.uz: 250. Ayb. — Jodugarlarning eng aqlli hakamlari, hatto jodugarlarning o'zlari ham jodugarlik aybiga amin bo'lsalar ham, baribir ayb yo'q edi. Har qanday ayb bilan ham shunday.

paras.en: 251. Misunderstood Sufferers. — Great natures suffer otherwise than their worshippers imagine; they suffer most severely from the ignoble, petty emotions of certain evil moments; in short, from doubt of their own greatness;—not however from the sacrifices and martyrdoms which their tasks require of them. As long as Prometheus sympathises with men and sacrifices himself for them, he is happy and proud in himself; but on becoming envious of Zeus and of the homage which mortals pay him—then Prometheus suffers!
paras.uz: 251. Noto'g'ri tushunilgan azob chekuvchilar. — Buyuk tabiatlar ularning muxlislari tasavvur qilganidan boshqacha azob chekadi; ular eng qattiq ba'zi yomon lahzalarning pastkash, mayda his-tuyg'ularidan azob chekadi; qisqasi, o'z buyukligiga shubhadan; — biroq vazifalari ulardan talab qiladigan qurbonliklar va shahidliklardan emas. Prometey odamlarga hamdardlik qilib, ular uchun o'zini qurbon qilar ekan, u o'zida baxtli va mag'rur; lekin Zevsga va bandalar unga ko'rsatadigan hurmatga hasad qila boshlaganda — o'shanda Prometey azob chekadi!

paras.en: 252. Better to be in Debt. — "Better to remain in debt than to pay with money which does not bear our stamp!"—that is what our sovereignty prefers.
paras.uz: 252. Qarzdor bo'lgan yaxshiroq. — «Bizning muhrimiz bo'lmagan pul bilan to'lagandan ko'ra qarzdor qolgan yaxshiroq!» — hukmronligimiz shuni afzal ko'radi.

paras.en: 253. Always at Home. — One day we attain our goal—and then refer with pride to the long journeys we have made to reach it. In truth, we did not notice that we travelled. We got into the habit of thinking that we were at home in every place.
paras.uz: 253. Doimo uyda. — Bir kun maqsadimizga erishamiz — va keyin unga yetish uchun qilgan uzoq sayohatlarimizni faxr bilan tilga olamiz. Aslida biz sayohat qilayotganimizni sezmadik. Biz har bir joyda uydamiz deb o'ylashga odatlanib qolgandik.

paras.en: 254. Against Embarrassment. — He who is always thoroughly occupied is rid of all embarrassment.
paras.uz: 254. Xijolatga qarshi. — Doimo butunlay band bo'lgan odam har qanday xijolatdan xoli.

paras.en: 255. Imitators. — A: "What? You don't want to have imitators?" B: "I don't want people to do anything after me; I want every one to do something before himself (as a pattern to himself)—just as I do." A: "Consequently—?"
paras.uz: 255. Taqlidchilar. — A: «Nima? Siz taqlidchilaringiz bo'lishini istamaysizmi?» B: «Men odamlarning mendan keyin biror narsa qilishini istamayman; men har kim o'zi oldida (o'ziga namuna sifatida) nimadir qilishini istayman — xuddi men qilgandek». A: «Demak —?»

paras.en: 256. Skinniness. — All profound men have their happiness in imitating the flying-fish for once, and playing on the crests of the waves; they think that what is best of all in things is their surface: their skinniness—sit venia verbo.
paras.uz: 256. Yuzakilik. — Barcha chuqur odamlar baxtini bir marta uchuvchi baliqqa taqlid qilib, to'lqinlar cho'qqisida o'ynashda topadi; ular narsalardagi eng yaxshi narsa ularning yuzasi, terisi deb o'ylashadi — sit venia verbo — so'zim uchun kechirasiz.

paras.en: 257. From Experience. — A person often does not know how rich he is, until he learns from experience what rich men even play the thief on him.
paras.uz: 257. Tajribadan. — Odam ko'pincha qanchalik boy ekanini bilmaydi, toki tajribadan qanday boy odamlar ham uni o'g'irlashini bilib olmaguncha.

paras.en: 258. The Deniers of Chance. — No conqueror believes in chance.
paras.uz: 258. Tasodifni inkor etuvchilar. — Hech bir bosqinchi tasodifga ishonmaydi.

paras.en: 259. From Paradise. — "Good and Evil are God's prejudices"—said the serpent.
paras.uz: 259. Jannatdan. — «Yaxshilik va Yomonlik — Xudoning xurofotlari», — dedi ilon.

paras.en: 260. One times One. — One only is always in the wrong, but with two truth begins.—One only cannot prove himself right; but two are already beyond refutation.
paras.uz: 260. Bir karra bir. — Yolg'iz odam doimo nohaq, lekin ikkita bilan haqiqat boshlanadi. — Yolg'iz odam o'zining haqligini isbotlay olmaydi; lekin ikkitasi allaqachon rad etib bo'lmaydigan.

paras.en: 261. Originality. — What is originality? To see something that does not yet bear a name, that cannot yet be named, although it is before everybody's eyes. As people are usually constituted, it is the name that first makes a thing generally visible to them.—Original persons have also for the most part been the namers of things.
paras.uz: 261. O'ziga xoslik. — O'ziga xoslik nima? Hali nomi yo'q, hali nomlab bo'lmaydigan, garchi hammaning ko'z oldida bo'lsa ham, nimanidir ko'rish. Odamlar odatda shunday tuzilganki, narsani ularga umumiy ko'rinadigan qiladigan narsa avvalo nom. — O'ziga xos odamlar ko'pincha narsalarga nom qo'yuvchilar ham bo'lgan.

paras.en: 262. Sub specie aeterni. — A: "You withdraw faster and faster from the living; they will soon strike you out of their lists!"—B: "It is the only way to participate in the privilege of the dead." A: "In what privilege?"—B: "No longer having to die."
paras.uz: 262. Sub specie aeterni — Abadiyat nuqtai nazaridan. — A: «Siz tiriklardan tobora tezroq uzoqlashyapsiz; ular tez orada sizni ro'yxatlaridan o'chirib tashlashadi!» — B: «Bu o'liklarning imtiyozidan bahramand bo'lishning yagona yo'li». A: «Qanday imtiyoz?» — B: «Endi o'lishga to'g'ri kelmasligi».

paras.en: 263. Without Vanity. — When we love we want our defects to remain concealed,—not out of vanity, but lest the person loved should suffer therefrom. Indeed, the lover would like to appear as a God,—and not out of vanity either.
paras.uz: 263. Manmanliksiz. — Sevganimizda kamchiliklarimiz yashirin qolishini istaymiz, — manmanlikdan emas, balki sevgan odamimiz bundan azob chekmasligi uchun. Haqiqatan ham, oshiq xudo bo'lib ko'rinishni istaydi, — va bu ham manmanlikdan emas.

paras.en: 264. What we Do. — What we do is never understood, but only praised and blamed.
paras.uz: 264. Biz nima qilamiz. — Biz qiladigan ish hech qachon tushunilmaydi, faqat maqtaladi va qoralanadi.

paras.en: 265. Ultimate Scepticism. — But what after all are man's truths?—They are his irrefutable errors.
paras.uz: 265. So'nggi skeptitsizm. — Lekin oxir-oqibat insonning haqiqatlari nima? — Ular uning rad etib bo'lmaydigan xatolari.

paras.en: 266. Where Cruelty is Necessary. — He who is great is cruel to his second-rate virtues and judgments.
paras.uz: 266. Shafqatsizlik qayerda zarur. — Buyuk odam o'zining ikkinchi darajali fazilatlari va hukmlariga nisbatan shafqatsiz.

paras.en: 267. With a high Aim. — With a high aim a person is superior even to justice, and not only to his deeds and his judges.
paras.uz: 267. Yuksak maqsad bilan. — Yuksak maqsadi bo'lgan odam hatto adolatdan ham ustun, nafaqat o'z ishlari va hakamlaridan.

paras.en: 268. What makes Heroic?. — To face simultaneously one's greatest suffering and one's highest hope.
paras.uz: 268. Nima qahramon qiladi? — Bir vaqtning o'zida eng katta azobingga va eng yuksak umidingga yuzma-yuz turish.

paras.en: 269. What dost thou Believe in?. — In this: That the weights of all things must be determined anew.
paras.uz: 269. Sen nimaga ishonasan? — Shunga: barcha narsalarning og'irligi yangidan belgilanishi kerak.

paras.en: 270. What Saith thy Conscience?. — "Thou shalt become what thou art."
paras.uz: 270. Vijdoning nima deydi? — «Sen o'zing bo'lgan narsaga aylanishing kerak».

paras.en: 271. Where are thy Greatest Dangers?. — In pity.
paras.uz: 271. Eng katta xavfing qayerda? — Achinishda.

paras.en: 272. What dost thou Love in others?. — My hopes.
paras.uz: 272. Boshqalarda nimani sevasan? — Umidlarimni.

paras.en: 273. Whom dost thou call Bad?. — Him who always wants to put others to shame.
paras.uz: 273. Kimni yomon deysan? — Doimo boshqalarni sharmanda qilmoqchi bo'lgan odamni.

paras.en: 274. What dost thou think most humane?. — To spare a person shame.
paras.uz: 274. Eng insoniy narsa deb nimani bilasan? — Odamni uyatdan saqlashni.

paras.en: 275. What is the Seal of Liberty Attained?. — To be no longer ashamed of oneself.
paras.uz: 275. Erishilgan erkinlikning muhri nima? — Endi o'zingdan uyalmaslik.

chapters.recap_uz: Uchinchi kitob qisqa aforizmlar bilan tugaydi: hayvonlar insonni «kuladigan hayvon» deb biladi; o'ziga xoslik — nomsiz narsani ko'rish. Oxirgi savol-javoblar: «Vijdoning nima deydi? — Sen o'zing bo'lgan narsaga aylanishing kerak».

chapters.title: Amor fati

paras.en: 276. For the New Year. — I still live, I still think; I must still live, for I must still think. Sum, ergo cogito: cogito, ergo sum. To-day everyone takes the liberty of expressing his wish and his favourite thought: well, I also mean to tell what I have wished for myself to-day, and what thought first crossed my mind this year,—a thought which ought to be the basis, the pledge and the sweetening of all my future life! I want more and more to perceive the necessary characters in things as the beautiful:—I shall thus be one of those who beautify things. Amor fati: let that henceforth be my love! I do not want to wage war with the ugly. I do not want to accuse, I do not want even to accuse the accusers. Looking aside, let that be my sole negation! And all in all, to sum up: I wish to be at any time hereafter only a yea-sayer!
paras.uz: 276. Yangi yil uchun. — Men hali yashayapman, hali o'ylayapman; men hali yashashim kerak, chunki hali o'ylashim kerak. Sum, ergo cogito: cogito, ergo sum — Mavjudman, demak o'ylayman: o'ylayman, demak mavjudman. Bugun har kim o'z istagi va sevimli fikrini ifodalashga erk beradi: xo'sh, men ham bugun o'zim uchun nimani tilaganimni va bu yil xayolimga birinchi bo'lib qanday fikr kelganini aytmoqchiman, — butun kelajak hayotimning asosi, garovi va shirinligi bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan fikr! Men narsalardagi zaruriy xususiyatlarni go'zal deb tobora ko'proq idrok etishni istayman: — shunda men narsalarni go'zallashtiruvchilardan biri bo'laman. Amor fati — taqdirni sevish: bundan buyon bu mening sevgim bo'lsin! Men xunuk narsa bilan urush qilishni istamayman. Ayblashni istamayman, hatto ayblovchilarni ayblashni ham istamayman. Nigohni chetga burish — mening yagona inkorim shu bo'lsin! Va umuman olganda, qisqasi: men bundan buyon har qanday vaqtda faqat «ha» deyuvchi bo'lishni istayman!

paras.en: 277. Personal Providence. — There is a certain climax in life, at which, notwithstanding all our freedom, and however much we may have denied all directing reason and goodness in the beautiful chaos of existence, we are once more in great danger of intellectual bondage, and have to face our hardest test. For now the thought of a personal Providence first presents itself before us with its most persuasive force, and has the best of advocates, apparentness, in its favour, now when it is obvious that all and everything that happens to us always turns out for the best.
paras.uz: 277. Shaxsiy taqdir. — Hayotda shunday bir cho'qqi borki, unda barcha erkinligimizga qaramay va hayotning go'zal xaosida har qanday yo'naltiruvchi aql va yaxshilikni qanchalik inkor etgan bo'lmaylik, biz yana aqliy qullikning katta xavfi ostida bo'lamiz va eng og'ir sinovimizga duch kelamiz. Chunki endi shaxsiy taqdir haqidagi fikr bizning oldimizda eng ishonarli kuchi bilan birinchi marta namoyon bo'ladi va uning foydasiga eng yaxshi himoyachi — ayonlik bor, endi bizga sodir bo'ladigan hamma narsa va har bir narsa doimo yaxshilikka chiqishi ravshan bo'lganda.

paras.en: The life of every day and of every hour seems to be anxious for nothing else but always to prove this proposition anew; let it be what it will, bad or good weather, the loss of a friend, a sickness, a calumny, the non-receipt of a letter, the spraining of one's foot, a glance into a shop-window, a counter-argument, the opening of a book, a dream, a deception:—it shows itself immediately, or very soon afterwards as something "not permitted to be absent,"—it is full of profound significance and utility precisely for us! Is there a more dangerous temptation to rid ourselves of the belief in the Gods of Epicurus, those careless, unknown Gods, and believe in some anxious and mean Divinity, who knows personally every little hair on our heads, and feels no disgust in rendering the most wretched services?
paras.uz: Har kunning va har soatning hayoti go'yo shu da'voni doimo yangidan isbotlashdan boshqa hech narsaga intilmayotgandek; nima bo'lmasin, yomon yoki yaxshi ob-havo, do'stni yo'qotish, kasallik, tuhmat, xat kelmay qolishi, oyoqni burab olish, do'kon oynasiga bir qarash, qarshi dalil, kitob ochish, tush, aldanish: — u darhol yoki tez orada «yo'q bo'lishiga ruxsat etilmagan» narsa sifatida namoyon bo'ladi, — u aynan biz uchun chuqur ma'no va foydaga to'la! Epikurning xudolariga, o'sha beparvo, noma'lum xudolarga bo'lgan ishonchdan qutulib, boshimizdagi har bir tukni shaxsan biladigan va eng ayanchli xizmatlarni ko'rsatishdan jirkanmaydigan qandaydir tashvishli va pastkash ilohga ishonish uchun bundan xavfliroq vasvasa bormi?

paras.en: Well—I mean in spite of all this! we want to leave the Gods alone (and the serviceable genii likewise), and wish to content ourselves with the assumption that our own practical and theoretical skilfulness in explaining and suitably arranging events has now reached its highest point. We do not want either to think too highly of this dexterity of our wisdom, when the wonderful harmony which results from playing on our instrument sometimes surprises us too much: a harmony which sounds too well for us to dare to ascribe it to ourselves. In fact, now and then there is one who plays with us—beloved Chance: he leads our hand occasionally, and even the all-wisest Providence could not devise any finer music than that of which our foolish hand is then capable.
paras.uz: Xo'sh — men hamma narsaga qaramay demoqchiman! biz xudolarni tinch qo'ymoqchimiz (xizmatchi jinlarni ham) va voqealarni tushuntirish va mos ravishda tartibga solishdagi o'zimizning amaliy va nazariy mahoratimiz endi eng yuqori nuqtasiga yetgan degan faraz bilan qanoatlanmoqchimiz. Biz cholg'uimizda chalishdan kelib chiqadigan ajoyib uyg'unlik ba'zan bizni haddan tashqari hayratga solganda, donoligimizning bu epchilligi haqida ham haddan tashqari yuqori o'ylashni istamaymiz: uni o'zimizga nisbat berishga jur'at etish uchun haddan tashqari yaxshi yangraydigan uyg'unlik. Haqiqatan ham, vaqti-vaqti bilan biz bilan birga chaladigan kimdir bor — sevimli Tasodif: u ba'zan qo'limizni yetaklaydi va hatto eng dono taqdir ham ahmoq qo'limiz o'shanda qodir bo'lgan musiqadan go'zalroq musiqani o'ylab topa olmasdi.

paras.en: 278. The Thought of Death. — It gives me a melancholy happiness to live in the midst of this confusion of streets, of necessities, of voices: how much enjoyment, impatience and desire, how much thirsty life and drunkenness of life comes to light here every moment! And yet it will soon be so still for all these shouting, lively, life-loving people! How everyone's shadow, his gloomy travelling-companion stands behind him! It is always as in the last moment before the departure of an emigrant-ship: people have more than ever to say to one another, the hour presses, the ocean with its lonely silence waits impatiently behind all the noise—so greedy, so certain of its prey! And all, all, suppose that the past has been nothing, or a small matter, that the near future is everything: hence this haste, this crying, this self-deafening and self-overreaching!
paras.uz: 278. O'lim haqidagi fikr. — Ko'chalar, zaruratlar, ovozlarning bu chalkashligi o'rtasida yashash menga g'amgin baxt beradi: bu yerda har lahzada qancha zavq, sabrsizlik va istak, qancha tashna hayot va hayot mastligi yuzaga chiqadi! Va shunga qaramay bu qichqirayotgan, jonli, hayotni sevuvchi odamlarning hammasi uchun tez orada shunchalik jim bo'ladi! Har kimning soyasi, uning ma'yus yo'ldoshi orqasida qanday turibdi! Doimo muhojirlar kemasi jo'nab ketishidan oldingi oxirgi lahzadagidek: odamlarning bir-biriga aytadigan gapi har qachongidan ko'p, soat shoshiltiradi, yolg'iz sukunati bilan okean barcha shovqin ortida sabrsiz kutadi — shunchalik ochko'z, o'ljasiga shunchalik ishonchli! Va hamma, hamma o'tmish hech narsa yoki kichkina narsa bo'lgan, yaqin kelajak hamma narsa deb faraz qiladi: shuning uchun bu shoshqaloqlik, bu qichqiriq, o'zini kar qilish va o'zidan oshib ketish!

paras.en: Everyone wants to be foremost in this future,—and yet death and the stillness of death are the only things certain and common to all in this future! How strange that this sole thing that is certain and common to all, exercises almost no influence on men, and that they are the furthest from regarding themselves as the brotherhood of death! It makes me happy to see that men do not want to think at all of the idea of death! I would fain do something to make the idea of life even a hundred times more worthy of their attention.
paras.uz: Har kim bu kelajakda birinchi bo'lishni istaydi, — va shunga qaramay o'lim va o'lim sukunati bu kelajakda hamma uchun ishonchli va umumiy bo'lgan yagona narsa! Qanchalik g'alati, hamma uchun ishonchli va umumiy bo'lgan bu yagona narsa odamlarga deyarli hech qanday ta'sir ko'rsatmaydi va ular o'zlarini o'lim birodarligi deb hisoblashdan eng uzoqda! Odamlar o'lim g'oyasi haqida umuman o'ylashni istamasligini ko'rish meni baxtli qiladi! Men hayot g'oyasini ularning e'tiboriga yana yuz baravar munosibroq qilish uchun nimadir qilishni istardim.

paras.en: 279. Stellar Friendship. — We were friends, and have become strangers to each other. But this is as it ought to be, and we do not want either to conceal or obscure the fact, as if we had to be ashamed of it. We are two ships, each of which has its goal and its course; we may, to be sure, cross one another in our paths, and celebrate a feast together as we did before,—and then the gallant ships lay quietly in one harbour, and in one sunshine, so that it might have been thought they were already at their goal, and that they had had one goal.
paras.uz: 279. Yulduzli do'stlik. — Biz do'st edik va bir-birimizga begona bo'lib qoldik. Lekin bu shunday bo'lishi kerak va biz bu haqiqatni, go'yo undan uyalishimiz kerakdek, yashirishni yoki xiralashtirishni istamaymiz. Biz ikki kemamiz, ularning har birining o'z maqsadi va yo'li bor; albatta, yo'llarimizda bir-birimiz bilan kesishib, avvalgidek birga bayram qilishimiz mumkin, — o'shanda jasur kemalar bitta bandargohda va bitta quyosh ostida jimgina turardi, shunda ular allaqachon maqsadlariga yetgan va ularning bitta maqsadi bo'lgan deb o'ylash mumkin edi.

paras.en: But then the almighty strength of our tasks forced us apart once more into different seas and into different zones, and perhaps we shall never see one another again,—or perhaps we may see one another, but not know one another again; the different seas and suns have altered us! That we had to become strangers to one another is the law to which we are subject: just by that shall we become more sacred to one another! Just by that shall the thought of our former friendship become holier! There is probably some immense, invisible curve and stellar orbit in which our courses and goals, so widely different, may be comprehended as small stages of the way,—let us raise ourselves to this thought!
paras.uz: Lekin keyin vazifalarimizning qudratli kuchi bizni yana turli dengizlar va turli mintaqalarga ajratib yubordi va balki biz bir-birimizni boshqa hech qachon ko'rmaymiz, — yoki balki ko'ramiz, lekin bir-birimizni tanimaymiz; turli dengizlar va quyoshlar bizni o'zgartirib yubordi! Bir-birimizga begona bo'lishimiz kerakligi — biz bo'ysunadigan qonun: aynan shu bilan biz bir-birimiz uchun muqaddasroq bo'lamiz! Aynan shu bilan oldingi do'stligimiz haqidagi fikr muqaddasroq bo'ladi! Ehtimol, qandaydir ulkan, ko'rinmas egri chiziq va yulduz orbitasi bor, unda bizning shunchalik farq qiladigan yo'llarimiz va maqsadlarimiz yo'lning kichik bosqichlari sifatida o'z ichiga olinishi mumkin, — keling, o'zimizni shu fikrgacha ko'taraylik!

paras.en: But our life is too short, and our power of vision too limited for us to be more than friends in the sense of that sublime possibility.—And so we will believe in our stellar friendship, though we should have to be terrestrial enemies to one another.
paras.uz: Lekin hayotimiz haddan tashqari qisqa va ko'rish qobiliyatimiz haddan tashqari cheklangan, shuning uchun biz o'sha yuksak imkoniyat ma'nosida do'stlardan ko'proq bo'la olmaymiz. — Shunday qilib, biz yulduzli do'stligimizga ishonamiz, garchi bir-birimizga yerdagi dushman bo'lishimiz kerak bo'lsa ham.

paras.en: 280. Architecture for Thinkers. — An insight is needed (and that probably very soon) as to what is specially lacking in our great cities—namely, quiet, spacious, and widely extended places for reflection, places with long, lofty colonnades for bad weather, or for too sunny days, where no noise of wagons or of shouters would penetrate, and where a more refined propriety would prohibit loud praying even to the priest: buildings and situations which as a whole would express the sublimity of self-communion and seclusion from the world. The time is past when the Church possessed the monopoly of reflection, when the vita contemplativa had always in the first place to be the vita religiosa: and everything that the Church has built expresses this thought.
paras.uz: 280. Mutafakkirlar uchun me'morchilik. — Katta shaharlarimizda ayniqsa nima yetishmasligini tushunish kerak (va bu ehtimol juda tez orada): ya'ni mulohaza uchun sokin, keng va uzoqqa cho'zilgan joylar, yomon ob-havo yoki haddan tashqari quyoshli kunlar uchun uzun, baland ustunli ayvonlari bo'lgan joylar, u yerga aravalar yoki qichqiruvchilarning shovqini kirmasin va nozikroq odob hatto ruhoniyga ham baland ovozda ibodat qilishni taqiqlasin: umuman olganda o'zi bilan suhbatlashish va dunyodan xilvatlashishning yuksakligini ifodalaydigan binolar va joylar. Cherkov mulohazaga monopoliyaga ega bo'lgan, vita contemplativa — mulohazakor hayot doimo birinchi navbatda vita religiosa — diniy hayot bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan vaqt o'tdi: va cherkov qurgan hamma narsa shu fikrni ifodalaydi.

paras.en: I know not how we could content ourselves with their structures, even if they should be divested of their ecclesiastical purposes: these structures speak a far too pathetic and too biassed speech, as houses of God and places of splendour for supernatural intercourse, for us godless ones to be able to think our thoughts in them. We want to have ourselves translated into stone and plant, we want to go for a walk in ourselves when we wander in these halls and gardens.
paras.uz: Ularning binolari, hatto cherkov maqsadlaridan xoli qilinsa ham, qanday qilib ular bilan qanoatlana olishimizni bilmayman: bu binolar Xudoning uylari va g'ayritabiiy muloqot uchun ulug'vorlik joylari sifatida haddan tashqari pafosli va haddan tashqari tarafkash tilda gapiradi, biz xudosizlar ularda o'z fikrlarimizni o'ylay olishimiz uchun. Biz o'zimizni tosh va o'simlikka tarjima qilmoqchimiz, bu zallar va bog'larda kezganimizda o'zimizda sayr qilmoqchimiz.

paras.en: 281. Knowing how to Find the End. — Masters of the first rank are recognised by knowing in a perfect manner how to find the end, in the whole as well as in the part; be it the end of a melody or of a thought, be it the fifth act of a tragedy or of a state affair. The masters of the second degree always become restless towards the end, and seldom dip down into the sea with such proud, quiet equilibrium as, for example, the mountain-ridge at Porto fino—where the Bay of Genoa sings its melody to an end.
paras.uz: 281. Oxirini topa bilish. — Birinchi darajali ustalar butunda ham, qismda ham oxirini mukammal tarzda topa bilishlari bilan taniladi; xoh kuyning yoki fikrning oxiri bo'lsin, xoh tragediya yoki davlat ishining beshinchi pardasi bo'lsin. Ikkinchi darajali ustalar oxirga yaqin doimo bezovtalanadi va kamdan-kam hollarda dengizga shunday mag'rur, sokin muvozanat bilan sho'ng'iydi, masalan, Portofinodagi tog' tizmasi kabi — u yerda Genuya ko'rfazi o'z kuyini oxirigacha kuylaydi.

paras.en: 282. The Gait. — There are mannerisms of the intellect by which even great minds betray that they originate from the populace, or from the semi-populace:—it is principally the gait and step of their thoughts which betray them; they cannot walk. It was thus that even Napoleon, to his profound chagrin, could not walk "legitimately" and in princely fashion on occasions when it was necessary to do so properly, as in great coronation processions and on similar occasions: even there he was always just the leader of a column—proud and brusque at the same time, and very self-conscious of it all.—It is something laughable to see those writers who make the folding robes of their periods rustle around them: they want to cover their feet.
paras.uz: 282. Yurish. — Aqlning shunday qiliqlari borki, ular bilan hatto buyuk aqllar ham oddiy xalqdan yoki yarim oddiy xalqdan kelib chiqqanini oshkor qiladi: — ularni asosan fikrlarining yurishi va qadami oshkor qiladi; ular yura olmaydi. Hatto Napoleon ham chuqur iztirob bilan buni to'g'ri qilish kerak bo'lgan paytlarda, masalan, buyuk toj kiyish yurishlarida va shunga o'xshash holatlarda «qonuniy» va shahzodalarcha yura olmagan: hatto u yerda ham u doimo shunchaki kolonna boshlig'i edi — bir vaqtning o'zida mag'rur va keskin, va bularning hammasini juda yaxshi anglagan holda. — Davrlarining burmali liboslarini atroflarida shitirlatadigan yozuvchilarni ko'rish kulgili: ular oyoqlarini yashirmoqchi.

paras.en: 283. Pioneers. — I greet all the signs indicating that a more manly and warlike age is commencing, which will, above all, bring heroism again into honour! For it has to prepare the way for a yet higher age, and gather the force which the latter will one day require,—the age which will carry heroism into knowledge, and wage war for the sake of ideas and their consequences.
paras.uz: 283. Kashshoflar. — Men erkakonaroq va jangovarroq davr boshlanayotganini ko'rsatadigan barcha belgilarni olqishlayman, u eng avvalo qahramonlikni yana sharafga qaytaradi! Chunki u yana ham yuksakroq davrga yo'l tayyorlashi va bir kun kelib ikkinchisiga kerak bo'ladigan kuchni yig'ishi kerak, — qahramonlikni bilimga olib kiradigan va g'oyalar va ularning oqibatlari uchun urush olib boradigan davr.

paras.en: For that end many brave pioneers are now needed, who, however, cannot originate out of nothing,—and just as little out of the sand and slime of present-day civilisation and the culture of great cities: men silent, solitary and resolute, who know how to be content and persistent in invisible activity: men who with innate disposition seek in all things that which is to be overcome in them: men to whom cheerfulness, patience, simplicity, and contempt of the great vanities belong just as much as do magnanimity in victory and indulgence to the trivial vanities of all the vanquished: men with an acute and independent judgment regarding all victors, and concerning the part which chance has played in the winning of victory and fame: men with their own holidays, their own work-days, and their own periods of mourning; accustomed to command with perfect assurance, and equally ready, if need be, to obey, proud in the one case as in the other, equally serving their own interests: men more imperilled, more productive, more happy!
paras.uz: Buning uchun hozir ko'p jasur kashshoflar kerak, biroq ular hech narsadan paydo bo'la olmaydi, — hozirgi tsivilizatsiya va katta shaharlar madaniyatining qumi va shilimshig'idan ham xuddi shunday kam: jim, yolg'iz va qat'iy odamlar, ko'rinmas faoliyatda qanoatli va sabotli bo'lishni biladiganlar: tug'ma moyillik bilan barcha narsalarda ularda yengilishi kerak bo'lgan narsani izlaydiganlar: quvnoqlik, sabr, soddalik va katta behudaliklarga nafrat ular uchun g'alabadagi saxiylik va barcha mag'lublarning mayda behudaliklariga muruvvat kabi tegishli odamlar: barcha g'oliblar va g'alaba va shon-shuhrat qozonishda tasodif o'ynagan rol haqida o'tkir va mustaqil hukmga ega odamlar: o'zlarining bayramlari, o'zlarining ish kunlari va o'zlarining motam davrlari bilan; to'liq ishonch bilan buyurishga odatlangan va kerak bo'lsa, xuddi shunday bo'ysunishga tayyor, birida ham, boshqasida ham mag'rur, ikkalasida ham o'z manfaatlariga xizmat qiladigan odamlar: ko'proq xavf ostidagi, samaraliroq, baxtliroq odamlar!

paras.en: For believe me!—the secret of realising the largest productivity and the greatest enjoyment of existence is to live in danger! Build your cities on the slope of Vesuvius! Send your ships into unexplored seas! Live in war with your equals and with yourselves! Be robbers and spoilers, ye knowing ones, as long as ye cannot be rulers and possessor! The time will soon pass when you can be satisfied to live like timorous deer concealed in the forests. Knowledge will finally stretch out her hand for that which belongs to her:—she means to rule and possess, and you with her!
paras.uz: Chunki menga ishoning! — hayotning eng katta samaradorligi va eng katta zavqini amalga oshirishning siri — xavf ostida yashash! Shaharlaringizni Vezuviy yonbag'rida quring! Kemalaringizni o'rganilmagan dengizlarga yuboring! O'zingizga tenglar va o'zingiz bilan urushda yashang! Bilimdonlar, hukmdor va egalar bo'la olmas ekansiz, qaroqchi va talonchi bo'linglar! O'rmonlarda yashiringan qo'rqoq kiyiklardek yashash bilan qanoatlana oladigan vaqt tez o'tib ketadi. Bilim oxir-oqibat o'ziga tegishli narsaga qo'lini cho'zadi: — u hukmronlik qilmoqchi va egalik qilmoqchi, siz ham u bilan birga!

paras.en: 284. Belief in Oneself. — In general, few men have belief in themselves:—and of those few some are endowed with it as a useful blindness or partial obscuration of intellect (what would they perceive if they could see to the bottom of themselves!). The others must first acquire the belief for themselves: everything good, clever, or great that they do, is first of all an argument against the sceptic that dwells in them: the question is how to convince or persuade this sceptic, and for that purpose genius almost is needed. They are signally dissatisfied with themselves.
paras.uz: 284. O'ziga ishonch. — Umuman olganda, o'ziga ishonadigan odamlar kam: — va o'sha ozchilikning ba'zilari bu ishonchga foydali ko'rlik yoki aqlning qisman xiralashishi sifatida ega (agar o'zlarining tubigacha ko'ra olsalar, nimani ko'rishardi!). Boshqalar avval bu ishonchni o'zlari uchun orttirishlari kerak: ular qiladigan har bir yaxshi, aqlli yoki buyuk ish avvalo ularning ichida yashaydigan skeptikka qarshi dalil: savol bu skeptikni qanday ishontirish yoki ko'ndirishda va buning uchun deyarli daho kerak. Ular o'zlaridan juda norozi.

paras.en: 285. Excelsior!. — "Thou wilt never more pray, never more worship, never more repose in infinite trust—thou refusest to stand still and dismiss thy thoughts before an ultimate wisdom, an ultimate virtue, an ultimate power,—thou hast no constant guardian and friend in thy seven solitudes—thou livest without the outlook on a mountain that has snow on its head and fire in its heart—there is no longer any requiter for thee, nor any amender with his finishing touch—there is no longer any reason in that which happens, or any love in that which will happen to thee—there is no longer any resting-place for thy weary heart, where it has only to find and no longer to seek, thou art opposed to any kind of ultimate peace, thou desirest the eternal recurrence of war and peace:—man of renunciation, wilt thou renounce in all these things? Who will give thee the strength to do so?
paras.uz: 285. Excelsior! — Yanada yuqoriga! — «Sen endi hech qachon ibodat qilmaysan, hech qachon sajda qilmaysan, hech qachon cheksiz ishonchda orom olmaysan — sen oliy donolik, oliy fazilat, oliy kuch oldida to'xtab, fikrlaringni bo'shatishni rad etasan, — yetti yolg'izligingda doimiy qo'riqchi va do'sting yo'q — sen boshida qor, yuragida olov bo'lgan tog'ga qarash imkonisiz yashaysan — endi sen uchun mukofotlovchi ham, oxirgi tegishi bilan tuzatuvchi ham yo'q — sodir bo'ladigan narsada endi aql yo'q, senga sodir bo'ladigan narsada sevgi yo'q — charchagan yuraging uchun endi faqat topishi kerak bo'lgan va endi izlashi shart bo'lmagan dam olish joyi yo'q, sen har qanday oxirgi tinchlikka qarshisan, sen urush va tinchlikning abadiy qaytishini istaysan: — voz kechish odami, sen bularning hammasidan voz kechasanmi? Senga bunga kim kuch beradi?

paras.en: No one has yet had this strength!"—There is a lake which one day refused to flow away, and threw up a dam at the place where it had hitherto flowed away: since then this lake has always risen higher and higher. Perhaps the very renunciation will also furnish us with the strength with which the renunciation itself can be borne; perhaps man will ever rise higher and higher from that point onward, when he no longer flows out into a God.
paras.uz: Hali hech kimda bu kuch bo'lmagan!» — Bir ko'l bor, u bir kun oqib ketishni rad etib, shu paytgacha oqib ketgan joyida to'g'on ko'tardi: o'shandan beri bu ko'l doimo tobora balandroq ko'tarilmoqda. Balki aynan voz kechish bizga voz kechishning o'zini ko'tarish mumkin bo'lgan kuchni ham berar; balki inson Xudoga oqib ketmay qo'ygan nuqtadan boshlab doimo tobora balandroq ko'tarilar.

paras.en: 286. A Digression. — Here are hopes; but what will you see and hear of them, if you have not experienced glance and glow and dawn of day in your own souls? I can only suggest—I cannot do more! To move the stones, to make animals men—would you have me do that? Alas, if you are yet stones and animals, seek first your Orpheus!
paras.uz: 286. Chetga chiqish. — Mana umidlar; lekin agar o'z qalblaringizda nigoh, yorqinlik va tong otishini boshdan kechirmagan bo'lsangiz, ulardan nimani ko'rasiz va eshitasiz? Men faqat ishora qila olaman — bundan ortig'ini qila olmayman! Toshlarni qimirlatish, hayvonlarni odamga aylantirish — buni qilishimni istaysizmi? Afsus, agar siz hali tosh va hayvon bo'lsangiz, avval o'z Orfeyingizni izlang!

paras.en: 287. Love of Blindness. — "My thoughts," said the wanderer to his shadow, "ought to show me where I stand, but they should not betray to me whither I go. I love ignorance of the future, and do not want to come to grief by impatience and anticipatory tasting of promised things."
paras.uz: 287. Ko'rlikni sevish. — «Fikrlarim, — dedi sayyoh soyasiga, — menga qayerda turganimni ko'rsatishi kerak, lekin qayerga ketayotganimni oshkor qilmasligi kerak. Men kelajakni bilmaslikni sevaman va sabrsizlik va va'da qilingan narsalarni oldindan tatib ko'rish bilan halok bo'lishni istamayman».
