chapters.recap_uz: To'rtinchi kitob — «Sanctus Januarius» — Yangi yil tilagi bilan boshlanadi: zarur narsani go'zal deb ko'rish, faqat «ha» deyuvchi bo'lish. O'lim haqidagi fikr, «yulduzli do'stlik», mutafakkirlar uchun me'morchilik va «xavf ostida yashang!» chaqirig'i.

chapters.title: Aboard ship, philosophers!

paras.en: 288. Lofty Moods. — It seems to me that most men do not believe in lofty moods, unless it be for the moment, or at the most for a quarter of an hour,—except the few who know by experience a longer duration of high feeling. But to be absolutely a man with a single lofty feeling, the incarnation of a single lofty mood—that has hitherto been only a dream and an enchanting possibility: history does not yet give us any trustworthy example of it. Nevertheless it could some day produce such men also—when a multitude of favourable conditions have been created and established, which at present even the happiest chance is unable to throw together. Perhaps that very state which has hitherto entered into our soul as an exception, felt with horror now and then, may be the usual condition of those future souls: a continuous movement between high and low, and the feeling of high and low, a constant state of mounting as on steps, and at the same time reposing as on clouds.
paras.uz: 288. Yuksak kayfiyatlar. — Menimcha, ko'pchilik odamlar yuksak kayfiyatlarga ishonmaydi, faqat bir lahzaga yoki nari borsa chorak soatga bo'lmasa, — yuksak tuyg'uning uzoqroq davomiyligini tajribadan biladigan ozchilikdan tashqari. Lekin mutlaqo yagona yuksak tuyg'uli odam, yagona yuksak kayfiyatning timsoli bo'lish — bu shu paytgacha faqat orzu va maftunkor imkoniyat bo'lgan: tarix bizga hali bunga ishonchli misol bermaydi. Shunga qaramay u bir kun kelib bunday odamlarni ham yetishtirishi mumkin — hozir hatto eng baxtli tasodif ham birga to'play olmaydigan ko'plab qulay sharoitlar yaratilib, mustahkamlanganda. Balki shu paytgacha qalbimizga istisno sifatida kirgan, vaqti-vaqti bilan dahshat bilan his qilingan aynan o'sha holat o'sha kelajak qalblarining odatiy holati bo'lar: baland va past o'rtasidagi uzluksiz harakat, baland va past tuyg'usi, go'yo zinapoyalardan doimo ko'tarilish va shu bilan birga go'yo bulutlarda orom olish holati.

paras.en: 289. Aboard Ship!. — When one considers how a full philosophical justification of his mode of living and thinking operates upon every individual—namely, as a warming, blessing, and fructifying sun, specially shining on him; how it makes him independent of praise and blame, self-sufficient, rich and generous in the bestowal of happiness and kindness; how it unceasingly transforms the evil to the good, brings all the energies to bloom and maturity, and altogether hinders the growth of the greater and lesser weeds of chagrin and discontent:—one at last cries out importunately: Oh, that many such new suns were created! The evil man, also, the unfortunate man, and the exceptional man, shall each have his philosophy, his rights, and his sunshine!
paras.uz: 289. Kemaga chiqinglar! — Odamning turmush va fikrlash tarzining to'liq falsafiy oqlanishi har bir shaxsga qanday ta'sir qilishini o'ylaganda — ya'ni unga alohida porlaydigan isituvchi, duo qiluvchi va samara beruvchi quyosh sifatida; u uni maqtov va qoralashdan qanday mustaqil, o'zi-o'ziga yetarli, baxt va mehribonlik ulashishda boy va saxiy qilishini; u yomonlikni qanday tinimsiz yaxshilikka aylantirib, barcha kuchlarni gullash va yetuklikka olib kelishini va qayg'u va norozilikning katta-kichik begona o'tlarining o'sishiga umuman to'sqinlik qilishini o'ylaganda: — odam oxir-oqibat qat'iyat bilan xitob qiladi: Oh, qaniydi shunday ko'p yangi quyoshlar yaratilsa! Yovuz odam ham, baxtsiz odam ham va istisno odam ham har biri o'z falsafasiga, o'z huquqlariga va o'z quyosh nuriga ega bo'lsin!

paras.en: It is not sympathy with them that is necessary!—we must unlearn this arrogant fancy, notwithstanding that humanity has so long learned it and used it exclusively—we have not to set up any confessor, exorcist, or pardoner for them! It is a new justice, however, that is necessary! And a new solution! And new philosophers! The moral earth also is round! The moral earth also has its antipodes! The antipodes also have their right to exist! there is still another world to discover—and more than one! Aboard ship! ye philosophers!
paras.uz: Ularga hamdardlik kerak emas! — biz bu takabbur xayolni, insoniyat uni shunchalik uzoq o'rgangan va faqat uni ishlatgan bo'lsa ham, unutishimiz kerak — biz ular uchun hech qanday iqror oluvchi, jin quvuvchi yoki gunohni kechiruvchi o'rnatmasligimiz kerak! Biroq yangi adolat kerak! Va yangi yechim! Va yangi faylasuflar! Axloqiy yer ham dumaloq! Axloqiy yerning ham antipodlari bor! Antipodlarning ham mavjud bo'lish huquqi bor! hali kashf etiladigan boshqa dunyo bor — va bittadan ko'proq! Kemaga chiqinglar! ey faylasuflar!

paras.en: 290. One Thing is Needful. — To "give style" to one's character—that is a grand and a rare art! He who surveys all that his nature presents in its strength and in its weakness, and then fashions it into an ingenious plan, until everything appears artistic and rational, and even the weaknesses enchant the eye—exercises that admirable art. Here there has been a great amount of second nature added, there a portion of first nature has been taken away:—in both cases with long exercise and daily labour at the task. Here the ugly, which does not permit of being taken away, has been concealed, there it has been re-interpreted into the sublime. Much of the vague, which refuses to take form, has been reserved and utilised for the perspectives:—it is meant to give a hint of the remote and immeasurable.
paras.uz: 290. Bitta narsa kerak. — O'z xarakteriga «uslub berish» — bu buyuk va kamyob san'at! O'z tabiati kuchi va zaifligida taqdim etadigan hamma narsani ko'zdan kechirib, keyin uni mohirona rejaga shakllantiradigan, toki hamma narsa badiiy va aqlli ko'rinsin, hatto zaifliklar ham ko'zni maftun etsin — o'sha odam bu ajoyib san'atni bajaradi. Bu yerda ko'p ikkinchi tabiat qo'shilgan, u yerda birinchi tabiatning bir qismi olib tashlangan: — ikkala holatda ham uzoq mashq va vazifa ustida kundalik mehnat bilan. Bu yerda olib tashlashga imkon bermaydigan xunuk narsa yashirilgan, u yerda u yuksaklikka qayta talqin qilingan. Shakl olishni rad etadigan noaniq narsaning ko'p qismi saqlanib, istiqbollar uchun ishlatilgan: — u uzoq va o'lchab bo'lmas narsaga ishora berish uchun mo'ljallangan.

paras.en: In the end, when the work has been completed, it is revealed how it was the constraint of the same taste that organised and fashioned it in whole or in part: whether the taste was good or bad is of less importance than one thinks,—it is sufficient that it was a taste!—It will be the strong imperious natures which experience their most refined joy in such constraint, in such confinement and perfection under their own law; the passion of their violent volition lessens at the sight of all disciplined nature, all conquered and ministering nature: even when they have palaces to build and gardens to lay out, it is not to their taste to allow nature to be free.—It is the reverse with weak characters who have not power over themselves, and hate the restriction of style: they feel that if this repugnant constraint were laid upon them, they would necessarily become vulgarised under it: they become slaves as soon as they serve, they hate service.
paras.uz: Oxirida, ish tugagach, uni butunlay yoki qisman tashkil etgan va shakllantirgan narsa bir xil didning majburlovi ekani ochiladi: did yaxshi yoki yomon bo'lgani odamlar o'ylaganidan kamroq ahamiyatga ega, — bu did bo'lgani kifoya! — Bunday majburlovda, o'z qonuni ostidagi bunday cheklanish va mukammallikda eng nozik quvonchni his qiladiganlar kuchli, hukmron tabiatlar bo'ladi; ularning shiddatli irodasi ehtirosi har qanday intizomli tabiatni, har qanday zabt etilgan va xizmat qiluvchi tabiatni ko'rganda kamayadi: hatto ular saroylar qurishi va bog'lar barpo etishi kerak bo'lganda ham, tabiatni erkin qo'yish ularning didiga to'g'ri kelmaydi. — O'zlari ustidan hokimiyati bo'lmagan va uslub cheklovidan nafratlanadigan zaif xarakterlarda esa aksincha: ular his qilishadiki, agar bu jirkanch majburlov ularga yuklansa, ular uning ostida muqarrar ravishda qo'pollashardi: ular xizmat qilishi bilanoq qulga aylanadi, ular xizmatdan nafratlanadi.

paras.en: Such intellects—they may be intellects of the first rank—are always concerned with fashioning or interpreting themselves and their surroundings as free nature—wild, arbitrary, fantastic, confused and surprising: and it is well for them to do so, because only in this manner can they please themselves! For one thing is needful: namely, that man should attain to satisfaction with himself—be it but through this or that fable and artifice: it is only then that man's aspect is at all endurable! He who is dissatisfied with himself is ever ready to avenge himself on that account: we others will be his victims, if only in having always to endure his ugly aspect. For the aspect of the ugly makes one mean and sad.
paras.uz: Bunday aqllar — ular birinchi darajali aqllar bo'lishi mumkin — doimo o'zlarini va atroflarini erkin tabiat sifatida — yovvoyi, o'zboshimcha, xayoliy, chalkash va hayratlanarli qilib shakllantirish yoki talqin qilish bilan band: va ular uchun shunday qilish yaxshi, chunki faqat shu tarzda ular o'zlarini mamnun qila oladi! Chunki bitta narsa kerak: ya'ni inson o'zidan mamnunlikka erishishi kerak — xoh u yoki bu afsona va hiyla orqali bo'lsin: faqat shundagina insonning qiyofasiga umuman chidash mumkin! O'zidan norozi odam shuning uchun doimo qasos olishga tayyor: biz boshqalar uning qurbonlari bo'lamiz, hech bo'lmasa doimo uning xunuk qiyofasiga chidashimiz kerakligi bilan. Chunki xunuk narsaning qiyofasi odamni pastkash va g'amgin qiladi.

paras.en: 291. Genoa. — I have looked upon this city, its villas and pleasure-grounds and the wide circuit of its inhabited heights and slopes, for a considerable time: in the end I must say that I see countenances out of past generations,—this district is strewn with the images of bold and autocratic men. They have lived and have wanted to live on—they say so with their houses, built and decorated for centuries, and not for the passing hour: they were well disposed to life, however ill-disposed they may often have been towards themselves.
paras.uz: 291. Genuya. — Men bu shaharga, uning villalari va sayrgohlariga, odam yashaydigan tepaliklari va yonbag'irlarining keng doirasiga ancha vaqt qaradim: oxirida aytishim kerakki, o'tgan avlodlarning yuzlarini ko'ryapman, — bu o'lka dadil va mustabid odamlarning tasvirlari bilan sochilgan. Ular yashashgan va yashashda davom etishni istashgan — ular buni o'tkinchi soat uchun emas, asrlar uchun qurilgan va bezatilgan uylari bilan aytishadi: ular hayotga xayrixoh edi, o'zlariga nisbatan ko'pincha qanchalik noxush bo'lmasin.

paras.en: I always see the builder, how he casts his eye on all that is built around him far and near, and likewise on the city, the sea, and the chain of mountains; how he expresses power and conquest in his gaze: all this he wishes to fit into his plan, and in the end make it his property, by its becoming a portion of the same. The whole district is overgrown with this superb, insatiable egoism of the desire to possess and exploit; and as these men when abroad recognised no frontiers, and in their thirst for the new placed a new world beside the old, so also at home everyone rose up against everyone else, and devised some mode of expressing his superiority, and of placing between himself and his neighbour his personal illimitableness.
paras.uz: Men doimo quruvchini ko'raman, u atrofida, uzoq va yaqindagi barcha qurilgan narsalarga, shuningdek, shaharga, dengizga va tog' tizmasiga qanday nazar tashlaydi; u nigohida qudrat va zabt etishni qanday ifodalaydi: u bularning hammasini o'z rejasiga moslashtirmoqchi va oxirida uni o'sha rejaning bir qismiga aylantirib, o'z mulkiga aylantirmoqchi. Butun o'lka egalik qilish va foydalanish istagining bu ajoyib, to'ymas xudbinligi bilan o'sib ketgan; va bu odamlar chet elda hech qanday chegarani tan olmagani va yangilikka tashnaliklarida eskisining yoniga yangi dunyoni qo'yganlari kabi, uyda ham har kim har kimga qarshi ko'tarildi va o'z ustunligini ifodalash va o'zi bilan qo'shnisi o'rtasiga shaxsiy cheksizligini qo'yish usulini o'ylab topdi.

paras.en: Everyone won for himself his home once more by over-powering it with his architectural thoughts, and by transforming it into a delightful sight for his race. When we consider the mode of building cities in the north, the law and the general delight in legality and obedience, impose upon us: we thereby divine the propensity to equality and submission which must have ruled in those builders.
paras.uz: Har kim o'z uyini me'moriy fikrlari bilan bosib olib, uni o'z zoti uchun yoqimli manzaraga aylantirib, yana bir bor o'zi uchun qo'lga kiritdi. Shimolda shahar qurish usulini o'ylaganimizda, qonun va qonuniylik va itoatkorlikdan umumiy zavq bizga ta'sir qiladi: shu orqali biz o'sha quruvchilarda hukmron bo'lgan bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan tenglik va bo'ysunishga moyillikni sezamiz.

paras.en: Here, however, on turning every corner you find a man by himself, who knows the sea, knows adventure, and knows the Orient, a man who is averse to law and to neighbour, as if it bored him to have to do with them, a man who scans all that is already old and established, with envious glances: with a wonderful craftiness of fantasy, he would like, at least in thought, to establish all this anew, to lay his hand upon it, and introduce his meaning into it—if only for the passing hour of a sunny afternoon, when for once his insatiable and melancholy soul feels satiety, and when only what is his own, and nothing strange, may show itself to his eye.
paras.uz: Biroq bu yerda har bir muyulishdan burilganingizda dengizni biladigan, sarguzashtni biladigan va Sharqni biladigan, o'zicha yashaydigan odamni topasiz, qonun va qo'shnini yoqtirmaydigan, go'yo ular bilan ish ko'rish uni zeriktirgandek, allaqachon eski va o'rnatilgan hamma narsani hasadli nigohlar bilan ko'zdan kechiradigan odamni: fantaziyaning ajoyib ayyorligi bilan u bularning hammasini hech bo'lmasa fikrda yangidan o'rnatishni, unga qo'l qo'yishni va unga o'z ma'nosini kiritishni istardi — hatto quyoshli tushdan keyingi o'tkinchi soat uchun bo'lsa ham, o'shanda bir marta uning to'ymas va g'amgin qalbi to'qlikni his qiladi va uning ko'ziga faqat o'ziniki bo'lgan narsa, begona hech narsa ko'rinmasin.

paras.en: 292. To the Preachers of Morality. — I do not mean to moralise, but to those who do, I would give this advice: if you mean ultimately to deprive the best things and the best conditions of all honour and worth, continue to speak of them in the same way as heretofore! Put them at the head of your morality, and speak from morning till night of the happiness of virtue, of repose of soul, of righteousness, and of reward and punishment in the nature of things: according as you go on in this manner, all these good things will finally acquire a popularity and a street-cry for themselves: but then all the gold on them will also be worn off, and more besides: all the gold in them will have changed into lead. Truly, you understand the reverse art of alchemy, the depreciating of the most valuable things!
paras.uz: 292. Axloq va'zgo'ylariga. — Men axloq o'qimoqchi emasman, lekin buni qiladiganlarga shunday maslahat bergan bo'lardim: agar siz oxir-oqibat eng yaxshi narsalar va eng yaxshi holatlarni barcha sharaf va qadrdan mahrum qilmoqchi bo'lsangiz, ular haqida shu paytgacha qanday gapirgan bo'lsangiz, shunday gapirishda davom eting! Ularni axloqingizning boshiga qo'ying va ertalabdan kechgacha fazilat baxti, ruh osoyishtaligi, adolat va narsalar tabiatidagi mukofot va jazo haqida gapiring: shu tarzda davom etganingiz sari bu yaxshi narsalarning hammasi oxir-oqibat ommaboplik va ko'cha jarchisi qichqirig'iga ega bo'ladi: lekin o'shanda ulardagi butun oltin ham yemirilib ketadi, va undan ham ko'proq: ulardagi butun oltin qo'rg'oshinga aylangan bo'ladi. Haqiqatan ham, siz alkimyoning teskari san'atini — eng qimmatli narsalarni qadrsizlantirishni tushunasiz!

paras.en: Try, just for once, another recipe, in order not to realise as hitherto the opposite of what you mean to attain: deny those good things, withdraw from them the applause of the populace and discourage the spread of them, make them once more the concealed chastities of solitary souls, say that morality is something forbidden! Perhaps you will thus win over for those things the sort of men who are only of any account, I mean the heroic. But then there must be something formidable in them, and not as hitherto something disgusting! Might one not be inclined to say at present with reference to morality what Master Eckardt says: "I pray God to deliver me from God!"
paras.uz: Bir marta boshqa retseptni sinab ko'ring, toki shu paytgacha bo'lgani kabi erishmoqchi bo'lgan narsangizning aksini amalga oshirmang: bu yaxshi narsalarni inkor eting, ulardan olomon olqishini oling va ularning tarqalishiga to'sqinlik qiling, ularni yana yolg'iz qalblarning yashirin iffatlariga aylantiring, axloq taqiqlangan narsa deb ayting! Balki shu tarzda bu narsalar uchun faqat qadri bor odamlarni, ya'ni qahramonlarni qozonarsiz. Lekin o'shanda ularda shu paytgacha bo'lgani kabi jirkanch narsa emas, balki qo'rqinchli nimadir bo'lishi kerak! Hozir axloqqa nisbatan usta Ekxart aytgan narsani aytishga moyil bo'lmasmidik: «Xudodan meni Xudodan qutqarishini so'rayman!»

paras.en: 293. Our Atmosphere. — We know it well: to him who only casts a glance now and then at science, as in taking a walk (in the manner of women, and alas! also like many artists), the strictness in its service, its inexorability in small matters as well as in great, its rapidity in weighing, judging and condemning, produce something of a feeling of giddiness and fright. It is especially terrifying to him that the hardest is here demanded, that the best is done without the reward of praise or distinction; it is rather as among soldiers—almost nothing but blame and sharp reprimand is heard; for doing well prevails here as the rule, doing ill as the exception; the rule, however, has, here as everywhere, a silent tongue. It is the same with this "severity of science" as with the manners and politeness of the best society: it frightens the uninitiated.
paras.uz: 293. Bizning atmosferamiz. — Biz buni yaxshi bilamiz: ilmga faqat vaqti-vaqti bilan, go'yo sayr qilayotgandek nazar tashlaydigan odamga (ayollar kabi, afsus! ko'p san'atkorlar kabi ham) uning xizmatidagi qattiqlik, katta va kichik masalalardagi murosasizligi, tortish, hukm qilish va qoralashdagi tezligi qandaydir bosh aylanishi va qo'rquv tuyg'usini beradi. Uni ayniqsa bu yerda eng og'ir narsa talab qilinishi, eng yaxshi ish maqtov yoki farqlash mukofotisiz bajarilishi dahshatga soladi; bu ko'proq askarlar orasidagidek — deyarli faqat qoralash va keskin tanbeh eshitiladi; chunki bu yerda yaxshi ishlash qoida, yomon ishlash istisno sifatida hukmron; biroq qoida bu yerda ham, hamma joydagidek, jim tilga ega. Bu «ilmning qattiqligi» bilan eng yaxshi jamiyatning odobi va xushmuomalaligi bilan bo'lgani kabi: u bexabarlarni qo'rqitadi.

paras.en: He, however, who is accustomed to it, does not like to live anywhere but in this clear, transparent, powerful, and highly electrified atmosphere, this manly atmosphere. Anywhere else it is not pure and airy enough for him: he suspects that there his best art would neither be properly advantageous to anyone else, nor a delight to himself, that through misunderstandings half of his life would slip through his fingers, that much foresight, much concealment, and reticence would constantly be necessary,—nothing but great and useless losses of power! In this keen and clear element, however, he has his entire power: here he can fly! Why should he again go down into those muddy waters where he has to swim and wade and soil his wings!—No!
paras.uz: Biroq unga odatlangan odam bu tiniq, shaffof, qudratli va kuchli elektrlangan atmosferadan, bu erkakona atmosferadan boshqa hech qayerda yashashni yoqtirmaydi. Boshqa hamma joyda u uning uchun yetarlicha toza va havodor emas: u gumon qiladiki, u yerda uning eng yaxshi san'ati na boshqa birovga to'g'ri foyda keltiradi, na o'ziga zavq beradi, noto'g'ri tushunishlar tufayli hayotining yarmi barmoqlari orasidan sirg'alib ketadi, doimo ko'p ehtiyotkorlik, ko'p yashirish va vazminlik kerak bo'ladi, — faqat kuchning katta va foydasiz yo'qotishlari! Biroq bu o'tkir va tiniq unsurda uning butun kuchi bor: bu yerda u ucha oladi! Nega u yana suzishi, kechib o'tishi va qanotlarini bulg'ashi kerak bo'lgan o'sha loyqa suvlarga tushishi kerak! — Yo'q!

paras.en: There it is too hard for us to live! we cannot help it that we are born for the atmosphere, the pure atmosphere, we rivals of the ray of light; and that we should like best to ride like it on the atoms of ether, not away from the sun, but towards the sun! That, however, we cannot do:—so we want to do the only thing that is in our power: namely, to bring light to the earth, we want to be "the light of the earth!" And for that purpose we have our wings and our swiftness and our severity, on that account we are manly, and even terrible like the fire. Let those fear us, who do not know how to warm and brighten themselves by our influence!
paras.uz: U yerda yashash biz uchun haddan tashqari og'ir! biz atmosfera, toza atmosfera uchun tug'ilganimizga, biz nur tolasining raqiblari ekanimizga va u kabi efir atomlarida quyoshdan uzoqqa emas, quyoshga qarab eng yaxshi chopishni istashimizga chora yo'q! Biroq buni qila olmaymiz: — shuning uchun qo'limizdan keladigan yagona narsani qilmoqchimiz: ya'ni yerga nur olib kelmoqchimiz, biz «yerning nuri» bo'lmoqchimiz! Va buning uchun bizda qanotlarimiz, tezligimiz va qattiqligimiz bor, shuning uchun biz erkakonamiz va hatto olovdek dahshatlimiz. Bizning ta'sirimiz bilan o'zini isitish va yoritishni bilmaydiganlar bizdan qo'rqsin!

paras.en: 294. Against the Disparagers of Nature. — They are disagreeable to me, those men in whom every natural inclination forthwith becomes a disease, something disfiguring, or even disgraceful. They have seduced us to the opinion that the inclinations and impulses of men are evil; they are the cause of our great injustice to our own nature, and to all nature! There are enough of men who may yield to their impulses gracefully and carelessly: but they do not do so, for fear of that imaginary "evil thing" in nature! That is the cause why there is so little nobility to be found among men: the indication of which will always be to have no fear of oneself, to expect nothing disgraceful from oneself, to fly without hesitation whithersoever we are impelled—we free-born birds! Wherever we come, there will always be freedom and sunshine around us.
paras.uz: 294. Tabiatni qoralovchilarga qarshi. — Har bir tabiiy moyillik darhol kasallikka, xunuklashtiruvchi yoki hatto sharmandali narsaga aylanadigan odamlar menga yoqimsiz. Ular bizni insonning moyilliklari va mayllari yomon degan fikrga yo'ldan urishgan; ular o'z tabiatimizga va butun tabiatga bo'lgan katta adolatsizligimizning sababchisi! Mayllariga nafis va beparvo berilishi mumkin bo'lgan odamlar yetarli: lekin ular tabiatdagi o'sha xayoliy «yomon narsa»dan qo'rqib, bunday qilishmaydi! Odamlar orasida olijanoblik shunchalik kam uchrashining sababi shu: uning belgisi doimo o'zingdan qo'rqmaslik, o'zingdan hech qanday sharmandalik kutmaslik, qayerga undalsak, o'sha yerga ikkilanmay uchish bo'ladi — biz erkin tug'ilgan qushlar! Qayerga kelmaylik, atrofimizda doimo erkinlik va quyosh nuri bo'ladi.

quiz.why_uz: Kuchli va zaif tomonlarni bitta badiiy rejaga solish.

quiz.q: Why should moralists say morality is forbidden?
o: To make it attractive to heroic men

chapters.recap_uz: Har kimning o'z falsafasi va quyoshi bo'lishi kerak: axloqiy yerning ham antipodlari bor. Xarakterga «uslub berish» — buyuk san'at. Genuya quruvchilari, axloq va'zgo'ylariga maslahat va ilm atmosferasi — «biz yerning nuri bo'lmoqchimiz».

chapters.title: We create the world

paras.en: 295. Short-lived Habits. — I love short-lived habits, and regard them as an invaluable means for getting a knowledge of many things and various conditions, to the very bottom of their sweetness and bitterness; my nature is altogether arranged for short-lived habits, even in the needs of its bodily health, and in general, as far as I can see, from the lowest up to the highest matters. I always think that this will at last satisfy me permanently (the short-lived habit has also that characteristic belief of passion, the belief in everlasting duration; I am to be envied for having found it and recognised it), and then it nourishes me at noon and at eve, and spreads a profound satisfaction around me and in me, so that I have no longing for anything else, not needing to compare, or despise, or hate.
paras.uz: 295. Qisqa muddatli odatlar. — Men qisqa muddatli odatlarni sevaman va ularni ko'p narsalar va turli holatlarni shirinligi va achchiqligining eng tubigacha bilishning bebaho vositasi deb bilaman; mening tabiatim butunlay qisqa muddatli odatlarga moslashgan, hatto jismoniy sog'lig'i ehtiyojlarida ham va umuman, ko'rishimcha, eng quyi masalalardan eng oliylarigacha. Men doimo bu meni oxir-oqibat abadiy qoniqtiradi deb o'ylayman (qisqa muddatli odatda ham ehtirosning o'ziga xos ishonchi — abadiy davomiylikka ishonch bor; uni topganim va tan olganim uchun menga havas qilsa bo'ladi), keyin u meni tushda va kechqurun oziqlantiradi va atrofimda va ichimda chuqur qoniqish yoyadi, shunda boshqa hech narsaga sog'inchim bo'lmaydi, solishtirishim, mensimasligim yoki nafratlanishimga hojat qolmaydi.

paras.en: But one day the habit has had its time: the good thing separates from me, not as something which then inspires disgust in me—but peaceably and as though satisfied with me, as I am with it; as if we had to be mutually thankful, and thus shook hands for farewell. And already the new habit waits at the door, and similarly also my belief—indestructible fool and sage that I am!—that this new habit will be the right one, the ultimate right one.
paras.uz: Lekin bir kun odatning vaqti tugaydi: yaxshi narsa mendan ajraladi, menda jirkanish uyg'otadigan narsa sifatida emas — balki tinchgina va go'yo men u bilan mamnun bo'lganimdek u ham mendan mamnundek; go'yo biz bir-birimizdan minnatdor bo'lishimiz kerakdek va shu tariqa xayrlashish uchun qo'l berishgandek. Va yangi odat allaqachon eshik oldida kutmoqda, xuddi shunday mening ishonchim ham — men yo'q qilib bo'lmas ahmoq va donishmandman! — bu yangi odat to'g'ri, oxirgi to'g'ri odat bo'ladi degan ishonch.

paras.en: So it is with me as regards foods, thoughts, men, cities, poems, music, doctrines, arrangements of the day, and modes of life.—On the other hand, I hate permanent habits, and feel as if a tyrant came into my neighbourhood, and as if my life's breath condensed, when events take such a form that permanent habits seem necessarily to grow out of them: for example, through an official position, through constant companionship with the same persons, through a settled abode, or through a uniform state of health. Indeed, from the bottom of my soul I am gratefully disposed to all my misery and sickness, and to whatever is imperfect in me, because such things leave me a hundred back-doors through which I can escape from permanent habits. The most unendurable thing, to be sure, the really terrible thing, would be a life without habits, a life which continually required improvisation:—that would be my banishment and my Siberia.
paras.uz: Men bilan ovqatlar, fikrlar, odamlar, shaharlar, she'rlar, musiqa, ta'limotlar, kun tartiblari va turmush tarzlariga nisbatan shunday. — Boshqa tomondan, men doimiy odatlardan nafratlanaman va voqealar doimiy odatlar muqarrar ravishda ulardan o'sib chiqadigan shakl olganda, go'yo yonimga zolim kelgandek va hayot nafasim quyuqlashgandek his qilaman: masalan, rasmiy lavozim orqali, bir xil odamlar bilan doimiy hamrohlik orqali, o'troq yashash joyi orqali yoki bir xil sog'liq holati orqali. Haqiqatan ham, qalbimning tubidan barcha baxtsizligim va kasalligimga va menda nomukammal bo'lgan hamma narsaga minnatdorman, chunki bunday narsalar menga doimiy odatlardan qochib qutulishim mumkin bo'lgan yuzta orqa eshik qoldiradi. Albatta, eng chidab bo'lmas narsa, chinakam dahshatli narsa — odatsiz hayot, doimo bado'ha talab qiladigan hayot bo'lardi: — bu mening surgunim va mening Sibirim bo'lardi.

paras.en: 296. A Fixed Reputation. — A fixed reputation was formerly a matter of the very greatest utility; and wherever society continues to be ruled by the herd-instinct, it is still most suitable for every individual to give to his character and business the appearance of unalterableness,—even when they are not so in reality. "One can rely on him, he remains the same"—that is the praise which has most significance in all dangerous conditions of society. Society feels with satisfaction that it has a reliable tool ready at all times in the virtue of this one, in the ambition of that one, and in the reflection and passion of a third one,—it honours this tool-like nature, this self-constancy, this unchangeableness in opinions, efforts, and even in faults, with the highest honours.
paras.uz: 296. Qat'iy obro'. — Qat'iy obro' ilgari eng katta foyda keltiradigan narsa edi; va jamiyat poda instinkti bilan boshqarilishda davom etayotgan har joyda har bir shaxs uchun o'z xarakteri va ishiga o'zgarmaslik ko'rinishini berish hali ham eng maqsadga muvofiq, — hatto ular haqiqatda shunday bo'lmasa ham. «Unga suyanish mumkin, u o'zgarmaydi» — jamiyatning barcha xavfli holatlarida eng katta ahamiyatga ega maqtov shu. Jamiyat birining fazilatida, boshqasining shuhratparastligida va uchinchisining mulohaza va ehtirosida doimo tayyor ishonchli qurolga ega ekanini mamnuniyat bilan his qiladi, — u bu quroldek tabiatni, bu o'ziga sodiqlikni, fikrlardagi, sa'y-harakatlardagi va hatto xatolardagi bu o'zgarmaslikni eng yuksak sharaflar bilan hurmat qiladi.

paras.en: Such a valuation, which prevails and has prevailed everywhere simultaneously with the morality of custom, educates "characters," and brings all changing, re-learning, and self-transforming into disrepute. Be the advantage of this mode of thinking ever so great otherwise, it is in any case the mode of judging which is most injurious to knowledge: for precisely the good-will of the knowing one ever to declare himself unhesitatingly as opposed to his former opinions, and in general to be distrustful of all that wants to be fixed in him—is here condemned and brought into disrepute. The disposition of the thinker, as incompatible with a "fixed reputation," is regarded as dishonourable, while the petrifaction of opinions has all the honour to itself:—we have at present still to live under the interdict of such rules!
paras.uz: Urf-odat axloqi bilan bir vaqtda hamma joyda hukmron bo'lgan va hukmron bo'lib kelgan bunday baho «xarakterlar»ni tarbiyalaydi va har qanday o'zgarish, qayta o'rganish va o'zini o'zgartirishni obro'sizlantiradi. Bu fikrlash tarzining foydasi boshqa jihatdan qanchalik katta bo'lmasin, bu har holda bilim uchun eng zararli hukm qilish tarzi: chunki aynan biluvchining o'zining oldingi fikrlariga qarshi ekanini doimo ikkilanmay e'lon qilishga va umuman unda qotib qolmoqchi bo'lgan hamma narsaga ishonchsizlik bilan qarashga bo'lgan yaxshi niyati bu yerda qoralanadi va obro'sizlantiriladi. Mutafakkirning moyilligi «qat'iy obro'» bilan mos kelmaydigan narsa sifatida nomusli deb hisoblanadi, fikrlarning toshga aylanishi esa butun sharafni o'ziga oladi: — biz hozir ham bunday qoidalarning taqiqi ostida yashashimiz kerak!

paras.en: How difficult it is to live when one feels that the judgment of many millenniums is around one and against one. It is probable that for many millenniums knowledge was afflicted with a bad conscience, and that there must have been much self-contempt and secret misery in the history of the greatest intellects.
paras.uz: Atrofingda va senga qarshi ko'p ming yilliklarning hukmi borligini his qilganda yashash qanchalik qiyin. Ehtimol, ko'p ming yillar davomida bilim yomon vijdon bilan azob chekkan va eng buyuk aqllar tarixida ko'p o'zidan nafratlanish va yashirin baxtsizlik bo'lgan bo'lsa kerak.

paras.en: 297. Ability to Contradict. — Everyone knows at present that the ability to endure contradiction is a high indication of culture. Some people even know that the higher man courts opposition, and provokes it, so as to get a cue to his hitherto unknown partiality. But the ability to contradict, the attainment of good conscience in hostility to the accustomed, the traditional and the hallowed,—that is more than both the above-named abilities, and is the really great, new and astonishing thing in our culture, the step of all steps of the emancipated intellect: who knows that?—
paras.uz: 297. Qarshi chiqa olish. — Hozir hamma qarshilikka chiday olish madaniyatning yuksak belgisi ekanini biladi. Ba'zi odamlar hatto yuksakroq odam shu paytgacha noma'lum bo'lgan tarafkashligiga ishora olish uchun qarshilikni izlashini va uni qo'zg'atishini ham biladi. Lekin qarshi chiqa olish, odatiy, an'anaviy va muqaddaslashtirilgan narsaga dushmanlikda toza vijdonga erishish, — bu yuqorida aytilgan ikkala qobiliyatdan ham ko'proq va bizning madaniyatimizdagi chinakam buyuk, yangi va hayratlanarli narsa, ozod bo'lgan aqlning qadamlar qadami: buni kim biladi? —

paras.en: 298. A Sigh. — I caught this notion on the way, and rapidly took the readiest, poor words to hold it fast, so that it might not again fly away. And now it has died in these dry words, and hangs and flaps about in them—and I hardly know now, when I look upon it, how I could have had such happiness when I caught this bird.
paras.uz: 298. Xo'rsinish. — Men bu fikrni yo'lda ushlab oldim va uni yana uchib ketmasligi uchun mahkam ushlab turish uchun tezda eng tayyor, kambag'al so'zlarni oldim. Endi esa u bu quruq so'zlarda o'lib qoldi, ularda osilib, pirpirab turibdi — va endi unga qaraganimda, bu qushni ushlaganimda qanday qilib shunday baxtga ega bo'lganimni zo'rg'a bilaman.

paras.en: 299. What one should Learn from Artists. — What means have we for making things beautiful, attractive, and desirable, when they are not so?—and I suppose they are never so in themselves! We have here something to learn from physicians, when, for example, they dilute what is bitter, or put wine and sugar into their mixing-bowl; but we have still more to learn from artists, who in fact, are continually concerned in devising such inventions and artifices. To withdraw from things until one no longer sees much of them, until one has even to see things into them, in order to see them at all—or to view them from the side, and as in a frame—or to place them so that they partly disguise themselves and only permit of perspective views—or to look at them through coloured glasses, or in the light of the sunset—or to furnish them with a surface or skin which is not fully transparent: we should learn all that from artists, and moreover be wiser than they. For this fine power of theirs usually ceases with them where art ceases and life begins; we, however, want to be the poets of our life, and first of all in the smallest and most commonplace matters.
paras.uz: 299. San'atkorlardan nimani o'rganish kerak. — Narsalar go'zal, jozibali va istalgan bo'lmaganda, ularni shunday qilish uchun qanday vositalarimiz bor? — va menimcha ular o'z-o'zidan hech qachon shunday emas! Bu yerda shifokorlardan o'rganadigan narsamiz bor, masalan, ular achchiq narsani suyultirganda yoki aralashtirish kosasiga sharob va shakar solganda; lekin san'atkorlardan yana ham ko'proq o'rganadigan narsamiz bor, ular aslida doimo bunday ixtirolar va hiylalarni o'ylab topish bilan band. Narsalardan ularni endi ko'p ko'rmaydigan darajada, hatto ularni umuman ko'rish uchun ularga nimanidir qo'shib ko'rish kerak bo'lgan darajada uzoqlashish — yoki ularga yondan va go'yo ramkada qarash — yoki ularni qisman o'zlarini niqoblaydigan va faqat istiqbolli ko'rinishlarga imkon beradigan qilib joylashtirish — yoki ularga rangli shishalar orqali yoki quyosh botishi nurida qarash — yoki ularga to'liq shaffof bo'lmagan yuza yoki teri berish: bularning hammasini san'atkorlardan o'rganishimiz kerak va bundan tashqari ulardan donoroq bo'lishimiz kerak. Chunki ularning bu nozik kuchi odatda san'at tugab, hayot boshlanadigan joyda ular bilan to'xtaydi; biz esa o'z hayotimizning shoirlari bo'lmoqchimiz, va eng avvalo eng kichik va eng oddiy masalalarda.

paras.en: 300. Prelude to Science. — Do you believe then that the sciences would have arisen and grown up if the sorcerers, alchemists, astrologers and witches had not been their forerunners; those who, with their promisings and foreshadowings, had first to create a thirst, a hunger, and a taste for hidden and forbidden powers? Yea, that infinitely more had to be promised than could ever be fulfilled, in order that something might be fulfilled in the domain of knowledge? Perhaps the whole of religion, also, may appear to some distant age as an exercise and a prelude, in like manner as the prelude and preparation of science here exhibit themselves, though not at all practised and regarded as such. Perhaps religion may have been the peculiar means for enabling individual men to enjoy but once the entire self-satisfaction of a God and all his self-redeeming power.
paras.uz: 300. Ilmga muqaddima. — Agar sehrgarlar, alkimyogarlar, munajjimlar va jodugarlar ularning o'tmishdoshlari bo'lmaganida, fanlar paydo bo'lib, o'sgan bo'larmidi deb ishonasizmi; o'z va'dalari va bashoratlari bilan avval yashirin va taqiqlangan kuchlarga tashnalik, ochlik va did yaratishi kerak bo'lganlar? Ha, bilim sohasida nimadir amalga oshishi uchun hech qachon amalga oshirib bo'lmaydigan narsadan cheksiz ko'proq narsa va'da qilinishi kerak edi? Balki butun din ham qandaydir uzoq davrga mashq va muqaddima bo'lib ko'rinar, xuddi bu yerda ilmning muqaddimasi va tayyorgarligi o'zini namoyon qilgani kabi, garchi umuman shunday mashq qilinmagan va shunday deb hisoblanmagan bo'lsa ham. Balki din alohida odamlarga bir marta xudoning butun o'zidan mamnunligi va uning butun o'zini qutqaruvchi kuchidan bahramand bo'lish imkonini beradigan o'ziga xos vosita bo'lgandir.

paras.en: Indeed!—one may ask—would man have learned at all to get on the tracks of hunger and thirst for himself, and to extract satiety and fullness out of himself, without that religious schooling and preliminary history? Had Prometheus first to fancy that he had stolen the light, and that he did penance for the theft—in order finally to discover that he had created the light, in that he had longed for the light, and that not only man, but also God had been the work of his hands and the clay in his hands? All mere creations of the creator?—just as the illusion, the theft, the Caucasus, the vulture, and the whole tragic Prometheia of all thinkers!
paras.uz: Haqiqatan ham! — so'rash mumkin — o'sha diniy maktab va dastlabki tarixsiz inson umuman o'zi uchun ochlik va tashnalik iziga tushishni va o'zidan to'qlik va to'liqlikni chiqarib olishni o'rgangan bo'larmidi? Prometey avval nurni o'g'irladim va o'g'irlik uchun tavba qilyapman deb xayol qilishi kerakmidi — toki oxir-oqibat nurni sog'ingani tufayli uni o'zi yaratganini va nafaqat inson, balki Xudo ham uning qo'llari ishi va qo'llaridagi loy bo'lganini kashf etishi uchun? Hammasi yaratuvchining shunchaki ijodlarimi? — xuddi xayol, o'g'irlik, Kavkaz, kalxat va barcha mutafakkirlarning butun tragik Prometeiyasi kabi!

paras.en: 301. Illusion of the Contemplative. — Higher men are distinguished from lower, by seeing and hearing immensely more, and in a thoughtful manner—and it is precisely this that distinguishes man from the animal, and the higher animal from the lower. The world always becomes fuller for him who grows up into the full stature of humanity; there are always more interesting fishing-hooks, thrown out to him; the number of his stimuli is continually on the increase, and similarly the varieties of his pleasure and pain,—the higher man becomes always at the same time happier and unhappier.
paras.uz: 301. Mulohazakorning xayoli. — Yuksakroq odamlar pastroqlardan beqiyos ko'proq va o'ychan tarzda ko'rish va eshitish bilan ajralib turadi — va aynan shu insonni hayvondan, yuksakroq hayvonni pastroqdan ajratib turadi. Insoniylikning to'liq bo'yiga o'sib boradigan odam uchun dunyo doimo to'laroq bo'lib boradi; unga doimo ko'proq qiziqarli qarmoqlar tashlanadi; uning qo'zg'atuvchilari soni doimo ortib boradi, xuddi shunday lazzat va og'rig'ining turlari ham, — yuksakroq odam doimo bir vaqtning o'zida baxtliroq va baxtsizroq bo'ladi.

paras.en: An illusion, however, is his constant accompaniment all along: he thinks he is placed as a spectator and auditor before the great pantomime and concert of life; he calls his nature a contemplative nature, and thereby overlooks the fact that he himself is also a real creator, and continuous poet of life,—that he no doubt differs greatly from the actor in this drama, the so-called practical man, but differs still more from a mere onlooker or spectator before the stage. There is certainly vis contemplativa, and re-examination of his work peculiar to him as poet, but at the same time, and first and foremost, he has the vis creativa, which the practical man or doer lacks, whatever appearance and current belief may say to the contrary.
paras.uz: Biroq bir xayol doimo uning hamrohi: u o'zini hayotning buyuk pantomimasi va kontserti oldida tomoshabin va tinglovchi sifatida qo'yilgan deb o'ylaydi; u o'z tabiatini mulohazakor tabiat deb ataydi va shu bilan o'zi ham haqiqiy yaratuvchi va hayotning uzluksiz shoiri ekanini e'tibordan chetda qoldiradi, — u shubhasiz bu dramadagi aktyordan, amaliy odam deb ataladigan kishidan juda farq qiladi, lekin sahna oldidagi shunchaki kuzatuvchi yoki tomoshabindan yana ham ko'proq farq qiladi. Albatta, unda vis contemplativa — mulohaza kuchi va shoir sifatida o'z asarini qayta ko'rib chiqish bor, lekin shu bilan birga va eng avvalo, unda vis creativa — yaratish kuchi bor, ko'rinish va hozirgi ishonch aksini qanday demasin, amaliy odam yoki ish qiluvchida u yo'q.

paras.en: It is we, we who think and feel, that actually and unceasingly make something which does not yet exist: the whole eternally increasing world of valuations, colours, weights, perspectives, gradations, affirmations and negations. This composition of ours is continually learnt, practised, and translated into flesh and actuality, and even into the commonplace, by the so-called practical men (our actors, as we have said). Whatever has value in the present world, has it not in itself, by its nature,—nature is always worthless:—but a value was once given to it, bestowed upon it, and it was we who gave and bestowed!
paras.uz: Biz, o'ylaydigan va his qiladiganlar, hali mavjud bo'lmagan nimanidir haqiqatan va tinimsiz yaratamiz: baholar, ranglar, og'irliklar, istiqbollar, darajalar, tasdiqlar va inkorlarning abadiy o'sib boruvchi butun dunyosini. Bu bizning kompozitsiyamiz amaliy odamlar (aytganimizdek, bizning aktyorlarimiz) tomonidan doimo o'rganiladi, mashq qilinadi va go'sht va haqiqatga, hatto oddiylikka tarjima qilinadi. Hozirgi dunyoda qadri bo'lgan har qanday narsaning qadri o'z-o'zidan, tabiatan emas, — tabiat doimo qadrsiz: — balki unga bir marta qadr berilgan, in'om qilingan va bergan va in'om qilgan biz edik!

paras.en: We only have created the world which is of any account to man!—But it is precisely this knowledge that we lack, and when we get hold of it for a moment we have forgotten it the next: we misunderstand our highest power, we contemplative men, and estimate ourselves at too low a rate,—we are neither as proud nor as happy as we might be.
paras.uz: Faqat biz insonga ahamiyatli bo'lgan dunyoni yaratdik! — Lekin aynan shu bilim bizga yetishmaydi va uni bir lahzaga qo'lga kiritsak, keyingi lahzada unutamiz: biz, mulohazakor odamlar, eng yuksak kuchimizni noto'g'ri tushunamiz va o'zimizni haddan tashqari past baholaymiz, — biz bo'lishimiz mumkin bo'lganchalik mag'rur ham, baxtli ham emasmiz.

paras.en: 302. The Danger of the Happiest Ones. — To have fine senses and a fine taste; to be accustomed to the select and the intellectually best as our proper and readiest fare; to be blessed with a strong, bold, and daring soul; to go through life with a quiet eye and a firm step, ever ready for the worst as for a festival, and full of longing for undiscovered worlds and seas, men and Gods; to listen to all joyous music, as if there, perhaps, brave men, soldiers and seafarers, took a brief repose and enjoyment, and in the profoundest pleasure of the moment were overcome with tears and the whole purple melancholy of happiness: who would not like all this to be his possession, his condition! It was the happiness of Homer! The condition of him who invented the Gods for the Greeks,—nay, who invented his Gods for himself!
paras.uz: 302. Eng baxtlilarning xavfi. — Nozik sezgilar va nozik didga ega bo'lish; tanlangan va aqlan eng yaxshi narsaga o'z va eng tayyor taomimiz sifatida odatlangan bo'lish; kuchli, dadil va jasur qalb bilan duo qilingan bo'lish; hayot bo'ylab sokin ko'z va qat'iy qadam bilan yurish, eng yomoniga bayramga tayyor bo'lgandek doimo tayyor va kashf etilmagan dunyolar va dengizlar, odamlar va xudolarga sog'inchga to'la bo'lish; barcha quvnoq musiqani, go'yo u yerda, balki, jasur odamlar, askarlar va dengizchilar qisqa dam olib, zavqlanayotgandek va lahzaning eng chuqur lazzatida ko'z yoshlari va baxtning butun qirmizi g'amginligiga berilgandek tinglash: kim bularning hammasi o'z mulki, o'z holati bo'lishini istamaydi! Bu Gomerning baxti edi! Yunonlar uchun xudolarni ixtiro qilgan, — yo'q, o'zi uchun o'z xudolarini ixtiro qilgan odamning holati!

paras.en: But let us not conceal the fact that with this happiness of Homer in one's soul, one is more liable to suffering than any other creature under the sun! And only at this price do we purchase the most precious pearl that the waves of existence have hitherto washed ashore! As its possessor one always becomes more sensitive to pain, and at last too sensitive: a little displeasure and loathing sufficed in the end to make Homer disgusted with life. He was unable to solve a foolish little riddle which some young fishers proposed to him! Yes, the little riddles are the dangers of the happiest ones!—
paras.uz: Lekin qalbida Gomerning bu baxti bilan odam quyosh ostidagi har qanday boshqa mavjudotdan ko'ra azobga ko'proq moyil ekanini yashirmaylik! Va faqat shu narxda biz hayot to'lqinlari shu paytgacha qirg'oqqa yuvib chiqargan eng qimmatli marvaridni sotib olamiz! Uning egasi sifatida odam doimo og'riqqa sezgirroq va oxir-oqibat haddan tashqari sezgir bo'ladi: oxirida ozgina norozilik va jirkanish Gomerni hayotdan bezdirishga kifoya qildi. U ba'zi yosh baliqchilar unga taklif qilgan ahmoqona kichkina jumboqni yecha olmadi! Ha, kichkina jumboqlar — eng baxtlilarning xavfi! —

paras.en: 303. Two Happy Ones. — Certainly this man, notwithstanding his youth, understands the improvisation of life, and astonishes even the acutest observers. For it seems that he never makes a mistake, although he constantly plays the most hazardous games. One is reminded of the improvising masters of the musical art, to whom even the listeners would fain ascribe a divine infallibility of the hand, notwithstanding that they now and then make a mistake, as every mortal is liable to do. But they are skilled and inventive, and always ready in a moment to arrange into the structure of the score the most accidental tone (where the jerk of a finger or a humour brings it about), and to animate the accident with a fine meaning and a soul.—Here is quite a different man: everything that he intends and plans fails with him in the long run.
paras.uz: 303. Ikki baxtli. — Albatta, bu odam yoshligiga qaramay hayot bado'hasini tushunadi va hatto eng o'tkir kuzatuvchilarni ham hayratga soladi. Chunki u doimo eng xavfli o'yinlarni o'ynasa ham, hech qachon xato qilmaydiganga o'xshaydi. Musiqa san'atining bado'hachi ustalarini eslatadi, tinglovchilar ham ularga qo'lning ilohiy xatosizligini nisbat berishni istaydi, garchi ular har bir banda kabi vaqti-vaqti bilan xato qilsalar ham. Lekin ular mohir va ixtirochi va eng tasodifiy ohangni (barmoqning siltanishi yoki kayfiyat uni keltirib chiqargan joyda) bir lahzada partitura tuzilishiga joylashtirishga va tasodifga nozik ma'no va ruh berishga doimo tayyor. — Mana butunlay boshqa odam: u niyat qilgan va rejalashtirgan hamma narsa uzoq muddatda muvaffaqiyatsiz bo'ladi.

paras.en: That on which he has now and again set his heart has already brought him several times to the abyss, and to the very verge of ruin; and if he has as yet got out of the scrape, it certainly has not been merely with a "black eye." Do you think he is unhappy over it? He resolved long ago not to regard his own wishes and plans as of so much importance. "If this does not succeed with me,"—he says to himself, "perhaps that will succeed; and on the whole I do not know but that I am under more obligation to thank my failures than any of my successes. Am I made to be headstrong, and to wear the bull's horns? That which constitutes the worth and the sum of life for me, lies somewhere else; I know more of life, because I have been so often on the point of losing it; and just on that account I have more of life than any of you!"
paras.uz: U vaqti-vaqti bilan ko'ngil qo'ygan narsa uni allaqachon bir necha marta tubsizlikka va halokatning aynan chekkasiga olib kelgan; va agar u hozircha bu balodan qutulgan bo'lsa, bu albatta shunchaki «ko'karib qolgan ko'z» bilan bo'lmagan. Uni bundan baxtsiz deb o'ylaysizmi? U allaqachon o'z istaklari va rejalarini bunchalik muhim deb hisoblamaslikka qaror qilgan. «Agar bu menda muvaffaqiyatli bo'lmasa, — deydi u o'ziga, — balki u muvaffaqiyatli bo'lar; va umuman olganda, muvaffaqiyatlarimning birortasidan ko'ra muvaffaqiyatsizliklarimga ko'proq minnatdor bo'lishim kerak emasligini bilmayman. Men o'jar bo'lish va buqa shoxlarini taqish uchun yaratilganmanmi? Men uchun hayotning qadri va yig'indisini tashkil etadigan narsa boshqa joyda; men hayotni ko'proq bilaman, chunki uni yo'qotish arafasida juda ko'p marta bo'lganman; va aynan shuning uchun menda sizlarning har biringizdan ko'proq hayot bor!»

chapters.recap_uz: Nitsshe qisqa muddatli odatlarni sevadi va doimiy odatlardan nafratlanadi. San'atkorlardan narsalarni go'zal ko'rsatishni o'rganish kerak. Mulohazakor odam o'zini tomoshabin deb o'ylaydi, aslida u qadriyatlar dunyosini yaratuvchi shoir.

chapters.title: Will and wave

paras.en: 304. In Doing we Leave Undone. — In the main all those moral systems are distasteful to me which say: "Do not do this! Renounce! Overcome thyself!" On the other hand I am favourable to those moral systems which stimulate me to do something, and to do it again from morning till evening, and dream of it at night, and think of nothing else but to do it well, as well as it is possible for me alone! From him who so lives there fall off one after the other the things that do not pertain to such a life: without hatred or antipathy, he sees this take leave of him to-day, and that to-morrow, like the yellow leaves which every livelier breeze strips from the tree: or he does not see at all that they take leave of him, so firmly is his eye fixed upon his goal, and generally forward, not sideways, backward, nor downward.
paras.uz: 304. Qilish bilan qilmay qo'yamiz. — Asosan menga «Buni qilma! Voz kech! O'zingni yeng!» deydigan barcha axloq tizimlari yoqmaydi. Boshqa tomondan, meni nimadir qilishga va uni ertalabdan kechgacha qayta-qayta qilishga, tunda u haqda tush ko'rishga va uni yaxshi, faqat men uchun mumkin bo'lganchalik yaxshi qilishdan boshqa hech narsa haqida o'ylamaslikka undaydigan axloq tizimlariga xayrixohman! Shunday yashaydigan odamdan bunday hayotga tegishli bo'lmagan narsalar birin-ketin tushib ketadi: u nafrat yoki jirkanishsiz bugun buni, ertaga uni o'zi bilan xayrlashayotganini ko'radi, xuddi har bir jonliroq shabada daraxtdan yulib oladigan sariq barglardek: yoki u ularning o'zi bilan xayrlashayotganini umuman ko'rmaydi, uning ko'zi maqsadiga, umuman oldinga, yonga emas, orqaga emas, pastga emas, shunchalik mahkam qadalgan.

paras.en: "Our doing must determine what we leave undone; in that we do, we leave undone"—so it pleases me, so runs my placitum. But I do not mean to strive with open eyes for my impoverishment; I do not like any of the negative virtues whose very essence is negation and self-renunciation.
paras.uz: «Qilganimiz qilmay qo'yadiganimizni belgilashi kerak; qilish bilan biz qilmay qo'yamiz» — menga shunday yoqadi, mening placitum'im — qarorim shunday. Lekin men ochiq ko'zlar bilan qashshoqlashishimga intilmoqchi emasman; mohiyati inkor va o'zidan voz kechishdan iborat bo'lgan salbiy fazilatlarning birortasini ham yoqtirmayman.

paras.en: 305. Self-control. — Those moral teachers who first and foremost order man to get himself into his own power, induce thereby a curious infirmity in him,—namely, a constant sensitiveness with reference to all natural strivings and inclinations, and as it were, a sort of itching. Whatever may henceforth drive him, draw him, allure or impel him, whether internally or externally—it always seems to this sensitive being, as if his self-control were in danger: he is no longer at liberty to trust himself to any instinct, to any free flight, but stands constantly with defensive mien, armed against himself, with sharp distrustful eye, the eternal watcher of his stronghold, to which office he has appointed himself. Yes, he can be great in that position! But how unendurable he has now become to others, how difficult even for himself to bear, how impoverished and cut off from the finest accidents of his soul! Yea, even from all further instruction! For we must be able to lose ourselves at times, if we want to learn something of what we have not in ourselves.
paras.uz: 305. O'zini boshqarish. — Insonga eng avvalo o'zini o'z hokimiyatiga olishni buyuradigan axloq o'qituvchilari shu bilan unda g'alati zaiflikni keltirib chiqaradi, — ya'ni barcha tabiiy intilishlar va moyilliklarga nisbatan doimiy sezgirlik va go'yo qandaydir qichishishni. Bundan buyon uni nima harakatga keltirmasin, tortmasin, yo'ldan urmasin yoki undamasin, xoh ichkaridan, xoh tashqaridan — bu sezgir mavjudotga doimo o'zini boshqarishi xavf ostidagidek tuyuladi: u endi hech qanday instinktga, hech qanday erkin parvozga o'zini ishona olmaydi, balki doimo himoya qiyofasida, o'ziga qarshi qurollangan holda, o'tkir ishonchsiz ko'z bilan, o'zi tayinlagan qal'asining abadiy qo'riqchisi sifatida turadi. Ha, u bu holatda buyuk bo'lishi mumkin! Lekin endi u boshqalarga qanchalik chidab bo'lmas bo'lib qoldi, hatto o'zi uchun ham ko'tarish qanchalik qiyin, ruhining eng go'zal tasodiflaridan qanchalik qashshoqlashgan va uzilgan! Ha, hatto keyingi har qanday ta'limdan ham! Chunki o'zimizda bo'lmagan narsadan nimanidir o'rganmoqchi bo'lsak, ba'zan o'zimizni yo'qota olishimiz kerak.

paras.en: 306. Stoic and Epicurean. — The Epicurean selects the situations, the persons, and even the events which suit his extremely sensitive, intellectual constitution; he renounces the rest—that is to say, by far the greater part of experience—because it would be too strong and too heavy fare for him. The Stoic, on the contrary, accustoms himself to swallow stones and vermin, glass-splinters and scorpions, without feeling any disgust: his stomach is meant to become indifferent in the end to all that the accidents of existence cast into it:—he reminds one of the Arabic sect of the Assaua, with which the French became acquainted in Algiers; and like those insensible persons, he also likes well to have an invited public at the exhibition of his insensibility, the very thing the Epicurean willingly dispenses with:—he has of course his "garden"!
paras.uz: 306. Stoik va epikurchi. — Epikurchi o'zining nihoyatda sezgir, aqliy tuzilishiga mos keladigan vaziyatlar, odamlar va hatto voqealarni tanlaydi; qolganidan — ya'ni tajribaning eng katta qismidan voz kechadi, chunki u uning uchun haddan tashqari kuchli va og'ir taom bo'lardi. Stoik esa, aksincha, hech qanday jirkanish his qilmay tosh va hasharotlar, shisha parchalari va chayonlarni yutishga o'zini odatlantiradi: uning oshqozoni oxir-oqibat hayot tasodiflari unga tashlaydigan hamma narsaga befarq bo'lishi kerak: — u fransuzlar Jazoirda tanishgan arab Isaviyya sektasini eslatadi; va o'sha sezgisiz odamlar kabi u ham o'z sezgisizligini namoyish qilishda taklif qilingan jamoatchilik bo'lishini yaxshi ko'radi, epikurchi bajonidil voz kechadigan aynan shu narsani: — uning, albatta, o'z «bog'i» bor!

paras.en: Stoicism may be quite advisable for men with whom fate improvises, for those who live in violent times and are dependent on abrupt and changeable individuals. He, however, who anticipates that fate will permit him to spin "a long thread," does well to make his arrangements in Epicurean fashion; all men devoted to intellectual labour have done it hitherto! For it would be a supreme loss to them to forfeit their fine sensibility, and acquire the hard, stoical hide with hedgehog prickles in exchange.
paras.uz: Taqdir bado'ha qiladigan odamlar uchun, shiddatli zamonlarda yashaydigan va keskin va o'zgaruvchan shaxslarga qaram bo'lganlar uchun stoitsizm juda maslahat qilinadigan bo'lishi mumkin. Biroq taqdir unga «uzun ip» yigirishga ruxsat beradi deb oldindan sezgan odam o'z ishlarini epikurchilarcha tartibga solsa yaxshi qiladi; aqliy mehnatga berilgan barcha odamlar shu paytgacha shunday qilishgan! Chunki ular uchun o'zlarining nozik sezgirligini yo'qotib, buning evaziga tipratikan tikanlari bilan qattiq, stoik terini olish eng katta yo'qotish bo'lardi.

paras.en: 307. In Favour of Criticism. — Something now appears to thee as an error which thou formerly lovedst as a truth, or as a probability: thou pushest it from thee and imaginest that thy reason has there gained a victory. But perhaps that error was then, when thou wast still another person—thou art always another person,—just as necessary to thee as all thy present "truths," like a skin, as it were, which concealed and veiled from thee much which thou still mayst not see. Thy new life, and not thy reason, has slain that opinion for thee: thou dost not require it any longer, and now it breaks down of its own accord, and the irrationality crawls out of it as a worm into the light. When we make use of criticism it is not something arbitrary and impersonal,—it is, at least very often, a proof that there are lively, active forces in us, which cast a skin. We deny, and must deny, because something in us wants to live and affirm itself, something which we perhaps do not as yet know, do not as yet see!—So much in favour of criticism.
paras.uz: 307. Tanqid foydasiga. — Ilgari haqiqat yoki ehtimollik sifatida sevgan narsang endi senga xato bo'lib ko'rinadi: sen uni o'zingdan itarasan va aqling u yerda g'alaba qozondi deb tasavvur qilasan. Lekin balki o'sha xato o'shanda, sen hali boshqa odam bo'lganingda — sen doimo boshqa odamsan — barcha hozirgi «haqiqat»laring kabi senga zarur bo'lgandir, go'yo hali ko'rmasligingiz mumkin bo'lgan ko'p narsani sendan yashirib, pardalab turgan teridek. Bu fikrni sen uchun aqling emas, yangi hayoting o'ldirdi: senga u endi kerak emas va endi u o'z-o'zidan qulab tushadi va aqlsizlik undan qurtdek yorug'likka o'rmalab chiqadi. Biz tanqiddan foydalanganimizda, bu o'zboshimcha va shaxssiz narsa emas, — bu hech bo'lmasa ko'pincha bizda teri tashlaydigan jonli, faol kuchlar borligining isboti. Biz inkor etamiz va inkor etishimiz kerak, chunki bizda nimadir yashashni va o'zini tasdiqlashni istaydi, biz balki hali bilmaydigan, hali ko'rmaydigan nimadir! — Tanqid foydasiga shuncha.

paras.en: 308. The History of each Day. — What is it that constitutes the history of each day for thee? Look at thy habits of which it consists: are they the product of numberless little acts of cowardice and laziness, or of thy bravery and inventive reason? Although the two cases are so different, it is possible that men might bestow the same praise upon thee, and that thou mightst also be equally useful to them in the one case as in the other. But praise and utility and respectability may suffice for him whose only desire is to have a good conscience,—not however for thee, the "trier of the reins," who hast a consciousness of the conscience!
paras.uz: 308. Har kunning tarixi. — Sen uchun har kunning tarixini nima tashkil etadi? U iborat bo'lgan odatlaringga qara: ular son-sanoqsiz kichik qo'rqoqlik va dangasalik harakatlarining mahsulimi yoki sening jasorating va ixtirochi aqlingningmi? Ikkala holat shunchalik farq qilsa ham, odamlar senga bir xil maqtov berishi va sen ham ularga birinchi holatda ikkinchisidagidek foydali bo'lishing mumkin. Lekin maqtov, foyda va obro' yagona istagi toza vijdon bo'lgan odamga yetarli bo'lishi mumkin, — biroq vijdonni anglaydigan sen, «yuraklarni sinovchi» uchun emas!

paras.en: 309. Out of the Seventh Solitude. — One day the wanderer shut a door behind him, stood still, and wept. Then he said: "Oh, this inclination and impulse towards the true, the real, the non-apparent, the certain! How I detest it! Why does this gloomy and passionate taskmaster follow just me? I should like to rest, but it does not permit me to do so. Are there not a host of things seducing me to tarry! Everywhere there are gardens of Armida for me, and therefore there will always be fresh separations and fresh bitterness of heart! I must set my foot forward, my weary wounded foot: and because I feel I must do this, I often cast grim glances back at the most beautiful things which could not detain me—because they could not detain me!"
paras.uz: 309. Yettinchi yolg'izlikdan. — Bir kun sayyoh orqasidan eshikni yopib, to'xtab qoldi va yig'ladi. Keyin dedi: «Oh, haqiqiy, real, ko'rinmaydigan, aniq narsaga bo'lgan bu moyillik va mayl! Undan qanchalik nafratlanaman! Nega bu ma'yus va ehtirosli nazoratchi aynan mening ortimdan yuradi? Men dam olmoqchiman, lekin u bunga yo'l qo'ymaydi. Meni to'xtashga vasvasa qiladigan narsalar ko'p emasmi! Hamma joyda men uchun Armida bog'lari bor va shuning uchun doimo yangi ayriliqlar va yurakning yangi achchiqligi bo'ladi! Men oyog'imni, charchagan yaralangan oyog'imni oldinga qo'yishim kerak: va buni qilishim kerakligini his qilganim uchun, ko'pincha meni ushlab qola olmagan eng go'zal narsalarga ortga qahrli nigohlar tashlayman — chunki ular meni ushlab qola olmadi!»

paras.en: 310. Will and Wave. — How eagerly this wave comes hither, as if it were a question of its reaching something! How it creeps with frightful haste into the innermost corners of the rocky cliff! It seems that it wants to forestall some one; it seems that something is concealed there that has value, high value.—And now it retreats somewhat more slowly, still quite white with excitement,—is it disappointed? Has it found what it sought? Does it merely pretend to be disappointed?—But already another wave approaches, still more eager and wild than the first, and its soul also seems to be full of secrets and of longing for treasure-seeking. Thus live the waves,—thus live we who exercise will!—I do not say more.—But what! Ye distrust me? Ye are angry at me, ye beautiful monsters? Do ye fear that I will quite betray your secret? Well!
paras.uz: 310. Iroda va to'lqin. — Bu to'lqin go'yo biror narsaga yetishi kerakdek, qanchalik ishtiyoq bilan bu yerga keladi! U toshloq qoyaning eng ichki burchaklariga qanday dahshatli shoshilish bilan o'rmalab kiradi! Go'yo u kimnidir ortda qoldirmoqchi; go'yo u yerda qadri bor, yuksak qadri bor nimadir yashiringan. — Endi u biroz sekinroq chekinadi, hayajondan hali ham oppoq, — hafsalasi pir bo'ldimi? Izlagan narsasini topdimi? Shunchaki hafsalasi pir bo'lgandek ko'rinadimi? — Lekin allaqachon birinchisidan ham ishtiyoqliroq va yovvoyiroq boshqa to'lqin yaqinlashmoqda va uning ruhi ham sirlar va xazina izlash sog'inchiga to'ladek. To'lqinlar shunday yashaydi, — iroda qiladigan biz shunday yashaymiz! — Boshqa gapirmayman. — Lekin nima! Menga ishonmaysizmi? Mendan g'azablanyapsizmi, ey go'zal mahluqlar? Sirlaringizni butunlay oshkor qilib qo'yaman deb qo'rqasizmi? Xo'p!

paras.en: Just be angry with me, raise your green, dangerous bodies as high as ye can, make a wall between me and the sun—as at present! Verily, there is now nothing more left of the world save green twilight and green lightning-flashes. Do as ye will, ye wanton creatures, roar with delight and wickedness—or dive under again, pour your emeralds down into the depths, and cast your endless white tresses of foam and spray over them—it is all the same to me, for all is so well with you, and I am so pleased with you for it all: how could I betray you! For—take this to heart!—I know you and your secret, I know your race! You and I are indeed of one race! You and I have indeed one secret!
paras.uz: Mendan g'azablanaveringlar, yashil, xavfli tanalaringizni iloji boricha baland ko'taringlar, men bilan quyosh o'rtasiga devor qilinglar — hozirgidek! Haqiqatan ham, endi dunyodan yashil g'ira-shira va yashil chaqmoq chaqnashlaridan boshqa hech narsa qolmadi. Xohlaganingizni qilinglar, ey sho'x mavjudotlar, zavq va yovuzlikdan bo'kiringlar — yoki yana sho'ng'inglar, zumradlaringizni qa'rga to'kinglar va ular ustiga ko'pik va chang'ozlarning cheksiz oq sochlarini tashlanglar — menga baribir, chunki sizlarda hammasi shunchalik yaxshi va men bularning hammasi uchun sizdan shunchalik mamnunman: qanday qilib sizni sotishim mumkin! Chunki — buni yodingizda tuting! — men sizni va sirlaringizni bilaman, zotingizni bilaman! Siz va men haqiqatan ham bir zotdanmiz! Siz va mening haqiqatan ham bitta sirimiz bor!

paras.en: 311. Broken Lights. — We are not always brave, and when we are weary, people of our stamp are liable to lament occasionally in this wise:—"It is so hard to cause pain to men—oh, that it should be necessary! What good is it to live concealed, when we do not want to keep to ourselves that which causes vexation? Would it not be more advisable to live in the madding crowd, and compensate individuals for sins that are committed and must be committed against mankind in general? Foolish with fools, vain with the vain, enthusiastic with enthusiasts? Would that not be reasonable when there is such an inordinate amount of divergence in the main? When I hear of the malignity of others against me—is not my first feeling that of satisfaction?
paras.uz: 311. Singan nurlar. — Biz doimo jasur emasmiz va charchaganimizda bizning toifamizdagi odamlar ba'zan shu tarzda nola qilishga moyil: — «Odamlarga og'riq berish shunchalik og'ir — oh, bu zarur ekanligi! Bizni g'azablantiradigan narsani o'zimizda saqlashni istamasak, yashirin yashashdan nima foyda? Aqldan ozgan olomon ichida yashab, umuman insoniyatga qarshi qilinadigan va qilinishi kerak bo'lgan gunohlar uchun alohida odamlarga tovon to'lash maqsadga muvofiqroq bo'lmasmidi? Ahmoqlar bilan ahmoq, manmanlar bilan manman, ishtiyoqlilar bilan ishtiyoqli? Asosiy narsada shunchalik haddan tashqari ko'p farq bo'lganda bu aqlli bo'lmasmidi? Boshqalarning menga qarshi yovuzligi haqida eshitganimda — mening birinchi tuyg'um mamnunlik emasmi?

paras.en: It is well that it should be so!—I seem to myself to say to them—I am so little in harmony with you, and have so much truth on my side: see henceforth that ye be merry at my expense as often as ye can! Here are my defects and mistakes, here are my illusions, my bad taste, my confusion, my tears, my vanity, my owlish concealment, my contradictions! Here you have something to laugh at! Laugh then, and enjoy yourselves!
paras.uz: Shunday bo'lgani yaxshi! — go'yo ularga aytayotgandek bo'laman — men siz bilan shunchalik kam uyg'unman va mening tomonimda shunchalik ko'p haqiqat bor: bundan buyon iloji boricha tez-tez mening hisobimdan quvnoq bo'lishga harakat qilinglar! Mana mening kamchiliklarim va xatolarim, mana mening xayollarim, yomon didim, chalkashligim, ko'z yoshlarim, manmanligim, boyqushdek yashirinishim, qarama-qarshiliklarim! Mana sizga kuladigan narsa! Unda kulinglar va zavqlaninglar!

paras.en: I am not averse to the law and nature of things, which is that defects and errors should give pleasure!—To be sure there were once 'more glorious' times, when as soon as any one got an idea, however moderately new it might be, he would think himself so indispensable as to go out into the street with it, and call to everybody: 'Behold! the kingdom of heaven is at hand!'—I should not miss myself, if I were a-wanting. We are none of us indispensable!"—As we have said, however, we do not think thus when we are brave; we do not think about it at all.
paras.uz: Men kamchiliklar va xatolar zavq berishi kerakligi haqidagi narsalar qonuni va tabiatiga qarshi emasman! — Albatta, bir paytlar «shonliroq» zamonlar bo'lgan, o'shanda kimdir g'oyaga ega bo'lishi bilanoq, u qanchalik o'rtacha yangi bo'lmasin, o'zini shunchalik zarur deb hisoblardiki, u bilan ko'chaga chiqib, hammaga: "Mana! Osmon shohligi yaqinlashdi!" deb chaqirardi. — Agar men yo'q bo'lsam, o'zimni sog'inmasdim. Hech birimiz zarur emasmiz!» — Biroq aytganimizdek, biz jasur bo'lganimizda bunday o'ylamaymiz; bu haqda umuman o'ylamaymiz.

paras.en: 312. My Dog. — I have given a name to my suffering, and call it "dog,"—it is just as faithful, just as importunate and shameless, just as entertaining, just as wise, as any other dog—and I can domineer over it, and vent my bad humour on it, as others do with their dogs, servants, and wives.
paras.uz: 312. Mening itim. — Men azobimga nom berdim va uni «it» deb atayman, — u har qanday boshqa it kabi sodiq, xuddi shunday surbet va uyatsiz, xuddi shunday qiziqarli, xuddi shunday dono — va men unga hukmronlik qilib, boshqalar o'z itlari, xizmatkorlari va xotinlari bilan qilganidek, unga yomon kayfiyatimni to'ka olaman.

paras.en: 313. No Picture of a Martyr. — I will take my cue from Raphael, and not paint any more martyr pictures. There are enough of sublime things without its being necessary to seek sublimity where it is linked with cruelty; moreover my ambition would not be gratified in the least if I aspired to be a sublime executioner.
paras.uz: 313. Shahid rasmi yo'q. — Men Rafaeldan o'rnak olaman va boshqa shahidlar rasmini chizmayman. Yuksaklikni shafqatsizlik bilan bog'liq joyda izlashga hojat bo'lmasdan ham yetarlicha yuksak narsalar bor; bundan tashqari, agar yuksak jallod bo'lishga intilsam, shuhratparastligim zarracha ham qondirilmasdi.

paras.en: 314. New Domestic Animals. — I want to have my lion and my eagle about me, that I may always have hints and premonitions concerning the amount of my strength or weakness. Must I look down on them to-day, and be afraid of them? And will the hour come once more when they will look up to me, and tremble?—
paras.uz: 314. Yangi uy hayvonlari. — Men atrofimda sherim va burgutim bo'lishini istayman, toki kuchim yoki zaifligim miqdori haqida doimo ishoralar va oldindan sezishlar bo'lsin. Bugun ularga past nazar bilan qarashim va ulardan qo'rqishim kerakmi? Va ular menga yuqoriga qarab, titraydigan soat yana keladimi? —

paras.en: 315. The Last Hour. — Storms are my danger. Shall I have my storm in which I shall perish, just as Oliver Cromwell perished in his storm? Or shall I go out as a light does, not first blown out by the wind, but grown tired and weary of itself—a burnt-out light? Or finally, shall I blow myself out, so as not to burn out!
paras.uz: 315. Oxirgi soat. — Bo'ronlar — mening xavfim. Oliver Kromvel o'z bo'ronida halok bo'lgani kabi, men ham o'z bo'ronimda halok bo'lamanmi? Yoki chiroq kabi o'chamanmi, avval shamol puflab o'chirmasdan, balki o'zidan charchab, holdan toyib — yonib tugagan chiroq kabi? Yoki nihoyat, yonib tugamaslik uchun o'zimni o'zim puflab o'chiramanmi!

paras.en: 316. Prophetic Men. — Ye cannot divine how sorely prophetic men suffer: ye think only that a fine "gift" has been given to them, and would fain have it yourselves,—but I will express my meaning by a simile. How much may not the animals suffer from the electricity of the atmosphere and the clouds! Some of them, as we see, have a prophetic faculty with regard to the weather, for example, apes (as one can observe very well even in Europe,—and not only in menageries, but at Gibraltar). But it never occurs to us that it is their sufferings—that are their prophets! When strong positive electricity, under the influence of an approaching cloud not at all visible, is suddenly converted into negative electricity, and an alteration of the weather is imminent, these animals then behave as if an enemy were approaching them, and prepare for defence, or flight: they generally hide themselves,—they do not think of the bad weather as weather, but as an enemy whose hand they already feel!
paras.uz: 316. Payg'ambarona odamlar. — Payg'ambarona odamlar qanchalik qattiq azob chekishini siz sezolmaysiz: siz faqat ularga go'zal «iqtidor» berilgan deb o'ylaysiz va o'zingizda ham bo'lishini xohlaysiz, — lekin men fikrimni o'xshatish bilan ifodalayman. Hayvonlar atmosfera va bulutlarning elektridan qanchalik azob chekishi mumkin! Ko'rib turganimizdek, ulardan ba'zilarida ob-havoga nisbatan payg'ambarona qobiliyat bor, masalan, maymunlarda (buni hatto Yevropada ham, va faqat hayvonot bog'larida emas, Gibraltarda ham juda yaxshi kuzatish mumkin). Lekin bizning xayolimizga hech qachon ularning payg'ambarlari — ularning azoblari ekani kelmaydi! Kuchli musbat elektr umuman ko'rinmaydigan yaqinlashayotgan bulut ta'sirida to'satdan manfiy elektrga aylanganda va ob-havoning o'zgarishi yaqin bo'lganda, bu hayvonlar go'yo ularga dushman yaqinlashayotgandek o'zini tutadi va himoyaga yoki qochishga tayyorlanadi: ular odatda yashirinishadi, — ular yomon ob-havoni ob-havo deb emas, balki qo'lini allaqachon his qilayotgan dushman deb o'ylaydi!

paras.en: 317. Retrospect. — We seldom become conscious of the real pathos of any period of life as such, as long as we continue in it, but always think it is the only possible and reasonable thing for us henceforth, and that it is altogether ethos and not pathos—to speak and distinguish like the Greeks. A few notes of music to-day recalled a winter and a house, and a life of utter solitude to my mind, and at the same time the sentiments in which I then lived: I thought I should be able to live in such a state always. But now I understand that it was entirely pathos and passion, something comparable to this painfully bold and truly comforting music,—it is not one's lot to have these sensations for years, still less for eternities: otherwise one would become too "ethereal" for this planet.
paras.uz: 317. Orqaga nazar. — Biz hayotning qaysi davrining haqiqiy pafosini, unda davom etar ekanmiz, kamdan-kam anglaymiz, balki doimo bu bundan buyon biz uchun yagona mumkin va aqlli narsa va u butunlay etos, pafos emas deb o'ylaymiz — yunonlar kabi gapirib va farqlasak. Bugun bir necha musiqa notasi xayolimga bir qishni, bir uyni va mutlaq yolg'izlik hayotini, shu bilan birga o'shanda yashagan tuyg'ularimni eslatdi: men doimo shunday holatda yashay olaman deb o'ylagandim. Lekin endi tushunamanki, bu butunlay pafos va ehtiros edi, bu og'riqli dadil va chinakam tasalli beruvchi musiqaga qiyoslasa bo'ladigan narsa, — bu tuyg'ularni yillar davomida, abadiyatlar davomida esa yana ham kamroq his qilish odamning qismati emas: aks holda odam bu sayyora uchun haddan tashqari «efir»li bo'lib qolardi.
