chapters.recap_uz: Nitsshe «qilma, voz kech» deydigan axloqni yoqtirmaydi: odam qiladigan ishi bilan keraksiz narsalarni tashlaydi. Stoik va epikurchi, tanqid foydasiga, to'lqinlar — iroda timsoli, azob — «itim», payg'ambar odamlarning azobi.

chapters.title: Life as a means to knowledge

paras.en: 318. Wisdom in Pain. — In pain there is as much wisdom as in pleasure: like the latter it is one of the best self-preservatives of a species. Were it not so, pain would long ago have been done away with; that it is hurtful is no argument against it, for to be hurtful is its very essence. In pain I hear the commanding call of the ship's captain: "Take in sail!" "Man," the bold seafarer, must have learned to set his sails in a thousand different ways, otherwise he could not have sailed long, for the ocean would soon have swallowed him up.
paras.uz: 318. Og'riqdagi donolik. — Og'riqda lazzatdagi kabi donolik bor: lazzat kabi u ham turning eng yaxshi o'zini saqlash vositalaridan biri. Agar shunday bo'lmaganida, og'riq allaqachon yo'q qilingan bo'lardi; uning zararli ekani unga qarshi dalil emas, chunki zararli bo'lish uning mohiyatining o'zi. Og'riqda men kema kapitanining buyruq chaqirig'ini eshitaman: «Yelkanlarni yig'!» Jasur dengizchi «inson» yelkanlarini ming xil usulda o'rnatishni o'rgangan bo'lishi kerak, aks holda u uzoq suza olmasdi, chunki okean uni tez orada yutib yuborardi.

paras.en: We must also know how to live with reduced energy: as soon as pain gives its precautionary signal, it is time to reduce the speed—some great danger, some storm, is approaching, and we do well to "catch" as little wind as possible.—It is true that there are men who, on the approach of severe pain, hear the very opposite call of command, and never appear more proud, more martial, or more happy, than when the storm is brewing; indeed, pain itself provides them with their supreme moments! These are the heroic men, the great pain-bringers of mankind: those few and rare ones who need just the same apology as pain generally,—and verily, it should not be denied them! They are forces of the greatest importance for preserving and advancing the species, were it only because they are opposed to smug ease, and do not conceal their disgust at this kind of happiness.
paras.uz: Biz kamaytirilgan kuch bilan yashashni ham bilishimiz kerak: og'riq o'zining ehtiyot signalini berishi bilanoq, tezlikni kamaytirish vaqti keldi — qandaydir katta xavf, qandaydir bo'ron yaqinlashmoqda va iloji boricha kam shamol «ushlasak» yaxshi qilamiz. — To'g'ri, shunday odamlar borki, qattiq og'riq yaqinlashganda aynan qarama-qarshi buyruq chaqirig'ini eshitadi va bo'ron yetilayotgandagidan ko'ra hech qachon mag'rurroq, jangovarroq yoki baxtliroq ko'rinmaydi; haqiqatan ham, og'riqning o'zi ularga eng oliy lahzalarini beradi! Bular qahramon odamlar, insoniyatning buyuk og'riq keltiruvchilari: umuman og'riqqa kerak bo'lgan uzrga muhtoj bo'lgan o'sha kam va kamyob odamlar, — va haqiqatan ham, bu ulardan ayanmasligi kerak! Ular turni saqlash va rivojlantirish uchun eng katta ahamiyatga ega kuchlar, hatto faqat o'zidan mamnun farovonlikka qarshi bo'lgani va bunday baxtga jirkanishlarini yashirmagani uchun ham.

paras.en: 319. As Interpreters of our Experiences. — One form of honesty has always been lacking among founders of religions and their kin:—they have never made their experiences a matter of the intellectual conscience. "What did I really experience? What then took place in me and around me? Was my understanding clear enough? Was my will directly opposed to all deception of the senses, and courageous in its defence against fantastic notions?"—None of them ever asked these questions, nor to this day do any of the good religious people ask them. They have rather a thirst for things which are contrary to reason, and they don't want to have too much difficulty in satisfying this thirst,—so they experience "miracles" and "regenerations," and hear the voices of angels! But we who are different, who are thirsty for reason, want to look as carefully into our experiences, as in the case of a scientific experiment, hour by hour, day by day! We ourselves want to be our own experiments, and our own subjects of experiment.
paras.uz: 319. Tajribalarimiz talqinchilari sifatida. — Din asoschilari va ularga o'xshashlarda halollikning bir shakli doimo yetishmagan: — ular hech qachon o'z tajribalarini aqliy vijdon masalasiga aylantirmagan. «Men aslida nimani boshdan kechirdim? O'shanda ichimda va atrofimda nima sodir bo'ldi? Aqlim yetarlicha tiniqmidi? Irodam sezgilarning har qanday aldanishiga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri qarshimidi va xayoliy tushunchalarga qarshi himoyada jasurmidi?» — Ularning hech biri bu savollarni hech qachon bermagan, bugungacha ham yaxshi dindorlarning hech biri ularni bermaydi. Ularda ko'proq aqlga zid narsalarga tashnalik bor va ular bu tashnalikni qondirishda haddan tashqari qiynalishni istamaydi, — shuning uchun ular «mo''jizalar» va «qayta tug'ilishlar»ni boshdan kechirishadi va farishtalarning ovozlarini eshitishadi! Lekin biz, boshqacha bo'lganlar, aqlga tashna bo'lganlar, tajribalarimizga ilmiy tajriba holatidagidek soatma-soat, kunma-kun diqqat bilan qarashni istaymiz! Biz o'zimiz o'z tajribalarimiz va o'z tajriba obyektlarimiz bo'lishni istaymiz.

paras.en: 320. On Meeting Again. — A: Do I quite understand you? You are in search of something? Where, in the midst of the present, actual world, is your niche and star? Where can you lay yourself in the sun, so that you also may have a surplus of well-being, that your existence may justify itself? Let everyone do that for himself—you seem to say, —and let him put talk about generalities, concern about others and society, out of his mind!—B: I want more; I am no seeker. I want to create my own sun for myself.
paras.uz: 320. Qayta uchrashganda. — A: Sizni to'liq tushunyapmanmi? Siz nimanidir izlayapsizmi? Hozirgi, haqiqiy dunyoning o'rtasida sizning burchagingiz va yulduzingiz qayerda? O'zingizni qayerda quyoshga yotqizishingiz mumkin, toki sizda ham farovonlik ortiqchaligi bo'lsin, mavjudligingiz o'zini oqlasin? Har kim buni o'zi uchun qilsin — go'yo aytmoqchidek ko'rinasiz — va umumiy narsalar haqidagi gaplarni, boshqalar va jamiyat haqidagi tashvishni xayolidan chiqarib tashlasin! — B: Men ko'proq narsani istayman; men izlovchi emasman. Men o'zim uchun o'z quyoshimni yaratmoqchiman.

paras.en: 321. A New Precaution. — Let us no longer think so much about punishing, blaming, and improving! We shall seldom be able to alter an individual, and if we should succeed in doing so, something else may also succeed, perhaps unawares: we may have been altered by him! Let us rather see to it that our own influence on all that is to come outweighs and overweighs his influence! Let us not struggle in direct conflict!—all blaming, punishing, and desire to improve comes under this category. But let us elevate ourselves all the higher! Let us ever give to our pattern more shining colours! Let us obscure the other by our light! No! We do not mean to become darker ourselves on his account, like all that punish and are discontented! Let us rather go aside! Let us look away!
paras.uz: 321. Yangi ehtiyot chorasi. — Endi jazolash, ayblash va yaxshilash haqida shunchalik ko'p o'ylamaylik! Biz shaxsni kamdan-kam o'zgartira olamiz va agar buni uddalasak, boshqa narsa ham, balki bexabar, muvaffaqiyatli bo'lishi mumkin: u bizni o'zgartirgan bo'lishi mumkin! Yaxshisi, kelajakdagi hamma narsaga o'z ta'sirimiz uning ta'siridan ustun va og'irroq bo'lishiga harakat qilaylik! To'g'ridan-to'g'ri to'qnashuvda kurashmaylik! — barcha ayblash, jazolash va yaxshilash istagi shu toifaga kiradi. Balki o'zimizni yanada yuqoriroq ko'taraylik! Namunamizga doimo yorqinroq ranglar beraylik! Boshqasini nurimiz bilan xiralashtiraylik! Yo'q! Biz barcha jazolovchilar va noroziylar kabi uning tufayli o'zimiz qorayishni istamaymiz! Yaxshisi chetga chiqaylik! Boshqa tomonga qaraylik!

paras.en: 322. A Simile. — Those thinkers in whom all the stars move in cyclic orbits, are not the most profound. He who looks into himself, as into an immense universe, and carries Milky Ways in himself, knows also how irregular all Milky Ways are; they lead into the very chaos and labyrinth of existence.
paras.uz: 322. O'xshatish. — Ichida barcha yulduzlar siklik orbitalarda harakatlanadigan mutafakkirlar eng chuqurlari emas. O'ziga ulkan koinotga qaragandek qaraydigan va ichida Somon yo'llarini olib yuradigan odam barcha Somon yo'llari qanchalik notekis ekanini ham biladi; ular hayotning aynan xaosi va labirintiga olib boradi.

paras.en: 323. Happiness in Destiny. — Destiny confers its greatest distinction upon us when it has made us fight for a time on the side of our adversaries. We are thereby predestined to a great victory.
paras.uz: 323. Taqdirdagi baxt. — Taqdir bizni bir muddat raqiblarimiz tarafida jang qilishga majbur qilganda, bizga eng katta farqini beradi. Shu bilan biz buyuk g'alabaga oldindan tayinlanamiz.

paras.en: 324. In Media Vita. — No! Life has not deceived me! On the contrary, from year to year I find it richer, more desirable and more mysterious—from the day on which the great liberator broke my fetters, the thought that life may be an experiment of the thinker—and not a duty, not a fatality, not a deceit!—And knowledge itself may be for others something different; for example, a bed of ease, or the path to a bed of ease, or an entertainment, or a course of idling,—for me it is a world of dangers and victories, in which even the heroic sentiments have their arena and dancing-floor. "Life as a means to knowledge"—with this principle in one's heart, one can not only be brave, but can even live joyfully and laugh joyfully! And who could know how to laugh well and live well, who did not first understand the full meaning of war and victory!
paras.uz: 324. In media vita — Hayotning o'rtasida. — Yo'q! Hayot meni aldamadi! Aksincha, yildan-yilga uni boyroq, orzu qilinadiganroq va sirliroq topyapman — buyuk ozod qiluvchi kishanlarimni sindirgan kundan boshlab, hayot mutafakkirning tajribasi bo'lishi mumkin degan fikr — burch emas, halokat emas, aldov emas! — Va bilimning o'zi boshqalar uchun boshqa narsa bo'lishi mumkin; masalan, orom to'shagi yoki orom to'shagiga yo'l, yoki ermak, yoki bekorchilik yo'li, — men uchun u xavflar va g'alabalar dunyosi, unda hatto qahramonona tuyg'ularning ham o'z maydoni va raqs maydoni bor. «Hayot bilimga vosita sifatida» — yurakda shu tamoyil bilan odam nafaqat jasur bo'la oladi, balki hatto quvnoq yashay oladi va quvnoq kula oladi! Va urush va g'alabaning to'liq ma'nosini avval tushunmagan kim yaxshi kulishni va yaxshi yashashni bila oladi!

paras.en: 325. What Belongs to Greatness. — Who can attain to anything great if he does not feel the force and will in himself to inflict great pain? The ability to suffer is a small matter: in that line, weak women and even slaves often attain masterliness. But not to perish from internal distress and doubt when one inflicts great anguish and hears the cry of this anguish—that is great, that belongs to greatness.
paras.uz: 325. Buyuklikka nima tegishli. — Agar odam o'zida katta og'riq berish kuchi va irodasini his qilmasa, kim buyuk narsaga erisha oladi? Azob chekish qobiliyati kichik narsa: bu borada zaif ayollar va hatto qullar ham ko'pincha mahoratga erishadi. Lekin katta iztirob berib, bu iztirobning qichqirig'ini eshitganda ichki qayg'u va shubhadan halok bo'lmaslik — bu buyuk, bu buyuklikka tegishli.

paras.en: 326. Physicians of the Soul and Pain. — All preachers of morality, as also all theologians, have a bad habit in common: all of them try to persuade man that he is very ill, and that a severe, final, radical cure is necessary. And because mankind as a whole has for centuries listened too eagerly to those teachers, something of the superstition that the human race is in a very bad way has actually come over men: so that they are now far too ready to sigh; they find nothing more in life and make melancholy faces at each other, as if life were indeed very hard to endure. In truth, they are inordinately assured of their life and in love with it, and full of untold intrigues and subtleties for suppressing everything disagreeable and for extracting the thorn from pain and misfortune.
paras.uz: 326. Ruh shifokorlari va og'riq. — Barcha axloq va'zgo'ylari, shuningdek, barcha ilohiyotchilarning umumiy yomon odati bor: ularning hammasi insonni u juda kasal ekaniga va qattiq, oxirgi, tubdan davolash zarurligiga ishontirishga urinadi. Va insoniyat umuman olganda asrlar davomida bu o'qituvchilarni haddan tashqari ishtiyoq bilan tinglagani uchun, odamlarni haqiqatan ham inson zoti juda yomon ahvolda degan xurofotdan nimadir chulg'ab olgan: shuning uchun ular endi xo'rsinishga haddan tashqari tayyor; ular hayotda boshqa hech narsa topishmaydi va bir-biriga g'amgin yuzlar qilishadi, go'yo hayotga chidash haqiqatan ham juda og'irdek. Aslida ular o'z hayotlariga haddan tashqari ishonadi va uni sevadi, barcha yoqimsiz narsalarni bostirish va og'riq va baxtsizlikdan tikanni sug'urib olish uchun aytib bo'lmas hiylalar va nozikliklarga to'la.

paras.en: It seems to me that people always speak with exaggeration about pain and misfortune, as if it were a matter of good behaviour to exaggerate here: on the other hand people are intentionally silent in regard to the number of expedients for alleviating pain; as for instance, the deadening of it, or feverish flurry of thought, or a peaceful position, or good and bad reminiscences, intentions, hopes,—also many kinds of pride and fellow-feeling which have almost the effect of anæsthetics: while in the greatest degree of pain fainting takes place of itself. We understand very well how to pour sweetness on our bitterness, especially on the bitterness of our soul; we find a remedy in our bravery and sublimity, as well as in the nobler delirium of submission and resignation.
paras.uz: Menimcha, odamlar og'riq va baxtsizlik haqida doimo bo'rttirib gapirishadi, go'yo bu yerda bo'rttirish yaxshi odob masalasidek: boshqa tomondan, odamlar og'riqni yengillatish vositalarining soni haqida qasddan jim turishadi; masalan, uni o'tmaslashtirish, yoki fikrning isitmali shoshqaloqligi, yoki osoyishta holat, yoki yaxshi va yomon xotiralar, niyatlar, umidlar, — shuningdek, deyarli og'riqsizlantiruvchi ta'sirga ega bo'lgan ko'p turdagi g'urur va hamdardlik: og'riqning eng yuqori darajasida esa hushdan ketish o'z-o'zidan sodir bo'ladi. Biz achchiqligimizga, ayniqsa qalbimizning achchiqligiga shirinlik quyishni juda yaxshi bilamiz; biz jasoratimiz va yuksakligimizda, shuningdek, bo'ysunish va taslimlikning olijanobroq alahsirashida davo topamiz.

paras.en: A loss scarcely remains a loss for an hour: in some way or other a gift from heaven has always fallen into our lap at the same moment—a new form of strength, for example: be it but a new opportunity for the exercise of strength! What have the preachers of morality not dreamt concerning the inner "misery" of evil men! What lies have they not told us about the misfortunes of impassioned men! Yes, lying is here the right word: they were only too well aware of the overflowing happiness of this kind of man, but they kept silent as death about it; because it was a refutation of their theory, according to which happiness only originates through the annihilation of the passions and the silencing of the will!
paras.uz: Yo'qotish zo'rg'a bir soat yo'qotish bo'lib qoladi: qandaydir tarzda xuddi o'sha lahzada doimo osmondan bir sovg'a quchog'imizga tushgan — masalan, kuchning yangi shakli: hech bo'lmasa kuchni ishlatish uchun yangi imkoniyat! Axloq va'zgo'ylari yovuz odamlarning ichki «baxtsizligi» haqida nimalarni orzu qilmagan! Ehtirosli odamlarning baxtsizliklari haqida bizga qanday yolg'onlar aytmagan! Ha, bu yerda yolg'on to'g'ri so'z: ular bunday odamning to'lib-toshgan baxtini juda yaxshi bilishgan, lekin bu haqda o'likdek jim turishgan; chunki bu ularning nazariyasini rad etardi, unga ko'ra baxt faqat ehtiroslarni yo'q qilish va irodani jim qilish orqali paydo bo'ladi!

paras.en: And finally, as regards the recipe of all those physicians of the soul and their recommendation of a severe radical cure, we may be allowed to ask: Is our life really painful and burdensome enough for us to exchange it with advantage for a Stoical mode of life, and Stoical petrification? We do not feel sufficiently miserable to have to feel ill in the Stoical fashion!
paras.uz: Va nihoyat, bu barcha ruh shifokorlarining retsepti va ularning qattiq tubdan davolash tavsiyasiga kelsak, bizga so'rashga ruxsat berilsin: hayotimiz haqiqatan ham uni stoik turmush tarzi va stoik toshga aylanish bilan foydali ravishda almashtirish uchun yetarlicha og'riqli va og'irmi? Biz stoiklarcha kasal his qilishimiz kerak bo'lgan darajada o'zimizni baxtsiz his qilmaymiz!

paras.en: 327. Taking Things Seriously. — The intellect is with most people an awkward, obscure and creaking machine, which is difficult to set in motion: they call it "taking a thing seriously" when they work with this machine, and want to think well—oh, how burdensome must good thinking be to them! That delightful animal, man, seems to lose his good-humour whenever he thinks well; he becomes "serious"! And "where there is laughing and gaiety, thinking cannot be worth anything:"—so speaks the prejudice of this serious animal against all "Joyful Wisdom."—Well, then! Let us show that it is prejudice!
paras.uz: 327. Narsalarni jiddiy qabul qilish. — Ko'pchilik odamlarda aql — noqulay, qorong'i va g'ichirlaydigan mashina, uni harakatga keltirish qiyin: ular bu mashina bilan ishlaganda va yaxshi o'ylamoqchi bo'lganda buni «narsani jiddiy qabul qilish» deyishadi — oh, yaxshi o'ylash ular uchun qanchalik og'ir bo'lsa kerak! O'sha yoqimtoy hayvon — inson yaxshi o'ylaganda har safar xushfe'lligini yo'qotadiganga o'xshaydi; u «jiddiy» bo'lib qoladi! Va «kulgi va quvnoqlik bor joyda fikrlashning hech qanday qadri bo'lishi mumkin emas»: — bu jiddiy hayvonning barcha «Quvnoq ilm»ga qarshi xurofoti shunday gapiradi. — Xo'p, unday bo'lsa! Bu xurofot ekanini ko'rsataylik!

paras.en: 328. Doing Harm to Stupidity. — It is certain that the belief in the reprehensibility of egoism, preached with such stubbornness and conviction, has on the whole done harm to egoism (in favour of the herd-instinct, as I shall repeat a hundred times!), especially by depriving it of a good conscience, and bidding us seek in it the true source of all misfortune. "Thy selfishness is the bane of thy life"—so rang the preaching for millenniums: it did harm, as we have said, to selfishness, and deprived it of much spirit, much cheerfulness, much ingenuity, and much beauty; it stultified and deformed and poisoned selfishness!—Philosophical antiquity, on the other hand, taught that there was another principal source of evil: from Socrates downwards, the thinkers were never weary of preaching that "your thoughtlessness and stupidity, your unthinking way of living according to rule, and your subjection to the opinion of your neighbour, are the reasons why you so seldom attain to happiness,—we thinkers are, as thinkers, the happiest of mortals." Let us not decide here whether this preaching against stupidity was more sound than the preaching against selfishness; it is certain, however, that stupidity was thereby deprived of its good conscience:—these philosophers did harm to stupidity.
paras.uz: 328. Ahmoqlikka zarar yetkazish. — Aniqki, shunday o'jarlik va ishonch bilan va'z qilingan xudbinlikning qoralanishga loyiqligiga ishonch umuman olganda xudbinlikka zarar keltirgan (poda instinkti foydasiga, buni yuz marta takrorlayman!), ayniqsa uni toza vijdondan mahrum qilib va bizga undan barcha baxtsizliklarning haqiqiy manbasini izlashni buyurib. «Xudbinliging — hayotingning balosi» — ming yillar davomida va'z shunday yangragan: u, aytganimizdek, xudbinlikka zarar keltirdi va uni ko'p ruhdan, ko'p quvnoqlikdan, ko'p zukkolikdan va ko'p go'zallikdan mahrum qildi; u xudbinlikni ahmoqlashtirdi, buzdi va zaharladi! — Falsafiy antik davr esa, aksincha, yomonlikning boshqa asosiy manbai borligini o'rgatgan: Sokratdan boshlab mutafakkirlar «sizning o'ylamasligingiz va ahmoqligingiz, qoidaga ko'ra o'ylamay yashashingiz va qo'shningizning fikriga bo'ysunishingiz — baxtga shunchalik kam erishishingizning sabablari, — biz mutafakkirlar, mutafakkir sifatida, bandalarning eng baxtlisimiz» deb va'z qilishdan hech qachon charchamagan. Bu yerda ahmoqlikka qarshi bu va'z xudbinlikka qarshi va'zdan sog'lomroq bo'lganmi-yo'qmi, hal qilmaylik; biroq aniqki, ahmoqlik shu bilan toza vijdonidan mahrum qilingan: — bu faylasuflar ahmoqlikka zarar yetkazgan.

paras.en: 329. Leisure and Idleness. — There is an Indian savagery, a savagery peculiar to the Indian blood, in the manner in which the Americans strive after gold: and the breathless hurry of their work—the characteristic vice of the new world—already begins to infect old Europe, and makes it savage also, spreading over it a strange lack of intellectuality. One is now ashamed of repose: even long reflection almost causes remorse of conscience. Thinking is done with a stop-watch, as dining is done with the eyes fixed on the financial newspaper; we live like men who are continually "afraid of letting opportunities slip." "Better do anything whatever, than nothing"—this principle also is a noose with which all culture and all higher taste may be strangled. And just as all form obviously disappears in this hurry of workers, so the sense for form itself, the ear and the eye for the melody of movement, also disappear.
paras.uz: 329. Bo'sh vaqt va bekorchilik. — Amerikaliklarning oltinga intilish tarzida hindcha vahshiylik, hind qoniga xos vahshiylik bor: va ularning ishidagi nafasni tiqadigan shoshqaloqlik — yangi dunyoning o'ziga xos illati — allaqachon eski Yevropaga yuqa boshlagan va uni ham vahshiylashtirib, ustiga g'alati aqlsizlikni yoymoqda. Endi odam osoyishtalikdan uyaladi: hatto uzoq mulohaza ham deyarli vijdon azobini keltiradi. Fikrlash sekundomer bilan qilinadi, xuddi tushlik ko'zlarni moliyaviy gazetaga qadab qilingani kabi; biz doimo «imkoniyatni qo'ldan boy berishdan qo'rqadigan» odamlardek yashaymiz. «Hech narsa qilmagandan ko'ra har qanday ishni qilgan yaxshiroq» — bu tamoyil ham barcha madaniyat va barcha yuksak didni bo'g'ib o'ldirish mumkin bo'lgan sirtmoq. Va bu ishchilar shoshqaloqligida har qanday shakl yaqqol yo'qolgani kabi, shakl tuyg'usining o'zi, harakat kuyiga quloq va ko'z ham yo'qoladi.

paras.en: The proof of this is the clumsy perspicuity which is now everywhere demanded in all positions where a person would like to be sincere with his fellows, in intercourse with friends, women, relatives, children, teachers, pupils, leaders and princes,—one has no longer either time or energy for ceremonies, for roundabout courtesies, for any esprit in conversation, or for any otium whatever. For life in the hunt for gain continually compels a person to consume his intellect, even to exhaustion, in constant dissimulation, overreaching, or forestalling: the real virtue nowadays is to do something in a shorter time than another person. And so there are only rare hours of sincere intercourse permitted: in them, however, people are tired, and would not only like "to let themselves go," but to stretch their legs out wide in awkward style.
paras.uz: Buning isboti — odam o'z yaqinlari bilan samimiy bo'lishni istagan barcha holatlarda, do'stlar, ayollar, qarindoshlar, bolalar, o'qituvchilar, o'quvchilar, rahbarlar va shahzodalar bilan muloqotda endi hamma joyda talab qilinadigan qo'pol ravshanlik, — endi marosimlar uchun, aylanma xushmuomalaliklar uchun, suhbatdagi har qanday esprit uchun yoki har qanday otium — bo'sh vaqt uchun na vaqt, na kuch bor. Chunki foyda ovidagi hayot odamni doimo aqlini doimiy niqoblanish, aldash yoki o'zib ketishda, hatto holdan toygunicha sarflashga majbur qiladi: hozirgi haqiqiy fazilat — biror ishni boshqa odamdan qisqaroq vaqtda qilish. Shuning uchun samimiy muloqotning faqat kamyob soatlariga ruxsat beriladi: biroq ularda odamlar charchagan va nafaqat «o'zini bo'shatib yuborishni», balki oyoqlarini noqulay tarzda keng cho'zishni ham istashadi.

paras.en: The way people write their letters nowadays is quite in keeping with the age; their style and spirit will always be the true "sign of the times." If there be still enjoyment in society and in art, it is enjoyment such as over-worked slaves provide for themselves. Oh, this moderation in "joy" of our cultured and uncultured classes! Oh, this increasing suspiciousness of all enjoyment! Work is winning over more and more the good conscience to its side: the desire for enjoyment already calls itself "need of recreation," and even begins to be ashamed of itself. "One owes it to one's health," people say, when they are caught at a picnic. Indeed, it might soon go so far that one could not yield to the desire for the vita contemplativa (that is to say, excursions with thoughts and friends), without self-contempt and a bad conscience.—Well!
paras.uz: Odamlarning hozir xat yozish tarzi davrga juda mos; ularning uslubi va ruhi doimo haqiqiy «zamon belgisi» bo'lib qoladi. Agar jamiyatda va san'atda hali ham zavq bo'lsa, bu haddan tashqari ishlagan qullar o'zlariga beradigan zavqdir. Oh, madaniyatli va madaniyatsiz tabaqalarimizning «quvonch»dagi bu mo'tadilligi! Oh, har qanday zavqqa bu ortib borayotgan shubha! Ish tobora ko'proq toza vijdonni o'z tarafiga og'dirmoqda: zavqqa bo'lgan istak allaqachon o'zini «dam olish ehtiyoji» deb ataydi va hatto o'zidan uyala boshlaydi. «Buni sog'lig'imiz uchun qilishimiz kerak», — deyishadi odamlar sayohatda tutib olinganda. Haqiqatan ham, tez orada shu darajaga borishi mumkinki, odam vita contemplativa'ga (ya'ni fikrlar va do'stlar bilan sayrlarga) bo'lgan istakka o'zidan nafratlanish va yomon vijdonsiz berila olmaydi. — Xo'p!

paras.en: Formerly it was the very reverse: it was "action" that suffered from a bad conscience. A man of good family concealed his work when need compelled him to labour. The slave laboured under the weight of the feeling that he did something contemptible:—the "doing" itself was something contemptible. "Only in otium and bellum is there nobility and honour:" so rang the voice of ancient prejudice!
paras.uz: Ilgari aynan aksincha edi: yomon vijdondan aziyat chekkan narsa «harakat» edi. Yaxshi oiladan bo'lgan odam ehtiyoj uni mehnat qilishga majbur qilganda ishini yashirardi. Qul jirkanch ish qilyapman degan tuyg'u og'irligi ostida mehnat qilardi: — «qilish»ning o'zi jirkanch narsa edi. «Faqat otium va bellum'dagina — bo'sh vaqt va urushdagina zodagonlik va sharaf bor»: qadimiy xurofotning ovozi shunday yangragan!

paras.en: 330. Applause. — The thinker does not need applause nor the clapping of hands, provided he be sure of the clapping of his own hands: the latter, however, he cannot do without. Are there men who could also do without this, and in general without any kind of applause? I doubt it: and even as regards the wisest, Tacitus, who is no calumniator of the wise, says: quando etiam sapientibus gloriæ cupido novissima exuitur—that means with him: never.
paras.uz: 330. Olqish. — Mutafakkirga olqish ham, qarsak ham kerak emas, faqat o'z qo'llarining qarsagiga ishonchi komil bo'lsa bas: biroq ikkinchisiz u qila olmaydi. Bunisiz ham, umuman har qanday olqishsiz ham qila oladigan odamlar bormi? Shubhalanaman: hatto eng donolarga kelsak ham, donolarga tuhmat qilmaydigan Tatsit shunday deydi: quando etiam sapientibus gloriae cupido novissima exuitur — hatto donolar ham shon-shuhrat istagini eng oxirida tashlaydi — bu uningcha: hech qachon degani.

quiz.q: What principle lets one live joyfully, according to aphorism 324?
o: Life as a means to knowledge
quiz.why_uz: «Hayot bilimga vosita sifatida».

quiz.q: What does pain say, like a ship's captain?
quiz.why_uz: Og'riq — kuchni kamaytirish uchun ehtiyot signali.

chapters.recap_uz: Og'riqda ham donolik bor — u «yelkanlarni yig'!» deydi. Din asoschilari tajribalarini aqliy vijdon bilan tekshirmagan. «Hayot meni aldamadi»: hayot — mutafakkirning tajribasi. Buyuklik — katta og'riq berib ham halok bo'lmaslik; zamonaviy shoshqaloqlik madaniyatni o'ldiradi.

chapters.title: One must learn to love

paras.en: 331. Better Deaf than Deafened. — Formerly a person wanted to have a calling, but that no longer suffices to-day, for the market has become too large,—there has now to be bawling. The consequence is that even good throats outcry each other, and the best wares are offered for sale with hoarse voices; without market-place bawling and hoarseness there is now no longer any genius.—It is, sure enough, an evil age for the thinker: he has to learn to find his stillness betwixt two noises, and has to pretend to be deaf until he finally becomes so. As long as he has not learned this, he is in danger of perishing from impatience and headaches.
paras.uz: 331. Kar qilinganidan kar bo'lgan yaxshi. — Ilgari odam o'z kasbiga ega bo'lishni istardi, lekin bugun bu endi yetarli emas, chunki bozor haddan tashqari katta bo'lib ketdi, — endi baqirish kerak. Natijada hatto yaxshi tomoqlar ham bir-birini bosib qichqiradi va eng yaxshi mollar bo'g'iq ovozlar bilan sotuvga qo'yiladi; bozor baqirig'i va bo'g'iqliksiz endi hech qanday daho yo'q. — Albatta, bu mutafakkir uchun yomon davr: u ikki shovqin orasida o'z sukunatini topishni o'rganishi va oxir-oqibat kar bo'lmaguncha o'zini kar qilib ko'rsatishi kerak. Buni o'rganmagunicha u sabrsizlik va bosh og'rig'idan halok bo'lish xavfi ostida.

paras.en: 332. The Evil Hour. — There has perhaps been an evil hour for every philosopher, in which he thought: What do I matter, if people should not believe my poor arguments!—And then some malicious bird has flown past him and twittered: "What do you matter? What do you matter?"
paras.uz: 332. Yomon soat. — Ehtimol, har bir faylasufning yomon soati bo'lgandir, unda u o'ylagan: Agar odamlar mening bechora dalillarimga ishonmasa, men nimaman! — Va keyin qandaydir g'arazli qush uning yonidan uchib o'tib, chug'urlagan: «Sen nimasan? Sen nimasan?»

paras.en: 333. What does Knowing Mean?. — Non ridere, non lugere, neque detestari, sed intelligere! says Spinoza, so simply and sublimely, as is his wont. Nevertheless, what else is this intelligere ultimately, but just the form in which the three other things become perceptible to us all at once? A result of the diverging and opposite impulses of desiring to deride, lament and execrate? Before knowledge is possible each of these impulses must first have brought forward its one-sided view of the object or event. The struggle of these one-sided views occurs afterwards, and out of it there occasionally arises a compromise, a pacification, a recognition of rights on all three sides, a sort of justice and agreement: for in virtue of the justice and agreement all those impulses can maintain themselves in existence and retain their mutual rights.
paras.uz: 333. Bilish nimani anglatadi? — Non ridere, non lugere, neque detestari, sed intelligere! — Kulma, yig'lama, la'natlama, balki tushun! — deydi Spinoza, o'ziga xos tarzda shunchalik oddiy va yuksak. Shunga qaramay, bu intelligere — tushunish oxir-oqibat boshqa uch narsa bizga birdaniga sezilarli bo'ladigan shakldan boshqa nima? Masxara qilish, nola qilish va la'natlash istagining ajraluvchi va qarama-qarshi mayllarining natijasi? Bilish mumkin bo'lishidan oldin bu mayllarning har biri avval obyekt yoki voqea haqidagi o'zining bir tomonlama qarashini oldinga surishi kerak. Bu bir tomonlama qarashlarning kurashi keyin sodir bo'ladi va undan ba'zan murosa, tinchlanish, uchala tomonning huquqlarini tan olish, qandaydir adolat va kelishuv paydo bo'ladi: chunki adolat va kelishuv tufayli bu mayllarning hammasi o'zini mavjudlikda saqlab, o'zaro huquqlarini saqlay oladi.

paras.en: We, to whose consciousness only the closing reconciliation scenes and final settling of accounts of these long processes manifest themselves, think on that account that intelligere is something conciliating, just and good, something essentially antithetical to the impulses; whereas it is only a certain relation of the impulses to one another. For a very long time conscious thinking was regarded as thinking proper: it is now only that the truth dawns upon us that the greater part of our intellectual activity goes on unconsciously and unfelt by us; I believe, however, that the impulses which are here in mutual conflict understand right well how to make themselves felt by one another, and how to cause pain:—the violent, sudden exhaustion which overtakes all thinkers, may have its origin here (it is the exhaustion of the battle-field).
paras.uz: Ongimizga bu uzoq jarayonlarning faqat yakuniy yarashish sahnalari va oxirgi hisob-kitoblari namoyon bo'ladigan biz shuning uchun intelligere yarashtiruvchi, adolatli va yaxshi narsa, mohiyatan mayllarga qarama-qarshi narsa deb o'ylaymiz; holbuki u faqat mayllarning bir-biriga ma'lum munosabati. Juda uzoq vaqt davomida ongli fikrlash haqiqiy fikrlash deb hisoblangan: faqat endigina bizga aqliy faoliyatimizning katta qismi ongsiz va bizga sezilmay kechishi haqidagi haqiqat ayon bo'lmoqda; biroq ishonamanki, bu yerda o'zaro kurashayotgan mayllar bir-biriga o'zlarini his qildirishni va og'riq berishni juda yaxshi tushunadi: — barcha mutafakkirlarni chulg'ab oladigan shiddatli, to'satdan holsizlik shu yerdan kelib chiqqan bo'lishi mumkin (bu jang maydonining holsizligi).

paras.en: Aye, perhaps in our struggling interior there is much concealed heroism, but certainly nothing divine, or eternally-reposing-in-itself, as Spinoza supposed. Conscious thinking, and especially that of the philosopher, is the weakest, and on that account also the relatively mildest and quietest mode of thinking: and thus it is precisely the philosopher who is most easily misled concerning the nature of knowledge.
paras.uz: Ha, balki bizning kurashayotgan ichki dunyomizda ko'p yashirin qahramonlik bordir, lekin Spinoza faraz qilganidek ilohiy yoki abadiy o'zida orom olayotgan hech narsa yo'q. Ongli fikrlash, ayniqsa faylasufniki, eng zaif va shuning uchun nisbatan eng yumshoq va eng sokin fikrlash tarzi: shuning uchun aynan faylasuf bilimning tabiati haqida eng oson adashadi.

paras.en: 334. One must Learn to Love. — This is our experience in music: we must first learn in general to hear, to hear fully, and to distinguish a theme or a melody, we have to isolate and limit it as a life by itself; then we need to exercise effort and good-will in order to endure it in spite of its strangeness, we need patience towards its aspect and expression, and indulgence towards what is odd in it:—in the end there comes a moment when we are accustomed to it, when we expect it, when it dawns upon us that we should miss it if it were lacking; and then it goes on to exercise its spell and charm more and more, and does not cease until we have become its humble and enraptured lovers, who want it, and want it again, and ask for nothing better from the world.—It is thus with us, however, not only in music: it is precisely thus that we have learned to love all things that we now love.
paras.uz: 334. Sevishni o'rganish kerak. — Musiqada tajribamiz shunday: avval umuman eshitishni, to'liq eshitishni va mavzu yoki kuyni ajratishni o'rganishimiz kerak, uni alohida hayot sifatida ajratib, chegaralashimiz kerak; keyin uning g'alatiligiga qaramay unga chidash uchun harakat va yaxshi niyat ko'rsatishimiz, uning qiyofasi va ifodasiga sabr, undagi g'alati narsalarga muruvvat ko'rsatishimiz kerak: — oxirida unga odatlanadigan, uni kutadigan, agar u yo'q bo'lsa sog'inishimiz ayon bo'ladigan lahza keladi; keyin u o'z sehri va jozibasini tobora ko'proq ko'rsatishda davom etadi va biz uning kamtarin va vajdga tushgan oshiqlariga aylanmagunimizcha to'xtamaydi, uni istaymiz, yana istaymiz va dunyodan undan yaxshiroq narsa so'ramaymiz. — Biroq biz bilan faqat musiqada emas shunday: biz hozir sevadigan barcha narsalarni aynan shu tarzda sevishni o'rganganmiz.

paras.en: We are always finally recompensed for our good-will, our patience, reasonableness and gentleness towards what is unfamiliar, by the unfamiliar slowly throwing off its veil and presenting itself to us as a new, ineffable beauty:—that is its thanks for our hospitality. He also who loves himself must have learned it in this way: there is no other way. Love also has to be learned.
paras.uz: Biz notanish narsaga nisbatan yaxshi niyatimiz, sabrimiz, aqlliligimiz va muloyimligimiz uchun oxir-oqibat doimo mukofotlanamiz, notanish narsa asta-sekin pardasini tashlab, bizga yangi, ta'riflab bo'lmas go'zallik sifatida namoyon bo'ladi: — bu uning mehmondo'stligimiz uchun minnatdorligi. O'zini sevadigan odam ham buni shu yo'l bilan o'rgangan bo'lishi kerak: boshqa yo'l yo'q. Sevgini ham o'rganish kerak.

paras.en: 335. Cheers for Physics!. — How many men are there who know how to observe? And among the few who do know,—how many observe themselves? "Everyone is furthest from himself"—all the "triers of the reins" know that to their discomfort; and the saying, "Know thyself," in the mouth of a God and spoken to man, is almost a mockery. But that the case of self-observation is so desperate, is attested best of all by the manner in which almost everybody talks of the nature of a moral action, that prompt, willing, convinced, loquacious manner, with its look, its smile, and its pleasing eagerness! Everyone seems inclined to say to you: "Why, my dear Sir, that is precisely my affair! You address yourself with your question to him who is authorised to answer, for I happen to be wiser with regard to this matter than in anything else.
paras.uz: 335. Fizikaga olqish! — Kuzatishni biladigan odamlar qancha? Va biladigan ozchilik orasida — o'zini qanchasi kuzatadi? «Har kim o'zidan eng uzoq» — barcha «yuraklarni sinovchilar» buni o'z noqulayliklariga biladi; va Xudoning og'zidan insonga aytilgan «O'zingni bil» so'zi deyarli masxara. Lekin o'zini kuzatish holatining shunchalik umidsiz ekanini eng yaxshi deyarli har kimning axloqiy harakatning tabiati haqida gapirish tarzi — o'sha tez, bajonidil, ishonchli, ezma tarz, o'z nigohi, tabassumi va yoqimli ishtiyoqi bilan tasdiqlaydi! Har kim sizga go'yo shunday demoqchi: «Axir, aziz janob, bu aynan mening ishim! Siz savolingiz bilan javob berishga vakolatli odamga murojaat qilyapsiz, chunki men bu masalada boshqa har qanday narsadan ko'ra donoroqman.

paras.en: Therefore, when a man decides that 'this is right,' when he accordingly concludes that 'it must therefore be done,' and thereupon does what he has thus recognised as right and designated as necessary—then the nature of his action is moral!" But, my friend, you are talking to me about three actions instead of one: your deciding, for instance, that "this is right," is also an action,—could one not judge either morally or immorally? Why do you regard this, and just this, as right?—"Because my conscience tells me so; conscience never speaks immorally, indeed it determines in the first place what shall be moral!"—But why do you listen to the voice of your conscience? And in how far are you justified in regarding such a judgment as true and infallible? This belief—is there no further conscience for it? Do you know nothing of an intellectual conscience? A conscience behind your "conscience"?
paras.uz: Demak, odam "bu to'g'ri" deb qaror qilganda, shunga ko'ra "demak, buni qilish kerak" degan xulosaga kelganda va keyin shu tariqa to'g'ri deb tan olgan va zarur deb belgilagan narsani qilganda — uning harakatining tabiati axloqiy!» Lekin, do'stim, siz menga bitta emas, uchta harakat haqida gapiryapsiz: masalan, sizning "bu to'g'ri" degan qaroringiz ham harakat, — uni axloqiy yoki axloqsiz baholab bo'lmaydimi? Nega aynan buni, faqat buni to'g'ri deb bilasiz? — «Chunki vijdonim menga shunday deydi; vijdon hech qachon axloqsiz gapirmaydi, haqiqatan ham u birinchi navbatda nima axloqiy bo'lishini belgilaydi!» — Lekin nega vijdoningizning ovoziga quloq solasiz? Va bunday hukmni to'g'ri va xatosiz deb hisoblashga qanchalik haqlisiz? Bu ishonch — uning uchun boshqa vijdon yo'qmi? Aqliy vijdon haqida hech narsa bilmaysizmi? Sizning «vijdoningiz» ortidagi vijdon haqida?

paras.en: Your decision, "this is right," has a previous history in your impulses, your likes and dislikes, your experiences and non-experiences; "how has it originated?" you must ask, and afterwards the further question: "what really impels me to give ear to it?" You can listen to its command like a brave soldier who hears the command of his officer. Or like a woman who loves him who commands. Or like a flatterer and coward, afraid of the commander. Or like a blockhead who follows because he has nothing to say to the contrary. In short, you can give ear to your conscience in a hundred different ways.
paras.uz: Sizning «bu to'g'ri» degan qaroringizning mayllaringizda, yoqtirish va yoqtirmasliklaringizda, tajribalaringiz va tajribasizliklaringizda oldingi tarixi bor; «u qanday paydo bo'lgan?» deb so'rashingiz kerak, keyin esa yana bir savol: «meni unga quloq solishga aslida nima undaydi?» Siz uning buyrug'ini ofitserining buyrug'ini eshitgan jasur askar kabi tinglashingiz mumkin. Yoki buyurayotgan odamni sevadigan ayol kabi. Yoki buyuruvchidan qo'rqadigan xushomadgo'y va qo'rqoq kabi. Yoki aksini aytishga gapi bo'lmagani uchun ergashadigan kallavaram kabi. Qisqasi, vijdoningizga yuzta turli yo'l bilan quloq solishingiz mumkin.

paras.en: But that you hear this or that judgment as the voice of conscience, consequently, that you feel a thing to be right—may have its cause in the fact that you have never reflected about yourself, and have blindly accepted from your childhood what has been designated to you as right: or in the fact that hitherto bread and honours have fallen to your share with that which you call your duty,—it is "right" to you, because it seems to be your "condition of existence" (that you, however, have a right to existence appears to you as irrefutable!). The persistency of your moral judgment might still be just a proof of personal wretchedness or impersonality; your "moral force" might have its source in your obstinacy—or in your incapacity to perceive new ideals!
paras.uz: Lekin siz u yoki bu hukmni vijdon ovozi sifatida eshitishingiz, demak, biror narsani to'g'ri deb his qilishingiz o'zingiz haqingizda hech qachon mulohaza qilmaganingiz va bolaligingizdan sizga to'g'ri deb belgilangan narsani ko'r-ko'rona qabul qilganingiz sababli bo'lishi mumkin: yoki shu paytgacha burchim deb ataydigan narsa bilan sizga non va sharaf nasib etgani sababli, — u siz uchun «to'g'ri», chunki u sizning «yashash shartingiz» bo'lib ko'rinadi (biroq yashashga haqqingiz borligi sizga rad etib bo'lmaydigan bo'lib ko'rinadi!). Axloqiy hukmingizning qat'iyligi hali ham shunchaki shaxsiy bechoralik yoki shaxssizlikning isboti bo'lishi mumkin; sizning «axloqiy kuchingiz» o'jarligingizdan — yoki yangi ideallarni ko'ra olmasligingizdan kelib chiqishi mumkin!

paras.en: And to be brief: if you had thought more acutely, observed more accurately, and had learned more, you would no longer under all circumstances call this and that your "duty" and your "conscience": the knowledge how moral judgments have in general always originated, would make you tired of these pathetic words,—as you have already grown tired of other pathetic words, for instance "sin," "salvation," and "redemption."—And now, my friend, do not talk to me about the categorical imperative! That word tickles my ear, and I must laugh in spite of your presence and your seriousness.
paras.uz: Qisqasi: agar siz o'tkirroq o'ylaganingizda, aniqroq kuzatganingizda va ko'proq o'rganganingizda, endi har qanday sharoitda buni va uni «burchim» va «vijdonim» demagan bo'lardingiz: axloqiy hukmlar umuman doimo qanday paydo bo'lganini bilish sizni bu pafosli so'zlardan bezdirardi, — xuddi siz allaqachon boshqa pafosli so'zlardan, masalan, «gunoh», «najot» va «qutqarilish»dan bezganingiz kabi. — Endi esa, do'stim, menga kategorik imperativ haqida gapirmang! Bu so'z qulog'imni qitiqlaydi va sizning hozirligingiz va jiddiyligingizga qaramay kulishim kerak.

paras.en: In this connection I recollect old Kant, who, as a punishment for having gained possession surreptitiously of the "thing in itself"—also a very ludicrous affair!—was imposed upon by the categorical imperative, and with that in his heart strayed back again to "God," the "soul," "freedom," and "immortality," like a fox which strays back into its cage: and it had been his strength and shrewdness which had broken open this cage!—What? You admire the categorical imperative in you? This "persistency" of your so-called moral judgment? This absoluteness of the feeling that "as I think on this matter, so must everyone think"? Admire rather your selfishness therein! And the blindness, paltriness, and modesty of your selfishness!
paras.uz: Shu munosabat bilan keksa Kant esimga tushadi, u «narsaning o'zi»ni yashirincha qo'lga kiritgani uchun jazo sifatida — bu ham juda kulgili ish! — kategorik imperativ tomonidan aldandi va u bilan yuragida yana «Xudo», «ruh», «erkinlik» va «o'lmaslik»ka qaytib adashdi, xuddi qafasiga qaytib adashgan tulkidek: va bu qafasni buzib ochgan uning kuchi va ziyrakligi edi! — Nima? Siz o'zingizdagi kategorik imperativga qoyil qolasizmi? Axloqiy deb ataladigan hukmingizning bu «qat'iyligi»ga? «Men bu masalada qanday o'ylasam, hamma shunday o'ylashi kerak» degan tuyg'uning bu mutlaqligiga? Yaxshisi undagi xudbinligingizga qoyil qoling! Va xudbinligingizning ko'rligi, arzimasligi va kamtarligiga!

paras.en: For it is selfishness in a person to regard his judgment as universal law, and a blind, paltry and modest selfishness besides, because it betrays that you have not yet discovered yourself, that you have not yet created for yourself any individual, quite individual ideal:—for this could never be the ideal of another, to say nothing of all, of every one!——He who still thinks that "each would have to act in this manner in this case," has not yet advanced half a dozen paces in self-knowledge: otherwise he would know that there neither are nor can be similar actions,—that every action that has been done, has been done in an entirely unique and inimitable manner, and that it will be the same with regard to all future actions; that all precepts of conduct (and even the most esoteric and subtle precepts of all moralities up to the present), apply only to the coarse exterior,—that by means of them, indeed, a semblance of equality can be attained, but only a semblance,—that in outlook or retrospect, every action is and remains an impenetrable affair,—that our opinions of "good," "noble" and "great" can never be demonstrated by our actions, because no action is cognisable,—that our opinions, estimates, and tables of values are certainly among the most powerful levers in the mechanism of our actions, that in every single case, nevertheless, the law of their mechanism is untraceable.
paras.uz: Chunki odamning o'z hukmini umumiy qonun deb hisoblashi xudbinlik, buning ustiga ko'r, arzimas va kamtar xudbinlik, chunki bu siz hali o'zingizni kashf etmaganingizni, o'zingiz uchun hech qanday shaxsiy, butunlay shaxsiy ideal yaratmaganingizni oshkor qiladi: — chunki bu hech qachon boshqasining ideali bo'la olmasdi, hammaning, har kimning ideali u yoqda tursin! —— Hali ham «bu holatda har kim shunday harakat qilishi kerak edi» deb o'ylaydigan odam o'zini bilishda hali yarim o'nlab qadam ham oldinga siljimagan: aks holda u bilardiki, o'xshash harakatlar na bor, na bo'lishi mumkin, — qilingan har bir harakat butunlay yagona va takrorlanmas tarzda qilingan va barcha kelajakdagi harakatlar bilan ham shunday bo'ladi; barcha xulq qoidalari (va hatto hozirgacha barcha axloqlarning eng ezoterik va nozik qoidalari) faqat qo'pol tashqi tomonga taalluqli, — ular yordamida haqiqatan ham tenglik ko'rinishiga erishish mumkin, lekin faqat ko'rinishiga, — oldinga yoki orqaga qaraganda har bir harakat o'tib bo'lmas ish bo'lib qoladi va shunday qoladi, — bizning «yaxshi», «olijanob» va «buyuk» haqidagi fikrlarimiz hech qachon harakatlarimiz bilan isbotlanishi mumkin emas, chunki hech bir harakatni bilib bo'lmaydi, — bizning fikrlarimiz, baholarimiz va qadriyatlar jadvallarimiz albatta harakatlarimiz mexanizmidagi eng qudratli richaglar qatorida, lekin har bir alohida holatda ularning mexanizmi qonunini kuzatib bo'lmaydi.

paras.en: Let us confine ourselves, therefore, to the purification of our opinions and appreciations, and to the construction of new tables of value of our own:—we will, however, brood no longer over the "moral worth of our actions"! Yes, my friends! As regards the whole moral twaddle of people about one another, it is time to be disgusted with it! To sit in judgment morally ought to be opposed to our taste! Let us leave this nonsense and this bad taste to those who have nothing else to do, save to drag the past a little distance further through time, and who are never themselves the present,—consequently to the many, to the majority! We, however, would seek to become what we are,—the new, the unique, the incomparable, making laws for ourselves and creating ourselves!
paras.uz: Shuning uchun keling, o'z fikrlarimiz va baholarimizni poklash va o'zimizning yangi qadriyatlar jadvallarimizni qurish bilan cheklanaylik: — biroq endi «harakatlarimizning axloqiy qadri» ustida bosh qotirmaymiz! Ha, do'stlarim! Odamlarning bir-biri haqidagi butun axloqiy vaysashiga kelsak, undan bezish vaqti keldi! Axloqan hukm chiqarib o'tirish didimizga zid bo'lishi kerak! Bu bema'nilik va bu yomon didni o'tmishni vaqt bo'ylab yana ozgina sudrab borishdan boshqa ishi bo'lmagan va o'zlari hech qachon hozirgi zamon bo'lmaganlarga, — demak, ko'pchilikka, ko'pchilikka qoldiraylik! Biz esa o'zimiz bo'lgan narsaga aylanishga intilamiz, — yangi, yagona, tengsiz, o'zimizga qonun chiqaruvchi va o'zimizni yaratuvchi!

paras.en: And for this purpose we must become the best students and discoverers of all the laws and necessities in the world. We must be physicists in order to be creators in that sense,—whereas hitherto all appreciations and ideals have been based on ignorance of physics, or in contradiction to it. And therefore, three cheers for physics! And still louder cheers for that which impels us to it—our honesty.
paras.uz: Va buning uchun biz dunyodagi barcha qonunlar va zaruratlarning eng yaxshi o'rganuvchilari va kashfiyotchilari bo'lishimiz kerak. O'sha ma'noda yaratuvchi bo'lish uchun biz fiziklar bo'lishimiz kerak, — holbuki shu paytgacha barcha baholar va ideallar fizikani bilmaslikka yoki unga zidlikka asoslangan. Shuning uchun fizikaga uch karra olqish! Va bizni unga undaydigan narsaga — halolligimizga yana ham balandroq olqish!

paras.en: 336. Avarice of Nature. — Why has nature been so niggardly towards humanity that she has not let human beings shine, this man more and that man less, according to their inner abundance of light? Why have not great men such a fine visibility in their rising and setting as the sun? How much less equivocal would life among men then be!
paras.uz: 336. Tabiatning xasisligi. — Nega tabiat insoniyatga shunchalik xasislik qilib, insonlarni ichki nur mo'lligiga ko'ra, birini ko'proq, boshqasini kamroq porlashiga yo'l qo'ymagan? Nega buyuk odamlar chiqishi va botishida quyosh kabi shunday go'zal ko'rinishga ega emas? Odamlar orasidagi hayot o'shanda qanchalik kamroq ikki ma'noli bo'lardi!

chapters.recap_uz: Bozor shovqini davrida mutafakkir kar bo'lishni o'rganishi kerak. Bilish — mayllarning murosasi. Musiqani sevishni o'rgangandek, hamma narsani sevishni o'rganamiz. «Fizikaga olqish!»: vijdon ham tekshirilishi kerak; har bir harakat yagona.

chapters.title: The heaviest burden

paras.en: 337. Future "Humanity.". — When I look at this age with the eye of a distant future, I find nothing so remarkable in the man of the present day as his peculiar virtue and sickness called "the historical sense." It is a tendency to something quite new and foreign in history: if this embryo were given several centuries and more, there might finally evolve out of it a marvellous plant, with a smell equally marvellous, on account of which our old earth might be more pleasant to live in than it has been hitherto. We moderns are just beginning to form the chain of a very powerful, future sentiment, link by link,—we hardly know what we are doing.
paras.uz: 337. Kelajakdagi «insoniylik». — Bu davrga uzoq kelajak ko'zi bilan qaraganimda, hozirgi odamda «tarixiy tuyg'u» deb ataladigan uning o'ziga xos fazilati va kasalligichalik diqqatga sazovor narsa topmayman. Bu tarixda butunlay yangi va begona narsaga moyillik: agar bu kurtakka bir necha asr va undan ko'proq vaqt berilsa, undan oxir-oqibat ajoyib o'simlik rivojlanishi mumkin, xuddi shunday ajoyib hidi bilan, uning tufayli bizning eski yerimizda shu paytgacha bo'lganidan ko'ra yoqimliroq yashash mumkin bo'lar. Biz zamonaviylar juda kuchli, kelajakdagi tuyg'uning zanjirini halqama-halqa endigina shakllantira boshladik, — nima qilayotganimizni deyarli bilmaymiz.

paras.en: It almost seems to us as if it were not the question of a new sentiment, but of the decline of all old sentiments:—the historical sense is still something so poor and cold, and many are attacked by it as by a frost, and are made poorer and colder by it. To others it appears as the indication of stealthily approaching age, and our planet is regarded by them as a melancholy invalid, who, in order to forget his present condition, writes the history of his youth. In fact, this is one aspect of the new sentiment.
paras.uz: Bizga go'yo gap yangi tuyg'u haqida emas, balki barcha eski tuyg'ularning tanazzuli haqida ketayotgandek tuyuladi: — tarixiy tuyg'u hali shunchalik kambag'al va sovuq narsaki, ko'plarni u sovuqdek uradi va ularni yana ham kambag'alroq va sovuqroq qiladi. Boshqalarga u yashirincha yaqinlashayotgan qarilikning belgisi bo'lib ko'rinadi va ular bizning sayyoramizni hozirgi ahvolini unutish uchun yoshligi tarixini yozayotgan g'amgin bemor deb hisoblashadi. Haqiqatan ham, bu yangi tuyg'uning bir jihati.

paras.en: He who knows how to regard the history of man in its entirety as his own history, feels in the immense generalisation all the grief of the invalid who thinks of health, of the old man who thinks of the dream of his youth, of the lover who is robbed of his beloved, of the martyr whose ideal is destroyed, of the hero on the evening of the indecisive battle which has brought him wounds and the loss of a friend.
paras.uz: Inson tarixini butunligicha o'z tarixi deb qaray biladigan odam ulkan umumlashmada sog'liq haqida o'ylayotgan bemorning, yoshlik tushi haqida o'ylayotgan qariyaning, sevgilisidan judo qilingan oshiqning, ideali vayron qilingan shahidning, unga yaralar va do'st yo'qotishini keltirgan noaniq jangning kechqurunidagi qahramonning butun qayg'usini his qiladi.

paras.en: But to bear this immense sum of grief of all kinds, to be able to bear it, and yet still be the hero who at the commencement of a second day of battle greets the dawn and his happiness, as one who has an horizon of centuries before and behind him, as the heir of all nobility, of all past intellect, and the obligatory heir (as the noblest) of all the old nobles; while at the same time the first of a new nobility, the equal of which has never been seen nor even dreamt of: to take all this upon his soul, the oldest, the newest, the losses, hopes, conquests, and victories of mankind: to have all this at last in one soul, and to comprise it in one feeling:—this would necessarily furnish a happiness which man has not hitherto known,—a God's happiness, full of power and love, full of tears and laughter, a happiness which, like the sun in the evening, continually gives of its inexhaustible riches and empties into the sea,—and like the sun, too, feels itself richest when even the poorest fisherman rows with golden oars! This divine feeling might then be called—humanity!
paras.uz: Lekin har xil qayg'ularning bu ulkan yig'indisini ko'tarish, uni ko'tara olish va shunga qaramay ikkinchi jang kuni boshida tongni va baxtini olqishlaydigan qahramon bo'lib qolish, oldida va orqasida asrlar ufqi bo'lgan odam sifatida, barcha zodagonlikning, barcha o'tmish aqlning merosxo'ri va barcha eski zodagonlarning (eng olijanobi sifatida) majburiy merosxo'ri sifatida; shu bilan birga hech qachon ko'rilmagan va hatto orzu qilinmagan yangi zodagonlikning birinchisi sifatida: bularning hammasini — insoniyatning eng eskisi, eng yangisi, yo'qotishlari, umidlari, zabtlari va g'alabalarini qalbiga olish: bularning hammasini oxir-oqibat bitta qalbda ega bo'lish va bitta tuyg'uda jamlash: — bu muqarrar ravishda inson shu paytgacha bilmagan baxtni berardi, — qudrat va sevgiga to'la, ko'z yoshlari va kulgiga to'la xudoning baxti, kechqurungi quyosh kabi tugamas boyligidan doimo beradigan va dengizga to'kiladigan baxt, — va quyosh kabi, hatto eng kambag'al baliqchi oltin eshkaklar bilan eshkak eshganda o'zini eng boy his qiladigan baxt! Bu ilohiy tuyg'u o'shanda — insoniylik deb atalishi mumkin edi!

paras.en: 338. The Will to Suffering and the Compassionate. — Is it to your advantage to be above all compassionate? And is it to the advantage of the sufferers when you are so? But let us leave the first question for a moment without an answer.—That from which we suffer most profoundly and personally is almost incomprehensible and inaccessible to every one else: in this matter we are hidden from our neighbour even when he eats at the same table with us. Everywhere, however, where we are noticed as sufferers, our suffering is interpreted in a shallow way; it belongs to the nature of the emotion of pity to divest unfamiliar suffering of its properly personal character:—our "benefactors" lower our value and volition more than our enemies.
paras.uz: 338. Azob chekish irodasi va rahmdillar. — Hammadan avval rahmdil bo'lish sizga foydalimi? Va siz shunday bo'lganingizda azob chekuvchilarga foydalimi? Lekin birinchi savolni bir lahzaga javobsiz qoldiraylik. — Biz eng chuqur va shaxsan azob chekadigan narsa deyarli har kimga tushunarsiz va yetib bo'lmas: bu masalada biz hatto qo'shnimiz biz bilan bir dasturxonda ovqatlansa ham undan yashiringanmiz. Biroq azob chekuvchi sifatida payqalgan har joyda azobimiz sayoz talqin qilinadi; begona azobni o'zining haqiqiy shaxsiy xarakteridan mahrum qilish achinish tuyg'usining tabiatiga tegishli: — bizning «xayrixohlarimiz» qadrimiz va irodamizni dushmanlarimizdan ko'ra ko'proq pasaytiradi.

paras.en: In most benefits which are conferred on the unfortunate there is something shocking in the intellectual levity with which the compassionate person plays the rôle of fate: he knows nothing of all the inner consequences and complications which are called misfortune for me or for you! The entire economy of my soul and its adjustment by "misfortune," the uprising of new sources and needs, the closing up of old wounds, the repudiation of whole periods of the past—none of these things which may be connected with misfortune preoccupy the dear sympathiser. He wishes to succour, and does not reflect that there is a personal necessity for misfortune; that terror, want, impoverishment, midnight watches, adventures, hazards and mistakes are as necessary to me and to you as their opposites, yea, that, to speak mystically, the path to one's own heaven always leads through the voluptuousness of one's own hell.
paras.uz: Baxtsizlarga ko'rsatiladigan ko'pchilik yaxshiliklarda rahmdil odamning taqdir rolini o'ynashidagi aqliy yengiltaklikda qandaydir dahshatli narsa bor: u men yoki siz uchun baxtsizlik deb ataladigan barcha ichki oqibatlar va chigalliklar haqida hech narsa bilmaydi! Ruhimning butun iqtisodi va uning «baxtsizlik» bilan sozlanishi, yangi manbalar va ehtiyojlarning ko'tarilishi, eski yaralarning bitishi, o'tmishning butun davrlarini rad etish — baxtsizlik bilan bog'liq bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan bu narsalarning hech biri aziz hamdardni o'ylantirmaydi. U yordam bermoqchi va baxtsizlikka shaxsiy zarurat borligi haqida o'ylamaydi; dahshat, muhtojlik, qashshoqlik, yarim tungi bedorliklar, sarguzashtlar, tavakkalchiliklar va xatolar menga va sizga ularning qarama-qarshilari kabi zarur, ha, mistik tarzda aytganda, o'z jannatingga yo'l doimo o'z do'zaxingning rohati orqali o'tadi.

paras.en: No, he knows nothing thereof. The "religion of compassion" (or "the heart") bids him help, and he thinks he has helped best when he has helped most speedily! If you adherents of this religion actually have the same sentiments towards yourselves which you have towards your fellows, if you are unwilling to endure your own suffering even for an hour, and continually forestall all possible misfortune, if you regard suffering and pain generally as evil, as detestable, as deserving of annihilation, and as blots on existence, well, you have then, besides your religion of compassion, yet another religion in your heart (and this is perhaps the mother of the former)—the religion of smug ease. Ah, how little you know of the happiness of man, you comfortable and good-natured ones!—for happiness and misfortune are brother and sister, and twins, who grow tall together, or, as with you, remain small together!
paras.uz: Yo'q, u bu haqda hech narsa bilmaydi. «Rahmdillik dini» (yoki «yurak dini») unga yordam berishni buyuradi va u eng tez yordam berganda eng yaxshi yordam berdim deb o'ylaydi! Agar siz, bu din tarafdorlari, haqiqatan ham o'zingizga nisbatan yaqinlaringizga nisbatan bo'lgan tuyg'ularga ega bo'lsangiz, agar o'z azobingizga hatto bir soat ham chidashni istamasangiz va har qanday mumkin bo'lgan baxtsizlikning doimo oldini olsangiz, agar azob va og'riqni umuman yomonlik, jirkanch, yo'q qilinishga loyiq va hayotdagi dog'lar deb hisoblasangiz, xo'sh, unda sizning yuragingizda rahmdillik dinidan tashqari yana bir din bor (va bu balki birinchisining onasidir) — o'zidan mamnun farovonlik dini. Oh, siz, qulaylik sevar va xushfe'llar, inson baxti haqida qanchalik kam bilasiz! — chunki baxt va baxtsizlik aka-singil va egizaklar, ular birga baland o'sadi yoki, siz bilan bo'lganidek, birga kichik qoladi!

paras.en: But now let us return to the first question.—How is it at all possible for a person to keep to his path! Some cry or other is continually calling one aside: our eye then rarely lights on anything without it becoming necessary for us to leave for a moment our own affairs and rush to give assistance. I know there are hundreds of respectable and laudable methods of making me stray from my course, and in truth the most "moral" of methods! Indeed, the opinion of the present-day preachers of the morality of compassion goes so far as to imply that just this, and this alone is moral:—to stray from our course to that extent and to run to the assistance of our neighbour. I am equally certain that I need only give myself over to the sight of one case of actual distress, and I, too, am lost!
paras.uz: Lekin endi birinchi savolga qaytaylik. — Odamning o'z yo'lida qolishi umuman qanday mumkin! Qandaydir qichqiriq doimo odamni chetga chaqiradi: o'shanda ko'zimiz kamdan-kam biror narsaga tushadiki, bir lahzaga o'z ishlarimizni qoldirib, yordamga shoshilish zarur bo'lmasin. Bilaman, meni yo'limdan adashtirishning yuzlab hurmatli va maqtovga loyiq usullari bor, va haqiqatan ham eng «axloqiy» usullar! Haqiqatan ham, hozirgi rahmdillik axloqi va'zgo'ylarining fikri shunchalik uzoqqa boradiki, aynan shu, faqat shu axloqiy deb nazarda tutadi: — o'z yo'limizdan shu darajada adashish va qo'shnimizga yordamga yugurish. Men xuddi shunday aminmanki, haqiqiy qayg'uning bitta holatini ko'rishga berilsam bas, men ham yo'qolaman!

paras.en: And if a suffering friend said to me, "See, I shall soon die, only promise to die with me"—I might promise it, just as—to select for once bad examples for good reasons—the sight of a small, mountain people struggling for freedom, would bring me to the point of offering them my hand and my life.
paras.uz: Va agar azob chekayotgan do'stim menga: «Qara, men tez orada o'laman, faqat men bilan birga o'lishga va'da ber», desa — men va'da berishim mumkin edi, xuddi — yaxshi sabablarga ko'ra bir marta yomon misollarni tanlasam — erkinlik uchun kurashayotgan kichik, tog'li xalqni ko'rish meni ularga qo'limni va hayotimni taklif qilish nuqtasiga olib kelgani kabi.

paras.en: Indeed, there is even a secret seduction in all this awakening of compassion, and calling for help: our "own way" is a thing too hard and insistent, and too far removed from the love and gratitude of others,—we escape from it and from our most personal conscience, not at all unwillingly, and, seeking security in the conscience of others, we take refuge in the lovely temple of the "religion of pity." As soon now as any war breaks out, there always breaks out at the same time a certain secret delight precisely in the noblest class of the people: they rush with rapture to meet the new danger of death, because they believe that in the sacrifice for their country they have finally that long-sought-for permission—the permission to shirk their aim:—war is for them a detour to suicide, a detour, however, with a good conscience.
paras.uz: Haqiqatan ham, rahmdillikni uyg'otish va yordamga chaqirishning bularning hammasida hatto yashirin vasvasa ham bor: bizning «o'z yo'limiz» haddan tashqari og'ir va talabchan va boshqalarning sevgisi va minnatdorligidan haddan tashqari uzoq narsa, — biz undan va eng shaxsiy vijdonimizdan umuman istamasdan qochmaymiz va boshqalarning vijdonida xavfsizlik izlab, «achinish dini»ning yoqimli ibodatxonasiga panoh topamiz. Endi qandaydir urush boshlanishi bilanoq, aynan xalqning eng olijanob tabaqasida doimo bir vaqtning o'zida qandaydir yashirin zavq boshlanadi: ular vajd bilan yangi o'lim xavfiga qarshi yugurishadi, chunki vatan uchun qurbonlikda nihoyat uzoq izlagan ruxsatni — maqsadlaridan qochish ruxsatini olganlariga ishonishadi: — urush ular uchun o'z joniga qasd qilishga aylanma yo'l, biroq toza vijdon bilan aylanma yo'l.

paras.en: And although silent here about some things, I will not, however, be silent about my morality, which says to me: Live in concealment in order that thou mayest live to thyself. Live ignorant of that which seems to thy age to be most important! Put at least the skin of three centuries betwixt thyself and the present day! And the clamour of the present day, the noise of wars and revolutions, ought to be a murmur to thee! Thou wilt also want to help, but only those whose distress thou entirely understandest, because they have one sorrow and one hope in common with thee—thy friends: and only in the way that thou helpest thyself:—I want to make them more courageous, more enduring, more simple, more joyful! I want to teach them that which at present so few understand, and the preachers of fellowship in sorrow least of all:—namely, fellowship in joy!
paras.uz: Va bu yerda ba'zi narsalar haqida jim tursam ham, mening axloqim haqida jim turmayman, u menga deydi: O'zing uchun yashashing uchun yashirin yasha. Davringga eng muhim bo'lib ko'rinadigan narsadan bexabar yasha! Hech bo'lmasa o'zing bilan hozirgi kun orasiga uch asrning terisini qo'y! Va hozirgi kunning shovqini, urushlar va inqiloblarning shovqini senga shivirlash bo'lishi kerak! Sen ham yordam bermoqchi bo'lasan, lekin faqat qayg'usini to'liq tushunadiganlaringga, chunki ular sen bilan bitta qayg'u va bitta umidga ega — do'stlaringga: va faqat o'zingga yordam bergan tarzda: — men ularni jasurroq, chidamliroq, soddaroq, quvnoqroq qilmoqchiman! Men ularga hozir juda kam odam tushunadigan narsani, qayg'udagi hamkorlik va'zgo'ylari esa hammadan kam tushunadigan narsani o'rgatmoqchiman: — ya'ni quvonchdagi hamkorlikni!

paras.en: 339. Vita femina. — To see the ultimate beauties in a work—all knowledge and good-will is not enough; it requires the rarest, good chance for the veil of clouds to move for once from the summits, and for the sun to shine on them. We must not only stand at precisely the right place to see this, our very soul itself must have pulled away the veil from its heights, and must be in need of an external expression and simile, so as to have a support and remain master of itself. All these, however, are so rarely united at the same time that I am inclined to believe that the highest summit of all that is good, be it work, deed, man, or nature, has hitherto remained for most people, and even for the best, as something concealed and shrouded:—that, however, which unveils itself to us, unveils itself to us but once.
paras.uz: 339. Vita femina — Hayot ayoldir. — Asardagi eng oliy go'zalliklarni ko'rish uchun barcha bilim va yaxshi niyat yetarli emas; bulutlar pardasi bir marta cho'qqilardan siljishi va quyosh ularga porlashi uchun eng kamyob, yaxshi tasodif kerak. Buni ko'rish uchun biz nafaqat aynan to'g'ri joyda turishimiz kerak, balki ruhimizning o'zi ham o'z cho'qqilaridan pardani tortib olgan bo'lishi va tayanchga ega bo'lish va o'zi ustidan hukmron qolish uchun tashqi ifoda va o'xshatishga muhtoj bo'lishi kerak. Biroq bularning hammasi bir vaqtning o'zida shunchalik kamdan-kam birlashadiki, men barcha yaxshi narsalarning eng oliy cho'qqisi, xoh asar, xoh ish, xoh inson yoki tabiat bo'lsin, shu paytgacha ko'pchilik odamlar uchun, hatto eng yaxshilari uchun ham yashirin va o'ralgan narsa bo'lib qolgan deb ishonishga moyilman: — biroq bizga o'zini ochadigan narsa bizga faqat bir marta ochiladi.

paras.en: The Greeks indeed prayed: "Twice and thrice, everything beautiful!" Ah, they had their good reason to call on the Gods, for ungodly actuality does not furnish us with the beautiful at all, or only does so once! I mean to say that the world is overfull of beautiful things, but it is nevertheless poor, very poor, in beautiful moments, and in the unveiling of those beautiful things. But perhaps this is the greatest charm of life: it puts a gold-embroidered veil of lovely potentialities over itself, promising, resisting, modest, mocking, sympathetic, seductive. Yes, life is a woman!
paras.uz: Yunonlar haqiqatan ham: «Ikki va uch marta, har bir go'zal narsa!» deb ibodat qilishgan. Oh, ularda xudolarga murojaat qilish uchun yaxshi sabablari bor edi, chunki xudosiz haqiqat bizga go'zallikni umuman bermaydi yoki faqat bir marta beradi! Aytmoqchimanki, dunyo go'zal narsalarga to'lib-toshgan, lekin shunga qaramay go'zal lahzalarda va o'sha go'zal narsalarning ochilishida kambag'al, juda kambag'al. Lekin balki hayotning eng katta jozibasi shudir: u o'zi ustiga yoqimli imkoniyatlarning oltin kashtali pardasini yopadi, va'da beruvchi, qarshilik qiluvchi, hayoli, masxaraomuz, hamdard, yo'ldan uruvchi. Ha, hayot ayoldir!

paras.en: 340. The Dying Socrates. — I admire the courage and wisdom of Socrates in all that he did, said—and did not say. This mocking and amorous demon and rat-catcher of Athens, who made the most insolent youths tremble and sob was not only the wisest babbler that has ever lived, but was just as great in his silence. I would that he had also been silent in the last moment of his life,—perhaps he might then have belonged to a still higher order of intellects. Whether it was death, or the poison, or piety, or wickedness—something or other loosened his tongue at that moment, and he said: "O Crito, I owe a cock to Asclepios." For him who has ears, this ludicrous and terrible "last word" implies: "O Crito, life is a long sickness!" Is it possible! A man like him, who had lived cheerfully and to all appearance as a soldier,—was a pessimist!
paras.uz: 340. O'layotgan Sokrat. — Men Sokratning qilgan, aytgan — va aytmagan hamma narsasidagi jasorati va donoligiga qoyil qolaman. Eng surbet yigitlarni titratib, yig'latgan Afinaning bu masxaraboz va oshiqona jini va kalamush ovchisi nafaqat hozirgacha yashagan eng dono vaysaqi edi, balki jimligida ham xuddi shunday buyuk edi. Qaniydi u hayotining oxirgi lahzasida ham jim tursa, — balki o'shanda u aqllarning yana ham yuksakroq tartibiga mansub bo'lar edi. O'lim bo'ldimi, yoki zahar, yoki taqvo, yoki yovuzlik — nimadir o'sha lahzada uning tilini bo'shatdi va u dedi: «Oh, Kriton, men Asklepiyga bir xo'roz qarzdorman». Qulog'i bor odam uchun bu kulgili va dahshatli «oxirgi so'z» shuni anglatadi: «Oh, Kriton, hayot — uzoq kasallik!» Nahotki! Quvnoq va har jihatdan askar kabi yashagan u kabi odam — pessimist bo'lgan!

paras.en: He had merely put on a good demeanour towards life, and had all along concealed his ultimate judgment, his profoundest sentiment! Socrates, Socrates had suffered from life! And he also took his revenge for it—with that veiled, fearful, pious, and blasphemous phrase! Had even a Socrates to revenge himself? Was there a grain too little of magnanimity in his superabundant virtue? Ah, my friends! We must surpass even the Greeks!
paras.uz: U shunchaki hayotga nisbatan yaxshi qiyofa kiygan va doimo o'zining oxirgi hukmini, eng chuqur tuyg'usini yashirgan! Sokrat, Sokrat hayotdan azob chekkan! Va u buning uchun ham o'ch oldi — o'sha pardalangan, dahshatli, taqvodor va kufrona ibora bilan! Hatto Sokrat ham o'ch olishi kerakmidi? Uning to'lib-toshgan fazilatida saxiylikdan bir donasi kammidi? Oh, do'stlarim! Biz hatto yunonlardan ham o'zib ketishimiz kerak!

paras.en: 341. The Heaviest Burden. — What if a demon crept after thee into thy loneliest loneliness some day or night, and said to thee: "This life, as thou livest it at present, and hast lived it, thou must live it once more, and also innumerable times; and there will be nothing new in it, but every pain and every joy and every thought and every sigh, and all the unspeakably small and great in thy life must come to thee again, and all in the same series and sequence—and similarly this spider and this moonlight among the trees, and similarly this moment, and I myself. The eternal sand-glass of existence will ever be turned once more, and thou with it, thou speck of dust!"—Wouldst thou not throw thyself down and gnash thy teeth, and curse the demon that so spake? Or hast thou once experienced a tremendous moment in which thou wouldst answer him:
paras.uz: 341. Eng og'ir yuk. — Agar bir kun yoki bir kecha qandaydir jin eng yolg'iz yolg'izligingga orqangdan o'rmalab kirib, senga: «Bu hayotni, hozir yashayotganingdek va yashab kelganingdek, yana bir marta va yana son-sanoqsiz marta yashashing kerak; va unda yangi hech narsa bo'lmaydi, balki har bir og'riq va har bir quvonch, har bir fikr va har bir xo'rsinish, hayotingdagi aytib bo'lmas darajada kichik va katta hamma narsa senga qaytib kelishi kerak, va hammasi bir xil qator va ketma-ketlikda — xuddi shunday bu o'rgimchak va daraxtlar orasidagi bu oy nuri, xuddi shunday bu lahza va men o'zim ham. Hayotning abadiy qum soati doimo yana ag'dariladi, sen ham u bilan birga, ey chang zarrasi!» desa-chi? — O'zingni yerga tashlab, tishlaringni g'ijirlatib, shunday gapirgan jinni la'natlamasmiding? Yoki bir marta shunday dahshatli lahzani boshdan kechirganmisanki, unda unga shunday javob bergan bo'larding:

paras.en: "Thou art a God, and never did I hear aught more divine!" If that thought acquired power over thee, as thou art, it would transform thee, and perhaps crush thee; the question with regard to all and everything: "Dost thou want this once more, and also for innumerable times?" would lie as the heaviest burden upon thy activity! Or, how wouldst thou have to become favourably inclined to thyself and to life, so as to long for nothing more ardently than for this last eternal sanctioning and sealing?—
paras.uz: «Sen xudosan va men hech qachon bundan ilohiyroq narsa eshitmaganman!» Agar bu fikr senga, qanday bo'lsang shunday, hukmronlik qilsa, seni o'zgartirardi va balki ezib tashlardi; hamma narsa va har bir narsaga nisbatan «Buni yana bir marta va yana son-sanoqsiz marta istaysanmi?» degan savol faoliyating ustida eng og'ir yuk bo'lib yotardi! Yoki bu oxirgi abadiy tasdiqlash va muhrlashdan ko'ra qizg'inroq hech narsani orzu qilmaslik uchun o'zingga va hayotga qanchalik xayrixoh bo'lishing kerak edi? —

paras.en: 342. Incipit Tragœdia. — When Zarathustra was thirty years old, he left his home and the Lake of Urmi, and went into the mountains. There he enjoyed his spirit and his solitude, and for ten years did not weary of it. But at last his heart changed,—and rising one morning with the rosy dawn, he went before the sun and spake thus unto it: "Thou great star! What would be thy happiness if thou hadst not those for whom thou shinest! For ten years hast thou climbed hither unto my cave: thou wouldst have wearied of thy light and of the journey, had it not been for me, mine eagle, and my serpent. But we awaited thee every morning, took from thee thine overflow, and blessed thee for it. Lo! I am weary of my wisdom, like the bee that hath gathered too much honey; I need hands outstretched to take it.
paras.uz: 342. Incipit tragoedia — Tragediya boshlanadi. — Zardusht o'ttiz yoshga to'lganda uyini va Urmiya ko'lini tark etib, tog'larga ketdi. U yerda o'z ruhi va yolg'izligidan zavqlandi va o'n yil davomida undan charchamadi. Lekin oxir-oqibat uning yuragi o'zgardi, — va bir kuni ertalab pushti tong bilan turib, quyosh oldiga chiqdi va unga shunday dedi: «Sen buyuk yulduz! Agar sen porlaydiganlaring bo'lmasa, baxting nima bo'lardi! O'n yil davomida sen bu yerga, g'orimga ko'tarilding: agar men, burgutim va ilonim bo'lmaganimizda, sen o'z nuringdan va sayohatdan charchagan bo'larding. Lekin biz seni har tong kutdik, sendan ortiqchangni oldik va buning uchun seni duo qildik. Mana! Men haddan tashqari ko'p asal yig'gan asalaridek donoligimdan charchadim; menga uni olish uchun cho'zilgan qo'llar kerak.

paras.en: I would fain bestow and distribute, until the wise have once more become joyous in their folly, and the poor happy in their riches. Therefore must I descend into the deep, as thou doest in the evening, when thou goest behind the sea and givest light also to the nether-world, thou most rich star! Like thee must I go down, as men say, to whom I shall descend. Bless me then, thou tranquil eye, that canst behold even the greatest happiness without envy! Bless the cup that is about to overflow, that the water may flow golden out of it, and carry everywhere the reflection of thy bliss! Lo! This cup is again going to empty itself, and Zarathustra is again going to be a man."—Thus began Zarathustra's down-going.
paras.uz: Men donolar yana o'z ahmoqliklarida quvnoq va kambag'allar o'z boyliklarida baxtli bo'lmaguncha in'om qilmoqchi va ulashmoqchiman. Shuning uchun men chuqurlikka tushishim kerak, xuddi sen kechqurun dengiz ortiga o'tib, quyi dunyoga ham nur berganingdek, ey eng boy yulduz! Sen kabi men ham, odamlar aytganidek, botishim kerak, men tushadigan odamlarga. Unda meni duo qil, ey hatto eng katta baxtni ham hasadsiz ko'ra oladigan sokin ko'z! To'lib-toshmoqchi bo'lgan kosani duo qil, toki undan suv oltin bo'lib oqsin va hamma joyga saodatingning aksini olib borsin! Mana! Bu kosa yana bo'shamoqchi va Zardusht yana inson bo'lmoqchi». — Zardushtning botishi shunday boshlandi.

chapters.recap_uz: To'rtinchi kitob cho'qqisi: tarixiy tuyg'u va «insoniylik», rahmdillik dinini tanqid, «hayot ayoldir», o'layotgan Sokrat va eng mashhur g'oya — abadiy qaytish: hayotingni son-sanoqsiz marta qayta yashashga rozimisan? Oxirida Zardusht tog'dan tushadi.

paras.en: 343. What our Cheerfulness Signifies. — The most important of more recent events—that "God is dead," that the belief in the Christian God has become unworthy of belief—already begins to cast its first shadows over Europe.
